---
<!-- definition-1: body_md -->
\label{definitiongeneralizedspaceofstates}
We will define {\em a space of states} (denoted ${ \relax{S}}$) to be a poset satisfying
\begin{itemize}
\@par\hangindent 2em ${ \relax{S}}$ is a down complete Inf semi-lattice 
\@par\hangindent 2em ${ \relax{S}}$ admits a bottom element (denoted $\bot_{{}_{ \relax{S}}}$).
\end{itemize}
The Infimum of a family $\{\,\sigma_i\;\vert\; i\in I\,\}\subseteq { \relax{S}}$ will be denoted $\bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{ \relax{S}}}}_{i\in I}\sigma_i$. The associated partial order on ${ \relax{S}}$ will be denoted by $\sqsubseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}}$.
<!-- end definition-1 -->
<!-- definition-2: body_md -->
\label{FiniteRankCondition}
We will say that the space of states ${ \relax{S}}$ satisfies the {\em Finite Rank Condition} iff 
\begin{eqnarray}
\forall U\subseteq { \relax{S}}\;\vert\; \widehat{\;U\;}{}^{{}^{{ \relax{S}}}},&&\exists \;\textit{\rm $V$ finite subset of ${ \relax{S}}$ with}\nonumber\\&& (\forall \sigma\in V,\exists \sigma'\in U, \sigma\sqsubseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma') \;\textit{\rm and}\;(\bigsqcup{}^{{}^{{ \relax{S}}}}  U=\bigsqcup{}^{{}^{{ \relax{S}}}}  V).\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\label{finiterank}
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end definition-2 -->
<!-- definition-3: body_md -->
\label{defpurestates}
We will say that {\em the space of states ${ \relax{S}}$ admits a description in terms of pure states} iff we have moreover
that the set of complely meet-irreducible elements of ${ \relax{S}}$, denoted ${ \relax{S}}^{{}^{pure}}$ and called {\em set of pure states}, is equal to the set of maximal elements $Max({ \relax{S}})$ and it 
 is a generating set for ${ \relax{S}}$, i.e.  
\begin{eqnarray}
&&\forall \sigma \in { \relax{S}}, \;\; \sigma= \bigsqcap{}^{{}^{ { \relax{S}}}}  \underline{\sigma}_{{}_{ { \relax{S}}}} ,\;\;\textit{\rm where}\;\;
\underline{\sigma}_{{}_{ { \relax{S}}}}:=
({ \relax{S}}^{{}^{pure}} \cap (\uparrow^{{}^{ { \relax{S}}}}\!\!\!\! \sigma) ) \;\;\textit{\rm and}\;\; { \relax{S}}^{{}^{pure}}=Max({ \relax{S}}).\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;
\label{completemeetirreducibleordergenerating}
\end{eqnarray}
Except if explicitly mentioned, we will not explicitly assume that the considered spaces of states admit a description in terms of pure states.
<!-- end definition-3 -->
<!-- definition-4: body_md -->
\label{defgeneralizedeffectspace}
The {\em space of effects}, denoted ${ \relax{E}}_{ \relax{S}}$ is defined to be 
\begin{eqnarray}
{ \relax{E}}_{ \relax{S}}:=\{ { \relax{l}}_{{}_{(\sigma,\sigma')}}\;\vert\; \sigma,\sigma'\in { \relax{S}},\;\neg \widehat{\sigma\sigma'}{}^{{}^{ \relax{S}}}\;\}\cup \{ { \relax{l}}_{{}_{(\sigma,\centerdot)}}\;\vert\; \sigma\in { \relax{S}}\;\}\cup \{ { \relax{l}}_{{}_{(\centerdot,\sigma)}}\;\vert\; \sigma\in { \relax{S}}\;\}\cup \{\, { \relax{l}}_{{}_{(\centerdot,\centerdot)}}\,\} &&\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;
\end{eqnarray}
as a set, with the following Inf semi-lattice law
\begin{eqnarray}
{ \relax{l}}_{{}_{(\sigma_1,\sigma'_1)}} \sqcap_{{}_{{ \relax{E}}_{ \relax{S}}}} { \relax{l}}_{{}_{(\sigma_2,\sigma'_2)}} &=& \left\{ \begin{array}{lcl}
{ \relax{l}}_{{}_{(\sigma_1\sqcup_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}} \sigma_2,\sigma'_1 \sqcup_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}} \sigma'_2)}} & \textit{\rm if} & \widehat{\sigma_1\sigma_2}{}^{{}^{ \relax{S}}}\;\textit{\rm and}\; \widehat{\sigma'_1\sigma'_2}{}^{{}^{ \relax{S}}}\\
{ \relax{l}}_{{}_{(\;\centerdot\;,\sigma'_1 \sqcup_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}} \sigma'_2)}} & \textit{\rm if} & \neg \widehat{\sigma_1\sigma_2}{}^{{}^{ \relax{S}}}\;\textit{\rm and}\; \widehat{\sigma'_1\sigma'_2}{}^{{}^{ \relax{S}}}\\
{ \relax{l}}_{{}_{(\sigma_1\sqcup_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}} \sigma_2,\;\centerdot\;)}} & \textit{\rm if} & \widehat{\sigma_1\sigma_2}{}^{{}^{ \relax{S}}}\;\textit{\rm and}\; \neg\widehat{\sigma'_1\sigma'_2}{}^{{}^{ \relax{S}}}\\
{ \relax{l}}_{{}_{(\centerdot,\centerdot)}} & \textit{\rm if} & \neg\widehat{\sigma_1\sigma_2}{}^{{}^{ \relax{S}}}\;\textit{\rm and}\; \neg\widehat{\sigma'_1\sigma'_2}{}^{{}^{ \relax{S}}}
\end{array}\right.\label{defcapES}
\end{eqnarray}
This expression is naturally extended to the whole set of effects (i.e. including the elements of the form ${ \relax{l}}_{{}_{(\sigma,\centerdot)}}$, ${ \relax{l}}_{{}_{(\centerdot,\sigma)}}$ and ${ \relax{l}}_{{}_{(\centerdot,\centerdot)}}$) as long as we adopt the convention defining 
\begin{eqnarray}
\forall \sigma\in { \relax{S}},\;\;\;\;\neg\widehat{\;\centerdot\;\sigma}{}^{{}^{ \relax{S}}}:= \textit{\rm TRUE}\;\;\;\;\;\;\; &\textit{\rm and}& \;\;\;\;\;\;\; \neg\widehat{\;\centerdot\;\centerdot\;}{}^{{}^{ \relax{S}}}:= \textit{\rm TRUE}.
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end definition-4 -->
<!-- definition-5: body_md -->
The evaluation map $\epsilon^{ \relax{S}}$ is defined by
\begin{eqnarray}
\epsilon^{ \relax{S}}_{{ \relax{l}}_{{}_{(\sigma,\sigma')}}}(\sigma'') &:= & \left\{ \begin{array}{lcl} \textit{\bf Y} & \textit{\rm if} & \sigma\sqsubseteq_{{}_{ \relax{S}}} \sigma''\\\textit{\bf N} & \textit{\rm if} & \sigma'\sqsubseteq_{{}_{ \relax{S}}} \sigma''\\ \bot & \textit{\rm otherwise } &\end{array}\right.\label{defepsilonS}
\end{eqnarray}
this expression is naturally extended to the whole set of effects by adopting the following convention
\begin{eqnarray}
\forall \sigma\in { \relax{S}},\;\; (\;\sigma\;\sqsubseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}}\centerdot ) & :=&\textit{\rm TRUE}.
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end definition-5 -->
<!-- definition-6: body_md -->
We will adopt the following notations :
\begin{eqnarray}
\bot_{{}_{{ \relax{E}}_{ \relax{S}}}} & := & { \relax{l}}_{{}_{(\centerdot,\centerdot)}}\\
{ \relax{Y}}_{{}_{{ \relax{E}}_{ \relax{S}}}} & := & { \relax{l}}_{{}_{(\bot_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}},\centerdot)}}\\
\forall \sigma_1,\sigma_2\in { \relax{S}}\cup\{\centerdot\},\;\;\;\;\;\; \overline{{ \relax{l}}_{{}_{(\sigma_1,\sigma_2)}}}& := & { \relax{l}}_{{}_{(\sigma_2,\sigma_1)}}
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end definition-6 -->
<!-- lemma-1: body_md -->
The evaluation map $\epsilon^{ \relax{S}}$ satisfies the following properties :
\begin{eqnarray}
\forall { \relax{l}}\in { \relax{E}}_{ \relax{S}},\forall S\subseteq { \relax{S}}, && { \epsilon}^{ \relax{S}}_{ { \relax{l}}}(\bigsqcap{}^{{}^{ \relax{S}}} S)=\bigwedge{}_{{}_{\sigma\in S}}\; { \epsilon}^{ \relax{S}}_{ { \relax{l}}}(\sigma),
 \label{axiomsigmainfsemilattice}\\
 \forall \sigma\in { \relax{S}},\forall E\subseteq { \relax{E}}_{ \relax{S}},&&{ \epsilon}^{ \relax{S}}_{\bigsqcap{}^{{}^{ \relax{E}_{ \relax{S}}}} E}(\sigma)=\bigwedge{}_{{}_{{ \relax{l}}\in E}}\; { \epsilon}^{ \relax{S}}_{ { \relax{l}}}(\sigma),\label{axiomEinfsemilattice}\\
 \forall { \relax{l}}\in { \relax{E}}_{ \relax{S}}, \forall \sigma\in { \relax{S}}, & & { \epsilon}^{ \relax{S}}_{ \overline{\; \relax{l}\;}}(\sigma)= \overline{{ \epsilon}^{ \relax{S}}_{ { \relax{l}}}(\sigma)},\label{etbar}\\
\forall \sigma\in { \relax{S}}, & & { \epsilon}^{ \relax{S}}_{{ \relax{Y}}_{ \relax{E}_{ \relax{S}}}}(\sigma)= \textit{\bf Y},\label{ety}\\
\forall \sigma\in { \relax{S}},  & & { \epsilon}^{ \relax{S}}_{\bot_{ \relax{E}_{ \relax{S}}}}(\sigma)= \bot.
\end{eqnarray}
and 
\begin{eqnarray}
&& \forall { \relax{l}},{ \relax{l}}'\in { \relax{E}}_{ \relax{S}},\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;(\, \forall \sigma\in { \relax{S}},\; { \epsilon}^{ \relax{S}}_{ { \relax{l}}}(\sigma)={ \epsilon}^{ \relax{S}}_{ { \relax{l}}'}(\sigma) \,) \Leftrightarrow  (\, { \relax{l}}= { \relax{l}}' \,),\label{Chuextensional}\\    
&& \forall \sigma,\sigma'\in { \relax{S}},\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;(\, \forall { \relax{l}}\in { \relax{E}}_{ \relax{S}},\; { \epsilon}^{ \relax{S}}_{ { \relax{l}}}(\sigma)={ \epsilon}^{ \relax{S}}_{ { \relax{l}}}(\sigma') \,) \Leftrightarrow  (\, \sigma= \sigma' \,)\label{Chuseparated}    
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end lemma-1 -->
<!-- lemma-2: body_md -->
\label{lemma2compatiblemeasurements}
If $(\sigma_1\sqcap_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}} \sigma_2)$ and $(\sigma'_1\sqcap_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}} \sigma'_2)$ admit no common upper-bound in ${ \relax{S}}$, then ${ \relax{l}}_{{}_{(\sigma_1,\sigma'_1)}}$ and ${ \relax{l}}_{{}_{(\sigma_2,\sigma'_2)}}$ admit a common upper-bound in ${ \relax{E}}_{ \relax{S}}$ which is ${ \relax{l}}_{{}_{(\sigma_1\sqcap_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}} \sigma_2,\sigma'_1\sqcap_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}} \sigma'_2)}}$.  As a consequence, the supremum $({ \relax{l}}_{{}_{(\sigma_1,\sigma'_1)}} \sqcup_{{}_{{ \relax{E}}_{ \relax{S}}}} { \relax{l}}_{{}_{(\sigma_2,\sigma'_2)}})$ exists in ${ \relax{E}}_{ \relax{S}}$ and is given by
\begin{eqnarray}
{ \relax{l}}_{{}_{(\sigma_1,\sigma'_1)}} \sqcup_{{}_{{ \relax{E}}_{ \relax{S}}}} { \relax{l}}_{{}_{(\sigma_2,\sigma'_2)}}  &=& { \relax{l}}_{{}_{(\sigma_1\sqcap_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}} \sigma_2,\sigma'_1\sqcap_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}} \sigma'_2)}}.
\end{eqnarray}
This result can be extended to the whole set of effects as long as we adopt the following conventions  
\begin{eqnarray}
(\;\centerdot\;\sqcap_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}} \sigma) := \sigma  \;\;\;\;\;\;\; &\textit{\rm and}& \;\;\;\;\;\;\;  (\;\centerdot\;\sqcap_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}} \;\centerdot\;) := \;\centerdot\;
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end lemma-2 -->
<!-- definition-7: body_md -->
We will consider the morphisms from a States/Effects Chu space $({ \relax{S}}_{A},{ \relax{E}}_{{ \relax{S}}_A},\epsilon^{{ \relax{S}}_A})$ to another States/Effects Chu space $({ \relax{S}}_{B},{ \relax{E}}_{{ \relax{S}}_B},\epsilon^{{ \relax{S}}_B})$, i.e.  pairs of maps $f : { \relax{S}}_{A} \rightarrow { \relax{S}}_{B}$ and $f^{\ast} : { \relax{E}}_{{ \relax{S}}_B}\rightarrow { \relax{E}}_{{ \relax{S}}_A}$ satisfying the following properties  
\begin{eqnarray} 
\forall \sigma_A\in { \relax{S}}_{A}, \forall { \relax{l}}_B \in { \relax{E}}_{{ \relax{S}}_B}&&\epsilon^{{ \relax{S}}_B}_{{ \relax{l}}_B}(f(\sigma_A))=\epsilon^{{ \relax{S}}_A}_{f^{\ast}({ \relax{l}}_B)}(\sigma_A).\label{defchumorphism}
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end definition-7 -->
<!-- remark-1: body_md -->
Note that, the eventual surjectivity of $f^{\ast}$ implies the injectivity of $f$.  This point uses the property ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@Chuseparated\endcsname\@firstoftwo{Chuseparated}}}).  Explicitly,
\begin{eqnarray}
\forall \sigma_A,\sigma'_A\in { \relax{S}}_{A},\;\; f(\sigma_A)=f(\sigma'_A) &\Leftrightarrow & (\,\forall { \relax{l}}_B\in { \relax{E}}_{{ \relax{S}}_B},\;\epsilon^{{ \relax{S}}_B}_{{ \relax{l}}_B}(f(\sigma_A))=\epsilon^{{ \relax{S}}_B}_{{ \relax{l}}_B}(f(\sigma'_A))\,)\nonumber\\
&\Leftrightarrow & (\,\forall { \relax{l}}_B\in { \relax{E}}_{{ \relax{S}}_B},\;\epsilon^{{ \relax{S}}_B}_{f^{\ast}({ \relax{l}}_B)}(\sigma_A)=\epsilon^{{ \relax{S}}_B}_{f^{\ast}({ \relax{l}}_B)}(\sigma'_A)\,)\nonumber\\
&\Leftrightarrow & (\,\forall { \relax{l}}'_B\in { \relax{E}}_{{ \relax{S}}_B},\;\epsilon^{{ \relax{S}}_B}_{{ \relax{l}}'_B}(\sigma_A)=\epsilon^{{ \relax{S}}_B}_{{ \relax{l}}'_B}(\sigma'_A)\,)\nonumber\\
&\Leftrightarrow & (\, \sigma_A=\sigma'_A\,).
\end{eqnarray}
In the same way,  using the properties ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@Chuextensional\endcsname\@firstoftwo{Chuextensional}}}) and the eventual surjectivity of $f$, we can deduce the injectivity of $f^{\ast}$.
<!-- end remark-1 -->
<!-- theorem-1: body_md -->
The left-component $f$ of a Chu morphism from $({ \relax{S}}_A,{ \relax{E}}_{{ \relax{S}}_A},\epsilon^{{ \relax{S}}_A})$ to $({ \relax{S}}_B,{ \relax{E}}_{{ \relax{S}}_B},\epsilon^{{ \relax{S}}_B})$ satisfies
\begin{eqnarray}
\forall S\subseteq { \relax{S}}_A,&& f(\bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{ \relax{S}}_A}} \! S) = \bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{ \relax{S}}_B}}_{{}_{\sigma\in S}} \; f(\sigma)\label{f12cap}
   
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  
\end{eqnarray}
                                                                                  
The right-component $f^{\ast}$ of a Chu morphism from $({ \relax{S}}_A,{ \relax{E}}_{{ \relax{S}}_A},\epsilon^{{ \relax{S}}_A})$ to $({ \relax{S}}_B,{ \relax{E}}_{{ \relax{S}}_B},\epsilon^{{ \relax{S}}_B})$ satisfies
\begin{eqnarray}
\forall E\subseteq { \relax{E}}_{{ \relax{S}}_B},&& f^{\ast}(\bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{ \relax{E}}_{{ \relax{S}}_B}}} \! E) = \bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{ \relax{E}}_{{ \relax{S}}_A}}}_{{}_{{ \relax{l}}\in E}} \; f^{\ast}({ \relax{l}})\label{f21cap}\\
                                                                                                                                                                                                                         
\forall { \relax{l}} \in { \relax{E}}_{{ \relax{S}}_B},&& f^{\ast}(\; \overline{\,{ \relax{l}}\,} \;) = \overline{f^{\ast}({ \relax{l}})}\label{f21bar}\\
&& f^{\ast}(\;{ \relax{Y}}_{{ \relax{E}}_{{ \relax{S}}_B}}\;) = { \relax{Y}}_{{ \relax{E}}_{{ \relax{S}}_A}}.\label{f21Y}    
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end theorem-1 -->
<!-- proof-1: body_md -->
All proofs follow the same trick based on the duality relation ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@defchumorphism\endcsname\@firstoftwo{defchumorphism}}}) and the separation property ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@Chuseparated\endcsname\@firstoftwo{Chuseparated}}}).  For example, for any $S\subseteq { \relax{S}}_A$ and any ${ \relax{l}} \in { \relax{E}}_{{ \relax{S}}_B}$, we have, using ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@defchumorphism\endcsname\@firstoftwo{defchumorphism}}}) and ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@axiomEinfsemilattice\endcsname\@firstoftwo{axiomEinfsemilattice}}}) :
\begin{eqnarray}
\epsilon^{{ \relax{S}}_B}_{{ \relax{l}}}(f(\bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{ \relax{S}}_A}} \!\! S)) &=& \epsilon^{{ \relax{S}}_A}_{f^{\ast}({ \relax{l}})}(\bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{ \relax{S}}_A}} \!\! S)\nonumber\\
&=& \bigwedge{}_{\sigma\in S} \; \epsilon^{{ \relax{S}}_A}_{f^{\ast}({ \relax{l}})}(\sigma)\nonumber\\
&=&  \bigwedge{}_{\sigma\in S} \; \epsilon^{{ \relax{S}}_B}_{{ \relax{l}}}(f(\sigma))\nonumber\\
&=&  \epsilon^{{ \relax{S}}_B}_{{ \relax{l}}}(\bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{ \relax{S}}_B}}_{\sigma\in S} f(\sigma))
\end{eqnarray}
We now use the property ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@Chuseparated\endcsname\@firstoftwo{Chuseparated}}}) to deduce ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@f12cap\endcsname\@firstoftwo{f12cap}}}).
<!-- end proof-1 -->
<!-- theorem-2: body_md -->
The composition of a morphism $(f ,f^{\ast})$ from $({ \relax{S}}_A,{ \relax{E}}_{{ \relax{S}}_A},\epsilon^{{ \relax{S}}_A})$ to $({ \relax{S}}_B,{ \relax{E}}_{{ \relax{S}}_B},\epsilon^{{ \relax{S}}_B})$ by another morphism $(g ,g^{\ast})$ defined from $({ \relax{S}}_B,{ \relax{E}}_{{ \relax{S}}_B},\epsilon^{{ \relax{S}}_B})$ to $({ \relax{S}}_C,{ \relax{E}}_{{ \relax{S}}_C},\epsilon^{{ \relax{S}}_C})$ is given by 
$( g\circ f ,f^{\ast} \circ g^{\ast})$ defining a valid morphism from $({ \relax{S}}_A,{ \relax{E}}_{{ \relax{S}}_A},\epsilon^{{ \relax{S}}_A})$ to $({ \relax{S}}_C,{ \relax{E}}_{{ \relax{S}}_C},\epsilon^{{ \relax{S}}_C})$.
<!-- end theorem-2 -->
<!-- proof-2: body_md -->
Using two times the duality property, we obtain
\begin{eqnarray} 
\epsilon^{{ \relax{S}}_C}_{{ \relax{l}}_C}(g\circ f (\sigma_A))&=&
\epsilon^{{ \relax{S}}_B}_{g^{\ast}({ \relax{l}}_C)}(f (\sigma_A))=
\epsilon^{{ \relax{S}}_A}_{f^{\ast} \circ g^{\ast}({ \relax{l}}_C)}(\sigma_A).
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end proof-2 -->
<!-- lemma-3: body_md -->
\label{aepsilonsigma}
Let us consider a states/effects Chu space $({ \relax{S}},{ \relax{E}}_{{ \relax{S}}},\epsilon^{{ \relax{S}}})$. 
Let us consider a map $(A : { \relax{S}}\longrightarrow { \relax{B}},  \sigma \mapsto { \relax{a}}_{\sigma})$ satisfying
\begin{eqnarray}
                                                                                                                                                                                          
\forall \{\sigma_i\;\vert\; i\in I\}\subseteq { \relax{S}},&&  { \relax{a}}_{{\bigsqcap{}^{{}^{ \relax{S}}}_{{}_{i\in i}}\sigma_i}} = \bigwedge{}_{{i\in I}} \;{ \relax{a}}_{{\sigma_i}},\label{theorema2}
\end{eqnarray}
Then, we have
\begin{eqnarray}
\exists \textit{\bf !} \;{ \relax{l}}\in { \relax{E}}_{ \relax{S}} & \vert & \forall \sigma\in { \relax{S}}, \; { \epsilon}^{ \relax{S}}_{{ \relax{l}}}(\sigma)={ \relax{a}}_{\sigma}.
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end lemma-3 -->
<!-- proof-3: body_md -->
Straightforward. If $\{\, \sigma\;\vert\; { \relax{a}}_{\sigma}=\textit{\bf Y}\,\}$ and $\{\, \sigma\;\vert\; { \relax{a}}_{\sigma}=\textit{\bf N}\,\}$ are not empty, it suffices to define $\Sigma_A:=\bigsqcap^{{}^{{ \relax{S}}}}\{\, \sigma\;\vert\; { \relax{a}}_{\sigma}=\textit{\bf Y}\,\}$,  $\Sigma_A':=\bigsqcap^{{}^{{ \relax{S}}}}\{\, \sigma\;\vert\; { \relax{a}}_{\sigma}=\textit{\bf N}\,\}$ and ${ \relax{l}}:={ \relax{l}}_{(\Sigma_A,\Sigma_A')} $ (the case where some or all of these subsets are empty is treated immediately).\\
The uniqueness of ${ \relax{l}}$ is guarantied by the property ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@Chuextensional\endcsname\@firstoftwo{Chuextensional}}}).
<!-- end proof-3 -->
<!-- theorem-3: body_md -->
For any map $f:{ \relax{S}}_A \longrightarrow { \relax{S}}_B$ satisfying 
\begin{eqnarray}
\forall \{\sigma_i\;\vert\; i\in I\}\subseteq { \relax{S}}_A, \; f({\bigsqcap{}^{{}^{ \relax{S}_A}}_{{}_{i\in i}}\sigma_i}) = \bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{ \relax{S}}_B}}_{{i\in I}} \;f(\sigma_i), 
\end{eqnarray}
there exists a unique map $f^\ast: { \relax{E}}_{ \relax{S}_B} \longrightarrow { \relax{E}}_{ \relax{S}_A}$ such that $(f,f^{\ast})$ is a morphism from the States/Effects Chu space $({ \relax{S}}_{A},{ \relax{E}}_{{ \relax{S}}_A},\epsilon^{{ \relax{S}}_A})$ to another States/Effects Chu space $({ \relax{S}}_{B},{ \relax{E}}_{{ \relax{S}}_B},\epsilon^{{ \relax{S}}_B})$.
<!-- end theorem-3 -->
<!-- proof-4: body_md -->
Direct consequence of Lemma {{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@aepsilonsigma\endcsname\@firstoftwo{aepsilonsigma}}}. It suffices to define $f^{\ast}$ as the map which associates to any ${ \relax{l}}\in { \relax{E}}_{ \relax{S}_B}$ the unique element ${ \relax{l}}'\in { \relax{E}}_{ \relax{S}_A}$ such that $\forall \sigma\in { \relax{S}}, \; { \epsilon}^{ \relax{S}_A}_{{ \relax{l}'}}(\sigma)={ \epsilon}^{ \relax{S}_B}_{{ \relax{l}}}(f(\sigma))$.
<!-- end proof-4 -->
<!-- theorem-4: body_md -->
\label{blepsilonsigma}
Let us consider a states/effects Chu space $({ \relax{S}},{ \relax{E}}_{{ \relax{S}}},\epsilon^{{ \relax{S}}})$. 
Let us consider a map $(B : { \relax{E}}_{{ \relax{S}}}\longrightarrow { \relax{B}},{ \relax{l}}\mapsto { \relax{b}}_{{ \relax{l}}})$ satisfying
\begin{eqnarray}
\forall \{{ \relax{l}}_i\;\vert\; i\in I\}\subseteq { \relax{E}}_{{ \relax{S}}},&&  { \relax{b}}_{{\bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{ \relax{E}}_{{ \relax{S}}}}}_{{}_{i\in i}}{ \relax{l}}_i}} = \bigwedge{}_{{i\in I}} \;{ \relax{b}}_{{{ \relax{l}}_i}},\label{theorembl2}\\
\forall { \relax{l}}\in { \relax{E}}_{{ \relax{S}}},&& { \relax{b}}_{\overline{\, \relax{l}\,}}=\overline{{ \relax{b}}_{{ \relax{l}}}},\label{theorembl3}\\
& & { \relax{b}}_{{ \relax{Y}}_{{ \relax{E}}_{{ \relax{S}}}}}=\textit{\bf Y}.\label{theorembl4}
\end{eqnarray}
Then, we have
\begin{eqnarray}
\exists \textit{\bf !} \; \sigma\in { \relax{S}} & \vert & \forall { \relax{l}}\in { \relax{E}}_{{ \relax{S}}}, \; { \epsilon}^{ \relax{S}}_{{ \relax{l}}}(\sigma)={ \relax{b}}_{{ \relax{l}}}.
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end theorem-4 -->
<!-- proof-5: body_md -->
Let us consider 
\begin{eqnarray}
{\relax{l}}_B &:=&\bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{{ \relax{E}}_{{ \relax{S}}}}}}\{\, { \relax{l}}\in { \relax{E}}_{{ \relax{S}}} \;\vert\; { \relax{b}}_{{ \relax{l}}}=\textit{\bf Y}\,\}
\end{eqnarray}  
Note that ${ \relax{l}}_B$ exists in ${ \relax{E}}_{{ \relax{S}}}$ because ${ \relax{E}}_{{ \relax{S}}}$ is a down-complete Inf semi-lattice and the subset $\{\, { \relax{l}}\in { \relax{E}}_{{ \relax{S}}} \;\vert\; { \relax{b}}_{{ \relax{l}}}=\textit{\bf Y}\,\}$ contains at least the element ${ \relax{Y}}_{{ \relax{E}}_{{ \relax{S}}}}$.  Moreover, ${ \relax{b}}_{{ \relax{l}}_B}=\textit{\bf Y}$ because of the relation ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@theorembl2\endcsname\@firstoftwo{theorembl2}}}). Note also that for any ${ \relax{l}}$ in ${ \relax{E}}_{{ \relax{S}}}$, we have ${ \relax{l}} \sqsupseteq_{{}_{{{ \relax{E}}_{{ \relax{S}}}}}} { \relax{l}}_B$ implies ${ \relax{b}}_{{ \relax{l}}}=\textit{\bf Y}$ because the property ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@theorembl2\endcsname\@firstoftwo{theorembl2}}}) implies the relation 
\begin{eqnarray}
\forall { \relax{l}}, { \relax{l}}'\in { \relax{E}}_{{ \relax{S}}},&& ({ \relax{l}} \sqsubseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{E}}_{{ \relax{S}}}}} { \relax{l}}')\Rightarrow ({ \relax{b}}_{{ \relax{l}}} \leq { \relax{b}}_{{ \relax{l}}'}).\label{theorembl1}
\end{eqnarray}
Conversely,  for any ${ \relax{l}}$ in ${ \relax{E}}_{{ \relax{S}}}$,  the property ${ \relax{b}}_{{ \relax{l}}}=\textit{\bf Y}$ implies ${ \relax{l}} \sqsupseteq_{{}_{{{ \relax{E}}_{ \relax{S}}}}} { \relax{l}}_B$ due to the definition of ${ \relax{l}}_B$. \\
Let us now introduce 
\begin{eqnarray}
\Sigma_{{}_{{ \relax{l}}_B}} &:=& \bigsqcap{}^{{}^{ \relax{S}}}({\epsilon}^{ \relax{S}}_{{ \relax{l}}_B})^{\;-1}(\textit{\bf Y}). 
\end{eqnarray}
We could suppose that ${ \relax{l}}_B={ \relax{l}}_{(\Sigma_{{ \relax{l}}_B},\Sigma'_{{ \relax{l}}_B})}$ for a certain $\Sigma'_{{ \relax{l}}_B}\in {\relax{S}}$. However, we note that, because of ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@theorembl2\endcsname\@firstoftwo{theorembl2}}}) and ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@theorembl4\endcsname\@firstoftwo{theorembl4}}}), we have ${ \relax{l}}_{(\Sigma_{{ \relax{l}}_B},\centerdot)}\sqsubset_{{}_{{{ \relax{E}}_{ \relax{S}}}}} { \relax{l}}_{(\Sigma_{{ \relax{l}}_B},\Sigma'_{{ \relax{l}}_B})}$ and ${ \relax{b}}_{{ \relax{l}}_{(\Sigma_{{ \relax{l}}_B},\centerdot)}}={ \relax{b}}_{{ \relax{l}}_{(\Sigma_{{ \relax{l}}_B},\Sigma'_{{ \relax{l}}_B})}\sqcap_{{}_{{{ \relax{E}}_{{ \relax{S}}}}}} { \relax{Y}}_{{ \relax{E}}_{{ \relax{S}}}} }= { \relax{b}}_{{ \relax{l}}_{(\Sigma_{{ \relax{l}}_B},\Sigma'_{{ \relax{l}}_B})}}\wedge { \relax{b}}_{{ \relax{Y}}_{{ \relax{E}}_{{ \relax{S}}}} }=\textit{\bf Y}$ which would contradict the definition of ${ \relax{l}}_B$.  Hence, we have to accept that ${ \relax{l}}_B={ \relax{l}}_{(\Sigma_{{ \relax{l}}_B},\centerdot)}$. \\
Due to this peculiar form of ${ \relax{l}}_B$, we deduce that, for any ${ \relax{l}}_{(\Sigma,\Sigma')}$ in ${ \relax{E}}_{{ \relax{S}}}$, the property ${ \relax{l}}_{(\Sigma,\Sigma')} \not\sqsupseteq_{{}_{{{ \relax{E}}_{ \relax{S}}}}} { \relax{l}}_B$ is then equivalent to the property $\Sigma\not\sqsupseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}} \Sigma_{{ \relax{l}}_B}$. Then, if ${ \relax{l}}_{(\Sigma,\Sigma')} \not\sqsupseteq_{{}_{{{ \relax{E}}_{{ \relax{S}}}}}} { \relax{l}}_B$ we cannot have $\epsilon^{ \relax{S}}_{{ \relax{l}}_{(\Sigma,\Sigma')}}(\Sigma_{{}_{{ \relax{l}}_B}})=\textit{\bf Y}$ (by the very definition of $\epsilon^{ \relax{S}}$). \\
On another part, for any ${ \relax{l}}$ in ${ \relax{E}}_{{ \relax{S}}}$ such that ${ \relax{l}} \sqsupseteq_{{}_{{{ \relax{E}}_{{ \relax{S}}}}}} { \relax{l}}_B$, we have $\epsilon^{ \relax{S}}_{{ \relax{l}}}(\Sigma_{{}_{{ \relax{l}}_B}})\geq \epsilon^{ \relax{S}}_{{ \relax{l}}_B}(\Sigma_{{}_{{ \relax{l}}_B}}) = \textit{\bf Y}$, i.e. $\epsilon^{ \relax{S}}_{{ \relax{l}}}(\Sigma_{{}_{{ \relax{l}}_B}}) = \textit{\bf Y}$. \\ 
We then conclude that the property $\epsilon^{ \relax{S}}_{{ \relax{l}}}(\Sigma_{{}_{{ \relax{l}}_B}}) = \textit{\bf Y}$ is equivalent to the property ${ \relax{l}} \sqsupseteq_{{}_{{{ \relax{E}}_{{ \relax{S}}}}}} { \relax{l}}_B$, or in other words 
\begin{eqnarray}
\forall { \relax{l}}\in { \relax{E}}_{{ \relax{S}}},\;\;\;\; \epsilon^{ \relax{S}}_{{ \relax{l}}}(\Sigma_{{}_{{ \relax{l}}_B}}) = \textit{\bf Y} &\Leftrightarrow & { \relax{b}}_{{ \relax{l}}}=\textit{\bf Y}. 
 \end{eqnarray}
  Using ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@theorembl3\endcsname\@firstoftwo{theorembl3}}}) and ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@etbar\endcsname\@firstoftwo{etbar}}}),  we then deduce that $(\epsilon^{ \relax{S}}_{{ \relax{l}}}(\Sigma_{{}_{{ \relax{l}}_B}}) = \textit{\bf N})\Leftrightarrow (\epsilon^{ \relax{S}}_{\overline{\, \relax{l}\,}}(\Sigma_{{}_{{ \relax{l}}_B}}) = \textit{\bf Y})\Leftrightarrow ({ \relax{b}}_{\overline{\, \relax{l}\,}}=\textit{\bf Y}) \Leftrightarrow ({ \relax{b}}_{{ \relax{l}}}=\textit{\bf N})$. \\
  As a final conclusion, we have for any ${ \relax{l}}\in { \relax{E}}_{{ \relax{S}}}$ the equality $\epsilon^{ \relax{S}}_{{ \relax{l}}}(\Sigma_{{}_{{ \relax{l}}_B}})={ \relax{b}}_{{ \relax{l}}}$. \\
Let us finally suppose that there exists $\sigma_1,\sigma_2\in { \relax{S}}$ such that $\forall { \relax{l}}\in { \relax{E}}_{{ \relax{S}}}, \; \epsilon_{{ \relax{l}}}(\sigma_1)={ \relax{b}}_{{ \relax{l}}}=\epsilon_{{ \relax{l}}}(\sigma_2)$. We then obtain $\sigma_1=\sigma_2$. The state $\sigma$ is then uniquely fixed to be $\Sigma_{{}_{{ \relax{l}}_B}}$.
<!-- end proof-5 -->
<!-- theorem-5: body_md -->
For any map $f^\ast:{ \relax{E}}_{ \relax{S}_B} \longrightarrow { \relax{E}}_{{ \relax{S}}_A}$ satisfying
\begin{eqnarray}
\forall E\subseteq { \relax{E}}_{{ \relax{S}}_B},&& f^{\ast}(\bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{ \relax{E}}_{{ \relax{S}}_B}}} \! E) = \bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{ \relax{E}}_{{ \relax{S}}_A}}}_{{}_{{ \relax{l}}\in E}} \; f^{\ast}({ \relax{l}})\\
\forall { \relax{l}} \in { \relax{E}}_{{ \relax{S}}_B},&& f^{\ast}(\; \overline{\,{ \relax{l}}\,} \;) = \overline{f^{\ast}({ \relax{l}})}\\
&& f^{\ast}(\;{ \relax{Y}}_{{ \relax{E}}_{{ \relax{S}}_B}}\;) = { \relax{Y}}_{{ \relax{E}}_{{ \relax{S}}_A}},
\end{eqnarray}
there exists a unique map $f:{ \relax{S}}_A \longrightarrow { \relax{S}}_B$ such that $(f,f^{\ast})$ is a morphism from the States/Effects Chu space $({ \relax{S}}_{A},{ \relax{E}}_{{ \relax{S}}_A},\epsilon^{{ \relax{S}}_A})$ to the States/Effects Chu space $({ \relax{S}}_{B},{ \relax{E}}_{{ \relax{S}}_B},\epsilon^{{ \relax{S}}_B})$.
<!-- end theorem-5 -->
<!-- proof-6: body_md -->
Direct consequence of Lemma {{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@blepsilonsigma\endcsname\@firstoftwo{blepsilonsigma}}}.  It suffices to define $f$ as the map which associates to any $\sigma \in { \relax{S}_A}$ the unique element $\sigma'\in { \relax{S}_B}$ such that $\forall { \relax{l}}\in { \relax{E}}_{ \relax{S}_B}, \; { \epsilon}^{ \relax{S}_B}_{{ \relax{l}}}(\sigma')={ \epsilon}^{ \relax{S}_A}_{f^{\ast}({ \relax{l}})}(\sigma)$ (in the application of the Lemma {{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@blepsilonsigma\endcsname\@firstoftwo{blepsilonsigma}}}, we simply choose ${ \relax{E}}:={ \relax{E}}_{{ \relax{S}}_B}$).
<!-- end proof-6 -->
<!-- definition-8: body_md -->
The set of morphisms from ${ \relax{S}}_A$ to ${ \relax{S}}_B$ will be denoted ${\relax{C}}({ \relax{S}}_A,{ \relax{S}}_B)$.
<!-- end definition-8 -->
<!-- definition-9: body_md -->
We define the infimum of two maps $f$ and $g$ satisfying ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@f12cap\endcsname\@firstoftwo{f12cap}}}) (resp. two maps $f^\ast$ and $g^\ast$ satisfying ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@f21cap\endcsname\@firstoftwo{f21cap}}})) by $\forall \sigma \in { \relax{S}}_A, (f\sqcap_{{}_{{\relax{C}}({ \relax{S}}_A,{ \relax{S}}_B)}} g)(\sigma):= f(\sigma) \sqcap_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}_B}} g(\sigma)$.
<!-- end definition-9 -->
<!-- theorem-6: body_md -->
The infimum of a morphism $(f ,f^{\ast})$ from $({ \relax{S}}_A,{ \relax{E}}_{{ \relax{S}}_A},\epsilon^{{ \relax{S}}_A})$ to $({ \relax{S}}_B,{ \relax{E}}_{{ \relax{S}}_B},\epsilon^{{ \relax{S}}_B})$ with another morphism $(g ,g^{\ast})$ defined from $({ \relax{S}}_A,{ \relax{E}}_{{ \relax{S}}_A},\epsilon^{{ \relax{S}}_A})$ to $({ \relax{S}}_B,{ \relax{E}}_{{ \relax{S}}_B},\epsilon^{{ \relax{S}}_B})$ defines a valid morphism from $({ \relax{S}}_A,{ \relax{E}}_{{ \relax{S}}_A},\epsilon^{{ \relax{S}}_A})$ to $({ \relax{S}}_B,{ \relax{E}}_{{ \relax{S}}_B},\epsilon^{{ \relax{S}}_B})$.
<!-- end theorem-6 -->
<!-- proof-7: body_md -->
Direct consequence of the duality property.
<!-- end proof-7 -->
<!-- definition-10: body_md -->
A {\em measurement} is a morphism ${ \relax{m}}$ from the state space ${ \relax{S}}$ to the space of evaluations ${ \relax{B}}$.  
The space of measurements associated to ${ \relax{S}}$ will be denoted ${\relax{M}}_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}}$.
<!-- end definition-10 -->
<!-- theorem-7: body_md -->
The space of measurements ${\relax{M}}_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}}$ is isomorphic to the space of effects ${ \relax{E}}_{ \relax{S}}$.
<!-- end theorem-7 -->
<!-- proof-8: body_md -->
An effect ${ \relax{l}}\in { \relax{E}}_{ \relax{S}}$ being given, the map ${ \relax{m}}_{{ \relax{l}}}$ defined by
\begin{eqnarray}
&& { \relax{m}}_{{ \relax{l}}}(\sigma) := \epsilon^{ \relax{S}}_{ \relax{l}}(\sigma),\;\;\;\forall \sigma\in { \relax{S}}.\label{measurementeffect}
\end{eqnarray}
 is a well defined homomorphism from ${ \relax{S}}$ to ${ \relax{B}}$.  Hence, the map
\begin{eqnarray}
&&\begin{array}{rcrcl}
\varphi & : & { \relax{E}}_{ \relax{S}} & \longrightarrow & {\relax{M}}_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}}\\
& & { \relax{l}} & \mapsto & { \relax{m}}_{{ \relax{l}}}\label{defvarphi}
\end{array}
\end{eqnarray}
is an homomorphism.  It is moreover bijective. Indeed, let us consider any ${ \relax{m}}$ in ${\relax{M}}_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}}$.  If $\{\, \sigma\;\vert\; { \relax{m}}({\sigma})=\textit{\bf Y}\,\}$ and $\{\, \sigma\;\vert\; { \relax{m}}({\sigma})=\textit{\bf N}\,\}$ are not empty, they are principal filters, and it suffices to associate to ${ \relax{m}}$ the states $\sigma_A:=\bigsqcap^{{}^{{ \relax{S}}}}\{\, \sigma\;\vert\; { \relax{m}}({\sigma})=\textit{\bf Y}\,\}$,  $\sigma_A':=\bigsqcap^{{}^{{ \relax{S}}}}\{\, \sigma\;\vert\; { \relax{m}}({\sigma})=\textit{\bf N}\,\}$ and the effect ${ \relax{l}}:={ \relax{l}}_{(\sigma_A,\sigma_A')} $ (the case where some or all of these subsets are empty is treated immediately).\\

As usual,  the data ${ \relax{m}}_{{ \relax{l}}}$ suffices to define a Chu morphism $({ \relax{m}}_{{ \relax{l}}},{ \relax{m}}^\ast_{{ \relax{l}}})$. Indeed, the map ${ \relax{m}}^\ast_{{ \relax{l}}} : { \relax{E}}_{ \relax{B}} \longrightarrow { \relax{E}}_{ \relax{S}}$ is defined by the duality relation ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@defchumorphism\endcsname\@firstoftwo{defchumorphism}}}), i.e.
 \begin{eqnarray}
 \forall \sigma\in { \relax{S}}, \forall { \relax{u}}\in { \relax{E}}_{ \relax{B}},&& \epsilon^{ \relax{S}}_{{ \relax{m}}^\ast_{{ \relax{l}}}({ \relax{u}})}(\sigma)=\epsilon^{ \relax{B}}_{{ \relax{u}}}({ \relax{m}}_{{ \relax{l}}}(\sigma))=\epsilon^{ \relax{B}}_{{ \relax{u}}}( \epsilon^{ \relax{S}}_{ \relax{l}}(\sigma))\label{appliedduality}
\end{eqnarray}
The expression of ${ \relax{m}}^\ast_{{ \relax{l}}}({ \relax{u}})$ for any ${ \relax{u}}$ in ${ \relax{E}}_{ \relax{B}}$ is reduced by the application of the three relations ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@f21cap\endcsname\@firstoftwo{f21cap}}})({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@f21bar\endcsname\@firstoftwo{f21bar}}})({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@f21Y\endcsname\@firstoftwo{f21Y}}}) to the property 
\begin{eqnarray}
{ \relax{m}}^\ast_{{ \relax{l}}}({ \relax{l}}_{(\textit{\bf Y},\textit{\bf N})}):={ \relax{l}}\label{mastu}
\end{eqnarray}
 which validity can be checked directly on ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@appliedduality\endcsname\@firstoftwo{appliedduality}}}).
<!-- end proof-8 -->
<!-- definition-11: body_md -->
\label{definitionstarstructure}
A {\em real structure} on a space of states ${ \relax{S}}$ is a pair $(\overline{ \relax{S}},\star)$ where
\begin{itemize}
\@par\hangindent 2em $\overline{ \relax{S}}$ is a subset of ${ \relax{S}}$ satisfying
\begin{eqnarray}
\bot_{{}_{ \relax{S}}} & \in & \overline{ \relax{S}}\\
\forall S\subseteq \overline{ \relax{S}},\;\;\;\; \bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{ \relax{S}}}}S & \in & \overline{ \relax{S}},
\end{eqnarray}
\@par\hangindent 2em $\overline{ \relax{S}}$ is {\em generated by its maximal elements}, i.e. 
 \begin{eqnarray}
\hspace{-1cm}&&\forall \sigma \in \overline{ \relax{S}}, \;\; \sigma= \bigsqcap{}^{{}^{ \overline{ \relax{S}}}}  \underline{\sigma}_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}} \;\;\textit{\rm where}\;\; \underline{\sigma}_{{}_{ \overline{ \relax{S}}}}:=\{\, \sigma'\in \overline{ \relax{S}}{}^{{}^{pure}}\;\vert\; \sigma'\sqsupseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}} \sigma\;\} \;\;\textit{\rm and}\;\; \overline{ \relax{S}}{}^{{}^{pure}}:=Max(\overline{ \relax{S}})\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;
\label{completemeetirreducibleordergeneratingS}
\end{eqnarray}
     
                 
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       
               
\@par\hangindent 2em $\star$ is a map from $\overline{ \relax{S}}\smallsetminus \{\bot_{{}_{ \relax{S}}}\}$ to $\overline{ \relax{S}}\smallsetminus \{\bot_{{}_{ \relax{S}}}\}$ satisfying
\begin{eqnarray}
\forall \sigma\in \overline{ \relax{S}}\smallsetminus \{\bot_{{}_{ \relax{S}}}\},&& (\sigma^{\star})^{\star}=\sigma \label{involutive}\\
\forall \sigma_1,\sigma_2\in \overline{ \relax{S}}\smallsetminus \{\bot_{{}_{ \relax{S}}}\},&& \sigma_1\sqsubseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma_2\;\;\Rightarrow\;\; \sigma_2^\star \sqsubseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}} \sigma_1^\star \label{orderreversing}\\
\forall \sigma\in \overline{ \relax{S}}\smallsetminus \{\bot_{{}_{ \relax{S}}}\},&&\neg\; \widehat{\sigma\sigma^\star}{}^{{}^{{ \relax{S}}}},\label{starcomplement}
\end{eqnarray}
                                                                                                                                                                           
                 
                                                                                                                                                                             
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               
               
\@par\hangindent 2em the sub Inf semi-lattice of ${ \relax{E}}_{ \relax{S}}$ formed by the elements of the following set
\begin{eqnarray}
\hspace{-0.5cm}\{\,{ \relax{l}}_{(\sigma,\sigma')}\;\vert\; \sigma,\sigma'\in \overline{ \relax{S}}\smallsetminus \{\bot_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}}\}, \sigma'\sqsupseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}} \sigma^\star\,\} \cup \{ { \relax{l}}_{{}_{(\sigma,\centerdot)}}\;\vert\; \sigma\in \overline{ \relax{S}}\;\}\cup \{ { \relax{l}}_{{}_{(\centerdot,\sigma)}}\;\vert\; \sigma\in \overline{ \relax{S}}\;\}\cup \{\, { \relax{l}}_{{}_{(\centerdot,\centerdot)}}\,\}\;\;\;\;\;\;\label{reducedspaceofeffects}
\end{eqnarray}
will be denoted $\overline{ \relax{E}}_{ \relax{S}}$ and will be assumed to satisfy
\begin{eqnarray}
&& \forall \sigma,\sigma'\in { \relax{S}},\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;(\, \forall { \relax{l}}\in \overline{ \relax{E}}_{ \relax{S}},\; { \epsilon}^{ \relax{S}}_{ { \relax{l}}}(\sigma)={ \epsilon}^{ \relax{S}}_{ { \relax{l}}}(\sigma') \,) \Leftrightarrow  (\, \sigma= \sigma' \,).\label{realChuseparated}    
\end{eqnarray}
\end{itemize}

\vspace{0.3cm}
The elements of $\overline{ \relax{S}}$ will be called {\em real states}, whereas the elements of ${ \relax{S}}\smallsetminus \overline{ \relax{S}}$ will be called {\em hidden states}. \\ 
The elements of $\overline{ \relax{S}}^{{}^{pure}}$ will be called {\em pure states}.\\
The elements of $\overline{ \relax{E}}_{ \relax{S}}$ will be called {\em real effects}.
<!-- end definition-11 -->
<!-- remark-2: body_md -->
We note without proof the following basic results
\begin{eqnarray}
&& \forall { \relax{l}},{ \relax{l}}'\in \overline{ \relax{E}}_{ \relax{S}},\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;(\, \forall \sigma\in { \relax{S}},\; { \epsilon}^{ \relax{S}}_{ { \relax{l}}}(\sigma)={ \epsilon}^{ \relax{S}}_{ { \relax{l}}'}(\sigma) \,) \Leftrightarrow  (\, { \relax{l}}= { \relax{l}}' \,),\label{realChuextensional}\\
&&\forall L\subseteq \overline{ \relax{E}}_{ \relax{S}},\;\;\;\;( \bigsqcap{}^{{}^{\overline{ \relax{E}}_{ \relax{S}}}}L) \in \overline{ \relax{E}}_{ \relax{S}},\label{axiomreduc2}\\
&& \forall { \relax{l}}\in \overline{ \relax{E}}_{ \relax{S}},\;\;\;\;\overline{\,{ \relax{l}}\,} \in \overline{ \relax{E}}_{ \relax{S}},\label{axiomreduc3}\\
&&{ \relax{Y}}_{{}_{{{ \relax{E}}}_{ \relax{S}}}} \in  \overline{ \relax{E}}_{ \relax{S}} \;\;\;\;\;\;\textit{\rm and} \;\;\;\;\;\; \bot_{{}_{{{ \relax{E}}}_{ \relax{S}}}} \in  \overline{ \relax{E}}_{ \relax{S}}.\label{axiomreduc4}
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end remark-2 -->
<!-- definition-12: body_md -->
We will define a binary relation on ${}{\relax{S}}\smallsetminus \{\bot_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}}\}$, denoted by $\underline{\perp}$ and called {\em orthogonality relation}, as follows :
\begin{eqnarray}
\hspace{-0.5cm}\forall \sigma,\sigma'\in {}{\relax{S}}\smallsetminus \{\bot_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}}\},&& \sigma \underline{\perp} \sigma'\;\;:\Leftrightarrow\;\; \left( \exists \omega\in \overline{ \relax{S}}\smallsetminus \{\bot_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\},\; \sigma\sqsupseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}}\omega \;\;\textit{\rm and}\;\; \sigma'\sqsupseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}}\omega^\star\right).\label{definorthoS}\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end definition-12 -->
<!-- definition-13: body_md -->
We will adopt the following standard notation for the orthogonal of a subset of ${}{\relax{S}}$
\begin{eqnarray}
\forall S\subseteq {}{\relax{S}} & & S^{\underline{\perp}}:=\{\,\sigma\in {}{\relax{S}} \;\vert\; \forall \sigma'\in S, \; \sigma \underline{\perp} \sigma'\,\}.\label{deforthosubset}
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end definition-13 -->
<!-- lemma-4: body_md -->
The operator defined on ${\mathcal{P}}({}{\relax{S}})$ which maps $S$ to $(S^{\underline{\perp}})^{\underline{\perp}}$ (which will eventually be denoted by $S^{{\underline{\perp}}{\underline{\perp}}}$) owns the following properties
\begin{eqnarray}
\forall S\subseteq {}{\relax{S}},&& S\subseteq S^{{\underline{\perp}}{\underline{\perp}}},\label{orthoorthoexpansive}\\
\forall S_1,S_2\subseteq {\relax{S}},&& S_1\subseteq S_2\;\Rightarrow\; S_1^{{\underline{\perp}}{\underline{\perp}}}\subseteq S_2^{{\underline{\perp}}{\underline{\perp}}}.\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\label{orthoorthomonotone}
\end{eqnarray}
We have moreover
\begin{eqnarray}
\forall S\subseteq {}{\relax{S}},&& ((S^{\underline{\perp}})^{\underline{\perp}})^{\underline{\perp}}=(S)^{\underline{\perp}}.\label{ortho3=ortho}
\end{eqnarray}
and then
\begin{eqnarray}
\forall S\subseteq {}{\relax{S}},&& (S^{{\underline{\perp}}{\underline{\perp}}})^{{\underline{\perp}}{\underline{\perp}}}=S^{{\underline{\perp}}{\underline{\perp}}}.\label{ortho4=ortho2}
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end lemma-4 -->
<!-- proof-9: body_md -->
The properties ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@orthoorthoexpansive\endcsname\@firstoftwo{orthoorthoexpansive}}}) and ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@orthoorthomonotone\endcsname\@firstoftwo{orthoorthomonotone}}}) are obtained trivially. \\
Concerning property ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@ortho3=ortho\endcsname\@firstoftwo{ortho3=ortho}}}), we have the following analysis. $((B^{\underline{\perp}})^{\underline{\perp}})^{\underline{\perp}}\supseteq B^{\underline{\perp}}$ is a consequence of the fact that the property ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@orthoorthoexpansive\endcsname\@firstoftwo{orthoorthoexpansive}}}) for $B^{\underline{\perp}}$, and $((B^{\underline{\perp}})^{\underline{\perp}})^{\underline{\perp}}\subseteq B^{\underline{\perp}}$ is a consequence of the action of the order inversing property of $\underline{\perp}$ on the property ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@orthoorthoexpansive\endcsname\@firstoftwo{orthoorthoexpansive}}}) for $B$.\\
The property ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@ortho4=ortho2\endcsname\@firstoftwo{ortho4=ortho2}}}) is a direct consequence of property ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@ortho3=ortho\endcsname\@firstoftwo{ortho3=ortho}}})
<!-- end proof-9 -->
<!-- definition-14: body_md -->
A subset $S$ of ${}{\relax{S}}$ will be said to be {\em orthoclosed} iff $(S^{\underline{\perp}})^{\underline{\perp}}=S$. The set of orthoclosed subsets of ${}{\relax{S}}$ will be denoted ${ \relax{H}}({}{\relax{S}}, {\underline{\perp}})$.
<!-- end definition-14 -->
<!-- lemma-5: body_md -->
\label{lemmavarnothing&E}
$\varnothing$ and $(\uparrow^{{}^{{}{\relax{S}}}}\!\!\!\bot_{{}_{{\relax{S}}}})$ are both elements of ${ \relax{H}}({}{\relax{S}}, {\underline{\perp}})$.
<!-- end lemma-5 -->
<!-- lemma-6: body_md -->
\label{lemmaorthocapsemi-lattice}
Equipped with the inclusion $\subseteq$, ${ \relax{H}}({}{\relax{S}}, {\underline{\perp}})$ is a partially ordered set. With the intersection $\cap$, ${ \relax{H}}({}{\relax{S}}, {\underline{\perp}})$ is a down complete Inf semi-lattice.
<!-- end lemma-6 -->
<!-- proof-10: body_md -->
The first assertion is trivial. Concerning the second assertion, let us consider two orthoclosed subsets $H,H'\in { \relax{H}}({}{\relax{S}}, {\underline{\perp}})$. The properties $H\cap H'\subseteq H,H'$ imply $(H\cap H')^{\underline{\perp}\underline{\perp}}\subseteq (H)^{\underline{\perp}\underline{\perp}}=H,(H')^{\underline{\perp}\underline{\perp}}=H'$ (due to the monotonicity of the orthogonal closure) and then $(H\cap H')^{\underline{\perp}\underline{\perp}}\subseteq (H \cap H')$. Using the first axiom of closure, we have also $(H\cap H')^{\underline{\perp}\underline{\perp}}\supseteq (H \cap H')$. This concludes the proof.
<!-- end proof-10 -->
<!-- lemma-7: body_md -->
As a consequence of property ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@ortho3=ortho\endcsname\@firstoftwo{ortho3=ortho}}}), we have that,  for any $S$ orthoclosed subset of ${}{\relax{S}}$, there exists a subset $S'$ of ${}{\relax{S}}$ such that $(S')^{\underline{\perp}}=S$, and conversely, any subset of the form $S^{\underline{\perp}}$ is orthoclosed.\\
As a conclusion, the image of ${ \mathcal{P}}({}{\relax{S}})$ by the orthogonality operator is exactly ${ \relax{H}}({}{\relax{S}}, {\underline{\perp}})$.
<!-- end lemma-7 -->
<!-- theorem-8: body_md -->
\label{orthocomplem0}
The set of orthoclosed subsets satisfies the following properties :
\begin{eqnarray}
\forall H\in { \relax{H}}({}{\relax{S}}, {\underline{\perp}}),&& (H^{\underline{\perp}})^{\underline{\perp}}=H,\\
\forall H_1,H_2\in { \relax{H}}({}{\relax{S}}, {\underline{\perp}}),&& (H_1\subseteq H_2)\;\Rightarrow \; (H_2^{\underline{\perp}} \subseteq H_1^{\underline{\perp}}).
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end theorem-8 -->
<!-- proof-11: body_md -->
The second relation is trivially deduced from Definition {{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@deforthosubset\endcsname\@firstoftwo{deforthosubset}}} of the orthogonal of a subset. The first relation is ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@ortho4=ortho2\endcsname\@firstoftwo{ortho4=ortho2}}}).
<!-- end proof-11 -->
<!-- definition-15: body_md -->
Using the results of the previous lemma, it appears natural to introduce the following orthogonality relation on the set of orthoclosed subsets ${ \relax{H}}({\relax{S}}, {\underline{\perp}})$
\begin{eqnarray}
\forall H_1,H_2\in { \relax{H}}({}{\relax{S}}, {\underline{\perp}}),\;\; H_1\;\underline{\perp}\; H_2 & :\Leftrightarrow & H_1^{\underline{\perp}} \supseteq H_2.\label{deforthoHSorthog}
\end{eqnarray} 
We use the same notation as the orthogonality relation of ${}{\relax{S}}$ because ${}{\relax{S}}$ is naturally injected into ${ \relax{H}}({}{\relax{S}}, {\underline{\perp}})$.\\
This orthogonality relation is obviously symmetric and irreflexive.
<!-- end definition-15 -->
<!-- definition-16: body_md -->
We will adopt the following notation for the suprema :
\begin{eqnarray}
\forall H_1,H_2\in { \relax{H}}({}{\relax{S}}, {\underline{\perp}}),&& H_1 \curlyvee H_2 := (H_1^{\underline{\perp}} \cap H_2^{\underline{\perp}})^{\underline{\perp}}.\label{demorgan}
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end definition-16 -->
<!-- definition-17: body_md -->
During this subsection, the map $\Theta^{\overline{ \relax{S}}}$ from ${ \relax{S}}$ to ${\mathcal{P}}(\overline{ \relax{S}})$ that will be used extensively, is defined by $\Theta^{\overline{ \relax{S}}}(\zeta):=Max((\downarrow_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}}\zeta)\cap \overline{ \relax{S}})$. For a detailed analysis of the properties of $\Theta^{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}$, see subsection {{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@subsectionpreliminaryhidden\endcsname\@firstoftwo{subsectionpreliminaryhidden}}}.
<!-- end definition-17 -->
<!-- lemma-8: body_md -->
\label{lemmaSorthogonal}
\begin{eqnarray}
\forall \sigma\in {}{\relax{S}},&& \{\sigma\}^{\underline{\perp}} = \bigcup{}_{\omega\in \Theta^{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}(\sigma)}(\uparrow^{{}^{{}{\relax{S}}}}\!\!\omega^\star),\\
\forall S\subseteq {}{\relax{S}},&& S^{\underline{\perp}} = \bigcap{}_{\sigma\in S}\;\{\sigma\}^{\underline{\perp}}.
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end lemma-8 -->
<!-- proof-12: body_md -->
Trivial.
<!-- end proof-12 -->
<!-- theorem-9: body_md -->
\label{expressionorthogonal}
For any $S\subseteq {}{\relax{S}}$, we define $U_S$ as the set of maps from $S$ to ${\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}$ mapping any $\sigma\in S$ to an element of $\Theta^{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}(\sigma)$.  In other words,
\begin{eqnarray}
U_S &:=& \{\,\phi\in {\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}^S \;\vert\; \forall \sigma\in S,\;\phi(\sigma)\in  \Theta^{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}(\sigma)\,\}.\label{defUS}
\end{eqnarray}
We then define, for any $S\subseteq {}{\relax{S}}$,  an element $V_S$ in $\widecheck{ \relax{S}}\cup \{\centerdot\}$ by
\begin{eqnarray}
V_S &:=& \{\,\bigsqcup{}^{{}^{{ \relax{S}}}}_{\sigma\in S} (\phi(\sigma))^\star\;\vert\; \phi\in U_S\,\}.
\end{eqnarray}
Endly, we have
\begin{eqnarray}
S^{\underline{\perp}} &=& \bigcup{}_{\alpha\in V_S}(\uparrow^{{}^{{}{\relax{S}}}}\!\!\alpha).\label{expressionSortho}
\end{eqnarray}
with the obvious convention $(\uparrow^{{}^{{}{\relax{S}}}}\!\!\centerdot) :=\varnothing$.
<!-- end theorem-9 -->
<!-- proof-13: body_md -->
Direct consequence of Lemma {{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@lemmaSorthogonal\endcsname\@firstoftwo{lemmaSorthogonal}}}.
<!-- end proof-13 -->
<!-- lemma-9: body_md -->
For any $S\subseteq {}{\relax{S}}$, we define $U_S$ as in {{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@defUS\endcsname\@firstoftwo{defUS}}}, and we have
\begin{eqnarray}
(S^{\underline{\perp}})^{\underline{\perp}} &=& \bigcap{}_{\phi\in U_S}\left( \bigcup{}_{\rho\in \Theta^{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}\left(\bigsqcup{}^{{}^{{}{\relax{S}}}}_{\sigma\in S} (\phi(\sigma))^\star\right)}(\uparrow^{{}^{{}{\relax{S}}}}\!\!\rho^\star)\right).\label{expressionSorthoortho}
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end lemma-9 -->
<!-- proof-14: body_md -->
Direct consequence of Theorem {{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@expressionorthogonal\endcsname\@firstoftwo{expressionorthogonal}}} and Lemma {{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@lemmaSorthogonal\endcsname\@firstoftwo{lemmaSorthogonal}}}.
<!-- end proof-14 -->
<!-- theorem-10: body_md -->
\label{theoremorthocomplementation}
We have the following ortho-complementation property :
\begin{eqnarray}
\forall H\in { \relax{H}}({\relax{S}}, {\underline{\perp}}),&&\left(H^{\underline{\perp}} \cap H  \right)=\varnothing.
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end theorem-10 -->
<!-- proof-15: body_md -->
Let us fix $S\subseteq {\relax{S}}$.\\
Let us suppose that there exists $\sigma\in {\relax{S}}$ such that $\sigma\in \left((S^{\underline{\perp}})^{\underline{\perp}} \cap (S^{\underline{\perp}})  \right)$.  We intent to exhibit a contradiction.\\
Using expressions ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@expressionSortho\endcsname\@firstoftwo{expressionSortho}}}) and ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@expressionSorthoortho\endcsname\@firstoftwo{expressionSorthoortho}}}), we deduce that 
\begin{itemize}
\@par\hangindent 2em there exists $\phi\in U_S$ such that $\left(\bigsqcup{}^{{}^{{}{\relax{S}}}}_{\sigma\in S} (\phi(\sigma))^\star\right) \sqsubseteq_{{}_{{}{\relax{S}}}} \sigma$,
\@par\hangindent 2em for any $\psi\in U_S$, there exists $\rho\in \Theta^{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}\left(\bigsqcup{}^{{}^{{ \relax{S}}}}_{\sigma\in S} (\psi(\sigma))^\star\right)$ such that $\rho^\star \sqsubseteq_{{}_{{}{\relax{S}}}} \sigma$.
\end{itemize}
From the first point, we deduce that for any $\kappa \in \Theta^{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}\left(\bigsqcup{}^{{}^{{}{\relax{S}}}}_{\sigma\in S} (\phi(\sigma))^\star\right)$ we have $\kappa \sqsubseteq_{{}_{{}{\relax{S}}}} \sigma$. Let us now choose for $\psi$ in the second point the element $\phi\in U_S$ fixed in the first point, and let us choose in the second point $\kappa$ to be equal to the $\rho$ fixed by the second point, we have then simultaneously $\rho \sqsubseteq_{{}_{{}{\relax{S}}}} \sigma$ and $\rho^\star \sqsubseteq_{{}_{{}{\relax{S}}}} \sigma$. We have then obtained that there exists an element $\rho\in \overline{\relax{S}}$ such that $\rho$ and $\rho^\star$ admit a common upper bound in ${}{\relax{S}}$, which is impossible. We have then obtained the announced contradiction. This concludes the proof.
<!-- end proof-15 -->
<!-- theorem-11: body_md -->
${ \relax{H}}({}{\relax{S}}, {\underline{\perp}})$ is a complete ortho-lattice.
<!-- end theorem-11 -->
<!-- proof-16: body_md -->
This result summarizes the results obtained in Lemma {{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@lemmavarnothing&E\endcsname\@firstoftwo{lemmavarnothing&E}}}, Lemma {{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@lemmaorthocapsemi-lattice\endcsname\@firstoftwo{lemmaorthocapsemi-lattice}}}, Theorem {{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@orthocomplem0\endcsname\@firstoftwo{orthocomplem0}}} and Theorem {{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@theoremorthocomplementation\endcsname\@firstoftwo{theoremorthocomplementation}}}.
<!-- end proof-16 -->
<!-- definition-18: body_md -->
\label{deflangleSrangle}
We will define the set $\langle {}{\relax{S}}\rangle$, as follows
\begin{eqnarray}
\hspace{-1.8cm}&&\langle{}{\relax{S}}\rangle :=  \{\, \{\sigma\}\;\vert\; \sigma\in ({}{\relax{S}}\smallsetminus \overline{\relax{S}})\,\} \cup \underbrace{{}{\relax{S}}} \cup\{\bot_{{}_{\relax{S}}} \}\;\;\textit{\rm with}\\
\hspace{-1.8cm}&&\underbrace{{}{\relax{S}}}:= \{\,S\subseteq \overline{{ \relax{S}}}\smallsetminus \{\bot_{{}_{\relax{S}}} \}\;\vert\; \exists \sigma\in {{}{\relax{S}}}\smallsetminus \{\bot_{{}_{\relax{S}}} \}\;\;\textit{\rm s.t.}\;\; \Theta^{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}(\sigma)=\{\,\alpha^\star\;\vert\; \alpha\in S\,\}\,\}.
\end{eqnarray}
We note obviously that ${}{\relax{S}}\subseteq \langle{}{\relax{S}}\rangle$.
<!-- end definition-18 -->
<!-- lemma-10: body_md -->
The set ${ \relax{H}}({}{\relax{S}}, {\underline{\perp}})$ of orthoclosed subsets of ${}{\relax{S}}$ is explicitly described in terms of $\langle {}{\relax{S}}\rangle$, as follows :
\begin{eqnarray}
{ \relax{H}}({}{\relax{S}}, {\underline{\perp}}) &=& \{\, (\uparrow^{{}^{{{}{\relax{S}}}}}S)\;\vert\; S\in \langle{}{\relax{S}}\rangle\cup \{\varnothing\}\,\}.
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end lemma-10 -->
<!-- proof-17: body_md -->
Direct consequence of formula ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@expressionSorthoortho\endcsname\@firstoftwo{expressionSorthoortho}}}).
<!-- end proof-17 -->
<!-- lemma-11: body_md -->
\label{rangleHsubsetH}
The action of the orthogonality operator on the elements of ${ \relax{H}}({}{\relax{S}}, {\underline{\perp}})$ is explicitly given by
\begin{eqnarray}
\varnothing^{\underline{\perp}} &=& (\uparrow^{{}^{{{}{\relax{S}}}}}\bot_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}} ),\\
(\uparrow^{{}^{{{}{\relax{S}}}}}\bot_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}} )^{\underline{\perp}} &=& \varnothing,\\
\forall \sigma\in \overline{ \relax{S}}\smallsetminus \{\bot_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}}\},\;\;(\uparrow^{{}^{{{}{\relax{S}}}}}\sigma )^{\underline{\perp}} &=&(\uparrow^{{}^{{{}{\relax{S}}}}}\sigma^\star ),\\
\forall \sigma\in {}{\relax{S}}\smallsetminus \overline{ \relax{S}},\;\; (\uparrow^{{}^{{{}{\relax{S}}}}}\sigma )^{\underline{\perp}} &=& \uparrow^{{}^{{{}{\relax{S}}}}} \{\, \alpha^\star\;\vert\; \alpha\in \Theta^{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}(\sigma)\;\},\\
\forall S\in \underbrace{{}{\relax{S}}},\;\;
(\uparrow^{{}^{{{}{\relax{S}}}}}S)^{\underline{\perp}} &=& \uparrow^{{}^{{{}{\relax{S}}}}} \bigsqcup{}^{{}^{{{}{\relax{S}}}}}\{\, \alpha^\star\;\vert\; \alpha\in S\;\}.
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end lemma-11 -->
<!-- proof-18: body_md -->
Direct consequence of Lemma {{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@lemmaSorthogonal\endcsname\@firstoftwo{lemmaSorthogonal}}}.
<!-- end proof-18 -->
<!-- definition-19: body_md -->
Let us consider that the states/effects Chu Spaces $({ \relax{S}}_A,{ \relax{E}}_{{ \relax{S}}_A},\epsilon^{{ \relax{S}}_A})$ and $({ \relax{S}}_B,{ \relax{E}}_{{ \relax{S}}_B},\epsilon^{{ \relax{S}}_B})$ are respectively equipped with real structures $(\overline{ \relax{S}}_A,\star)$ and $(\overline{ \relax{S}}_B,\star)$ (we use the same notations for the star involutions as long as there can be no ambiguities). \\
Any morphism $(f ,f^{\ast})$ from the states/effects Chu Space $({ \relax{S}}_A,{ \relax{E}}_{{ \relax{S}}_A},\epsilon^{{ \relax{S}}_A})$ to the states/effects Chu Space $({ \relax{S}}_B,{ \relax{E}}_{{ \relax{S}}_B},\epsilon^{{ \relax{S}}_B})$ satisfying
\begin{eqnarray}
f^{\ast}(\overline{ \relax{E}}_{{ \relax{S}}_B}) & \subseteq & \overline{ \relax{E}}_{{ \relax{S}}_A}.\label{defrealmorphism}
\end{eqnarray}
will be said to be {\em a real-morphism}.\\
The set of real morphisms from ${ \relax{S}}_A$ to ${ \relax{S}}_B$ will be denoted $\overline{\relax{C}}({ \relax{S}}_A,{ \relax{S}}_B)$.
<!-- end definition-19 -->
<!-- definition-20: body_md -->
If ${ \relax{S}}$ admits a real structure, we can define the set of {\em real measurements,} denoted by $ \overline{\relax{M}}_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}}$, as the image by $\varphi$ (defined in ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@defvarphi\endcsname\@firstoftwo{defvarphi}}})) of $\overline{ \relax{E}}_{ \relax{S}}$.
<!-- end definition-20 -->
<!-- lemma-12: body_md -->
Real measurements (as defined in previous definition) are obviously real morphisms from ${ \relax{S}}$ to ${ \relax{B}}$.
<!-- end lemma-12 -->
<!-- proof-19: body_md -->
From the defining equation ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@mastu\endcsname\@firstoftwo{mastu}}}), we deduce immediately the property ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@defrealmorphism\endcsname\@firstoftwo{defrealmorphism}}}) as soon as the considered measurement is a real measurement.
<!-- end proof-19 -->
<!-- definition-21: body_md -->
\label{deterministicmeasurement}
A real measurement ${\relax{m}}\in \overline{\relax{M}}_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}}$ satisfying 
\begin{eqnarray}
{\relax{m}}(\overline{ \relax{S}}{}^{{}^{pure}}) &\subseteq & \{\textit{\bf Y},\textit{\bf N}\}
\end{eqnarray}
is said to be {\em a deterministic real measurement}.
<!-- end definition-21 -->
<!-- definition-22: body_md -->
\label{deterministicspace}
The space of states ${ \relax{S}}$ equipped with its real structure $(\overline{ \relax{S}},\star)$ is said to be {\em a deterministic space of states} (or {\em a simplex space of states}) iff ${\relax{m}}_{{ \relax{l}}}$ is a deterministic real measurement for every ${{ \relax{l}}} \in  \{\,{ \relax{l}}_{(\sigma,\sigma^\star)}\;\vert\; \sigma\in \overline{ \relax{S}}{}^{{}^{pure}}\,\}$.
\begin{eqnarray}
(\overline{ \relax{S}},\star)\;\textit{\rm deterministic} & \Leftrightarrow & \forall \sigma\in \overline{ \relax{S}}{}^{{}^{pure}},\; {\relax{m}}_{{ \relax{l}}_{(\sigma,\sigma^\star)}}(\overline{ \relax{S}}{}^{{}^{pure}}) \subseteq  \{\textit{\bf Y},\textit{\bf N}\}
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end definition-22 -->
<!-- lemma-13: body_md -->
\label{lemmaUsimplex}
The space of states ${ \relax{S}}$ equipped with its real structure $(\overline{ \relax{S}},\star)$ is a deterministic space of states iff 
\begin{eqnarray}
\forall \sigma \in \overline{ \relax{S}},\exists \textit{\bf !} \;U_\sigma\subseteq \overline{ \relax{S}}{}^{{}^{pure}} & \vert & \sigma=\bigsqcap{}^{{}^{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}U_\sigma.\label{simplexdecompunique}
\end{eqnarray}
(we note that necessarily $U_\sigma=\underline{\sigma}_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}$)
<!-- end lemma-13 -->
<!-- proof-20: body_md -->
Let us consider that ${ \relax{S}}$ equipped with its real structure $(\overline{ \relax{S}},\star)$ is a deterministic space of states, and let us suppose that there exists $\sigma_1,\sigma_2\in \overline{ \relax{S}}\smallsetminus \{\bot_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}}\}$ and $\sigma_3\in \overline{ \relax{S}}{}^{{}^{pure}}$ such that 
\begin{eqnarray}
\sigma_3 \sqsupseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}} (\sigma_1\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma_2)\;\;\textit{\rm and} \;\; \sigma_3\not\sqsupseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma_1\;\;\textit{\rm and}\;\;   \sigma_3\not\sqsupseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma_2\;\;\textit{\rm and}\;\;  \sigma_1\parallel_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma_2.\label{simplexdecompuniqueproof1}
\end{eqnarray}
Let us exhibit a contradiction. As long as $\sigma_3\not\sqsupseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma_1$ we know that $\forall \omega\in \underline{\sigma_1}_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}},  \omega\not\sqsupseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma_3$ and then ${\relax{m}}_{{ \relax{l}}_{(\sigma_3,\sigma_3^\star)}}(\omega)\not=\textit{\bf Y}$ and then ${\relax{m}}_{{ \relax{l}}_{(\sigma_3,\sigma_3^\star)}}(\omega)=\textit{\bf N}$ (here we use ${\relax{m}}_{{ \relax{l}}_{(\sigma_3,\sigma_3^\star)}}(\overline{ \relax{S}}{}^{{}^{pure}}) \subseteq  \{\textit{\bf Y},\textit{\bf N}\}$). As a consequence, using the homomorphic property of the measurement, we obtain ${\relax{m}}_{{ \relax{l}}_{(\sigma_3,\sigma_3^\star)}}(\sigma_1)=\textit{\bf N}$, or in other words $\sigma_1\sqsupseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma_3^\star$. Analogously, we obtain $\sigma_2\sqsupseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma_3^\star$. As a result, we obtain $(\sigma_1\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma_2)\sqsupseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma_3^\star$. But we have assumed $\sigma_3 \sqsupseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}} (\sigma_1\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma_2)$ which leads to the announced contradiction.  We have then proved the negation of the property ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@simplexdecompuniqueproof1\endcsname\@firstoftwo{simplexdecompuniqueproof1}}}).\\
Let us now imagine that the property ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@simplexdecompunique\endcsname\@firstoftwo{simplexdecompunique}}}) is not satisfied.  Then, there exists a subset $U$ of $\underline{\sigma}_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}$ which is minimal for the inclusion among the subsets of $\underline{\sigma}_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}$ satisfying $\sigma=\bigsqcap{}^{{}^{\relax{S}}} U$, and there exists $\sigma'$ element of $\underline{\sigma}_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}} \smallsetminus U$.\\ Let us then introduce $U_1$ and $U_2$ such that $U_1\cap U_2=\varnothing$ and $U_1\cup U_2=U$. Now, we define $\sigma_1:=\bigsqcap{}^{{}^{\relax{S}}} U_1$, $\sigma_2:=\bigsqcap{}^{{}^{\relax{S}}} U_2$ and $\sigma_3:=\sigma'$. They satisfy ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@simplexdecompuniqueproof1\endcsname\@firstoftwo{simplexdecompuniqueproof1}}}) which is contradictory. Then, we have proved the property ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@simplexdecompunique\endcsname\@firstoftwo{simplexdecompunique}}}).\\
Reciprocally, let us suppose that the property ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@simplexdecompunique\endcsname\@firstoftwo{simplexdecompunique}}}) is satisfied.  We have then for any $\sigma\in \overline{ \relax{S}}\smallsetminus \{\bot_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}}\}$ the basic result $U_{\bot_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}}}=U_{\sigma} \cup U_{\sigma^\star}$, which leads to the property ${\relax{m}}_{{ \relax{l}}_{(\sigma,\sigma^\star)}}(\overline{ \relax{S}}{}^{{}^{pure}}) \subseteq  \{\textit{\bf Y},\textit{\bf N}\}$. This concludes the proof.
<!-- end proof-20 -->
<!-- lemma-14: body_md -->
$(\overline{ \relax{S}},\star)$ is deterministic iff $(\overline{ \relax{S}}{}^{{}^{pure}},\underline{\perp})$ is completely reducible, i.e. iff
\begin{eqnarray}
\forall A\subseteq \overline{ \relax{S}}{}^{{}^{pure}}\;\vert\; A=A^{\underline{\perp}\underline{\perp}},&\textit{\rm we have}& A\cup A^{\underline{\perp}}=\overline{ \relax{S}}{}^{{}^{pure}},\;\;\;\;A\cap A^{\underline{\perp}}=\varnothing.
\end{eqnarray}
Here, the operator $(\cdot)^{\underline{\perp}}$ designates the operator from $\mathcal{P}(\overline{ \relax{S}}{}^{{}^{pure}})$ to itself which maps $A$ to $\{\sigma\in \overline{ \relax{S}}{}^{{}^{pure}}\;\vert\; \forall \sigma'\in A, \sigma\underline{\perp}\sigma'\}$.
<!-- end lemma-14 -->
<!-- proof-21: body_md -->
We note that, at the end of the proof of Lemma {{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@lemmaUsimplex\endcsname\@firstoftwo{lemmaUsimplex}}}, we have shown the following result
\begin{eqnarray}
\hspace{-1cm}(\overline{ \relax{S}},\star)\;\textit{\rm deterministic} & \Leftrightarrow & \forall \sigma\in \overline{ \relax{S}}\smallsetminus \{\bot_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}}\},\; {\relax{m}}_{{ \relax{l}}_{(\sigma,\sigma^\star)}}(\overline{ \relax{S}}{}^{{}^{pure}}) \subseteq  \{\textit{\bf Y},\textit{\bf N}\}
\end{eqnarray}
the announced result is then obtained.
<!-- end proof-21 -->
<!-- lemma-15: body_md -->
We have also obtained the following characterization
\begin{eqnarray}
\hspace{-1cm}(\overline{ \relax{S}},\star)\;\textit{\rm NOT deterministic} & \Leftrightarrow &\exists\sigma_1,\sigma_2\in \overline{ \relax{S}}\smallsetminus \{\bot_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}}\},\exists\sigma_3\in \overline{ \relax{S}}{}^{{}^{pure}}\;\;\vert\;\; \label{threestatesnotdeterministic}\\
&&\sigma_3 \sqsupseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}} (\sigma_1\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma_2)\;\;\textit{\rm and} \;\; \sigma_3\not\sqsupseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma_1\;\;\textit{\rm and}\;\;   \sigma_3\not\sqsupseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma_2\;\;\textit{\rm and}\;\;  \sigma_1\parallel_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma_2.\nonumber
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end lemma-15 -->
<!-- proof-22: body_md -->
This result has already been proved along the proof of Lemma {{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@lemmaUsimplex\endcsname\@firstoftwo{lemmaUsimplex}}}.
<!-- end proof-22 -->
<!-- theorem-12: body_md -->
Let us suppose that $\overline{ \relax{S}}$ is a simplex space of states and let $\star$ be defined by
\begin{eqnarray}
\forall \sigma\in \overline{ \relax{S}},&&\sigma^\star := \bigsqcap{}^{{}^{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}_{\alpha\in \overline{ \relax{S}}{}^{{}^{pure}}\!\!\!\!\smallsetminus \underline{\sigma}_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}} \alpha.\label{starsimplex}
\end{eqnarray}
Then, $(\overline{ \relax{S}}, \star)$ is a real structure of $\overline{ \relax{S}}$.\\
Conversely, let us consider ${ \relax{S}}$ a space of states which admits a real structure $(\overline{ \relax{S}}, \star)$. Let us suppose that $\overline{ \relax{S}}$ is a simplex space of states.  Then, we have necessarily ${ \relax{S}}=\overline{ \relax{S}}$.
<!-- end theorem-12 -->
<!-- proof-23: body_md -->
As long as $\overline{\relax{S}}$ is a simplex space of states, the star map $\star$ defined on the real structure of ${\relax{S}}$ is necessarily given by the formula ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@starsimplex\endcsname\@firstoftwo{starsimplex}}}).\\
The first part of the theorem is trivial to check. \\
Let us now assume that the real structure of ${ \relax{S}}$ is a simplex space of states and let us prove that ${ \relax{S}}=\overline{ \relax{S}}$.\\
Let us then consider two elements $\sigma$ and $\sigma'$ in $\overline{\relax{S}}$ such that $\neg \;\widehat{\sigma \sigma'}{}^{{}^{\overline{\relax{S}}}}$.  Let us suppose that $\widehat{\sigma \sigma'}{}^{{}^{{\relax{S}}}}$.\\
As long as $\overline{\relax{S}}$ is a simplex, we must necessarily have $\sigma^\star \sqsubseteq_{{}_{\overline{\relax{S}}}} \sigma'$.  As a consequence, we have $\widehat{\sigma\,\sigma^\star}{}^{{}^{{\relax{S}}}}$ which contradicts the condition $\neg\; \widehat{\sigma\sigma^\star}{}^{{}^{{ \relax{S}}}}$ imposed for a real structure. \\ 
As a conclusion,  ${ \relax{S}}\smallsetminus \overline{\relax{S}}$ is empty.
<!-- end proof-23 -->
<!-- definition-23: body_md -->
Traditionally, an Inf semi-lattice ${ \relax{S}}$ is said to be {\em distributive} iff 
\begin{eqnarray}
&&\hspace{-2cm} \forall \sigma,\sigma_1,\sigma_2\in { \relax{S}}\;\vert\; \sigma\not= \sigma_1,\sigma_2 ,\;\;\;\;\;\; (\sigma_1 \sqcap_{{}_{ \relax{S}}} \sigma_2) \sqsubseteq_{{}_{ \relax{S}}}  \sigma  \Rightarrow \nonumber\\ 
&&\exists \sigma'_1,\sigma'_2\in { \relax{S}}\;\vert\; (\,\sigma_1 \sqsubseteq_{{}_{ \relax{S}}} \sigma'_1,\;\;\; \sigma_2 \sqsubseteq_{{}_{ \relax{S}}} \sigma'_2\;\;\;\textit{\rm and}\;\;\; \sigma = \sigma'_1 \sqcap_{{}_{ \relax{S}}} \sigma'_2\,).\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end definition-23 -->
<!-- lemma-16: body_md -->
A simplex space of states is necessarily distributive as an Inf semi-lattice.
<!-- end lemma-16 -->
<!-- proof-24: body_md -->
Let us first assume that ${\relax{S}}$ is a simplex space of states. 
Let us consider $\sigma,\sigma_1,\sigma_2\in { \relax{S}}$ such that $\sigma\not= \sigma_1,\sigma_2 $ and $ (\sigma_1 \sqcap_{{}_{ \relax{S}}} \sigma_2) \sqsubseteq_{{}_{ \relax{S}}}  \sigma$. We have then $\underline{\sigma}_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}} \subseteq (\underline{\sigma_1}_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}}\cup \underline{\sigma_2}_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}})$. If we define $\sigma'_1:=\bigsqcap{}^{{}^{\relax{S}}}(\underline{\sigma_1}_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}}\cap \underline{\sigma}_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}})$ and $\sigma'_2:=\bigsqcap{}^{{}^{\relax{S}}}(\underline{\sigma_2}_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}}\cap \underline{\sigma}_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}})$ we check immediately that $\sigma_1 \sqsubseteq_{{}_{ \relax{S}}} \sigma'_1,\;\;\; \sigma_2 \sqsubseteq_{{}_{ \relax{S}}} \sigma'_2$ and $\sigma = \sigma'_1 \sqcap_{{}_{ \relax{S}}} \sigma'_2$. As a result, ${\relax{S}}$ is distributive.
<!-- end proof-24 -->
<!-- definition-24: body_md -->
\label{completelyindeterministicspace}
The space of states ${ \relax{S}}$ equipped with its real structure $(\overline{ \relax{S}},\star)$ is said to be {\em a completely indeterministic space of states} iff,  
\begin{eqnarray}  
\forall \sigma,\lambda\in \overline{ \relax{S}}{}^{{}^{pure}}\;\vert\; \sigma\sqsupseteq_{{}_{ \relax{S}}}\lambda^\star, && \exists \kappa \in \overline{ \relax{S}}{}^{{}^{pure}}\;\vert\; \kappa\not\sqsupseteq_{{}_{ \relax{S}}}\sigma^\star\;\textit{\rm and}\; \kappa\not\sqsupseteq_{{}_{ \relax{S}}}\lambda^\star.
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end definition-24 -->
<!-- lemma-17: body_md -->
\label{lemmairreducibility}
If $(\overline{ \relax{S}},\star)$ is completely indeterministic then $(\overline{ \relax{S}}{}^{{}^{pure}},\underline{\perp})$ is irreducible, i.e.  
\begin{eqnarray}
\nexists A\subseteq \overline{ \relax{S}}{}^{{}^{pure}}\;\vert\; (\, A=A^{\underline{\perp}\underline{\perp}},\;\;\;\;\varnothing \varsubsetneq A \varsubsetneq \overline{ \relax{S}}{}^{{}^{pure}},\;\;\;\; A\cup A^{\underline{\perp}}=\overline{ \relax{S}}{}^{{}^{pure}},\;\;\;\;A\cap A^{\underline{\perp}}=\varnothing\,).\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;
\end{eqnarray}
Here again, the operator $(\cdot)^{\underline{\perp}}$ designates the operator from $\mathcal{P}(\overline{ \relax{S}}{}^{{}^{pure}})$ to itself which maps $A$ to $\{\sigma\in \overline{ \relax{S}}{}^{{}^{pure}}\;\vert\; \forall \sigma'\in A, \sigma\underline{\perp}\sigma'\}$.
<!-- end lemma-17 -->
<!-- proof-25: body_md -->
Let us consider a completely indeterministic $(\overline{ \relax{S}},\star)$. Let us suppose that $(\overline{ \relax{S}}{}^{{}^{pure}},\underline{\perp})$ is reducible and let us exhibit a contradiction. Let us then consider $A\subseteq \overline{ \relax{S}}{}^{{}^{pure}}$ such that $A=A^{\underline{\perp}\underline{\perp}}$ and $\varnothing \varsubsetneq A \varsubsetneq \overline{ \relax{S}}{}^{{}^{pure}}$ and $A\cup A^{\underline{\perp}}=\overline{ \relax{S}}{}^{{}^{pure}}$ and $A\cap A^{\underline{\perp}}=\varnothing$. Let us fix $\sigma$ an element of $A$. For any $\omega$ satisfying $\omega\not\!\!\underline{\perp} \sigma$ we cannot have $\omega\in A^{\underline{\perp}}$ and then, by assumption, $\omega\in A$. Let us now consider $\lambda \in A^{\underline{\perp}}$. As long as $\lambda\underline{\perp}\sigma$ and $(\overline{ \relax{S}},\star)$ being completely indeterministic, there exists $\kappa\in \overline{ \relax{S}}{}^{{}^{pure}}$ such that $\kappa\not\!\!\!\underline{\perp}\sigma$ and $\kappa\not\!\!\!\underline{\perp}\lambda$. From $\kappa\not\!\!\!\underline{\perp}\sigma$ we deduce that $\kappa\in A$. However, from $\kappa\not\!\!\!\underline{\perp}\lambda$ we deduce that $\lambda\notin A^{\underline{\perp}}$ which is contradictory. This concludes the proof of the assertion.
<!-- end proof-25 -->
<!-- definition-25: body_md -->
\label{linearindeterministicspace}
The space of states ${ \relax{S}}$ equipped with its real structure $(\overline{ \relax{S}},\star)$ is said to be {\em linear} iff, 
\begin{eqnarray}
&&\hspace{-1cm}\forall \sigma_1,\sigma_2\in \overline{ \relax{S}}{}^{{}^{pure}}\;\vert\;                                                          
(\sigma_1\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma_2)\raisebox{1.3ex}{\,\rotatebox{180}{$\sqsupseteq$}}\,_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma_1,\sigma_2, \nonumber\\
&& \exists \sigma_3 \in { \relax{S}}\;\vert\; (\,\sigma_3\not\sqsupseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma_1\;\textit{\rm and}\; \sigma_3\not\sqsupseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma_2\;\textit{\rm and}\; \sigma_3\raisebox{1.3ex}{\,\rotatebox{180}{$\sqsubseteq$}}\,_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}}(\sigma_1\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma_2)\,).\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end definition-25 -->
<!-- lemma-18: body_md -->
\begin{eqnarray}
\forall { \relax{F}},{ \relax{F}}'\in { \mathcal{F}}(\overline{{ \relax{S}}}),&& { \relax{F}}\subseteq { \relax{F}}' \;\;\Rightarrow\;\; \Omega({ \relax{F}})\sqsubseteq \Omega({ \relax{F}}').
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end lemma-18 -->
<!-- proof-26: body_md -->
Trivial.
<!-- end proof-26 -->
<!-- lemma-19: body_md -->
\begin{eqnarray}
\forall \sigma\in {{ \relax{S}}},&& \{\,\sigma'\in \overline{{ \relax{S}}}\;\vert\; \sigma'\sqsubseteq_{{}_{{{ \relax{S}}}}}\sigma\,\} \in { \mathcal{F}}(\overline{{ \relax{S}}}).
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end lemma-19 -->
<!-- proof-27: body_md -->
The only non trivial part is the chain-completeness of $\{\,\sigma'\in \overline{{ \relax{S}}}\;\vert\; \sigma'\sqsubseteq_{{}_{{{ \relax{S}}}}}\sigma\,\}$. It derives from the chain-completeness of $\overline{{ \relax{S}}}$ which can be derived from the down-completeness of $\overline{{ \relax{S}}}$ using the star operation.
<!-- end proof-27 -->
<!-- definition-26: body_md -->
We will denote by ${\widehat{{\mathcal{P}}(\overline{{ \relax{S}}})}}$ the subset of ${\mathcal{P}}(\overline{{ \relax{S}}})$ formed by the collections $J\in {\mathcal{P}}(\overline{{ \relax{S}}})$ which admit a common upper-bound in ${ \relax{S}}$.  Due to the down-completeness of ${ \relax{S}}$, the elements of such a collection admit a supremum in ${ \relax{S}}$.
<!-- end definition-26 -->
<!-- lemma-20: body_md -->
\label{PastlowersubsetP}
${\widehat{{\mathcal{P}}(\overline{{ \relax{S}}})}} $ is a lower subset (i.e.  it is downward closed) of $({\mathcal{P}}(\overline{{ \relax{S}}}),\sqsubseteq)$ containing every elements of the form $\{\sigma\}$ for $\sigma\in \overline{{ \relax{S}}}$.
<!-- end lemma-20 -->
<!-- proof-28: body_md -->
Trivial.
<!-- end proof-28 -->
<!-- definition-27: body_md -->
\label{definitionTheta}
We have already introduced the following map
\begin{eqnarray}
\begin{array}{lclcl}
\Theta^{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}} & : & {{ \relax{S}}} & \longrightarrow & {\widehat{{\mathcal{P}}(\overline{{ \relax{S}}})}}\\
& & \sigma & \mapsto & \Omega(\{\,\sigma'\in \overline{{ \relax{S}}}\;\vert\; \sigma'\sqsubseteq_{{}_{{{ \relax{S}}}}}\sigma\,\}).\label{defThetaS}
\end{array}
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end definition-27 -->
<!-- definition-28: body_md -->
\label{definitionLambda}
We also introduce the following map 
\begin{eqnarray}
\begin{array}{lclcl}
\Lambda^{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}} & : & {\widehat{{\mathcal{P}}(\overline{{ \relax{S}}})}} & \longrightarrow & { \relax{S}}\\
& & J & \mapsto &\Lambda^{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}(J):=\bigsqcup{}^{{}^{{ \relax{S}}}}J.
\end{array}
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end definition-28 -->
<!-- lemma-21: body_md -->
\label{lemmaLambda}
\begin{eqnarray}
\forall \sigma\in {{ \relax{S}}},\exists J:=\Theta^{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}(\sigma)\in {\widehat{{\mathcal{P}}(\overline{{ \relax{S}}})}} & \vert & \Lambda^{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}(J)=\sigma.
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end lemma-21 -->
<!-- proof-29: body_md -->
Let us consider $\sigma\in {{ \relax{S}}}$ and let us introduce $\sigma':=\bigsqcup{}^{{}^{{ \relax{S}}}}\{\,\alpha\in \overline{{ \relax{S}}}\;\vert\; \alpha\sqsubseteq_{{}_{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}}\sigma\,\}$.  We note that for any ${ \relax{l}}\in \overline{ \relax{E}}_{ \relax{S}}$, we have $\epsilon^{{ \relax{S}}}_{ \relax{l}}(\sigma)=\epsilon^{{ \relax{S}}}_{ \relax{l}}(\sigma')$ and then, due to the condition ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@realChuseparated\endcsname\@firstoftwo{realChuseparated}}}), we then conclude that $\sigma=\sigma'$.
<!-- end proof-29 -->
<!-- lemma-22: body_md -->
\label{galoisthetaSbar}
The pair $(\Theta^{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}},\Lambda^{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}})$ is a Galois connection, i.e.
\begin{eqnarray}
\forall J\in {\widehat{{\mathcal{P}}(\overline{{ \relax{S}}})}},\forall \sigma\in {{ \relax{S}}},&& J \sqsubseteq \Theta^{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}(\sigma) \;\; \Leftrightarrow \;\; \Lambda^{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}(J)\sqsubseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}} \sigma.
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end lemma-22 -->
<!-- definition-29: body_md -->
\label{definitionJSbar}
We will denote by $cl^{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}$ the closure associated to the previous Galois connection, i.e.
\begin{eqnarray}
\begin{array}{lclcl}
cl^{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}} & : & {\widehat{{\mathcal{P}}(\overline{{ \relax{S}}})}} & \longrightarrow & {\widehat{{\mathcal{P}}(\overline{{ \relax{S}}})}}\\
& & J & \mapsto &\Theta^{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}} \circ \Lambda^{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}(J).
\end{array}\label{expressioncl}
\end{eqnarray}
We will denote by ${ \relax{J}}_{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}$ the set of closed elements in ${\widehat{{\mathcal{P}}(\overline{{ \relax{S}}})}}$, i.e. ${ \relax{J}}_{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}:=cl^{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}({\widehat{{\mathcal{P}}(\overline{{ \relax{S}}})}})$.
<!-- end definition-29 -->
<!-- theorem-13: body_md -->
We have as usual
\begin{eqnarray}
\forall J\in {\widehat{{\mathcal{P}}(\overline{{ \relax{S}}})}},&& J\sqsubseteq cl^{{{ \relax{S}}'}}(J),\label{closure1}\\
\forall J,J'\in {\widehat{{\mathcal{P}}(\overline{{ \relax{S}}})}},&& J\sqsubseteq J' \;\;\Rightarrow\;\;cl^{{{ \relax{S}}'}}(J)\sqsubseteq cl^{{{ \relax{S}}'}}(J'),\label{closure2}\\
\forall J\in {\widehat{{\mathcal{P}}(\overline{{ \relax{S}}})}},&& cl^{{{ \relax{S}}'}}\circ cl^{{{ \relax{S}}'}}(J) = cl^{{{ \relax{S}}'}}(J).\label{closure3}
   
                                                                                        
                                                                                                                                                                                              
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end theorem-13 -->
<!-- lemma-23: body_md -->
\label{JSbarfirstcondition}
\begin{eqnarray}
\forall J\in { \relax{J}}_{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}},\forall \sigma,\sigma'\in J,&& \sigma\not=\sigma' \;\;\Rightarrow\;\; \neg \widehat{\sigma\sigma'}{}^{{}^{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}}.\label{defJSbar2}
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end lemma-23 -->
<!-- proof-30: body_md -->
Let us consider $ \sigma,\sigma'\in \Theta^{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}(\alpha)$ with $\sigma\not=\sigma'$. Let us suppose that $\widehat{\sigma\sigma'}{}^{{}^{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}}$. We have then $(\sigma\sqcup_{{}_{{{ \relax{S}}}}}\sigma')\in \overline{{ \relax{S}}}$ and also $(\sigma\sqcup_{{}_{{{ \relax{S}}}}}\sigma')\sqsubseteq_{{}_{{{ \relax{S}}}}}\alpha$, and we have obviously $\sigma\sqsubset_{{}_{{{ \relax{S}}}}} (\sigma\sqcup_{{}_{{{ \relax{S}}}}}\sigma')$. These points lead to a contradiction as we have assumed that $ \sigma$ is a  {maximal element} of $\{\,\alpha'\in \overline{{ \relax{S}}}\;\vert\; \alpha'\sqsubseteq_{{}_{{{ \relax{S}}}}}\alpha\,\}$.
<!-- end proof-30 -->
<!-- lemma-24: body_md -->
\label{JSbarsecondcondition}
\begin{eqnarray}
\forall J\in { \relax{J}}_{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}},\forall \sigma,\sigma'\in J,&& \sigma'\not\sqsupseteq_{{}_{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}}\sigma^\star.\label{defJSbar3}
\end{eqnarray}
Note that this condition is equivalent to the following one
\begin{eqnarray}
\forall J\in { \relax{J}}_{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}},\nexists \omega\in \overline{{ \relax{S}}} & \vert & \{\omega,\omega^\star\}\sqsubseteq J.\label{defJSbar3b}
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end lemma-24 -->
<!-- proof-31: body_md -->
Let us consider $\sigma,\sigma'\in \Theta^{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}(\alpha)$. 
If we had $\sigma'\sqsupseteq_{{}_{{{ \relax{S}}}}}\sigma^\star$, $\alpha$ would be a common upper bound of $\sigma$ and $\sigma^\star$ in ${{ \relax{S}}}$. This point would contradict the fact that $\neg\widehat{\sigma\sigma^\star}{}^{{}^{{{ \relax{S}}}}}$ by the definition of the $\star$ map. \\
The analogous formulation ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@defJSbar3b\endcsname\@firstoftwo{defJSbar3b}}}) is derived from ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@defJSbar3\endcsname\@firstoftwo{defJSbar3}}}) using the order-reversing property of the star.
<!-- end proof-31 -->
<!-- lemma-25: body_md -->
\label{lemmaposetJSbar}
The pre-order $\sqsubseteq$ defined on ${ \mathcal{P}}(\overline{{ \relax{S}}})$ is in fact a partial order on ${ \relax{J}}_{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}$.
<!-- end lemma-25 -->
<!-- proof-32: body_md -->
Let us consider $J$ and $J'$ two elements of ${ \relax{J}}_{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}$ and let us assume that $J\sqsubseteq J'$ and $J'\sqsubseteq J$. Due to $J\sqsubseteq J'$, we deduce that for any $ \sigma\in J$ there exists $\sigma'\in J'$ such that $\sigma \sqsubseteq_{{}_{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}} \sigma'$. For this $\sigma'$, the property $J'\sqsubseteq J$ implies that there exists $\sigma''\in J$ such that $\sigma' \sqsubseteq_{{}_{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}} \sigma''$. However, due to the property ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@defJSbar2\endcsname\@firstoftwo{defJSbar2}}}) we necessarily have $\sigma=\sigma''$, and then $\sigma=\sigma'$ by antisymmetry of $\sqsupseteq_{{}_{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}}$. This concludes the proof.
<!-- end proof-32 -->
<!-- lemma-26: body_md -->
\label{infimumJ}
The infimum of two elements $J$ and $J'$ of ${ \relax{J}}_{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}$, denoted $J\sqcap_{{}_{{ \relax{J}}_{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}}} J'$ is given as follows
\begin{eqnarray}
