J\sqcap_{{}_{{ \relax{J}}_{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}}} J' &=& Max \left( (\downarrow_{{}_{ \relax{S}}}\bigsqcup{}^{{}^{{{ \relax{S}}}}}J) \cap (\downarrow_{{}_{ \relax{S}}}\bigsqcup{}^{{}^{{{ \relax{S}}}}}J') \cap {\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}
\right)\\
&=& J\sqcap J'\\
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             
&=& Max \{\, \sigma\sqcap_{{}_{{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}}\sigma'\;\vert\; \sigma\in J,\sigma'\in J'\,\}.\label{infimumJprop}
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end lemma-26 -->
<!-- proof-33: body_md -->
Let us consider $J$ and $J'$ two elements of ${ \relax{J}}_{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}$ (i.e. $cl^{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}(J)=J$ and $cl^{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}(J')=J'$). We first note that $(J\sqcap J') \sqsubseteq J$ and $J$ is in ${\widehat{{\mathcal{P}}(\overline{{ \relax{S}}})}}$, and then, using Lemma {{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@PastlowersubsetP\endcsname\@firstoftwo{PastlowersubsetP}}} we deduce that $(J\sqcap J')$ is in ${\widehat{{\mathcal{P}}(\overline{{ \relax{S}}})}}$.\\
Now, let us consider $J''$ in ${ \relax{J}}_{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}$ such that $J''\sqsubseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{J}}_{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}}}J$ and $J''\sqsubseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{J}}_{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}}}J'$. We have that, for any $\sigma''\in J''$, there exists $\sigma\in J$,$\sigma'\in J'$ such that $\sigma''\sqsubseteq_{{}_{{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}}}\sigma$ and $\sigma''\sqsubseteq_{{}_{{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}}}\sigma'$, and then such that $\sigma''\sqsubseteq_{{}_{{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}}}(\sigma\sqcap_{{}_{{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}}}\sigma')$. As a result, we have $J''\sqsubseteq Max\{\, \sigma\sqcap_{{}_{{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}}\sigma'\;\vert\; \sigma\in J,\sigma'\in J'\,\}$.
<!-- end proof-33 -->
<!-- lemma-27: body_md -->
\label{supremumJ}
Let $I$ and $I'$ be two elements of ${ \relax{J}}_{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}$ such that there exists $I''\in { \relax{J}}_{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}$ with $I\sqsubseteq I''$ and $I'\sqsubseteq I''$.\\
The supremum of $I$ and $I'$ in ${{ \relax{J}}_{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}}$ (denoted $I\sqcup_{{}_{{ \relax{J}}_{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}}} I'$) exists and is simply given by
\begin{eqnarray}
I\sqcup_{{}_{{ \relax{J}}_{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}}} I' &=& cl^{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}(I \cup I').
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end lemma-27 -->
<!-- proof-34: body_md -->
Let $I$ and $I'$ be two elements of ${ \relax{J}}_{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}$.  Because of the down-completeness of ${ \relax{J}}_{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}$ and of the fact that $I$ and $I'$ admit a common-upper-bound, the supremum of $I$ and $I'$ do exist.\\
The supremum $I\sqcup_{{}_{{ \relax{J}}_{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}}} I'$ must be the smallest closed element upper-bounding for $\sqsubseteq$ the elements $I$ and $I'$. This supremum is then given by $cl^{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}(I \cup I')$.  Note that the expression $cl^{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}(I \cup I')$ is well defined because of the existence of $I''$.
<!-- end proof-34 -->
<!-- theorem-14: body_md -->
The map $\Theta^{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}$ is an isomorphism from ${ \relax{S}}$ to ${ \relax{J}}_{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}$.
<!-- end theorem-14 -->
<!-- proof-35: body_md -->
In order to prove the injective property for $\Theta^{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}$, it suffices to note that, for any $\sigma,\sigma'\in { \relax{S}}$, the property $\Theta^{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}(\sigma)=\Theta^{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}(\sigma')$ implies $\Lambda^{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}\circ \Theta^{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}(\sigma)=\Lambda^{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}\circ \Theta^{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}(\sigma')$, i.e.  $\sigma=\sigma'$ (see Lemma {{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@lemmaLambda\endcsname\@firstoftwo{lemmaLambda}}}).\\
The surjectivity property for $\Theta^{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}$ is a consequence of the injectivity of $\Lambda^{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}$ on ${ \relax{J}}_{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}$.\\
As a left component of a Galois connection, the map $\Theta^{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}$ preserves infima.
<!-- end proof-35 -->
<!-- lemma-28: body_md -->
$\{\,J\in { \relax{J}}_{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}} \;\vert\; Card(J)=1\,\}$ is isomorphic to $\overline{{ \relax{S}}}$. In other words,
\begin{eqnarray}
\{\,J\in { \relax{J}}_{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}} \;\vert\; Card(J)=1\,\}& \cong & \overline{{ \relax{S}}}.
\end{eqnarray}
and for any $\sigma,\sigma'\in {\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}$, we have
\begin{eqnarray}
\{\sigma\}\sqcap_{{}_{{ \relax{J}}_{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}}} \{\sigma'\} & = & \{\sigma\sqcap_{{}_{{{ \relax{S}}'}}}\sigma'\}.
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end lemma-28 -->
<!-- proof-36: body_md -->
If $\sigma\in \overline{{ \relax{S}}}$ we have obviously $\Theta^{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}(\sigma)=\{\sigma\}$. 
Conversely, Let us assume that $Card(\Theta^{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}(\sigma))=1$ and let us suppose that  $\sigma\in {{ \relax{S}}}\smallsetminus \overline{{ \relax{S}}}$. We denote $\sigma'$ the unique element of $\Theta^{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}(\sigma)$. We then have $\sigma\not=\sigma'$. However, we observe immediately that, for any $\alpha\in \overline{{ \relax{S}}}$, $\epsilon^{{ \relax{S}}}_{{\relax{l}}_{{}_{(\alpha,\alpha^\star)}}}(\sigma)=\epsilon^{{ \relax{S}}}_{{\relax{l}}_{{}_{(\alpha,\alpha^\star)}}}(\sigma')$. Then, using ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@realChuseparated\endcsname\@firstoftwo{realChuseparated}}}) we deduce $\sigma=\sigma'$ which contradicts the assumption. We then obtain $\sigma\in \overline{{ \relax{S}}}$.\\
The second property is trivial to check.
<!-- end proof-36 -->
<!-- lemma-29: body_md -->
\label{lemmatricky}
We have necessarily, for any $I$ subset of $\overline{{ \relax{S}}}$
\begin{eqnarray}
I\in { \relax{J}}_{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}&\Rightarrow & I = Max\{\,\bigsqcup{}^{{}^{{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}}} J\;\vert\; J\sqsubseteq I\;\textit{\rm and}\;\widehat{\;J\;}{}^{{}^{{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}}}\}.
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end lemma-29 -->
<!-- proof-37: body_md -->
Let us consider $I\in { \relax{J}}_{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}$.\\
Let $J$ be a subset of ${\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}$ satisfying $J\sqsubseteq I$ and $\widehat{\;J\;}{}^{{}^{{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}}}$. We have then $J\in {\widehat{{\mathcal{P}}(\overline{{ \relax{S}}})}}$ (we can then apply $cl^{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}$ on $J$). We have then also $\{\bigsqcup{}^{{}^{{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}}} J\}=cl^{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}(J)\sqsubseteq cl^{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}(I)=I$. Hence, $Max\{\,\bigsqcup{}^{{}^{{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}}} J\;\vert\; J\sqsubseteq I\;\textit{\rm and}\;\widehat{\;J\;}{}^{{}^{{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}}}\}\sqsubseteq I$. \\
On another part, for any $\sigma\in I$ we have $\{\sigma\}\sqsubseteq I$ and $\widehat{\;\sigma\;}{}^{{}^{{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}}}$, and then $\{\sigma\} \sqsubseteq \{\,\bigsqcup{}^{{}^{{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}}} J\;\vert\; J\sqsubseteq I\;\textit{\rm and}\;\widehat{\;J\;}{}^{{}^{{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}}}\}$. As a result, we have then $I \sqsubseteq Max\{\,\bigsqcup{}^{{}^{{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}}} J\;\vert\; J\sqsubseteq I\;\textit{\rm and}\;\widehat{\;J\;}{}^{{}^{{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}}}\}$. \\ 
As long as we have $\forall \sigma,\sigma'\in Max\{\,\bigsqcup{}^{{}^{{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}}} J\;\vert\; J\sqsubseteq I\;\textit{\rm and}\;\widehat{\;J\;}{}^{{}^{{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}}}\}$ the property $\neg \widehat{\;\sigma \sigma'\;}{}^{{}^{{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}}}$, we can use the antisymmetry of $\sqsubseteq$ and we have then $I = Max\{\,\bigsqcup{}^{{}^{{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}}} J\;\vert\; J\sqsubseteq I\;\textit{\rm and}\;\widehat{\;J\;}{}^{{}^{{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}}}\}$.
<!-- end proof-37 -->
<!-- lemma-30: body_md -->
Let us denote by $U:=\Theta^{\overline{ \relax{S}}}(\xi)\in { \relax{J}}_{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}\;\;$ for any $\xi\in { \relax{S}}$. We then have
\begin{eqnarray}
\forall \kappa\in {\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}, \exists \varphi \in U & \vert & \forall \chi\in U,\; (\kappa \sqcap_{{}_{{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}}} \chi) 
\sqsubseteq_{{}_{{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}}}
(\kappa \sqcap_{{}_{{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}}} \varphi).\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\label{fundamentalformula}
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end lemma-30 -->
<!-- proof-38: body_md -->
Let us first remark that, if we denote $U:=\Theta^{\overline{ \relax{S}}}(\xi)$, we have in Lemma {{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@lemmatricky\endcsname\@firstoftwo{lemmatricky}}} that $Max \{\, (\bigsqcup{}^{{}^{{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}}} V)\;\vert\; V\sqsubseteq U, \;\widehat{\;V\;}{}^{{}^{{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}}}\,\}=U$.\\
Let us now fix $\kappa\in {\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}$.  Let us denote by $X_U$ the subset $\{\,\kappa \sqcap_{{}_{{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}}}\omega\;\vert\; \omega\in U\,\}$. We note that $\widehat{\;X_U\;}{}^{{}^{{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}}}$ because $(\kappa \sqcap_{{}_{{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}}}\chi) \sqsubseteq_{{}_{{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}}} \kappa$ for any $\chi\in U$ and we have then
\begin{eqnarray}
\bigsqcup{}^{{}^{{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}}} X_U & \sqsubseteq_{{}_{{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}}} & \kappa.\label{eq1pre}
\end{eqnarray}
We also note that
\begin{eqnarray}
\bigsqcup{}^{{}^{{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}}} X_U=
\bigsqcup{}^{{}^{{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}}}\{\,\kappa \sqcap_{{}_{{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}}}\chi\;\vert\; \chi\in U\,\} &\sqsubseteq & Max \{\, (\bigsqcup{}^{{}^{{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}}} V)\;\vert\; V\sqsubseteq U, \;\widehat{\;V\;}{}^{{}^{{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}}}\,\}=U.\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;
\end{eqnarray}
In other words, 
\begin{eqnarray}
\exists \varphi \in U & \vert & \bigsqcup{}^{{}^{{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}}}\{\,\kappa \sqcap_{{}_{{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}}}\chi\;\vert\; \chi\in U\,\} \sqsubseteq_{{}_{{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}}} \varphi. \label{eq2pre}
\end{eqnarray}
From ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@eq1pre\endcsname\@firstoftwo{eq1pre}}}) and ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@eq2pre\endcsname\@firstoftwo{eq2pre}}}), we have then obtained
\begin{eqnarray}
\exists \varphi \in U & \vert & \bigsqcup{}^{{}^{{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}}}\{\,\kappa \sqcap_{{}_{{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}}}\chi\;\vert\; \chi\in U\,\} \sqsubseteq_{{}_{{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}}} (\kappa \sqcap_{{}_{{\overline{{ \relax{S}}}}}} \varphi). 
\end{eqnarray}
This concludes the proof.
<!-- end proof-38 -->
<!-- definition-30: body_md -->
\label{definitionrealspaceofstates}
We will define {\em a real space of states} to be a quadruple $({\relax{S}}',{ \mathcal{Q}}({ \relax{S}}'),cl^{{{ \relax{S}}'}},\star)$ such that
\begin{itemize}
\@par\hangindent 2em ${ \relax{S}}'$ is a down complete Inf semi-lattice with bottom element $\bot_{{}_{ \relax{S}'}}$.  We require ${ \relax{S}}'$ to be generated by its maximal elements, i.e. 
 \begin{eqnarray}
\hspace{-1.5cm}&&\forall \sigma \in { \relax{S}}', \;\; \sigma= \bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{ \relax{S}}'}}  \underline{\sigma}_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}'}} \;\;\textit{\rm where}\;\;
\underline{\sigma}_{{}_{ { \relax{S}}'}}:=\{\, \sigma'\in { \relax{S}'}{}^{{}^{pure}}\;\vert\; \sigma'\sqsupseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}'}}} \sigma\;\}
\;\;\textit{\rm and}\;\; { \relax{S}'}{}^{{}^{pure}}:=Max({ \relax{S}'})\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;
\label{RECcompletemeetirreducibleordergeneratingS}
\end{eqnarray}
\@par\hangindent 2em if we denote by $({ \mathcal{P}}({ \relax{S}}'),\sqsubseteq)$ the pre-ordered set defined by
\begin{eqnarray}
\forall I,I'\in { \mathcal{P}}({ \relax{S}}'),&& I\sqsubseteq I' \;\;:\Leftrightarrow \;\; \forall \sigma\in I,\exists \sigma'\in I'\;\vert\; \sigma \sqsubseteq_{{}_{{{ \relax{S}}'}}} \sigma'\label{RECDefinitionpreorderPSbar}
\end{eqnarray}
then ${ \mathcal{Q}}({ \relax{S}}')$ is a given sub-poset of $({ \mathcal{P}}({ \relax{S}}'),\sqsubseteq)$ satisfying
\begin{eqnarray}
&&\forall V\subseteq { \relax{S}}',\;\; \widehat{\;V\;}{}^{{}^{{ \relax{S}}'}}\;\;\Rightarrow\;\;V\in  { \mathcal{Q}}({ \relax{S}}').\label{RECQ1}
                                                                                                                                                                                                               
\end{eqnarray}
\@par\hangindent 2em $\star$ is a map from ${ \relax{S}}'\smallsetminus \{\bot_{{}_{ \relax{S}'}}\}$ to ${ \relax{S}}'\smallsetminus \{\bot_{{}_{ \relax{S}'}}\}$ satisfying
\begin{eqnarray}
\forall \sigma\in { \relax{S}}'\smallsetminus \{\bot_{{}_{ \relax{S}'}}\},&& (\sigma^{\star})^{\star}=\sigma, \label{RECinvolutive}\\
\forall \sigma_1,\sigma_2\in { \relax{S}}'\smallsetminus \{\bot_{{}_{ \relax{S}'}}\},&& \sigma_1\sqsubseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}'}}}\sigma_2\;\;\Rightarrow\;\; \sigma_2^\star \sqsubseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}'}}} \sigma_1^\star, \label{RECorderreversing}\\
                                                                                                                                                                          
\forall J\in { \mathcal{Q}}({ \relax{S}}'),\forall \sigma\in { \relax{S}}', & & \{\sigma,\sigma^\star\}\not\sqsubseteq J. \label{RECinconsistent}
                                                                                                                                                                                                
\end{eqnarray}
\@par\hangindent 2em $cl^{{{ \relax{S}}'}}$ is a map defined from ${ \mathcal{P}}({ \relax{S}}')$ to ${ \mathcal{P}}({ \relax{S}}')$ and satisfying 
\begin{eqnarray}
\forall J\in {\mathcal{Q}}({ \relax{S}}'),\;&& cl^{{ \relax{S}}'}(J)\in {\mathcal{Q}}({ \relax{S}}'),\label{basicRECQ}\\
\forall J\in { \mathcal{P}}({ \relax{S}}'),&& J\sqsubseteq cl^{{{ \relax{S}}'}}(J),\label{kuratowski1}\\
\forall J,J'\in { \mathcal{P}}({ \relax{S}}'),&& J\sqsubseteq J' \;\;\Rightarrow\;\;cl^{{{ \relax{S}}'}}(J)\sqsubseteq cl^{{{ \relax{S}}'}}(J'),\label{kuratowski2}\\
\forall J\in { \mathcal{P}}({ \relax{S}}'),&& cl^{{{ \relax{S}}'}}\circ cl^{{{ \relax{S}}'}}(J) = cl^{{{ \relax{S}}'}}(J),\label{kuratowski3}\\
\forall \sigma\in { \relax{S}}',&& cl^{{{ \relax{S}}'}}(\{\sigma\})=\{\sigma\},\\
\forall J\in cl^{{{ \relax{S}}'}}({ \mathcal{Q}}({ \relax{S}}')),\forall \sigma,\sigma'\in J,&& \widehat{\sigma\sigma'}{}^{{}^{{{ \relax{S}}'}}}\;\;\Rightarrow\;\; \sigma=\sigma' ,\label{RECdefJSbar2}\\
\forall J,J'\in { \mathcal{P}}({ \relax{S}}'),&&(\,J\sqsubseteq J'\;\;\textit{\rm and}\;\; J'\in cl^{{{ \relax{S}}'}}({ \mathcal{Q}}({ \relax{S}}'))\,)\;\Rightarrow\; J\in { \mathcal{Q}}({ \relax{S}}').\label{RECQ2}\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;
\end{eqnarray}
\end{itemize}
<!-- end definition-30 -->
<!-- theorem-15: body_md -->
\label{theoremcompletion}
We will assume that $({\relax{S}}',{ \mathcal{Q}}({ \relax{S}}'),cl^{{{ \relax{S}}'}},\star)$ is a real space of states.\\
We define ${ \relax{J}}_{{{ \relax{S}}'}}$ to be the set $cl^{{{ \relax{S}}'}}({ \mathcal{Q}}({ \relax{S}}'))$. The Inf semi-lattice structure being given by ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@RECdefJsqbarJ\endcsname\@firstoftwo{RECdefJsqbarJ}}}). We define the generalized space of effects as in Definition {{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@defgeneralizedeffectspace\endcsname\@firstoftwo{defgeneralizedeffectspace}}} (it is necessary to use the formula for the suprema established in ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@supremaJ\endcsname\@firstoftwo{supremaJ}}}) ). The reduced space of effects is defined as in ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@reducedspaceofeffectsprime\endcsname\@firstoftwo{reducedspaceofeffectsprime}}}). Then, we define an evaluation map ${ \epsilon}^{{ \relax{J}}_{{{ \relax{S}}'}}}$ on the whole ${ \relax{J}}_{{{ \relax{S}}'}}$ as in ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@defepsilonS\endcsname\@firstoftwo{defepsilonS}}}).                                                                                                                                                                     
\\
As a result, ${ \relax{J}}_{{{ \relax{S}}'}}$ is a well defined space of states which admits the real structure $({{{ \relax{S}}'}},\star)$. The elements of ${{{ \relax{S}}'}}$ are the real states, whereas the elements of 
  ${ \relax{J}}_{{{ \relax{S}}'}}\smallsetminus {{{ \relax{S}}'}}$ are the hidden states.
<!-- end theorem-15 -->
<!-- theorem-16: body_md -->
\label{completionsimplex}
Let $({\relax{S}}',{ \mathcal{Q}}({ \relax{S}}'),cl^{{{ \relax{S}}'}},\star)$ be a real space of states. We will assume that ${\relax{S}}'$ is a simplex space of states. Then, ${ \relax{J}}_{{{ \relax{S}}'}}={\relax{S}}'$.
<!-- end theorem-16 -->
<!-- proof-39: body_md -->
Let us begin by recalling that, as long as ${\relax{S}}'$ is a simplex space of states, the star map $\star$ is necessarily given by ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@starsimplex\endcsname\@firstoftwo{starsimplex}}}).\\
Let us consider two elements $\sigma$ and $\sigma'$ in ${\relax{S}}'$ such that $\neg \;\widehat{\sigma \sigma'}{}^{{}^{{\relax{S}}'}}$.  Let us suppose that $\{\sigma,\sigma'\}\in { \mathcal{Q}}({ \relax{S}}')$.\\
As long as ${\relax{S}}'$ is a simplex, we must necessarily have $\sigma^\star \sqsubseteq_{{}_{{\relax{S}}'}} \sigma'$, i.e. $\{\sigma,\sigma^\star\}\sqsubseteq \{\sigma,\sigma'\}$.  As a consequence, we have $\{\sigma,\sigma^\star\}\in { \mathcal{Q}}({ \relax{S}}')$ which contradicts the condition ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@RECinconsistent\endcsname\@firstoftwo{RECinconsistent}}}). \\ 
As a conclusion, if ${\relax{S}}'$ is a simplex space of states, then ${ \relax{J}}_{{{ \relax{S}}'}}\smallsetminus {\relax{S}}'$ is empty.
<!-- end proof-39 -->
<!-- definition-31: body_md -->
We will consider a map from ${\mathcal{P}}({ \relax{S}}')$ to ${\mathcal{P}}({ \relax{S}}')$ denoted ${\relax{c}}^{{ \relax{S}}'}$ and defined by
\begin{eqnarray}
{\relax{c}}^{{ \relax{S}}'}(U)&:=&Max \{\,\bigsqcup{}^{{}^{{ \relax{S}}'}} V\;\vert\; V\sqsubseteq U\;\;\textit{\rm and}\;\; \widehat{\;V\;}{}^{{}^{{ \relax{S}}'}}\,\}\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\label{definitioncompleterealspaceofstates2}
\end{eqnarray}
(here, we are directly inspired by the Lemma {{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@lemmatricky\endcsname\@firstoftwo{lemmatricky}}}).
<!-- end definition-31 -->
<!-- lemma-31: body_md -->
${\relax{c}}^{{ \relax{S}}'}$ is {\em a pre-closure}. In other words,
\begin{eqnarray}
\forall U\in {\mathcal{P}}({ \relax{S}}'),\;&& U\sqsubseteq {\relax{c}}^{{ \relax{S}}'}(U),\label{propB3}\\
\forall U_1,U_2\in {\mathcal{P}}({ \relax{S}}'),\;&& U_1\sqsubseteq U_2\;\;\Rightarrow\;\; {\relax{c}}^{{ \relax{S}}'}(U_1)\sqsubseteq {\relax{c}}^{{ \relax{S}}'}(U_2).\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\label{propB4}
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end lemma-31 -->
<!-- proof-40: body_md -->
The property ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@propB3\endcsname\@firstoftwo{propB3}}}) is easily deduced from the definition ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@definitioncompleterealspaceofstates2\endcsname\@firstoftwo{definitioncompleterealspaceofstates2}}}). Indeed, we have, for any $\sigma\in U$, $\{\sigma\}\sqsubseteq U$ and $\widehat{\;\{\sigma\}\;}{}^{{}^{{ \relax{S}}'}}$ and $(\bigsqcup{}^{{}^{{ \relax{S}}'}}\{\sigma\})=\sigma$. As a result, we have $\sigma \in \{\,\bigsqcup{}^{{}^{{ \relax{S}}'}} V\;\vert\; V\sqsubseteq U\;\;\textit{\rm and}\;\; \widehat{\;V\;}{}^{{}^{{ \relax{S}}'}}\,\}$ and then $\{\sigma\}\sqsubseteq {\relax{c}}^{{ \relax{S}}'}(U)$. As a final conclusion, we obtain $U\sqsubseteq {\relax{c}}^{{ \relax{S}}'}(U)$. \\
Concerning the property ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@propB4\endcsname\@firstoftwo{propB4}}}), we have the following analysis. For any $\sigma\in \{\,\bigsqcup{}^{{}^{{ \relax{S}}'}} V\;\vert\; V\sqsubseteq U_1\;\;\textit{\rm and}\;\; \widehat{\;V\;}{}^{{}^{{ \relax{S}}'}}\,\}$ there exists $V\sqsubseteq U_1$ such that $\sigma=\bigsqcup{}^{{}^{{ \relax{S}}'}} V$. But $U_1\sqsubseteq U_2$ implies $V\sqsubseteq U_2$ and then $\sigma\in \{\,\bigsqcup{}^{{}^{{ \relax{S}}'}} V\;\vert\; V\sqsubseteq U_2\;\;\textit{\rm and}\;\; \widehat{\;V\;}{}^{{}^{{ \relax{S}}'}}\,\}$. As a consequence, we have $\{\sigma\}\sqsubseteq {\relax{c}}^{{ \relax{S}}'}(U_2)$, and then $\{\,\bigsqcup{}^{{}^{{ \relax{S}}'}} V\;\vert\; V\sqsubseteq U_1\;\;\textit{\rm and}\;\; \widehat{\;V\;}{}^{{}^{{ \relax{S}}'}}\,\}\sqsubseteq {\relax{c}}^{{ \relax{S}}'}(U_2)$. As a result, we obtain ${\relax{c}}^{{ \relax{S}}'}(U_1)\sqsubseteq {\relax{c}}^{{ \relax{S}}'}(U_2)$. 
This concludes the proof.
<!-- end proof-40 -->
<!-- remark-3: body_md -->
We have then proved that ${\relax{c}}^{{ \relax{S}}'}$ is {\em a pre-closure}. However, for some ${ \relax{S}}'$ it appears that ${\relax{c}}^{{ \relax{S}}'}$ is not a closure. In other words,
\begin{eqnarray}
\exists U\in {\mathcal{P}}({ \relax{S}}')&\vert & {\relax{c}}^{{ \relax{S}}'}\circ {\relax{c}}^{{ \relax{S}}'}(U)\not= {\relax{c}}^{{ \relax{S}}'}(U),\label{propB5}
\end{eqnarray}
Let us consider the following case for the Inf semi-lattice ${ \relax{S}}'$ :
\begin{eqnarray}
&&\begin{tikzpicture}
  \node (a) at (-0.5,1) {$w$};
  \node (b) at (0,2) {$x$};
  \node (c) at (0.5,1) {$z$};
  \node (d) at (-1,0) {$u_{1}$};
  \node (e) at (0,0) {$u_{3}$};
  \node (f) at (1,0) {$u_{2}$};
  \node (g) at (-2,0) {$v_{1}$};
  \node (h) at (2,0) {$v_{2}$};
  \node (i) at (0,1) {$y$};
  \node (min) at (0,-1) {$\bot$};
  \draw (min) -- (d) -- (a) (min) -- (g) (min) -- (h) (d) -- (i) -- (f) 
  (e) -- (min) -- (f) -- (c) (a) -- (g) (c) -- (h)
  (g) -- (b) (h) -- (b);
  \draw[preaction={draw=white, -,line width=4pt}] (a) -- (e) -- (c);
\end{tikzpicture} 
\end{eqnarray}
If we choose $U:=\{u_1,u_2,u_3\}$ we observe that ${\relax{c}}^{{ \relax{S}}'}(U)=\{w,z,y\}$, but we have ${\relax{c}}^{{ \relax{S}}'}\circ {\relax{c}}^{{ \relax{S}}'} (U)=\{w,z,y,x\}$.
<!-- end remark-3 -->
<!-- lemma-32: body_md -->
We have
\begin{eqnarray}
\forall U\in {\mathcal{P}}({ \relax{S}}')&\vert & {\relax{c}}^{{ \relax{S}}'}\circ {\relax{c}}^{{ \relax{S}}'}(U)\sqsupseteq {\relax{c}}^{{ \relax{S}}'}(U),\label{propB5bis}
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end lemma-32 -->
<!-- proof-41: body_md -->
Direct consequence of properties ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@propB3\endcsname\@firstoftwo{propB3}}}) and ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@propB4\endcsname\@firstoftwo{propB4}}}).
<!-- end proof-41 -->
<!-- definition-32: body_md -->
We define the map $cl_c^{{ \relax{S}}'}$ from ${\mathcal{P}}({ \relax{S}}')$ to ${\mathcal{P}}({ \relax{S}}')$ by
\begin{eqnarray}
\forall U\in {\mathcal{P}}({ \relax{S}}'),\;&& cl_c^{{ \relax{S}}'}(U) := \bigsqcup{}_{n\geq 1} ({\relax{c}}^{{ \relax{S}}'})^{\circ n}(U)\label{definitioncompleterealspaceofstates3}
\end{eqnarray}
(we have denoted $({\relax{c}}^{{ \relax{S}}'})^{\circ n}$ the n-th composition by ${\relax{c}}^{{ \relax{S}}'}$).
<!-- end definition-32 -->
<!-- lemma-33: body_md -->
$cl_c^{{ \relax{S}}'}$ satisfies
\begin{eqnarray}
\forall U\in {\mathcal{P}}({ \relax{S}}'),\;&& U\sqsubseteq cl_c^{{ \relax{S}}'}(U),\label{propB3c}\\
\forall U_1,U_2\in {\mathcal{P}}({ \relax{S}}'),\;&& U_1\sqsubseteq U_2\;\;\Rightarrow\;\; cl_c^{{ \relax{S}}'}(U_1)\sqsubseteq cl_c^{{ \relax{S}}'}(U_2).\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\label{propB4c}
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end lemma-33 -->
<!-- proof-42: body_md -->
The properties ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@propB3c\endcsname\@firstoftwo{propB3c}}}) ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@propB4c\endcsname\@firstoftwo{propB4c}}}) are direct consequences of the properties ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@propB3\endcsname\@firstoftwo{propB3}}}) ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@propB4\endcsname\@firstoftwo{propB4}}}).
<!-- end proof-42 -->
<!-- theorem-17: body_md -->
Let us now suppose that ${ \relax{S}}'$ satisfies the {\em Finite Rank Condition} (Definition {{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@FiniteRankCondition\endcsname\@firstoftwo{FiniteRankCondition}}}).\\
Then, $cl_c^{{ \relax{S}}'}$ satisfies the idempotency property
\begin{eqnarray}
\forall U\subseteq { \relax{S}}',\;&& cl_c^{{ \relax{S}}'}\circ cl_c^{{ \relax{S}}'}(U)= cl_c^{{ \relax{S}}'}(U).\label{propB5c}
\end{eqnarray}
and the following algebraicity property 
\begin{eqnarray}
\hspace{-0.5cm}\forall U\subseteq { \relax{S}}', \forall \{\sigma\}\sqsubseteq cl_c^{{ \relax{S}}'}(U),\;\exists \;\textit{\rm $V$ finite subset of ${ \relax{S}}'$ with $V\sqsubseteq U$ such that}\; \{\sigma\}\sqsubseteq cl_c^{{ \relax{S}}'}(V).\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\label{algebraicclosure}
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end theorem-17 -->
<!-- proof-43: body_md -->
First of all, by choosing $U$ to be a chain in ${ \relax{S}}'$ (explicitly $U:=\{\,u_i\;\vert\; i\geq 1\,\}$ with $u_i\sqsubseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}'}}u_j$ for $i\leq j$) in ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@finiterank\endcsname\@firstoftwo{finiterank}}}), we note that the Finite Rank Condition ensures that the chain $U$ is stabilizing, i.e.  $\exists n\in \mathbb{N}$ with $u_n=u_k$ for any $k\geq n$ (this means that ${ \relax{S}}'$ satisfies the {\em Ascending Chain Condition}).\\
Secondly we note that, if ${ \relax{S}}'$ satisfies the Finite Rank Condition, we then have the following {\em algebraicity} property for ${\relax{c}}^{{ \relax{S}}'}$ :
\begin{eqnarray}
\hspace{-0.5cm}\forall U\subseteq { \relax{S}}', \forall \{\sigma\}\sqsubseteq {\relax{c}}^{{ \relax{S}}'}(U),\;\exists \;\textit{\rm $V$ finite subset of ${ \relax{S}}'$ with $V\sqsubseteq U$ such that}\; \{\sigma\}\sqsubseteq {\relax{c}}^{{ \relax{S}}'}(V).\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\label{algebraicpreclosure}
\end{eqnarray}
We now intent to deduce a similar property for $cl_c^{{ \relax{S}}'}$. \\
Let us consider $\sigma\in { \relax{S}}'$ such that $\{\sigma\}\sqsubseteq cl_c^{{ \relax{S}}'}(U)$. Using the Ascending Chain Condition deduced from the Finite Rank Condition, and the fact that the sequence $({\relax{c}}^{{ \relax{S}}'})^{\circ n}(U)$ forms a nest for $\sqsubseteq$, we deduce that there must exist an integer $n$ such that $\{\sigma\}\sqsubseteq ({\relax{c}}^{{ \relax{S}}'})^{\circ n}(U)$.  From ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@algebraicpreclosure\endcsname\@firstoftwo{algebraicpreclosure}}}), we then deduce that there exists $V$ finite subset of ${ \relax{S}}'$ with $V\sqsubseteq U$ such that $\{\sigma\}\sqsubseteq ({\relax{c}}^{{ \relax{S}}'})^{\circ n}(V)$. Therefore, we obtain $\{\sigma\}\sqsubseteq \bigsqcup{}_{n\geq 1} ({\relax{c}}^{{ \relax{S}}'})^{\circ n}(V)=cl_c^{{ \relax{S}}'}(V)$. As a conclusion, we have obtained ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@algebraicclosure\endcsname\@firstoftwo{algebraicclosure}}}).\\
Let us now come back to the proof of property ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@propB5c\endcsname\@firstoftwo{propB5c}}}).\\
Let us consider $\sigma\in { \relax{S}}'$ such that $\{\sigma\}\sqsubseteq cl_c^{{ \relax{S}}'}\circ cl_c^{{ \relax{S}}'}(U)$. Using the already proved algebraicity property ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@algebraicclosure\endcsname\@firstoftwo{algebraicclosure}}}), we deduce that there exists a finite subset of ${ \relax{S}}'$ denoted $V$ such that $V\sqsubseteq cl_c^{{ \relax{S}}'}(U)$ and satisfying $\{\sigma\}\sqsubseteq cl_c^{{ \relax{S}}'}(V)$. Then, since $V$ is finite, there must exist an integer $k$ such that $V\sqsubseteq ({\relax{c}}^{{ \relax{S}}'})^{\circ k}(U)$. Therefore, we have $ cl_c^{{ \relax{S}}'}(V) = \bigsqcup{}_{n\geq 1} ({\relax{c}}^{{ \relax{S}}'})^{\circ n}(V) \sqsubseteq \bigsqcup{}_{n\geq 1} ({\relax{c}}^{{ \relax{S}}'})^{\circ n}(({\relax{c}}^{{ \relax{S}}'})^{\circ k}(U))=\bigsqcup{}_{n\geq 1} ({\relax{c}}^{{ \relax{S}}'})^{\circ (n+k)}(U)\sqsubseteq \bigsqcup{}_{n\geq 1} ({\relax{c}}^{{ \relax{S}}'})^{\circ n}(U)$. As a result, we have obtained $\{\sigma\}\sqsubseteq \bigsqcup{}_{n\geq 1} ({\relax{c}}^{{ \relax{S}}'})^{\circ n}(U)=cl_c^{{ \relax{S}}'}(U)$.                                                           
We have then obtained the inequality 
\begin{eqnarray}  
\forall U\subseteq { \relax{S}}',\;&& cl_c^{{ \relax{S}}'}\circ cl_c^{{ \relax{S}}'}(U) \sqsubseteq cl_c^{{ \relax{S}}'}(U).\label{propB5cfirst}
\end{eqnarray}
The inequality
\begin{eqnarray}
\forall U\subseteq { \relax{S}}',\;&& cl_c^{{ \relax{S}}'}\circ cl_c^{{ \relax{S}}'}(U) \sqsupseteq cl_c^{{ \relax{S}}'}(U).\label{propB5csecond}
\end{eqnarray}
is a direct consequence of properties ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@propB3c\endcsname\@firstoftwo{propB3c}}}) and ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@propB4c\endcsname\@firstoftwo{propB4c}}}).
<!-- end proof-43 -->
<!-- remark-4: body_md -->
We are convinced that the Finite Rank Condition imposed as a prerequisite for the previous theorem could be alleged. This is not the purpose of the present paper to enter into this detail, and we let this point for a future study.
<!-- end remark-4 -->
<!-- definition-33: body_md -->
\label{definitioncompleterealspaceofstatesQc}
We define the following subsets of ${ \mathcal{P}}({ \relax{S}}')$ :
\begin{eqnarray}
{\mathcal{K}}({ \relax{S}}')&:=&\{\,U\subseteq { \relax{S}}'\smallsetminus \{\bot_{{}_{ \relax{S}'}}\} \;\vert\; \forall \sigma,\sigma'\in U,\;\sigma^\star \not\sqsubseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}'}}\sigma'
\,\}\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\label{definitioncompleterealspaceofstates1propk}\\
{\mathcal{Q}}_c({ \relax{S}}')&:=&\{\,U\subseteq { \relax{S}}'\smallsetminus \{\bot_{{}_{ \relax{S}'}}\} \;\vert\; cl_c^{{ \relax{S}}'}(U)\in {\mathcal{K}}({ \relax{S}}')
\,\}\;\cup\; \{\bot_{{}_{ \relax{S}'}}\}
\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\label{definitioncompleterealspaceofstates1prop}
\end{eqnarray}
and
\begin{eqnarray}
&& { \relax{J}}^c_{{{ \relax{S}}'}}:=cl_c^{{{ \relax{S}}'}}({ \mathcal{Q}}_c({ \relax{S}}')).\label{definitioncompleterealspaceofstates1propJc}
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end definition-33 -->
<!-- lemma-34: body_md -->
${\mathcal{Q}}_c({ \relax{S}}')$ satisfies the property : 
\begin{eqnarray}
\forall K,K'\subseteq { \relax{S}}'\smallsetminus \{\bot_{{}_{ \relax{S}'}}\}, \;\;\;\;(\,K\sqsubseteq K'\;\;\textit{\rm and}\;\;K'\in {\mathcal{Q}}_c({ \relax{S}}')\,) &\Rightarrow & K\in {\mathcal{Q}}_c({ \relax{S}}').\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\label{Qlowersubset}
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end lemma-34 -->
<!-- proof-44: body_md -->
First of all, we recall the property : 
\begin{eqnarray}
\forall K,K'\subseteq { \relax{S}}'\smallsetminus \{\bot_{{}_{ \relax{S}'}}\}, \;\;\;\;(\,K\sqsubseteq K'\;\;\textit{\rm and}\;\;K'\in {\mathcal{K}}({ \relax{S}}')\,) &\Rightarrow & K\in {\mathcal{K}}({ \relax{S}}').\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\label{Klowersubset}
\end{eqnarray}
Indeed, let us consider $ K,K'\subseteq { \relax{S}}'\smallsetminus \{\bot_{{}_{ \relax{S}'}}\}$ such that $K\sqsubseteq K'$ and $K'\in {\mathcal{K}}({ \relax{S}}')$.
For any $\sigma,\sigma'\in K$ there exists $\kappa,\kappa'\in K'$ such that $\sigma\sqsubseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}'}}}\kappa$ and $\sigma'\sqsubseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}'}}}\kappa'$. By assumption we have $\kappa^\star \not\sqsubseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}'}}\kappa'$, and we then deduce $\sigma^\star \not\sqsubseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}'}}\sigma'$. This concludes the proof of ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@Klowersubset\endcsname\@firstoftwo{Klowersubset}}}).\\
Now, let us consider $K,K'\subseteq { \relax{S}}'\smallsetminus \{\bot_{{}_{ \relax{S}'}}\}$, such that $K\sqsubseteq K'$ and $K'\in {\mathcal{Q}}_c({ \relax{S}}')$. We have, using monotonicity of $cl_c^{{ \relax{S}}'}$, the property $cl_c^{{ \relax{S}}'}(K)\sqsubseteq cl_c^{{ \relax{S}}'}(K')$. And $K'\in {\mathcal{Q}}_c({ \relax{S}}')$ means $cl_c^{{ \relax{S}}'}(K')\in {\mathcal{K}}({ \relax{S}}')$. Now, we use ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@Klowersubset\endcsname\@firstoftwo{Klowersubset}}}) to deduce that $cl_c^{{ \relax{S}}'}(K)\in {\mathcal{K}}({ \relax{S}}')$, i.e.  $K\in {\mathcal{Q}}_c({ \relax{S}}')$. This concludes the proof.
<!-- end proof-44 -->
<!-- lemma-35: body_md -->
\begin{eqnarray}
\forall K\in {\mathcal{Q}}_c({ \relax{S}}'),\;&& cl_c^{{ \relax{S}}'}(K)\in {\mathcal{Q}}_c({ \relax{S}}').\label{propB2}
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end lemma-35 -->
<!-- proof-45: body_md -->
Let us consider $K\in {\mathcal{Q}}_c({ \relax{S}}')$.  By definition, we have $cl_c^{{ \relax{S}}'}(K)\in {\mathcal{K}}({ \relax{S}}')$ and then, using the idempotency of $cl_c^{{ \relax{S}}'}$, we have $cl_c^{{ \relax{S}}'}(cl_c^{{ \relax{S}}'}(K))=cl_c^{{ \relax{S}}'}(K)\in {\mathcal{K}}({ \relax{S}}')$. In other words, $cl_c^{{ \relax{S}}'}(K)\in {\mathcal{Q}}_c({ \relax{S}}')$.
<!-- end proof-45 -->
<!-- lemma-36: body_md -->
\begin{eqnarray}
\hspace{-1cm}\forall U\in cl_c^{{{ \relax{S}}'}}({ \mathcal{Q}}_c({ \relax{S}}')),\forall \sigma_1,\sigma_2\in U,&& \widehat{\sigma_1\sigma_2}{}^{{}^{{{ \relax{S}}'}}}\;\;\Rightarrow\;\; \sigma_1=\sigma_2.\label{propB1}
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end lemma-36 -->
<!-- proof-46: body_md -->
It suffices to prove the following simpler property :
\begin{eqnarray}
\hspace{-1cm}\forall U\in {\relax{c}}^{{{ \relax{S}}'}}({ \mathcal{Q}}_c({ \relax{S}}')),\forall \sigma_1,\sigma_2\in U,&& \widehat{\sigma_1\sigma_2}{}^{{}^{{{ \relax{S}}'}}}\;\;\Rightarrow\;\; \sigma_1=\sigma_2.
\end{eqnarray}
Let us consider two elements $\sigma,\sigma'\in {\relax{c}}^{{{ \relax{S}}'}}(U)$. There exists $V,V'\sqsubseteq U$ which are maximal for $\sqsubseteq$ among subsets of $U$ satisfying $\widehat{\;V\;}{}^{{}^{{ \relax{S}}'}}$ and $\widehat{\;V'\;}{}^{{}^{{ \relax{S}}'}}$ and such that $\sigma=\bigsqcup{}^{{}^{{ \relax{S}}'}} V$ and $\sigma'=\bigsqcup{}^{{}^{{ \relax{S}}'}} V'$. If we had $\widehat{\;\sigma\sigma'\;}{}^{{}^{{ \relax{S}}'}}$, we would have $\widehat{\;V\cup V'\;}{}^{{}^{{ \relax{S}}'}}$. This point contradicts the assumption of maximality for $V$ and $V'$. This concludes the proof.
<!-- end proof-46 -->
<!-- lemma-37: body_md -->
${\mathcal{Q}}_c({ \relax{S}}')$ satisfies
\begin{eqnarray}
\forall U\subseteq { \relax{S}}',&& \widehat{\;U\;}{}^{{}^{{ \relax{S}'}}}\;\;\Rightarrow\;\; U\in { \mathcal{Q}}_c({ \relax{S}}'),\label{propA1}
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end lemma-37 -->
<!-- proof-47: body_md -->
Let us consider $U\subseteq { \relax{S}}'$ such that $\widehat{\;U\;}{}^{{}^{{ \relax{S}'}}}$. In order to check   the property ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@propA1\endcsname\@firstoftwo{propA1}}}),  it suffices to note that $cl_c^{{ \relax{S}}'}(U)=\{\bigsqcup{}^{{}^{{ \relax{S}}'}}U\}$ and to remark that any singleton associated to an element of ${ \relax{S}}'$ is necessarily in ${\mathcal{K}}({ \relax{S}}')$.
<!-- end proof-47 -->
<!-- lemma-38: body_md -->
${\mathcal{Q}}_c({ \relax{S}}')$ satisfies
\begin{eqnarray}
\forall J\in { \mathcal{Q}}_c({ \relax{S}}'),\forall \sigma\in { \relax{S}}'\smallsetminus \{\bot_{{}_{ \relax{S}'}}\}, & & \{\sigma,\sigma^\star\}\not\sqsubseteq J,\label{propA2}
\end{eqnarray}
In other words, we have
\begin{eqnarray}
{ \mathcal{Q}}_c({ \relax{S}}') & \subseteq & { \mathcal{K}}({ \relax{S}}').
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end lemma-38 -->
<!-- proof-48: body_md -->
Let us consider $J\in { \mathcal{Q}}_c({ \relax{S}}')$ and let us suppose that there exists $\sigma\in { \relax{S}}'\smallsetminus \{\bot_{{}_{ \relax{S}'}}\}$ such that $\{\sigma,\sigma^\star\}\sqsubseteq J$. Then, let us introduce $J':=cl_c^{{ \relax{S}}'}(J)$. Due to the basic properties of the closure $cl_c^{{ \relax{S}}'}$, we know that $J'$ satisfies $J\sqsubseteq J'$. Moreover, from $J\in { \mathcal{Q}}_c({ \relax{S}}')$, we deduce that $J'\in {\mathcal{K}}({ \relax{S}}')$. Now, we use ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@Klowersubset\endcsname\@firstoftwo{Klowersubset}}}) to conclude that $J\in {\mathcal{K}}({ \relax{S}}')$. This result contradicts the existence of $\sigma\in { \relax{S}}'\smallsetminus \{\bot_{{}_{ \relax{S}'}}\}$ such that $\{\sigma,\sigma^\star\}\sqsubseteq J$. This concludes the proof of ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@propA2\endcsname\@firstoftwo{propA2}}}).
<!-- end proof-48 -->
<!-- lemma-39: body_md -->
\label{lemmasignifySinQ}
\begin{eqnarray}
  S\in {\mathcal{Q}}_c({ \relax{S}}') &\Leftrightarrow & \forall \alpha,\beta\in cl_c^{{{ \relax{S}}'}}(S),\;\alpha^\star\not\sqsubseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}'}}\beta.
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end lemma-39 -->
<!-- proof-49: body_md -->
Trivial rewriting of the definition of ${\mathcal{Q}}_c({ \relax{S}}')$.
<!-- end proof-49 -->
<!-- theorem-18: body_md -->
$({\relax{S}}',{ \mathcal{Q}}_c({ \relax{S}}'),cl_c^{{{ \relax{S}}'}},\star)$ satisfies the axiomatic of a real space of states.
<!-- end theorem-18 -->
<!-- proof-50: body_md -->
This result summarizes the previous lemmas.
<!-- end proof-50 -->
<!-- definition-34: body_md -->
The real space of states ${ \relax{J}}^c_{{{ \relax{S}}'}}$ (defined according to Definition {{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@definitioncompleterealspaceofstatesQc\endcsname\@firstoftwo{definitioncompleterealspaceofstatesQc}}}) is called {\em the maximal ontic completion} of $({ \relax{S}}',\star)$. \\
In the following, we will denote $({\relax{S}}',{ \mathcal{Q}}_c({ \relax{S}}'),cl_c^{{{ \relax{S}}'}},\star)$ shortly by $(\!({\relax{S}}',\star)\!)_c$.
<!-- end definition-34 -->
<!-- definition-35: body_md -->
A subset $U$ of ${\relax{S}}'$ is said to be {\em admissible}                                                             
 iff $U$ is an element of ${ \mathcal{Q}}_c({ \relax{S}}')$.
<!-- end definition-35 -->
<!-- definition-36: body_md -->
We will say that {\em the ontic completion of $({\relax{S}}',\star)$ 
is complete} iff we have
 \begin{eqnarray}
 {\mathcal{Q}}_c({ \relax{S}}') &\supseteq & \widehat{\mathcal{K}}({ \relax{S}}')
\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\nonumber\\
 \widehat{\mathcal{K}}({ \relax{S}}') &:= & \{\,U\subseteq { \relax{S}}'\smallsetminus \{\bot_{{}_{ \relax{S}'}}\} \;\vert\; \forall \sigma,\sigma'\in U,\;\sigma^\star \not\sqsubseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}'}}\sigma'
\;\textit{\rm and}\;\sigma\not=\sigma'\;\Rightarrow\;\neg\,\widehat{\sigma\,\sigma'}{}^{{}^{{ \relax{S}}'}}
\,\}\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;
\label{propertyadmitscopletionmaximal}
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end definition-36 -->
<!-- theorem-19: body_md -->
\label{theoremNOcompleteontic}
We will assume the following basic property for ${\relax{S}}'$ : 
\begin{eqnarray}
\sigma,\sigma'\in {{\relax{S}}'}{}^{{}^{pure}},&&(\sigma\sqcap_{{}_{{{\relax{S}}'}}}\sigma')\raisebox{1.3ex}{\,\rotatebox{180}{$\sqsupseteq$}}\,_{{}_{{{\relax{S}}'}}}\sigma,\sigma'.\label{assumedcovering}
\end{eqnarray}
Let us now consider two distinct pure states $ \sigma_1,\sigma_2\in {{\relax{S}}'}{}^{{}^{pure}}$ such that $(\sigma_1\sqcap_{{}_{{{\relax{S}}'}}}\sigma_2)\not= \bot_{{}_{{{\relax{S}}'}}}$ and $\sigma_1^\star \not\sqsubseteq_{{}_{{{\relax{S}}'}}}\sigma_2$, we have then $\{\sigma_1,\sigma_2\}\in \widehat{\mathcal{K}}({{\relax{S}}'})$ but $cl_c^{{{\relax{S}}'}}(\{\sigma_1,\sigma_2\})\notin {\mathcal{K}}({{\relax{S}}'})$, i.e. $\{\sigma_1,\sigma_2\}\notin {\mathcal{Q}}_c({{\relax{S}}'})$. \\
As a conclusion, if ${\relax{S}}'$ satisfies the assumed property ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@assumedcovering\endcsname\@firstoftwo{assumedcovering}}}) and if there exists $\sigma_1,\sigma_2\in {{\relax{S}}'}{}^{{}^{pure}}$ such that $(\sigma_1\sqcap_{{}_{{{\relax{S}}'}}}\sigma_2)\not= \bot_{{}_{{{\relax{S}}'}}}$, then the ontic completion of $({{\relax{S}}'},\star)$ cannot be complete.
<!-- end theorem-19 -->
<!-- proof-51: body_md -->
Let us fix $\sigma_1,\sigma_2$ in ${{\relax{S}}'}{}^{{}^{pure}}$ such that $\sigma_1^\star \not\sqsubseteq_{{}_{{{\relax{S}}'}}}\sigma_2$.\\
First of all, we note that, as long as $(\sigma_1\sqcap_{{}_{{{\relax{S}}'}}}\sigma_2)\not= \bot_{{}_{{{\relax{S}}'}}}$ we know that there exists $\sigma_3$ in ${{\relax{S}}'}{}^{{}^{pure}}$ such that $\sigma_1^\star \sqsubseteq_{{}_{{{\relax{S}}'}}}\sigma_3$ and $(\sigma_1\sqcap_{{}_{{{\relax{S}}'}}}\sigma_2)\not\sqsubseteq_{{}_{{{\relax{S}}'}}}\sigma_3$. Indeed, if it was not the case we would have $\bot_{{}_{{{\relax{S}}'}}}\not=(\sigma_1\sqcap_{{}_{{{\relax{S}}'}}}\sigma_2)\sqsubseteq_{{}_{{{\relax{S}}'}}}(\bigsqcap_{\sigma_3\in \underline{\sigma_1^\star}_{{}_{{\relax{S}}'}}}\sigma_3)=\sigma_1^\star$ and then $(\sigma_1\sqcap_{{}_{{{\relax{S}}'}}}\sigma_2)=\sigma_1^\star$ which implies $\sigma_1\sqsupseteq_{{}_{{{\relax{S}}'}}}\sigma_1^\star$ which is false. As a conclusion, 
\begin{eqnarray}
\exists \sigma_3\in {{\relax{S}}'}{}^{{}^{pure}}\;\vert\; \sigma_1^\star \sqsubseteq_{{}_{{{\relax{S}}'}}}\sigma_3\;\textit{\rm and}\; (\sigma_1\sqcap_{{}_{{{\relax{S}}'}}}\sigma_2)\not\sqsubseteq_{{}_{{{\relax{S}}'}}}\sigma_3.
\end{eqnarray}
We have obviously the same result if we replace $\sigma_1$ by $\sigma_2$.\\
Let us now use the assumed property satisfied by ${{\relax{S}}'}$.\\
We have $(\sigma_1\sqcap_{{}_{{{\relax{S}}'}}}\sigma_3)\raisebox{1.3ex}{\,\rotatebox{180}{$\sqsupseteq$}}\,_{{}_{{{\relax{S}}'}}}\sigma_3,\sigma_1$ and $(\sigma_2\sqcap_{{}_{{{\relax{S}}'}}}\sigma_3)\raisebox{1.3ex}{\,\rotatebox{180}{$\sqsupseteq$}}\,_{{}_{{{\relax{S}}'}}}\sigma_3,\sigma_2$. We have then to distinguish the following two options : (1) $(\sigma_1\sqcap_{{}_{{{\relax{S}}'}}}\sigma_3)\sqcup_{{}_{{{\relax{S}}'}}}(\sigma_2\sqcap_{{}_{{{\relax{S}}'}}}\sigma_3)=(\sigma_1\sqcap_{{}_{{{\relax{S}}'}}}\sigma_3)=(\sigma_2\sqcap_{{}_{{{\relax{S}}'}}}\sigma_3)$, or (2) $(\sigma_1\sqcap_{{}_{{{\relax{S}}'}}}\sigma_3)\sqcup_{{}_{{{\relax{S}}'}}}(\sigma_2\sqcap_{{}_{{{\relax{S}}'}}}\sigma_3)=\sigma_3$.  Let us now show that the first option is excluded.  We have necessarily $\sigma_1\sqcap_{{}_{{{\relax{S}}'}}}\sigma_2\sqcap_{{}_{{{\relax{S}}'}}}\sigma_3 \sqsubseteq_{{}_{{{\relax{S}}'}}}\sigma_1\sqcap_{{}_{{{\relax{S}}'}}}\sigma_2\sqsubset_{{}_{{{\relax{S}}'}}}\sigma_1$. Using $(\sigma_1\sqcap_{{}_{{{\relax{S}}'}}}\sigma_3)=(\sigma_2\sqcap_{{}_{{{\relax{S}}'}}}\sigma_3)$ and $\sigma_1\sqcap_{{}_{{{\relax{S}}'}}}\sigma_3\raisebox{1.3ex}{\,\rotatebox{180}{$\sqsupseteq$}}\,_{{}_{{{\relax{S}}'}}}\sigma_1$ we then deduce that $\sigma_1\sqcap_{{}_{{{\relax{S}}'}}}\sigma_2=\sigma_1\sqcap_{{}_{{{\relax{S}}'}}}\sigma_3$, and then $\sigma_1\sqcap_{{}_{{{\relax{S}}'}}}\sigma_2\sqsubseteq_{{}_{{{\relax{S}}'}}}\sigma_3$, which contradicts the assumption on $\sigma_3$.\\
We have then obtained the necessary condition : $(\sigma_1\sqcap_{{}_{{{\relax{S}}'}}}\sigma_3)\sqcup_{{}_{{{\relax{S}}'}}}(\sigma_2\sqcap_{{}_{{{\relax{S}}'}}}\sigma_3)=\sigma_3$.  As a consequence, we deduce
\begin{eqnarray}
\{\sigma_1,\sigma_2,\sigma_3\} &\sqsubseteq & Max \{\,\bigsqcup{}^{{}^{{{\relax{S}}'}}} V\;\vert\; V\sqsubseteq \{\sigma_1,\sigma_2\}\;\;\textit{\rm and}\;\; \widehat{\;V\;}{}^{{}^{{{\relax{S}}'}}}\,\}={\relax{c}}^{{{\relax{S}}'}}(\{\sigma_1,\sigma_2\})\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\\
&\sqsubseteq & cl_c^{{{\relax{S}}'}}(\{\sigma_1,\sigma_2\})
\end{eqnarray}
But now we recall that ($\sigma_1^\star \sqsubseteq_{{}_{{{\relax{S}}'}}}\sigma_3$ or $\sigma_2^\star \sqsubseteq_{{}_{{{\relax{S}}'}}}\sigma_3$) to conclude that $cl_c^{{{\relax{S}}'}}(\{\sigma_1,\sigma_2\})\notin {\mathcal{K}}({{\relax{S}}'})$. Noting that, by assumption, we have $\{\sigma_1,\sigma_2\}\in \widehat{\mathcal{K}}({{\relax{S}}'})$ we deduce that the ontic completion of $({{\relax{S}}'},\star)$ cannot be complete.
<!-- end proof-51 -->
<!-- definition-37: body_md -->
\label{definnubullet}
The set ${ \mathcal{P}}(\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{A}} \times \overline{{ \relax{S}}_{B}})$ is equipped with the Inf semi-lattice structure $\cup$ and with the following maps defined for any $ {\relax{l}}_{A}\in { \relax{E}}_{A}$ and ${\relax{l}}_{B}\in { \relax{E}}_{B}$,
\begin{eqnarray}
\hspace{-2cm} \begin{array}{rcrcl}
 & & \nu\,{}^{\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{A}}\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{B}}}_{{\relax{l}}_A,{\relax{l}}_B}: { \mathcal{P}}(\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{A}} \times \overline{{ \relax{S}}_{B}}) & \longrightarrow & { \relax{B}}\\
& & \{\,(\sigma_{i,A},\sigma_{i,B})\;\vert\; i\in I\,\} & \mapsto &  \bigwedge{}_{i\in I}\; {\epsilon}\,{}^{{ \relax{S}}_{A}}_{{ \relax{l}}_A}(\sigma_{i,A}) \bullet {\epsilon}\,{}^{{ \relax{S}}_{B}}_{{ \relax{l}}_B}(\sigma_{i,B}).
\end{array}
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end definition-37 -->
<!-- definition-38: body_md -->
${ \mathcal{P}}(\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{A}} \times \overline{{ \relax{S}}_{B}})$ is equipped with a congruence relation defined between any two elements $u_{AB}$ and $u'_{AB}$ of ${ \mathcal{P}}(\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{A}} \times \overline{{ \relax{S}}_{B}})$ by
\begin{eqnarray}
(\,u_{AB} \approx u'_{AB}\,) & :\Leftrightarrow &
(\,\forall {\relax{l}}_A\in { \relax{E}}_{A},\forall {\relax{l}}_B\in { \relax{E}}_{B},\;\;
\nu\,{}^{\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{A}}\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{B}}}_{{\relax{l}}_A,{\relax{l}}_B} (u_{AB})=\nu\,{}^{\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{A}}\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{B}}}_{{\relax{l}}_A,{\relax{l}}_B} (u'_{AB})\,).\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end definition-38 -->
<!-- definition-39: body_md -->
The space ${{\overline{S}}}_{AB}=\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{A}} \widetilde{\otimes} \overline{{ \relax{S}}_{B}}$ is built as the quotient of ${ \mathcal{P}}(\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{A}} \times \overline{{ \relax{S}}_{B}})$ under the congruence relation $\approx$.  
\begin{eqnarray}
\forall \sigma_{AB}\in { \mathcal{P}}(\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{A}} \times \overline{{ \relax{S}}_{B}}), && \widetilde{\sigma_{AB}}:=\{\, u_{AB}\;\vert\; \sigma_{AB}\approx u_{AB}\,\}.
\end{eqnarray}
The map $\nu\,{}^{\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{A}}\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{B}}}_{{\relax{l}}_A,{\relax{l}}_B}$ will be abusively defined as a map from ${{\overline{S}}}_{AB}$ to ${ \relax{B}}$ by $\nu\,{}^{\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{A}}\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{B}}}_{{\relax{l}}_A,{\relax{l}}_B}(\widetilde{\sigma_{AB}}):= \nu\,{}^{\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{A}}\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{B}}}_{{\relax{l}}_A,{\relax{l}}_B}({\sigma_{AB}})$ for any $\sigma_{AB}$ in ${ \mathcal{P}}(\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{A}} \times \overline{{ \relax{S}}_{B}})$.\\
The element $\widetilde{u}\in {{\overline{S}}}_{AB}$ associated to the element $u:=\{\, (\sigma_{i,A},\sigma_{i,B})\;\vert\; i\in I\,\}\in { \mathcal{P}}(\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{A}} \times \overline{{ \relax{S}}_{B}})$ will be denoted $\bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{{\overline{S}}}_{AB}}}_{i\in I} \sigma_{i,A}\widetilde{\otimes}\sigma_{i,B}$.
<!-- end definition-39 -->
<!-- lemma-40: body_md -->
\label{lemmainclusiontensor}
There exists a map denoted $\iota^{{{\overline{S}}}_{AB}}$ from $\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{A}} {\times} \overline{{ \relax{S}}_{B}}$ to ${{\overline{S}}}_{AB}$. We have explicitly
\begin{eqnarray}
\iota^{{{\overline{S}}}_{AB}}(\sigma_A,\sigma_B) &:=& \widetilde{(\sigma_A,\sigma_B)}.
\end{eqnarray}
We will adopt the basic notation $\sigma_A\widetilde{\otimes}\sigma_B:=\iota^{{{\overline{S}}}_{AB}}(\sigma_A,\sigma_B)$
<!-- end lemma-40 -->
<!-- lemma-41: body_md -->
\label{lemmaseparatedminimal}
By construction, we have
\begin{eqnarray}
&&\hspace{-1.8cm}\forall \; \left(\bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{{\overline{S}}}_{AB}}}_{i\in I} \sigma_{i,A}\widetilde{\otimes} \sigma_{i,B}\right) \in {{\overline{S}}}_{AB},\; \forall \; \left(\bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{{\overline{S}}}_{AB}}}_{j\in J} \sigma'_{j,A}\widetilde{\otimes} \sigma'_{j,B}\right) \in {{\overline{S}}}_{AB},\nonumber\\
&&\hspace{-1.8cm}\left(\forall {\relax{l}}_A\in { \relax{E}}_{A},{\relax{l}}_B\in { \relax{E}}_{B},\;\; \bigwedge{}_{i\in I}{\epsilon}\,{}^{{ \relax{S}}_A}_{{\relax{l}}_A} (\sigma_{i,A})\bullet {\epsilon}\,{}^{{ \relax{S}}_B}_{{\relax{l}}_B} (\sigma_{i,B})=
\bigwedge{}_{j\in J}{\epsilon}\,{}^{{ \relax{S}}_A}_{{\relax{l}}_A} (\sigma'_{j,A})\bullet {\epsilon}\,{}^{{ \relax{S}}_B}_{{\relax{l}}_B} (\sigma'_{j,B}) \right)\nonumber\\
&&\hspace{5cm} \;\Rightarrow\; (\,\bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{{\overline{S}}}_{AB}}}_{i\in I} \sigma_{i,A}\widetilde{\otimes} \sigma_{i,B} = \bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{{\overline{S}}}_{AB}}}_{j\in J} \sigma'_{j,A}\widetilde{\otimes} \sigma'_{j,B}\,).\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end lemma-41 -->
<!-- theorem-20: body_md -->
For any $\{\,\sigma_{i,A}\;\vert\; i\in I\,\}\subseteq \overline{{ \relax{S}}_{A}}$, $\{\,\sigma_{j,B}\;\vert\; j\in J\,\}\subseteq \overline{{ \relax{S}}_{B}}$, $\sigma_A\in \overline{{ \relax{S}}_{A}}$ and $\sigma_B\in \overline{{ \relax{S}}_{B}}$, we have the two following fundamental properties
\begin{eqnarray}
&& (\bigsqcap{}^{{}^{\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{A}}}}_{i\in I}\,\sigma_{i,A})\widetilde{\otimes} \sigma_B =  \bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{{{\overline{S} }}_{AB}}}}_{i\in I} (\sigma_{i,A}\widetilde{\otimes} \sigma_B),\label{pitensor=tensorpi1preminimal}\\
&& \sigma_A \widetilde{\otimes}  (\bigsqcap{}^{{}^{\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{B}}}}_{i\in I}\,\sigma_{i,B}) =  \bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{{{\overline{S} }}_{AB}}}}_{i\in I} (\sigma_A \widetilde{\otimes} \sigma_{i,B}).\label{pitensor=tensorpi2preminimal}
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end theorem-20 -->
<!-- proof-52: body_md -->
Using the homomorphic property for ${\epsilon}\,{}^{{ \relax{S}}_A}$ and the distributivity property between $\bullet$ and $\wedge$ in ${\relax{B}}$, we deduce
\begin{eqnarray}
{\epsilon}\,{}^{{ \relax{S}}_A}_{{\relax{l}}_A} (\bigsqcap{}^{{}^{\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{A}}}}_{i\in I}\sigma_{i,A}) \bullet {\epsilon}\,{}^{{ \relax{S}}_B}_{{\relax{l}}_B} (\sigma_B) 
&=&
(\bigwedge{}_{i\in I}\;{\epsilon}\,{}^{{ \relax{S}}_A}_{{\relax{l}}_A} (\sigma_{i,A})) \bullet {\epsilon}\,{}^{{ \relax{S}}_B}_{{\relax{l}}_B} (\sigma_B) \nonumber\\
&=&
\bigwedge{}_{i\in I}\;(\,{\epsilon}\,{}^{{ \relax{S}}_A}_{{\relax{l}}_A} (\sigma_{i,A})\bullet {\epsilon}\,{}^{{ \relax{S}}_B}_{{\relax{l}}_B} (\sigma_B)),\label{demobifilterproperty}
\end{eqnarray}
and then, using Lemma {{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@lemmaseparatedminimal\endcsname\@firstoftwo{lemmaseparatedminimal}}}, we obtain the property ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@pitensor=tensorpi1preminimal\endcsname\@firstoftwo{pitensor=tensorpi1preminimal}}}). We obtain the property ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@pitensor=tensorpi2preminimal\endcsname\@firstoftwo{pitensor=tensorpi2preminimal}}}) along the same lines of proof.
<!-- end proof-52 -->
<!-- definition-40: body_md -->
\label{defsqsubseteqSAB}
${{\overline{S} }}_{AB}$ is equipped with a partial order defined according to
\begin{eqnarray}
\forall \widetilde{\sigma}_{AB},\widetilde{\sigma}'_{AB} \in {{{\overline{S} }}_{AB}},\;\;\;\; (\,\widetilde{\sigma}_{AB} \sqsubseteq_{{}_{{{\overline{S} }}_{AB}}} \widetilde{\sigma}'_{AB}\,) & :\Leftrightarrow &\nonumber\\
&&\hspace{-2cm}(\,\forall {\relax{l}}_A\in { \relax{E}}_{A},\forall {\relax{l}}_B\in { \relax{E}}_{B},\;\;
{\nu}\,{}^{\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{A}{ \relax{S}}_{B}}}_{{\relax{l}}_A, {\relax{l}}_B} (\widetilde{\sigma}_{AB})\leq {\nu}\,{}^{\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{A}{ \relax{S}}_{B}}}_{{\relax{l}}_A,{\relax{l}}_B} (\widetilde{\sigma}'_{AB})\,).\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end definition-40 -->
<!-- lemma-42: body_md -->
\label{Lemmadevelopetildeleqetilde}
Let us consider $u_{AB}:=\{\, (\sigma_{i,A},\sigma_{i,B})\;\vert\; i\in I\,\}$ an element of ${ \mathcal{P}}(\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{A}} \times \overline{{ \relax{S}}_{B}})$. We have explicitly, for any $\sigma_{A}\in { \relax{S}}_{A}$ and $\sigma_{B}\in { \relax{S}}_{B}$, the following equivalence
\begin{eqnarray}
 \left( \widetilde{u_{AB}} \sqsubseteq_{{}_{{{\overline{S} }}_{AB}}} \widetilde{(\sigma_{A}, \sigma_{B})} \right)
&\Leftrightarrow &
\left( (\bigsqcap{}^{{}_{\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{A}}}}_{k\in I}\; \sigma_{k,A}) \;\sqsubseteq_{{}_{\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{A}}}}\sigma_{A}
\;\;\textit{\rm and}\;\;
(\bigsqcap{}^{{}_{\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{B}}}}_{m\in I} \;\sigma_{m,B})\; \sqsubseteq_{{}_{\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{B}}}} \sigma_{B}
\;\;\textit{\rm and}\;\;\right.\nonumber\\
&&\hspace{-2cm}\left.\left(\forall \varnothing \varsubsetneq K  \varsubsetneq I, \;\; (\bigsqcap{}^{{}_{\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{A}}}}_{k\in K}\; \sigma_{k,A}) \;\sqsubseteq_{{}_{\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{A}}}}\sigma_{A}\;\;\;\textit{\rm or}\;\;\; (\bigsqcap{}^{{}_{\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{B}}}}_{m\in I-K} \;\sigma_{m,B})\; \sqsubseteq_{{}_{\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{B}}}} \sigma_{B}\right) \right).\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;
\label{developmentetildeordersimplify}
\end{eqnarray}
It is recalled that ${ \relax{S}}_{A}$ and ${ \relax{S}}_{B}$ are down-complete Inf semi-lattice and then the infima in this formula are well-defined.
<!-- end lemma-42 -->
<!-- proof-53: body_md -->
We intent to expand the inequality $ \widetilde{u_{AB}} \sqsubseteq_{{}_{{{\overline{S} }}_{AB}}} \widetilde{(\sigma_{A}, \sigma_{B})}$. It is equivalent to
\begin{eqnarray}
\forall {\relax{l}}_A\in { \relax{E}}_{A}, \forall {\relax{l}}_B\in { \relax{E}}_{B},&&
\left( \bigwedge{}_{i\in I}\;
{\epsilon}\,{}^{{ \relax{S}}_{A}}_{{\relax{l}}_A} ( \sigma_{i,A})\bullet {\epsilon}\,{}^{{ \relax{S}}_{B}}_{{\relax{l}}_B} ( \sigma_{i,B})\right)
\leq
{\epsilon}\,{}^{{ \relax{S}}_{A}}_{{\relax{l}}_A} (\sigma_{A}) \bullet {\epsilon}\,{}^{{ \relax{S}}_{B}}_{{\relax{l}}_B}(\sigma_{B}).\label{assumptionorder2}\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;
\end{eqnarray}
We intent to choose a pertinent set of effects ${\relax{l}}_A\in { \relax{E}}_{A}$
 and ${\relax{l}}_B\in { \relax{E}}_{B}$ to reformulate this inequality. \\
Let us firstly choose ${\relax{l}}_B={ \relax{Y}}_{{}_{{ \relax{E}}_{B}}}$. Using  ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@expressionbullet\endcsname\@firstoftwo{expressionbullet}}}), we obtain
\begin{eqnarray}
{\epsilon}\,{}^{{ \relax{S}}_{A}}_{{ \relax{l}}_A}(\bigsqcap{}^{{}^{\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{A}}}}_{i\in I}\; \sigma_{i,A})\leq {\epsilon}\,{}^{{ \relax{S}}_{A}}_{{ \relax{l}}_A}(\sigma_{A})
,\forall { \relax{l}}_A \in { \relax{E}}_A,
\end{eqnarray} 
which leads immediately
\begin{eqnarray}
\bigsqcap{}^{{}^{\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{A}}}}_{i\in I}\; \sigma_{i,A} \;\sqsubseteq_{{}_{\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{A}}}} \sigma_{A}.\label{ineqBY}
\end{eqnarray}
Choosing ${\relax{l}}_A={ \relax{Y}}_{{}_{{ \relax{E}}_{A}}}$, we obtain along the same line 
\begin{eqnarray}
\bigsqcap{}^{{}^{\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{B}}}}_{i\in I} \;\sigma_{i,B}\; \sqsubseteq_{{}_{\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{B}}}} \sigma_{B}.\label{ineqAY}
\end{eqnarray}
Let us now consider $\varnothing \varsubsetneq K  \varsubsetneq I$ and let us choose the real effects ${ \relax{l}}_A$ and ${ \relax{l}}_B$ as follows
\begin{eqnarray}
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  
{ \relax{l}}_A:={ \relax{l}}_{(\centerdot\,,\,\bigsqcap{}^{{}^{\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{A}}}}_{k\in K}\; \sigma_{k,A})} && { \relax{l}}_B:={ \relax{l}}_{(\centerdot\,,\,\bigsqcap{}^{{}^{\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{B}}}}_{m\in I-K}\; \sigma_{m,B})}
\end{eqnarray}
Note that ${ \relax{l}}_A$ and ${ \relax{l}}_B$ are \underline{real} effects because $\bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{ \relax{S}}_{A}}}_{k\in K}\; \sigma_{k,A}\in \overline{{ \relax{S}}_{A}}$ and $\bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{ \relax{S}}_{B}}}_{m\in I-K}\; \sigma_{m,B}\in \overline{{ \relax{S}}_{B}}$.\\
We deduce, from the assumption ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@assumptionorder2\endcsname\@firstoftwo{assumptionorder2}}}), that, for this $\varnothing \varsubsetneq K  \varsubsetneq I$, we have
\begin{eqnarray}
 &&(\bigsqcap{}^{{}^{\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{A}}}}_{k\in K}\; \sigma_{k,A} \;\sqsubseteq_{{}_{\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{A}}}} \sigma_{A}) \;\;\textit{\rm or}\;\; (\bigsqcap{}^{{}^{\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{B}}}}_{m\in I-K} \;\sigma_{m,B}\; \sqsubseteq_{{}_{\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{B}}}} \sigma_{B}).\label{ineqN}
\end{eqnarray}
We let the reader check that we have obtained the whole set of independent inequalities reformulating the property ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@assumptionorder2\endcsname\@firstoftwo{assumptionorder2}}}).
<!-- end proof-53 -->
<!-- theorem-21: body_md -->
\label{theoremaxiomA1bipartitepre}
${{\overline{S} }}_{AB}$ is a down-complete Inf semi-lattice with
\begin{eqnarray}
\forall \{\,u_i\;\vert\; i\in I\,\}\subseteq { \mathcal{P}}(\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{A}} \times \overline{{ \relax{S}}_{B}}),&&\bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{{\overline{S} }}_{AB}}}_{i\in I} \; \widetilde{u_i}  = \widetilde{\bigcup{}_{i\in I}\; u_i}.\label{tensorinfSAB}
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end theorem-21 -->
<!-- theorem-22: body_md -->
\label{bottomcompound}
If ${ \relax{S}}_{A}$ and ${ \relax{S}}_{B}$ admit $\bot_{{}_{{\relax{S}}_A}}$ and $\bot_{{}_{{\relax{S}}_B}}$ respectively as bottom elements, then
${{\overline{S} }}_{AB}$ admits a bottom element explicitly given by $\bot_{{}_{{{\overline{S} }}_{AB}}}=\bot_{{}_{{\relax{S}}_A}}\widetilde{\otimes}\bot_{{}_{{\relax{S}}_B}}$.
<!-- end theorem-22 -->
<!-- proof-54: body_md -->
Trivial using the expansion ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@developmentetildeordersimplify\endcsname\@firstoftwo{developmentetildeordersimplify}}}).
<!-- end proof-54 -->
<!-- theorem-23: body_md -->
\label{theorempartialtracesminimal}
We have the two following homomorphisms
\begin{eqnarray}
\hspace{-1cm}\begin{array}{rcrclccrcrcl}
&  &\zeta^{\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{A}}\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{B}}}_{(1)} : \;\;\;\;\;\; {{\overline{S} }}_{AB} & \longrightarrow & \overline{{ \relax{S}}_{A}}  & & &  &  &\zeta^{\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{A}}\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{B}}}_{(2)} : \;\;\;\;\;\; {{\overline{S} }}_{AB} & \longrightarrow & \overline{{ \relax{S}}_{B}}  \\
& & \bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{ \overline{S} }_{AB}}}_{i\in I} \sigma_{i,A} \widetilde{\otimes} \sigma_{i,B} & \mapsto & \bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{A}}}}}_{i\in I} \sigma_{i,A}  & & & & & \bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{ \overline{S} }_{AB}}}_{i\in I} \sigma_{i,A} \widetilde{\otimes} \sigma_{i,B} & \mapsto & \bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{B}}}}}_{i\in I}  \sigma_{i,B}
\end{array}
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end theorem-23 -->
<!-- definition-41: body_md -->
{\bf \@nx\protect\@empty\@nx\csname cite \endcsname{Fraser1976}}\label{theoremtensorbasic}
The canonical tensor product denoted ${S}_{AB}:=\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{A}} \otimes \overline{{ \relax{S}}_{B}}$ of the two Inf semi-lattices $\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{A}}$ and $\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{B}}$ is obtained as the solution of the following universal problem : there exists a bi-homomorphism, denoted $\iota$ from $\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{A}} \times \overline{{ \relax{S}}_{B}}$ to ${S}_{AB}$, such that, for any Inf semi-lattice ${ \relax{S}}$ and any bi-homomorphism $f$ from $\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{A}} \times \overline{{ \relax{S}}_{B}}$ to ${ \relax{S}}$,  there is a unique homomorphism $g$ from ${S}_{AB}$ to ${ \relax{S}}$ with $f = g \circ \iota$. We denote $\iota(\sigma,\sigma')=\sigma \otimes \sigma'$ for any $\sigma\in \overline{{ \relax{S}}_{A}}$ and $\sigma'\in \overline{{ \relax{S}}_{B}}$.  \\
The tensor product ${S}_{AB}$ exists and is unique up to isomorphism, it is built as the homomorphic image of the free $\sqcap$ semi-lattice generated by the set $\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{A}} \times \overline{{ \relax{S}}_{B}}$ under the congruence relation determined by identifying $(\sigma_1 \sqcap_{{}_{\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{A}}}}\sigma_2, \sigma')$ with $(\sigma_1,  \sigma')\sqcap (\sigma_2, \sigma')$ for all $\sigma_1,\sigma_2\in \overline{{ \relax{S}}_{A}}, \sigma'\in \overline{{ \relax{S}}_{B}}$ and identifying  $(\sigma, \sigma'_1 \sqcap_{{}_{\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{B}}}}\sigma'_2)$ with $(\sigma,  \sigma'_1)\sqcap (\sigma, \sigma'_2)$ for all $\sigma\in \overline{{ \relax{S}}_{A}},\sigma'_1,\sigma'_2\in \overline{{ \relax{S}}_{B}}$. \\
Then, from now on, ${S}_{AB}$ is the Inf semi-lattice (the infimum of $S\subseteq {S}_{AB}$ will be denoted $\bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{S}_{AB}}} S$) generated by the elements $\sigma_A \otimes \sigma_B$ with $\sigma_A \in \overline{{ \relax{S}}_{A}}, \sigma_B \in \overline{{ \relax{S}}_{B}}$ and subject exclusively to the conditions 
\begin{eqnarray}
&&\left\{\begin{array}{l}
(\sigma_A\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{A}}}}\sigma'_A)\otimes \sigma_B = (\sigma_A\otimes \sigma_B)\sqcap_{{}_{{S}_{AB}}}(\sigma'_A\otimes \sigma_B),\\
 \sigma_A \otimes (\sigma_B\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{B}}}}\sigma'_B) = (\sigma_A\otimes \sigma_B)\sqcap_{{}_{{S}_{AB}}}(\sigma_A\otimes \sigma'_B). 
\end{array}\right.
\end{eqnarray}
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       
The space ${S}_{AB}=\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{A}} \otimes \overline{{ \relax{S}}_{B}}$ is turned into a partially ordered set with the following binary relation
\begin{eqnarray}
\forall \sigma_{AB},\sigma'_{AB} \in {S}_{AB},\;\;\;\; 
(\,\sigma_{AB} \sqsubseteq_{{}_{{S}_{AB}}} \sigma'_{AB}\,) & :\Leftrightarrow &
(\,\sigma_{AB} \sqcap_{{}_{{S}_{AB}}} \sigma'_{AB} = \sigma_{AB}\,).\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end definition-41 -->
<!-- definition-42: body_md -->
A non-empty subset ${ \relax{R}}$ of $\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{A}} \times \overline{{ \relax{S}}_{B}}$ is called a bi-filter iff 
\begin{eqnarray}
&&\forall \sigma_A,\sigma_{1,A},\sigma_{2,A}\in \overline{{ \relax{S}}_{A}},\forall \sigma_B,\sigma_{1,B},\sigma_{2,B}\in \overline{{ \relax{S}}_{B}},\nonumber\\
&&(\,  (\sigma_{1,A},\sigma_{1,B})\leq (\sigma_{2,A},\sigma_{2,B}) \;\;\textit{\rm and}\;\; (\sigma_{1,A},\sigma_{1,B})\in { \relax{R}} \,)\;\;\Rightarrow\;\; (\sigma_{2,A},\sigma_{2,B})\in { \relax{R}},\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\label{defbifilter1}\\
&&(\sigma_{1,A},\sigma_{B}),(\sigma_{2,A},\sigma_{B})\in { \relax{R}}\;\;\Rightarrow\;\; (\sigma_{1,A}\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{{ \relax{S}}_A}}}\sigma_{2,A},\sigma_{B})\in { \relax{R}},\label{defbifilter2}\\
&&(\sigma_{A},\sigma_{1,B}),(\sigma_{A},\sigma_{2,B})\in { \relax{R}}\;\;\Rightarrow\;\; (\sigma_{A},\sigma_{1,B}\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{{ \relax{S}}_B}}}\sigma_{2,B})\in { \relax{R}}.\label{defbifilter3}
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end definition-42 -->
<!-- definition-43: body_md -->
If $\{(\sigma_{1,A},\sigma_{1,B}),\cdots,(\sigma_{n,A},\sigma_{n,B})\}$ is a non-empty finite subset of $\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{A}} \times \overline{{ \relax{S}}_{B}}$, then the intersection of all bi-filters of $\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{A}} \times \overline{{ \relax{S}}_{B}}$ which contain $(\sigma_{1,A},\sigma_{1,B})$, $\cdots$, $(\sigma_{n,A},\sigma_{n,B})$ is a bi-filter, which we denote by ${ \relax{F}}\{(\sigma_{1,A},\sigma_{1,B}),\cdots,(\sigma_{n,A},\sigma_{n,B})\}$.
<!-- end definition-43 -->
<!-- lemma-43: body_md -->
\label{FalphaF}
If $F$ is a filter of ${S}_{AB}$ then the set $\alpha(F):=\{\,(\sigma_{A},\sigma_{B})\in \overline{{ \relax{S}}_{A}} \times \overline{{ \relax{S}}_{B}}\;\vert\; \sigma_{A}\otimes \sigma_{B} \in F\;\}$ is a bi-filter of $\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{A}} \times \overline{{ \relax{S}}_{B}}$.
<!-- end lemma-43 -->
<!-- lemma-44: body_md -->
{\bf \@nx\protect\@empty\@nx\csname cite \endcsname[Lemma 1]{Fraser1978}}\label{sigmainFinequality}
Let us choose $\sigma_A,\sigma_{1,A},\cdots,\sigma_{n,A}\in \overline{{ \relax{S}}_{A}}$ and $\sigma_B,\sigma_{1,B},\cdots,\sigma_{n,B}\in \overline{{ \relax{S}}_{B}}$. Then, 
\begin{eqnarray}
\hspace{-1cm}(\sigma_{A},\sigma_{B})\in { \relax{F}}\{(\sigma_{1,A},\sigma_{1,B}),\cdots,(\sigma_{n,A},\sigma_{n,B})\} & \Leftrightarrow & \left( \bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{S}_{AB}}}_{1\leq i\leq n}\; \sigma_{i,A}\otimes \sigma_{i,B}\right) \sqsubseteq_{{}_{{S}_{AB}}} \sigma_{A}\otimes \sigma_{B}.\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end lemma-44 -->
<!-- lemma-45: body_md -->
{\bf \@nx\protect\@empty\@nx\csname cite \endcsname[Theorem 1]{Fraser1978}}\label{orderimpliespolynomial}\\
Let us choose $\sigma_A,\sigma_{1,A},\cdots,\sigma_{n,A}\in \overline{{ \relax{S}}_{A}}$ and $\sigma_B,\sigma_{1,B},\cdots,\sigma_{n,B}\in \overline{{ \relax{S}}_{B}}$. Then, 
\begin{eqnarray}
&&\hspace{-2cm} \left( \bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{S}_{AB}}}_{1\leq i\leq n}\; \sigma_{i,A}\otimes \sigma_{i,B}\right) \sqsubseteq_{{}_{{S}_{AB}}} \sigma_{A}\otimes \sigma_{B}  \Leftrightarrow \nonumber\\  
&& (\,\textit{\rm there exists a n$-$ary lattice polynomial $p$}\;\vert\; \sigma_{A}\sqsupseteq_{{}_{\overline{{ \relax{S}}_A}}} p(\sigma_{1,A},\cdots,\sigma_{n,A})\nonumber\\
&&\textit{\rm and}\;\;  \sigma_{B}\sqsupseteq_{{}_{\overline{{ \relax{S}}_B}}} p^\ast(\sigma_{1,B},\cdots,\sigma_{n,B}) \,).
\end{eqnarray}
where $p^\ast$ denotes the lattice polynomial obtained from $p$ by dualizing the lattice operations.
<!-- end lemma-45 -->
<!-- definition-44: body_md -->
We denote by ${\overline{S} }{}^{fin}_{AB}$ the sub-poset of ${\overline{S} }_{AB}$ formed by finite infima of pure tensors. 
It is also a sub- Inf semi-lattice of ${\overline{S} }_{AB}$.
<!-- end definition-44 -->
<!-- definition-45: body_md -->
We denote by
\begin{eqnarray}
\widetilde{ \relax{F}}\{(\sigma_{i,A},\sigma_{i,B})\;\vert\; i\in I\}&:=&\{\,(\sigma'_A,\sigma'_B)\;\vert\; (\bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{\overline{S} }_{AB}}}_{i\in I} \sigma_{i,A}\widetilde{\otimes} \sigma_{i,B}) \sqsubseteq_{{}_{{\overline{S} }_{AB}}}   \sigma'_{A}\widetilde{\otimes} \sigma'_{B}\}\nonumber\\ 
                                                                                                                                       
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end definition-45 -->
<!-- theorem-24: body_md -->
\label{theoremsqsubseteqPABgeqSAB} 
We have the following obvious property relating the partial orders of ${{\overline{S} }}{}^{fin}_{AB}$ and ${S}_{AB}$. For any $\{(\sigma_{i,A},\sigma_{i,B})\;\vert\; i\in I\}\subseteq_{fin} S_{AB}$,
\begin{eqnarray}
(\bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{S}_{AB}}}_{i\in I} \sigma_{i,A}\otimes \sigma_{i,B}) \sqsubseteq_{{}_{{S}_{AB}}}  \sigma'_{A}\otimes \sigma'_{B}  & \Rightarrow & (\bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{\overline{S} }_{AB}}}_{i\in I} \sigma_{i,A}\widetilde{\otimes} \sigma_{i,B}) \sqsubseteq_{{}_{{\overline{S} }_{AB}}}   \sigma'_{A}\widetilde{\otimes} \sigma'_{B}.\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end theorem-24 -->
<!-- proof-55: body_md -->
First of all, it is clear that $\widetilde{ \relax{F}}\{(\sigma_{i,A},\sigma_{i,B})\;\vert\; i\in I\}$ is a bi-filter.\\ 
Secondly, it is easy to check that $(\sigma_{k,A},\sigma_{k,B})\in \widetilde{ \relax{F}}\{(\sigma_{i,A},\sigma_{i,B})\;\vert\; i\in I\}$ for any $k\in I$. Indeed, for any $K\subseteq I$, if $k\in K$ we have $(\bigsqcap{}^{{}_{\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{A}}}}_{l\in K}\; \sigma_{l,A}) \;\sqsubseteq_{{}_{\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{A}}}}\sigma_{k,A} $ and if $k\notin K$ we have $(\bigsqcap{}^{{}_{\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{B}}}}_{m\in I-K} \;\sigma_{m,B})\; \sqsubseteq_{{}_{\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{B}}}} \sigma_{k,B}$. \\
As a conclusion,  and by definition of ${ \relax{F}}\{(\sigma_{i,A},\sigma_{i,B})\;\vert\; i\in I\}$ as the intersection of all bi-filters containing $(\sigma_{i,A},\sigma_{i,B})$ for any $i\in I$, we have then 
$\widetilde{ \relax{F}}\{(\sigma_{i,A},\sigma_{i,B})\;\vert\; i\in I\} \supseteq  { \relax{F}}\{(\sigma_{i,A},\sigma_{i,B})\;\vert\; i\in I\}$.\\
We now use Lemma {{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@sigmainFinequality\endcsname\@firstoftwo{sigmainFinequality}}} to obtain the announced result.
<!-- end proof-55 -->
<!-- theorem-25: body_md -->
\label{theoremsqsubseteqPAB=SAB}
If $\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{A}}$ \underline{or} $\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{B}}$ are distributive (for example as simplex spaces of states), then ${{\overline{S} }}{}^{fin}_{AB}$ and ${S}_{AB}$ are isomorphic posets.
<!-- end theorem-25 -->
<!-- proof-56: body_md -->
We suppose that $\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{A}}$ or $\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{B}}$ is distributive and we intent to prove that ${ \relax{F}}\{(\sigma_{i,A},\sigma_{i,B})\;\vert\; i\in I\}=\widetilde{ \relax{F}}\{(\sigma_{i,A},\sigma_{i,B})\;\vert\; i\in I\}$ for any $\{(\sigma_{i,A},\sigma_{i,B})\;\vert\; i\in I\}\subseteq_{fin} \overline{{ \relax{S}}_{A}}\times \overline{{ \relax{S}}_{B}}$.\\
Let us prove the following fact : every bi-filter $F$ which contains $(\sigma_{k,A},\sigma_{k,B})$ for any $k\in I$ contains also $\widetilde{ \relax{F}}\{(\sigma_{i,A},\sigma_{i,B})\;\vert\; i\in I\}$.  In fact, we can show that, for any bi-filter $F$ we have
\begin{eqnarray}
&&\hspace{-1cm}(\forall k\in I,\;(\sigma_{k,A},\sigma_{k,B})\in F) \Rightarrow \nonumber \\
&& (\bigsqcup{}^{{}_{\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{A}}}}_{K\in { \mathcal{K}}}\bigsqcap{}^{{}_{\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{A}}}}_{k\in K}\; \sigma_{k,A}, \bigsqcup{}^{{}_{\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{A}}}}_{K'\in { \mathcal{K}}'}\bigsqcap{}^{{}_{\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{B}}}}_{m\in I-K'} \;\sigma_{m,B})\in F, \nonumber\\
&& \forall { \mathcal{K}},{ \mathcal{K}}'\subseteq 2^I,{ \mathcal{K}}\cup { \mathcal{K}}'=2^I, { \mathcal{K}}\cap { \mathcal{K}}'=\varnothing, \{\varnothing\}\in { \mathcal{K}}', I\in { \mathcal{K}}.\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\label{intermediatedistrib}
\end{eqnarray}

The first step towards ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@intermediatedistrib\endcsname\@firstoftwo{intermediatedistrib}}}) is obtained by checking that $\forall { \mathcal{K}},{ \mathcal{K}}'\subseteq 2^I,{ \mathcal{K}}\cup { \mathcal{K}}'=2^I, { \mathcal{K}}\cap { \mathcal{K}}'=\varnothing, \{\varnothing\}\in { \mathcal{K}}', I\in { \mathcal{K}}$,
\begin{eqnarray}
 && (\bigsqcup{}^{{}^{{ \relax{S}}}}_{K'\in { \mathcal{K}}'}\bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{ \relax{S}}}}_{m\in I-K'} \;\sigma_{m}) \sqsupseteq_{{}_{ \relax{S}}}
(\bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{ \relax{S}}}}_{K\in { \mathcal{K}}}\bigsqcup{}^{{}^{{ \relax{S}}}}_{k\in K}\; \sigma_{k})\label{firststep}
\end{eqnarray}
for any distributive ${ \relax{S}}$ and any collection of elements of ${ \relax{S}}$  denoted $\sigma_k$ for $k\in I$ for which these two sides of inequality exist.  To check this fact, we have to note that,  using \@nx\protect\@empty\@nx\csname cite \endcsname[Lemma 8 p. 50]{Balbes1975}, we have first of all
\begin{eqnarray}
(\bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{ \relax{S}}}}_{K\in { \mathcal{K}}}\bigsqcup{}^{{}^{{ \relax{S}}}}_{k\in K}\; \sigma_{k})= \bigsqcup{}^{{}^{{ \relax{S}}}}\!\!\! \left\{ \bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{ \relax{S}}}}_{K\in { \mathcal{K}}} \pi_K(A) \;\vert\; A\in \prod_{K\in { \mathcal{K}}} K \right\},
\end{eqnarray}
where $\pi_K$ denotes the projection of the component indexed by K in the cardinal product $\prod_{K\in { \mathcal{K}}} K$. Moreover,  for any $A\in \prod_{K\in { \mathcal{K}}} K$,  there exists $L\in { \mathcal{K}}'$ such that $\bigcup \{ \pi_K(A) \;\vert\; K\in { \mathcal{K}}\}\;\supseteq\; (I\smallsetminus L)$ and then $(\bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{ \relax{S}}}}_{K\in { \mathcal{K}}} \pi_K(A)) \sqsubseteq_{{}_{ \relax{S}}} (\bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{ \relax{S}}}}_{m\in I-L} \;\sigma_{m}) \sqsubseteq_{{}_{ \relax{S}}} (\bigsqcup{}^{{}^{{ \relax{S}}}}_{K'\in { \mathcal{K}}'}\bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{ \relax{S}}}}_{m\in I-K'} \;\sigma_{m})$. As a result, we obtain the property ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@firststep\endcsname\@firstoftwo{firststep}}}).\\

The second step towards ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@intermediatedistrib\endcsname\@firstoftwo{intermediatedistrib}}}) consists in showing that 
\begin{eqnarray}
(\forall k\in I,\;(\sigma_{k,A},\sigma_{k,B})\in F) & \Rightarrow & (\bigsqcup{}^{{}_{\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{A}}}}_{K\in { \mathcal{K}}}\bigsqcap{}^{{}_{\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{A}}}}_{k\in K}\; \sigma_{k,A},  \bigsqcap{}^{{}_{\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{B}}}}_{K\in { \mathcal{K}}}\bigsqcup{}^{{}_{\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{B}}}}_{k\in K}\; \sigma_{k,B})\;\in F\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;
\end{eqnarray}
for any ${ \mathcal{K}}\subseteq 2^I$. This intermediary result is obtained by induction on the complexity of the polynomial $(\bigsqcup{}^{{}_{\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{A}}}}_{K\in { \mathcal{K}}}\bigsqcap{}^{{}_{\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{A}}}}_{k\in K}\; \sigma_{k,A})$ by using the following elementary result
\begin{eqnarray}
&&\forall \sigma_A,\sigma'_A\in \overline{{ \relax{S}}_A},\sigma_B,\sigma'_B\in \overline{{ \relax{S}}_B},\;\;\;\; \left( (\sigma_A,\sigma_B),(\sigma'_A,\sigma'_B)\in F \right) \Rightarrow \nonumber\\
&&\hspace{2cm} \left\{
\begin{array}{l}
(\sigma_A \sqcup_{{}_{\overline{{ \relax{S}}_A}}} \sigma'_A,\sigma_B \sqcap_{{}_{\overline{{ \relax{S}}_B}}} \sigma'_B)\in F\nonumber\\
(\sigma_A \sqcap_{{}_{\overline{{ \relax{S}}_A}}} \sigma'_A,\sigma_B \sqcup_{{}_{\overline{{ \relax{S}}_B}}} \sigma'_B)\in F
\end{array}\right.
\end{eqnarray}
trivially deduced using the bi-filter character of $F$, i.e. properties ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@defbifilter1\endcsname\@firstoftwo{defbifilter1}}})({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@defbifilter2\endcsname\@firstoftwo{defbifilter2}}})({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@defbifilter3\endcsname\@firstoftwo{defbifilter3}}}). \\

As a final conclusion,  using the explicit definition of ${ \relax{F}}\{(\sigma_{i,A},\sigma_{i,B})\;\vert\; i\in I\}$ as the intersection of all bi-ideals containing $(\sigma_{k,A},\sigma_{k,B})$ for any $k\in I$,  we obtain $\widetilde{ \relax{F}}\{(\sigma_{i,A},\sigma_{i,B})\;\vert\; i\in I\}={ \relax{F}}\{(\sigma_{i,A},\sigma_{i,B})\;\vert\; i\in I\}$.\\

${{\overline{S} }}{}^{fin}_{AB}$ and ${S}_{AB}$ are then isomorphic posets.
<!-- end proof-56 -->
<!-- theorem-26: body_md -->
\label{SASBditribandcup}
If ${ \relax{S}}_A$ \underline{and} ${{ \relax{S}}_B}$ are  simplex spaces of states, then ${{\overline{S} }}_{AB}$ is also a simplex space of states.  In other words, the bipartite experiments based on a pair ${ \relax{S}}_A,{ \relax{S}}_B$ of deterministic spaces of states are described by a deterministic space of states obtained as the canonical tensor product ${ \relax{S}}_A {\otimes}{ \relax{S}}_B$ (Indeed, using Theorem {{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@theoremsqsubseteqPAB=SAB\endcsname\@firstoftwo{theoremsqsubseteqPAB=SAB}}}, we have also ${{\overline{S} }}{}^{fin}_{AB}={S}_{AB}$ in this situation).
\\
In that case, the explicit expression for the supremum of two elements in ${{\overline{S} }}{}^{fin}_{AB}$ is given by
\begin{eqnarray}
&&\hspace{-1cm}(\bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{{\overline{S} }}_{AB}}}_{i\in I} \sigma_{i,A}\widetilde{\otimes} \sigma_{i,B}) \sqcup{}_{{}_{{{\overline{S} }}_{AB}}} (\bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{{\overline{S} }}_{AB}}}_{j\in J} \sigma'_{j,A}\widetilde{\otimes} \sigma'_{j,B}) = \nonumber\\
&&\hspace{1cm} =\bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{{\overline{S} }}_{AB}}}_{i\in I,\;j\in J}\; (\sigma_{i,A}\sqcup_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}_A}}\sigma'_{j,A}) \widetilde{\otimes} (\sigma_{i,B} \sqcup_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}_B}} \sigma'_{j,B}). \;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\label{formulacupSAB}
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end theorem-26 -->
<!-- proof-57: body_md -->
If  ${{\overline{S} }}_{AB}$ were not a simplex, it would mean that we would have a family  $(\sigma_{i,A}\widetilde{\otimes}\sigma_{i,B})_{i\in I}$ of pure states of ${{\overline{S} }}_{AB}$, and another pure state $\sigma_{A}\widetilde{\otimes}\sigma_{B}$ such that 
\begin{eqnarray}
\bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{{\overline{S} }}_{AB}}}_{i\in I} \sigma_{i,A}\widetilde{\otimes} \sigma_{i,B} &\sqsubseteq_{{{\overline{S} }}_{AB}}
& \sigma_{A}\widetilde{\otimes}\sigma_{B} \label{equationforsimplextensor}
\end{eqnarray}
but with
\begin{eqnarray}
\sigma_{A}\widetilde{\otimes}\sigma_{B} &\notin &
\{\,\sigma_{i,A}\widetilde{\otimes} \sigma_{i,B} \;\vert\; i\in I\,\}.
\end{eqnarray}
However, using the expansion ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@developmentetildeordersimplify\endcsname\@firstoftwo{developmentetildeordersimplify}}}) with ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@equationforsimplextensor\endcsname\@firstoftwo{equationforsimplextensor}}}), we deduce $\sigma_{B}\sqsupseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}_B}} \bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{ \relax{S}}_B}}_{i\in I} \sigma_{i,B}$ and $\sigma_{A}\sqsupseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}_A}} \bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{ \relax{S}}_A}}_{i\in I} \sigma_{i,A}$ and $\forall \varnothing \varsubsetneq K  \varsubsetneq I, \;\; (\bigsqcap{}^{{}_{{ \relax{S}}_{A}}}_{k\in K}\; \sigma_{k,A}) \;\sqsubseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}_{A}}}\sigma_{A}\;\;\;\textit{\rm or}\;\;\; (\bigsqcap{}^{{}_{{ \relax{S}}_{B}}}_{m\in I-K} \;\sigma_{m,B})\; \sqsubseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}_{B}}} \sigma_{B}$. Now, we use the simplexity of ${ \relax{S}}_A$ and ${ \relax{S}}_B$ to deduce that $\sigma_{B}\in \{\,\sigma_{i,B}\;\vert\; i\in I\,\}$ and $\sigma_{A}\in \{\,\sigma_{i,A}\;\vert\; i\in I\,\}$ and $\forall \varnothing \varsubsetneq K  \varsubsetneq I, \;\; \sigma_{A}\in \{\,\sigma_{i,A}\;\vert\; i\in K\,\}\;\;\;\textit{\rm or}\;\;\; \sigma_{B}\in \{\,\sigma_{i,B}\;\vert\; i\in I-K\,\}$. We then obtain immediately the following result : there exists a unique $i\in I$ such that $\sigma_{A}\widetilde{\otimes}\sigma_{B}=\sigma_{i,A}\widetilde{\otimes} \sigma_{i,B}$. We have then obtained a contradiction. As a conclusion, ${{\overline{S} }}_{AB}$ is a simplex.\\ 
Endly, the formula ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@formulacupSAB\endcsname\@firstoftwo{formulacupSAB}}}) is a direct consequence of the distributivity in ${{\overline{S} }}_{AB}$ (see \@nx\protect\@empty\@nx\csname cite \endcsname[Theorem 3]{Fraser1978}).
<!-- end proof-57 -->
<!-- theorem-27: body_md -->
\label{theorempuretilde} 
\begin{eqnarray}
{{{ \overline{S}}}}{}^{\;{}^{pure}}_{AB} & = & \{\, \sigma_A \widetilde{\otimes} \sigma_B\;\vert\; \sigma_A \in \overline{ \relax{S}}^{\;{}^{pure}}_{A}, \sigma_B \in \overline{ \relax{S}}^{\;{}^{pure}}_{B}\,\} = Max({{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB})
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end theorem-27 -->
<!-- proof-58: body_md -->
First of all, it is a tautological fact that the completely meet-irreducible elements of  ${{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}$ are necessarily pure tensors of  ${{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}$, i.e.  elements of the form $\sigma_A \widetilde{\otimes} \sigma_B$. \\
Let us then consider $\sigma_A \widetilde{\otimes} \sigma_B$ a completely meet-irreducible element of ${{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}$ and let us assume that $\sigma_A  = \bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{ \relax{S}}_{A}}}_{i\in I} \sigma_{i,A}$ for $ \sigma_{i,A}\in \overline{ \relax{S}}_{A}$ for any $i\in I$. We have then $(\sigma_A \widetilde{\otimes} \sigma_B) = ((\bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{ \relax{S}}_{A}}}_{i\in I} \sigma_{i,A})\widetilde{\otimes}  \sigma_B)=\bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}}_{i\in I} ( \sigma_{i,A}\widetilde{\otimes}  \sigma_B)$.  On another part, $\sigma_A \widetilde{\otimes} \sigma_B$ being completely meet-irreducible in ${{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}$, there exists $k\in I$ such that $\sigma_A \widetilde{\otimes} \sigma_B=\sigma_{k,A} \widetilde{\otimes} \sigma_B$, i.e, $\sigma_A=\sigma_{k,A}$. As a conclusion, $\sigma_A$ is completely meet-irreducible. In the same way, $\sigma_B$ is completely meet-irreducible.  As a first result, pure states of ${{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}$ are necessarily of the form $\sigma_A \widetilde{\otimes} \sigma_B$ with $\sigma_A \in \overline{ \relax{S}}{}^{\;{}^{pure}}_{A}, \sigma_B \in \overline{ \relax{S}}{}^{\;{}^{pure}}_{B}$.\\
Conversely, let us consider $\sigma_A$ a pure state of $\overline{ \relax{S}}_{A}$ and $\sigma_B$ a pure state of $\overline{ \relax{S}}_{B}$, and let us suppose that $ (\bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}}_{i\in I} \sigma_{i,A}\widetilde{\otimes}  \sigma_{i,B})  =  (\sigma_A \widetilde{\otimes} \sigma_B)$ with $\sigma_{i,A}\in \overline{ \relax{S}}_{A}$ and $\sigma_{i,B}\in \overline{ \relax{S}}_{B}$ for any $i\in I$. We now exploit the two conditions $(\bigsqcap{}^{{}_{{ \relax{S}}_{A}}}_{k\in I}\; \sigma_{k,A}) = \sigma_{A}$ and $(\bigsqcap{}^{{}_{{ \relax{S}}_{B}}}_{m\in I} \;\sigma_{m,B}) = \sigma_{B}$ derived from the expansion ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@developmentetildeordersimplify\endcsname\@firstoftwo{developmentetildeordersimplify}}}).  From $\sigma_A\in Max(\overline{ \relax{S}}_{A})$ and $\sigma_B\in Max(\overline{ \relax{S}}_{B})$, we deduce that $\sigma_{i,A} = \sigma_A$ and $\sigma_{j,B} = \sigma_B$ for any $i,j\in I$.
