As a second result, we have then obtained that the state $(\sigma_A \widetilde{\otimes} \sigma_B)$, with $\sigma_A$ a pure state of $\overline{ \relax{S}}_{A}$ and $\sigma_B$ a pure state of $\overline{ \relax{S}}_{B}$, is completely meet-irreducible.\\
From the expansion ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@developmentetildeordersimplify\endcsname\@firstoftwo{developmentetildeordersimplify}}}), we deduce also immediately that $(\sigma_A \widetilde{\otimes} \sigma_B)\in Max({{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB})$ as long as $\sigma_A\in Max(\overline{ \relax{S}}_{A})$ and $\sigma_B\in Max(\overline{ \relax{S}}_{B})$.
<!-- end proof-58 -->
<!-- theorem-28: body_md -->
\label{theoremA4Ptilde}
\begin{eqnarray}
&&\forall \sigma \in {{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}, \;\; \sigma= \bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}}  \underline{\,\sigma\,}_{{}_{ {{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}},\;\;\textit{\rm where}\;\;
\underline{\,\sigma\,}_{{}_{ {{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}}=
({{{ \overline{S}}}}{}_{AB}^{\,{}^{pure}} \cap (\uparrow^{{}^{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}}\!\!\!\! \sigma) ).
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end theorem-28 -->
<!-- proof-59: body_md -->
Let us fix $\sigma \in {{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}$.\\ 
We note that $\sigma \sqsubseteq_{{}_{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}} \sigma'$ for any $\sigma'\in ({{{ \overline{S}}}}{}_{AB}^{\,{}^{pure}} \cap (\uparrow^{{}^{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}}\!\!\!\! \sigma)) $ and then $\sigma \sqsubseteq_{{}_{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}} \bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}}  \underline{\sigma}_{{}_{ {{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}}$. \\
Secondly,  denoting  
$\sigma:=(\bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}}_{i\in I} \sigma_{i,A}\widetilde{\otimes}  \sigma_{i,B})$, we note immediately that, for any 
$\sigma_{A} \in \overline{ \relax{S}}_{A}^{pure}$ and $\sigma_{B} \in \overline{ \relax{S}}_{B}^{pure}$, if 
$\sigma_{A}\sqsupseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}_{A}}} \sigma_{i,A}$ and $ \sigma_{B}\sqsupseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}_{B}}} \sigma_{i,B}$, then $(\sigma_{A}\widetilde{\otimes}  \sigma_{B}) \sqsupseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}_{AB}}} \sigma$, i.e. $(\sigma_{A}\widetilde{\otimes}  \sigma_{B}) \in \underline{\sigma}_{{}_{ {{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}}$. As a consequence, we have
\begin{eqnarray}
(\bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}}_{i\in I}\bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}}_{\sigma_{A} \in \overline{ \relax{S}}_{A}^{pure}\;\vert\; \sigma_{A}\sqsupseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}_{A}}} \sigma_{i,A}}\bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}}_{\sigma_{B} \in \overline{ \relax{S}}_{B}^{pure}\;\vert\; \sigma_{B}\sqsupseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}_{B}}} \sigma_{i,B}} \sigma_{A}\widetilde{\otimes}  \sigma_{B}) \sqsupseteq_{{}_{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}} \bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}}  \underline{\sigma}_{{}_{ {{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}}.\;\;\;\;\;\;\;
\end{eqnarray}
Endly, we have
\begin{eqnarray}
\sigma &=&\bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}}_{i\in I} \sigma_{i,A}\widetilde{\otimes}  \sigma_{i,B} =  
\bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}}_{i\in I} (\bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}}_{\sigma_{A} \in \overline{ \relax{S}}_{A}^{pure}\;\vert\; \sigma_{A}\sqsupseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}_{A}}} \sigma_{i,A}}\sigma_{A})\widetilde{\otimes}  (\bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}}_{\sigma_{B} \in \overline{ \relax{S}}_{B}^{pure}\;\vert\; \sigma_{B}\sqsupseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}_{B}}} \sigma_{i,B}}\sigma_{B})\nonumber\\
&= & 
\bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}}_{i\in I}\bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}}_{\sigma_{A} \in \overline{ \relax{S}}_{A}^{pure}\;\vert\; \sigma_{A}\sqsupseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}_{A}}} \sigma_{i,A}}\bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}}_{\sigma_{B} \in \overline{ \relax{S}}_{B}^{pure}\;\vert\; \sigma_{B}\sqsupseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}_{B}}} \sigma_{i,B}} \sigma_{A}\widetilde{\otimes}  \sigma_{B}.
\end{eqnarray}
As a final conclusion, we obtain
\begin{eqnarray}
\sigma = (\bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}}_{i\in I}\bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}}_{\sigma_{A} \in \overline{ \relax{S}}_{A}^{pure}\;\vert\; \sigma_{A}\sqsupseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}_{A}}} \sigma_{i,A}}\bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}}_{\sigma_{B} \in \overline{ \relax{S}}_{B}^{pure}\;\vert\; \sigma_{B}\sqsupseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}_{B}}} \sigma_{i,B}} \sigma_{A}\widetilde{\otimes}  \sigma_{B}) = \bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}}  \underline{\sigma}_{{}_{ {{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}}.\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end proof-59 -->
<!-- theorem-29: body_md -->
\label{formulacupStilde}
Let $\widetilde{\sigma}_{AB}$ and $\widetilde{\sigma}'_{AB}$ be two elements of ${{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}$ having a common upper-bound. Then the supremum of $\{\widetilde{\sigma}_{AB},\widetilde{\sigma}'_{AB}\}$ exists in ${{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}$ and its expression is given by
\begin{eqnarray}
\widetilde{\sigma}_{AB} \sqcup_{{}_{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}} \widetilde{\sigma}'_{AB} = \bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}}_{\widetilde{\sigma} \in (\underline{\widetilde{\sigma}_{AB}}_{{}_{ {{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}}\!\!\!\!\!\!\!\!\!\cap\; \underline{\widetilde{\sigma}'_{AB}}_{{}_{ {{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}}\!\!\!\!\!\!\!\!\!)} \; \widetilde{\sigma}\label{formulacupPtilde2}
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end theorem-29 -->
<!-- proof-60: body_md -->
As long as $\widetilde{\sigma}_{AB}$ and $\widetilde{\sigma}'_{AB}$ have a common upper-bound, $\underline{\widetilde{\sigma}_{AB}}\cap \underline{\widetilde{\sigma}'_{AB}}$ is not empty. Secondly, it is clear that $\widetilde{\sigma}_{AB}= (\bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}}_{\widetilde{\sigma} \in \underline{\widetilde{\sigma}_{AB}}} \; \widetilde{\sigma})\; \sqsubseteq_{{}_{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}} \bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}}_{\widetilde{\sigma} \in \underline{\widetilde{\sigma}_{AB}}\cap \underline{\widetilde{\sigma}'_{AB}}} \; \widetilde{\sigma}$ and $\widetilde{\sigma}'_{AB}= (\bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}}_{\widetilde{\sigma} \in \underline{\widetilde{\sigma}'_{AB}}} \; \widetilde{\sigma})\; \sqsubseteq_{{}_{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}} \bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}}_{\widetilde{\sigma} \in \underline{\widetilde{\sigma}_{AB}}\cap \underline{\widetilde{\sigma}'_{AB}}} \; \widetilde{\sigma}$. Then, if we suppose there exists $\widetilde{\sigma}''_{AB}$ such that $\widetilde{\sigma}_{AB}, \widetilde{\sigma}'_{AB} \sqsubseteq_{{}_{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}} \widetilde{\sigma}''_{AB}$ we can use Theorem {{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@theoremA4Ptilde\endcsname\@firstoftwo{theoremA4Ptilde}}} to obtain the decomposition $\widetilde{\sigma}''_{AB}=(\bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}}_{\widetilde{\sigma} \in \underline{\widetilde{\sigma}''_{AB}}} \; \widetilde{\sigma})$ with necessarily $\forall \widetilde{\sigma}\in \underline{\widetilde{\sigma}''_{AB}},$ $\widetilde{\sigma}_{AB} \sqsubseteq_{{}_{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}}\widetilde{\sigma}$ and $\widetilde{\sigma}'_{AB} \sqsubseteq_{{}_{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}}\widetilde{\sigma}$, i.e. $\widetilde{\sigma}\in  \underline{\widetilde{\sigma}_{AB}}\cap \underline{\widetilde{\sigma}'_{AB}}$, and then $(\bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}}_{\widetilde{\sigma} \in \underline{\widetilde{\sigma}_{AB}}\cap \underline{\widetilde{\sigma}'_{AB}}} \; \widetilde{\sigma}) \sqsubseteq_{{}_{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}} \widetilde{\sigma}''_{AB}$.
<!-- end proof-60 -->
<!-- lemma-46: body_md -->
$\overline{ \relax{S}}_{A}$ and $\overline{ \relax{S}}_{B}$ being atomic, then ${{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}$ is also atomic, i.e. 
\begin{eqnarray}
\exists { \mathcal{A}}_{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}\subseteq {{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB} & \vert &\forall \alpha_{AB}\in { \mathcal{A}}_{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}},\;\; (\bot_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}_{A}}}\widetilde{\otimes} \bot_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}_{B}}}) \raisebox{1.3ex}{\,\rotatebox{180}{$\sqsupseteq$}}\,_{{}_{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}} \alpha_{AB},\\
&&\forall \sigma_{AB} \in {{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}, \;\; \exists \alpha_{AB}\in { \mathcal{A}}_{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}\;\vert\; \alpha_{AB}\sqsubseteq_{{}_{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}} \sigma_{AB}.\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;
\end{eqnarray}
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    
The set of atoms of ${{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}$ is indeed defined by
\begin{eqnarray}
{ \mathcal{A}}_{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}} & := & \{\, (\alpha_A \widetilde{\otimes}\bot_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}_{B}}})\sqcap_{{}_{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}} (\bot_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}_{A}}}\widetilde{\otimes} \alpha_B)\;\vert\; \alpha_A\in { \mathcal{A}}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}_{A}},\; \alpha_B\in { \mathcal{A}}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}_{B}}\,\}.
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end lemma-46 -->
<!-- proof-61: body_md -->
Using the expansion ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@developmentetildeordersimplify\endcsname\@firstoftwo{developmentetildeordersimplify}}}), we deduce immediately 
\begin{eqnarray}
\forall \alpha_A\in { \mathcal{A}}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}_{A}},\forall \alpha_B\in { \mathcal{A}}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}_{B}}, && (\alpha_A \widetilde{\otimes}\bot_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}_{B}}})\sqcap_{{}_{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}} (\bot_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}_{A}}}\widetilde{\otimes} \alpha_B) \;\not\sqsubseteq_{{}_{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}} \; \bot_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}_{A}}} \widetilde{\otimes}\bot_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}_{B}}}.\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;
\end{eqnarray}
In other words,  $\bot_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}_{A}}} \widetilde{\otimes}\bot_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}_{B}}} \sqsubset_{{}_{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}}  
(\alpha_A \widetilde{\otimes}\bot_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}_{B}}})\sqcap_{{}_{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}} (\bot_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}_{A}}}\widetilde{\otimes} \alpha_B)$.\\

Secondly, let us show that, for any $\sigma_{AB}:=(\bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}}_{i\in I} \sigma_{i,A}\widetilde{\otimes} \sigma_{i,B})$ distinct from $\bot_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}_{A}}} \widetilde{\otimes}\bot_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}_{B}}}$, there exist $\alpha_A\in { \mathcal{A}}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}_{A}}$ and $\alpha_B\in { \mathcal{A}}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}_{B}}$ such that $((\alpha_A \widetilde{\otimes}\bot_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}_{B}}})\sqcap_{{}_{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}} (\bot_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}_{A}}}\widetilde{\otimes} \alpha_B)) \sqsubseteq_{{}_{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}}  \sigma_{AB}$. Using once again the expansion ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@developmentetildeordersimplify\endcsname\@firstoftwo{developmentetildeordersimplify}}}), we know that $\sigma_{AB} \sqsupset_{{}_{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}}  
\bot_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}_{A}}} \widetilde{\otimes}\bot_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}_{B}}}$ (or, in other words, $\sigma_{AB} \not\sqsubseteq_{{}_{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}}  
\bot_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}_{A}}} \widetilde{\otimes}\bot_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}_{B}}}$) implies that there exists $\varnothing \subseteq K \subseteq I$ such that $(\bigsqcap{}^{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}_{A}}}_{k\in K}\; \sigma_{k,A}) \;\sqsupset_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}_{A}}} \bot_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}_{A}}}$ and $(\bigsqcap{}^{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}_{B}}}_{m\in I-K} \;\sigma_{m,B})\; \sqsupset_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}_{B}}} \bot_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}_{B}}} $. Let us fix such a $K$ and let us choose $\alpha_A\in { \mathcal{A}}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}_{A}}$ and $\alpha_B\in { \mathcal{A}}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}_{B}}$ such that $(\bigsqcap{}^{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}_{A}}}_{k\in K}\; \sigma_{k,A}) \;\sqsupseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}_{A}}} \alpha_A$ and $(\bigsqcap{}^{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}_{B}}}_{m\in I-K} \;\sigma_{m,B})\; \sqsupseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}_{B}}} \alpha_B$.  We obtain $(\bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}}_{i\in K} \sigma_{i,A}\widetilde{\otimes} \sigma_{i,B}) \;\sqsupseteq_{{}_{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}} (\alpha_A \widetilde{\otimes} \bot_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}_{B}}})$ and $(\bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}}_{i\in I-K} \sigma_{i,A}\widetilde{\otimes} \sigma_{i,B}) \;\sqsupseteq_{{}_{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}} (\bot_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}_{A}}} \widetilde{\otimes} \alpha_B)$. As a first conclusion, we obtain $((\alpha_A \widetilde{\otimes}\bot_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}_{B}}})\sqcap_{{}_{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}} (\bot_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}_{A}}}\widetilde{\otimes} \alpha_B)) \sqsubseteq_{{}_{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}}  \sigma_{AB}$. \\

Thirdly, let us consider $\sigma_{AB}:=(\bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}}_{i\in I} \sigma_{i,A}\widetilde{\otimes} \sigma_{i,B})$ such that $\sigma_{AB} \sqsubseteq_{{}_{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}}  
(\alpha_A \widetilde{\otimes}\bot_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}_{B}}})\sqcap_{{}_{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}} (\bot_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}_{A}}}\widetilde{\otimes} \alpha_B)$. As a first case, we may have obviously $\sigma_{AB}=\bot_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}_{A}}} \widetilde{\otimes}\bot_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}_{B}}}$. If however $\sigma_{AB}\not= \bot_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}_{A}}} \widetilde{\otimes}\bot_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}_{B}}}$, the previous result implies that there exist $\alpha'_A\in { \mathcal{A}}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}_{A}}$ and $\alpha'_B\in { \mathcal{A}}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}_{B}}$ such that $((\alpha'_A \widetilde{\otimes}\bot_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}_{B}}})\sqcap_{{}_{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}} (\bot_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}_{A}}}\widetilde{\otimes} \alpha'_B)) \sqsubseteq_{{}_{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}}  \sigma_{AB}$.  Using once again the expansion ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@developmentetildeordersimplify\endcsname\@firstoftwo{developmentetildeordersimplify}}}), we deduce immediately that $\alpha_A=\alpha'_A$ and $\alpha_B=\alpha'_B$. As a result, we obtain
\begin{eqnarray}
&&\hspace{-1cm} \sigma_{AB} \sqsubseteq_{{}_{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}}  
(\alpha_A \widetilde{\otimes}\bot_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}_{B}}})\sqcap_{{}_{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}} (\bot_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}_{A}}}\widetilde{\otimes} \alpha_B) \Rightarrow \nonumber\\
&&\hspace{1cm} \left( \sigma_{AB}=\bot_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}_{A}}} \widetilde{\otimes}\bot_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}_{B}}} \;\;\textit{\rm or}\;\; \sigma_{AB}=(\alpha_A \widetilde{\otimes}\bot_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}_{B}}})\sqcap_{{}_{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}} (\bot_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}_{A}}}\widetilde{\otimes} \alpha_B) \right).\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;
\end{eqnarray}
As a second conclusion, we then obtain $\bot_{{}_{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}}\raisebox{1.3ex}{\,\rotatebox{180}{$\sqsupseteq$}}\,_{{}_{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}}  
(\alpha_A \widetilde{\otimes}\bot_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}_{B}}})\sqcap_{{}_{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}} (\bot_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}_{A}}}\widetilde{\otimes} \alpha_B)$.
<!-- end proof-61 -->
<!-- definition-46: body_md -->
We define the map $\star$ from ${{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}\smallsetminus \{\bot_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}_{A}}}\widetilde{\otimes} \bot_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}_{B}}} \}$ to itself as follows. 
\begin{eqnarray}
\forall \alpha\in \overline{ \relax{S}}{}_{A}^{{}^{pure}},\beta \in \overline{ \relax{S}}{}_{B}^{{}^{pure}} ,&& (\alpha\widetilde{\otimes}\beta)^\star := \alpha^\star\widetilde{\otimes} \bot_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}_{B}}} \sqcap_{{}_{{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}}} \bot_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}_{A}}}\widetilde{\otimes} \beta^\star\\
\forall \sigma\in {{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}\smallsetminus \{\bot_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}_{A}}}\widetilde{\otimes} \bot_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}_{B}}} \},&& \sigma^\star := \bigsqcup{}^{{}^{{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}}}_{\omega\;\in \;\underline{\, \sigma \,}_{{}_{{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}}}} \omega^\star.
\end{eqnarray}
 Let $\sigma$ be an element of ${{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}$.
<!-- end definition-46 -->
<!-- theorem-30: body_md -->
The map $\star$ is involutive and order-reversing and satisfies $\forall \sigma\in {{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}\smallsetminus \{\bot_{{}_{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}}\},\;\;\;\; \neg \;\widehat{\sigma^{\star}\sigma}{}^{{}^{{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}}}$.
<!-- end theorem-30 -->
<!-- proof-62: body_md -->
First of all, the order-reversing property is easy to derive. Indeed, $\sigma\sqsupseteq_{{}_{{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}}}\sigma'$ implies $\underline{\, \sigma \,}_{{}_{{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}}}\subseteq \underline{\, \sigma' \,}_{{}_{{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}}}$, and then implies $\sigma^\star \sqsubseteq_{{}_{{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}}}\sigma'{}^\star$.\\
Let us now consider $((\alpha\widetilde{\otimes}\beta)^\star)^\star$ for $\alpha\in \overline{ \relax{S}}{}_{A}^{{}^{pure}},\beta \in \overline{ \relax{S}}{}_{B}^{{}^{pure}}$. Due to the order-reversing property and the fact that $(\alpha\widetilde{\otimes}\beta)^\star$ is an atom, we know that $((\alpha\widetilde{\otimes}\beta)^\star)^\star$ is an element of ${{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}^{\;{}^{pure}}$. A direct computation shows that $((\alpha\widetilde{\otimes}\beta)^\star)^\star
\sqsubseteq_{{}_{{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}}}
\alpha\widetilde{\otimes}\beta$. Indeed, for any $\omega\in \underline{\alpha^\star}_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}_{A}}}$ and any $\omega'\in \overline{ \relax{S}}{}_{B}^{{}^{pure}}$, we have $\omega^\star \widetilde{\otimes} \bot_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}_{B}}} \sqcap_{{}_{{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}}} \bot_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}_{A}}}\widetilde{\otimes} \omega'{}^\star  \sqsubseteq_{{}_{{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}}} \alpha \widetilde{\otimes} \beta$. And for any $\omega\in \underline{\beta^\star}_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}_{B}}}$ and any $\omega'\in \overline{ \relax{S}}{}_{A}^{{}^{pure}}$, we have $\omega'{}^\star \widetilde{\otimes} \bot_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}_{B}}} \sqcap_{{}_{{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}}} \bot_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}_{A}}}\widetilde{\otimes} \omega{}^\star  \sqsubseteq_{{}_{{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}}} \alpha \widetilde{\otimes} \beta$. Using these two results, we obtain $(\alpha^\star\widetilde{\otimes} \bot_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}_{B}}} \sqcap_{{}_{{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}}} \bot_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}_{A}}}\widetilde{\otimes} \beta^\star)^\star  \sqsubseteq_{{}_{{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}}} \alpha \widetilde{\otimes} \beta$. As a first conclusion, we then obtain $((\alpha\widetilde{\otimes}\beta)^\star)^\star
=\alpha\widetilde{\otimes}\beta$\\
Now, using the order-reversing property, we deduce 
\begin{eqnarray}
(\sigma^\star)^\star := (\bigsqcup{}^{{}^{{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}}}_{\omega\;\in \;\underline{\, \sigma \,}_{{}_{{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}}}} \omega^\star)^\star=\bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}}}_{\omega\;\in \;\underline{\, \sigma \,}_{{}_{{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}}}} (\omega^\star)^\star=\bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}}}_{\omega\;\in \;\underline{\, \sigma \,}_{{}_{{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}}}} \omega=\sigma
\end{eqnarray}
The property $\forall \sigma\in { \relax{S}}'\smallsetminus \{\bot_{{}_{ \relax{S}'}}\}, \neg \;\widehat{\sigma^{\star}\sigma}{}^{{}^{{ \relax{S}'}}}$ is also required for the map $\star$. This property is easy to check using the formula ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@developmentetildeordersimplify\endcsname\@firstoftwo{developmentetildeordersimplify}}}).  Indeed, for any $\{\,(\sigma_{i,A},\sigma_{i,B})\;\vert\;i\in I\}\subseteq \overline{ \relax{S}}_{A}^{{}^{pure}}\times \overline{ \relax{S}}_{B}^{{}^{pure}}$ and any $(\sigma_{A},\sigma_{B})\in \overline{ \relax{S}}{}_{A}^{{}^{pure}}\times \overline{ \relax{S}}{}_{B}^{{}^{pure}}$, we have that
\begin{eqnarray}
\left(\bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}}_{i\in I} \sigma_{i,A}\widetilde{\otimes} \sigma_{i,B}\right)\sqsubseteq_{{}_{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}}
\sigma_{A}\widetilde{\otimes}_{{}_{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}}\sigma_{B}
\end{eqnarray}
is equivalent to
\begin{eqnarray}
 &&\hspace{-1cm}
\left( (\bigsqcap{}^{{}_{{ \relax{S}}_{A}}}_{k\in I}\; \sigma_{k,A}) \;\sqsubseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}_{A}}}\sigma_{A}
\;\;\textit{\rm and}\;\;
(\bigsqcap{}^{{}_{{ \relax{S}}_{B}}}_{m\in I} \;\sigma_{m,B})\; \sqsubseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}_{B}}} \sigma_{B}
\;\;\textit{\rm and}\;\;\right.\nonumber\\
&&\left.\left(\forall \varnothing \varsubsetneq K  \varsubsetneq I, \;\; (\bigsqcap{}^{{}_{{ \relax{S}}_{A}}}_{k\in K}\; \sigma_{k,A}) \;\sqsubseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}_{A}}}\sigma_{A}\;\;\;\textit{\rm or}\;\;\; (\bigsqcap{}^{{}_{{ \relax{S}}_{B}}}_{m\in I-K} \;\sigma_{m,B})\; \sqsubseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}_{B}}} \sigma_{B}\right) \right).\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;
\end{eqnarray}
On another part, 
\begin{eqnarray}
\left(\bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}}_{i\in I} \sigma_{i,A}\widetilde{\otimes} \sigma_{i,B}\right)^\star=\left(\bigsqcup{}^{{}^{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}}_{i\in I}(\sigma_{i,A}^\star\widetilde{\otimes} \bot_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}_{B}}} \sqcap_{{}_{{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}}} \bot_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}_{A}}}\widetilde{\otimes} \sigma_{i,B}^\star)\right) 
\sqsubseteq_{{}_{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}}
\sigma_{A}\widetilde{\otimes}_{{}_{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}}\sigma_{B}\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;
\end{eqnarray}
is equivalent to
\begin{eqnarray}
 &&\hspace{-1cm}
\left( (\bigsqcup{}^{{}_{{ \relax{S}}_{A}}}_{k\in I}\; \sigma_{k,A}^\star) \;\sqsubseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}_{A}}}\sigma_{A}
\;\;\textit{\rm or}\;\;
(\bigsqcup{}^{{}_{{ \relax{S}}_{B}}}_{m\in I} \;\sigma_{m,B}^\star)\; \sqsubseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}_{B}}} \sigma_{B}
\;\;\textit{\rm or}\;\;\right.\nonumber\\
&&\left.\left(\exists \varnothing \varsubsetneq K  \varsubsetneq I, \;\; (\bigsqcup{}^{{}_{{ \relax{S}}_{A}}}_{k\in K}\; \sigma_{k,A}^\star) \;\sqsubseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}_{A}}}\sigma_{A}\;\;\;\textit{\rm and}\;\;\; (\bigsqcup{}^{{}_{{ \relax{S}}_{B}}}_{m\in I-K} \;\sigma_{m,B}^\star)\; \sqsubseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}_{B}}} \sigma_{B}\right) \right).\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;
\end{eqnarray}
As a conclusion, we obtain that either there exists $\varnothing \varsubsetneq K  \subseteq I$ such that $(\bigsqcap{}^{{}_{{ \relax{S}}_{A}}}_{k\in K}\; \sigma_{k,A})$ and $(\bigsqcup{}^{{}_{{ \relax{S}}_{A}}}_{k\in K}\; \sigma_{k,A}^\star)$ admit $\sigma_A$ as their common upper bound, or there exists $\varnothing \varsubsetneq K  \subseteq I$ such that $(\bigsqcap{}^{{}_{{ \relax{S}}_{B}}}_{k\in K}\; \sigma_{k,B})$ and $(\bigsqcup{}^{{}_{{ \relax{S}}_{B}}}_{k\in K}\; \sigma_{k,B}^\star)$ admit $\sigma_B$ as their common upper bound. We have then obtained a contradiction.  Hence, $\left(\bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}}_{i\in I} \sigma_{i,A}\widetilde{\otimes} \sigma_{i,B}\right)$ and $\left(\bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}}_{i\in I} \sigma_{i,A}\widetilde{\otimes} \sigma_{i,B}\right)^\star$ do not admit any common upper bound in ${{{ \overline{S}}}}{}_{AB}^{\,{}^{pure}}$.
<!-- end proof-62 -->
<!-- theorem-31: body_md -->
\label{firstcoveringlemma}
Let us suppose that $\overline{ \relax{S}}_A$ and $\overline{ \relax{S}}_B$ both satisfy the following basic property
\begin{eqnarray}
\hspace{-0.5cm}\forall \alpha,\beta\in \overline{ \relax{S}}{}^{{}^{pure}},&& \beta\not=\alpha \;\;\Rightarrow \;\; (\alpha\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\beta) \raisebox{1.3ex}{\,\rotatebox{180}{$\sqsupseteq$}}\,_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\alpha,\beta.\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\label{coveringpropertySbarpre}
\end{eqnarray}
Then ${{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}$ satisfies the same property. \\
In other words, for any $\sigma,\omega\in {{{ \overline{S}}}}{}_{AB}^{{}^{pure}}$ such that $\omega\not=\sigma$ we have then $(\omega\sqcap_{{}_{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}}\sigma)\raisebox{1.3ex}{\,\rotatebox{180}{$\sqsupseteq$}}\,_{{}_{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}}\sigma,\omega$.
<!-- end theorem-31 -->
<!-- proof-63: body_md -->
Trivial consequence of the expansion formula ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@developmentetildeordersimplify\endcsname\@firstoftwo{developmentetildeordersimplify}}}).
<!-- end proof-63 -->
<!-- theorem-32: body_md -->
\label{secondcoveringlemma}
Let us suppose that $\overline{ \relax{S}}_A$ and $\overline{ \relax{S}}_B$ both satisfy the following basic property
\begin{eqnarray}
\hspace{-0.5cm}\forall \lambda,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,\delta\in \overline{ \relax{S}}{}^{{}^{pure}} \;\textit{\rm distinct},&& (\,(\alpha\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{\relax{S}}}}\beta)\not=(\gamma\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{\relax{S}}}}\delta)\;\;\;\textit{\rm and}\;\;\;(\alpha\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{\relax{S}}}}\beta),(\gamma\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{\relax{S}}}}\delta)\raisebox{1.3ex}{\,\rotatebox{180}{$\sqsupseteq$}}\,_{{}_{\relax{S}}}\lambda \,) \;\;\Rightarrow \nonumber\\
&&\hspace{1cm} (\alpha\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\beta\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\gamma\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\delta) \raisebox{1.3ex}{\,\rotatebox{180}{$\sqsupseteq$}}\,_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}(\alpha\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{\relax{S}}}}\beta),(\gamma\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{\relax{S}}}}\delta).\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\label{secondcoveringpropertySbarpre}
\end{eqnarray}
Then ${{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}$ satisfies the same property.  \\
In other words, if we consider $\lambda,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,\delta\in {{{ \overline{S}}}}{}_{AB}^{{}^{pure}}$ distinct, such that $(\,(\alpha\sqcap_{{}_{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}}\beta)\not=(\gamma\sqcap_{{}_{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}}\delta)$ and $(\alpha\sqcap_{{}_{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}}\beta),(\gamma\sqcap_{{}_{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}}\delta)\raisebox{1.3ex}{\,\rotatebox{180}{$\sqsupseteq$}}\,_{{}_{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}}\lambda \,)$, we have then $(\alpha\sqcap_{{}_{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}}\beta\sqcap_{{}_{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}}\gamma\sqcap_{{}_{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}}\delta) \raisebox{1.3ex}{\,\rotatebox{180}{$\sqsupseteq$}}\,_{{}_{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}}(\alpha\sqcap_{{}_{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}}\beta),(\gamma\sqcap_{{}_{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}}\delta)$.
<!-- end theorem-32 -->
<!-- proof-64: body_md -->
Direct consequence of the expansion formula ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@developmentetildeordersimplify\endcsname\@firstoftwo{developmentetildeordersimplify}}}). Indeed, $\lambda,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,\delta\in {{{ \overline{S}}}}{}_{AB}^{{}^{pure}}$ all distinct with $(\,(\alpha\sqcap_{{}_{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}}\beta)\not=(\gamma\sqcap_{{}_{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}}\delta)$ and $(\alpha\sqcap_{{}_{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}}\beta),(\gamma\sqcap_{{}_{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}}\delta)\raisebox{1.3ex}{\,\rotatebox{180}{$\sqsupseteq$}}\,_{{}_{{{{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}}}}}\lambda \,)$, imply that we are in one of the following cases (we denote $\lambda:=\sigma_\lambda\widetilde{\otimes}\kappa_\lambda$, $\alpha:=\sigma_\alpha\widetilde{\otimes}\kappa_\alpha$, $\beta:=\sigma_\beta\widetilde{\otimes}\kappa_\beta$,$\gamma:=\sigma_\gamma\widetilde{\otimes}\kappa_\gamma$, $\delta:=\sigma_\delta\widetilde{\otimes}\kappa_\delta$ with $\sigma_\lambda,\sigma_\alpha,\sigma_\beta,\sigma_\gamma,\sigma_\delta\in {{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}}{}_{A}^{{}^{pure}}$, $\kappa_\lambda,\sigma_\alpha,\sigma_\beta,\sigma_\gamma,\sigma_\delta\in {{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}}{}_{B}^{{}^{pure}}$): \\
(1)  $\kappa_\alpha=\kappa_\beta=\kappa_\lambda$ and $\kappa_\gamma=\kappa_\delta=\kappa_\lambda$ and $(\sigma_\alpha\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{\relax{S}_A}}}\sigma_\beta),(\sigma_\gamma\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{\relax{S}}_A}}\sigma_\delta)\raisebox{1.3ex}{\,\rotatebox{180}{$\sqsupseteq$}}\,_{{}_{\overline{\relax{S}_A}}}\sigma_\lambda$ and $(\sigma_\alpha\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{\relax{S}}_A}}\sigma_\beta)\not=(\sigma_\gamma\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{\relax{S}}_A}}\sigma_\delta)$.\\
(2) $\sigma_\alpha=\sigma_\beta=\sigma_\lambda$ and $\sigma_\gamma=\sigma_\delta=\sigma_\lambda$ and $(\kappa_\alpha\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{\relax{S}_B}}}\kappa_\beta),(\kappa_\gamma\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{\relax{S}}_B}}\kappa_\delta)\raisebox{1.3ex}{\,\rotatebox{180}{$\sqsupseteq$}}\,_{{}_{\overline{\relax{S}}_B}}\kappa_\lambda$ and $(\kappa_\alpha\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{\relax{S}}_B}}\kappa_\beta)\not=(\kappa_\gamma\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{\relax{S}}_B}}\kappa_\delta)$.\\
(3) $\sigma_\alpha=\sigma_\beta=\sigma_\lambda$ and $\kappa_\gamma=\kappa_\delta=\kappa_\lambda$ and $(\kappa_\alpha\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{\relax{S}_B}}}\kappa_\beta)\raisebox{1.3ex}{\,\rotatebox{180}{$\sqsupseteq$}}\,_{{}_{\overline{\relax{S}}_B}}\kappa_\lambda$ and $(\sigma_\gamma\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{\relax{S}_A}}}\sigma_\delta)\raisebox{1.3ex}{\,\rotatebox{180}{$\sqsupseteq$}}\,_{{}_{\overline{\relax{S}}_A}}\sigma_\lambda$.\\
(4) $\kappa_\alpha=\kappa_\beta=\kappa_\lambda$ and $\sigma_\gamma=\sigma_\delta=\sigma_\lambda$ and $(\sigma_\alpha\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{\relax{S}_A}}}\sigma_\beta)\raisebox{1.3ex}{\,\rotatebox{180}{$\sqsupseteq$}}\,_{{}_{\overline{\relax{S}}_A}}\sigma_\lambda$ and $(\kappa_\gamma\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{\relax{S}_B}}}\kappa_\delta)\raisebox{1.3ex}{\,\rotatebox{180}{$\sqsupseteq$}}\,_{{}_{\overline{\relax{S}}_B}}\kappa_\lambda$.\\
In the case (1) we then apply the property ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@secondcoveringpropertySbarpre\endcsname\@firstoftwo{secondcoveringpropertySbarpre}}}) satisfied by ${{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}}{}_{A}$ to conclude\\
In the case (2) we then apply the property ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@secondcoveringpropertySbarpre\endcsname\@firstoftwo{secondcoveringpropertySbarpre}}}) satisfied by ${{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}}{}_{B}$ to conclude.\\
In the case (3) we just observe that $(\alpha\sqcap_{{}_{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}}\beta\sqcap_{{}_{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}}\gamma\sqcap_{{}_{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}}\delta)=(\sigma_\gamma\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{\relax{S}_A}}}\sigma_\delta)\widetilde{\otimes}\kappa_\lambda \sqcap_{{}_{\overline{S}_{AB}}} \sigma_\lambda \widetilde{\otimes}(\kappa_\alpha\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{\relax{S}_B}}}\kappa_\beta)$ and we recall that 
$(\kappa_\alpha\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{\relax{S}}_A}}\kappa_\beta)\raisebox{1.3ex}{\,\rotatebox{180}{$\sqsupseteq$}}\,_{{}_{\overline{\relax{S}}_B}}\kappa_\lambda$ and $(\sigma_\gamma\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{\relax{S}}_A}}\sigma_\delta)\raisebox{1.3ex}{\,\rotatebox{180}{$\sqsupseteq$}}\,_{{}_{\overline{\relax{S}}_A}}\sigma_\lambda$ to conclude.\\
The case (4) is similar to the case (3).
<!-- end proof-64 -->
<!-- theorem-33: body_md -->
The minimal tensor product is adequate for the description of bipartite deterministic experiments.
<!-- end theorem-33 -->
<!-- proof-65: body_md -->
By assumption, ${ \relax{S}}_{A}$ and ${ \relax{S}}_{B}$ are deterministic spaces of states and then ${ \relax{S}}_{A}$ and ${ \relax{S}}_{B}$ admit trivial real structures (see  property ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@starsimplex\endcsname\@firstoftwo{starsimplex}}}) ) with ${ \relax{S}}_{A}=\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{A}}$ and ${ \relax{S}}_{B}=\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{B}}$.  We then consider ${ \relax{S}}_{A}\boxtimes { \relax{S}}_{B}=\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{A}}\widetilde{\otimes}\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{B}}=\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{A}}{\otimes}\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{B}}$.\\
First of all, we observe that the requirements ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@tensorinfimum\endcsname\@firstoftwo{tensorinfimum}}}) and ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@tensorbot\endcsname\@firstoftwo{tensorbot}}}) are direct consequences of Theorem {{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@theoremaxiomA1bipartitepre\endcsname\@firstoftwo{theoremaxiomA1bipartitepre}}} and Theorem {{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@bottomcompound\endcsname\@firstoftwo{bottomcompound}}}. \\
Then, because of the Theorem {{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@SASBditribandcup\endcsname\@firstoftwo{SASBditribandcup}}}, we know that ${ \relax{S}}_{A} {\boxtimes} { \relax{S}}_{B}$ is also a deterministic space of states, and then ${ \relax{S}}_{A} {\boxtimes} { \relax{S}}_{B}$ admits a real structure according to ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@starsimplex\endcsname\@firstoftwo{starsimplex}}}). This real structure $(\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{A} \boxtimes { \relax{S}}_{B}},\star)$ is simply given by $\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{A} \boxtimes { \relax{S}}_{B}}=\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{A}} \widetilde{\otimes} \overline{{ \relax{S}}_{B}}$ and the star $\star$ is the involution defined in ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@starsimplex\endcsname\@firstoftwo{starsimplex}}}).\\
Secondly, the requirement ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@inclusionpuretensors\endcsname\@firstoftwo{inclusionpuretensors}}}) is guarantied by Lemma {{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@lemmainclusiontensor\endcsname\@firstoftwo{lemmainclusiontensor}}} and the basic properties ${ \relax{S}}_{A}=\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{A}}$ and ${ \relax{S}}_{B}=\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{B}}$.\\
Thirdly, the requirements ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@pitensor=tensorpi1pre\endcsname\@firstoftwo{pitensor=tensorpi1pre}}}) and ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@pitensor=tensorpi2pre\endcsname\@firstoftwo{pitensor=tensorpi2pre}}}) are guarantied by the properties ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@pitensor=tensorpi1preminimal\endcsname\@firstoftwo{pitensor=tensorpi1preminimal}}}) and ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@pitensor=tensorpi2preminimal\endcsname\@firstoftwo{pitensor=tensorpi2preminimal}}}) using ${ \relax{S}}_{A}=\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{A}}$ and ${ \relax{S}}_{B}=\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{B}}$.\\
Endly, the requirement ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@requirementpartialtraces\endcsname\@firstoftwo{requirementpartialtraces}}}) is guarantied by Theorem {{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@theorempartialtracesminimal\endcsname\@firstoftwo{theorempartialtracesminimal}}}.
<!-- end proof-65 -->
<!-- definition-47: body_md -->
\label{definitiongenerictensorproduct}
We define the tensor product of ${ \relax{S}}_A={ \relax{J}}^c_{{\overline{ \relax{S}}_A}}$ and ${ \relax{S}}_B={ \relax{J}}^c_{{\overline{ \relax{S}}_B}}$ denoted ${ \relax{S}}_A\widehat{\otimes}{ \relax{S}}_B$ by
\begin{eqnarray}
{ \relax{S}}_A\;\widehat{\otimes}\; { \relax{S}}_B &:=& { \relax{J}}^c_{{\overline{ \relax{S}}_A}\widetilde{\otimes}{\overline{ \relax{S}}_B}}
\end{eqnarray}
We note that the ontic completion of $(\overline{ \relax{S}}_{A}\widetilde{\otimes} \overline{ \relax{S}}_{B},\star)$ can be defined because the basic conditions are fulfilled.
<!-- end definition-47 -->
<!-- lemma-47: body_md -->
\label{generictensordowncomplete}
${{{ \relax{S}}_A}\widehat{\otimes} {{ \relax{S}}_{B}}}$ is a down complete Inf semi-lattice. 
The lowest bound is given by $\bot_{{}_{{{{ \relax{S}}_A}\widehat{\otimes} {{ \relax{S}}_{B}}}}}=\bot_{{}_{{{\overline{ \relax{S}}_A}\widetilde{\otimes} {\overline{ \relax{S}}_{B}}}}}$.
<!-- end lemma-47 -->
<!-- proof-66: body_md -->
Direct consequence of the construction of the ontic completion $(\!( \overline{ \relax{S}}_{A}\widetilde{\otimes} \overline{ \relax{S}}_{B},\star)\!)_c$.
<!-- end proof-66 -->
<!-- lemma-48: body_md -->
\label{generictensorstarstructure}
${{{ \relax{S}}_A}\widehat{\otimes} {{ \relax{S}}_{B}}}$ admits a real structure given by $({\overline{ \relax{S}}_A}\widetilde{\otimes} {\overline{ \relax{S}}_B},\star)$.
<!-- end lemma-48 -->
<!-- proof-67: body_md -->
Direct consequence of Theorem {{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@theoremcompletion\endcsname\@firstoftwo{theoremcompletion}}} for ${{{ \relax{S}}_A}\widehat{\otimes} {{ \relax{S}}_{B}}}$ defined as the ontic completion of $({\overline{ \relax{S}}_A}\widetilde{\otimes} {\overline{ \relax{S}}_B},\star)$.
<!-- end proof-67 -->
<!-- lemma-49: body_md -->
\label{generictensorpuretensors}
There exists a map $\iota^{{{ \relax{S}}_A}\widehat{\otimes} {{ \relax{S}}_{B}}}$ from $\overline{{ \relax{S}}_A} {\times} \overline{{ \relax{S}}_{B}}$ to ${{{ \relax{S}}_A}\widehat{\otimes} {{ \relax{S}}_{B}}}$.
<!-- end lemma-49 -->
<!-- proof-68: body_md -->
Trivial
<!-- end proof-68 -->
<!-- lemma-50: body_md -->
\label{generictensorlocaltomography}
\begin{eqnarray}
&&\hspace{-1cm}\forall \; \left(\bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{{{{ \relax{S}}_A}\widehat{\otimes} {{ \relax{S}}_{B}}}}}}_{i\in I} \sigma_{i,A}\widehat{\otimes} \sigma_{i,B}\right) \in \overline{{{ \relax{S}}_A}\widehat{\otimes} {{ \relax{S}}_{B}}},\; \forall \; \left(\bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{{{{ \relax{S}}_A}\widehat{\otimes} {{ \relax{S}}_{B}}}}}}_{j\in J} \sigma'_{j,A}\widehat{\otimes} \sigma'_{j,B}\right) \in \overline{{{ \relax{S}}_A}\widehat{\otimes} {{ \relax{S}}_{B}}},\nonumber\\
&&\hspace{-1cm}\left(\forall {\relax{l}}_A\in { \relax{E}}_{A},{\relax{l}}_B\in { \relax{E}}_{B},\;\; \bigwedge{}_{i\in I}{\epsilon}\,{}^{{ \relax{S}}_A}_{{\relax{l}}_A} (\sigma_{i,A})\bullet {\epsilon}\,{}^{{ \relax{S}}_B}_{{\relax{l}}_B} (\sigma_{i,B})=\bigwedge{}_{j\in J}{\epsilon}\,{}^{{ \relax{S}}_A}_{{\relax{l}}_A} (\sigma'_{j,A})\bullet {\epsilon}\,{}^{{ \relax{S}}_B}_{{\relax{l}}_B} (\sigma'_{j,B}) \right)\nonumber\\
&&\hspace{4cm} \;\Rightarrow\; (\,\bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{{{{ \relax{S}}_A}\widehat{\otimes} {{ \relax{S}}_{B}}}}}}_{i\in I} \sigma_{i,A}\widehat{\otimes} \sigma_{i,B} = \bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{{{{ \relax{S}}_A}\widehat{\otimes} {{ \relax{S}}_{B}}}}}}_{j\in J} \sigma'_{j,A}\widehat{\otimes} \sigma'_{j,B}\,).\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end lemma-50 -->
<!-- proof-69: body_md -->
Direct consequence of the definition of the tensor product.
<!-- end proof-69 -->
<!-- lemma-51: body_md -->
\label{generictensorbimorphic}
We have the two required bimorphic properties for the tensor product. Explicitly, for any $\{\,\sigma_{i,A}\;\vert\; i\in I\,\}\subseteq \overline{{ \relax{S}}_{A}}$, $\{\,\sigma_{j,B}\;\vert\; j\in J\,\}\subseteq \overline{{ \relax{S}}_{B}}$, $\sigma_A\in \overline{{ \relax{S}}_{A}}$ and $\sigma_B\in \overline{{ \relax{S}}_{B}}$, we have
\begin{eqnarray}
&& (\bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{{ \relax{S}}_{A}}}}_{i\in I}\,\sigma_{i,A})\widehat{\otimes} \sigma_B =  \bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{{{{ \relax{S}}_A \widehat{\otimes} { \relax{S}}_{B}}}}}}_{i\in I} (\sigma_{i,A}\widehat{\otimes} \sigma_B),\label{pitensor=tensorpi1pregeneric}\\
&& \sigma_A \widehat{\otimes}  (\bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{{ \relax{S}}_{B}}}}_{i\in I}\,\sigma_{i,B}) =  \bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{{{{ \relax{S}}_A \widehat{\otimes} { \relax{S}}_{B}}}}}}_{i\in I} (\sigma_A \widehat{\otimes} \sigma_{i,B}).\label{pitensor=tensorpi2pregeneric}
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end lemma-51 -->
<!-- proof-70: body_md -->
Direct consequence of Lemma {{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@generictensorlocaltomography\endcsname\@firstoftwo{generictensorlocaltomography}}}.
<!-- end proof-70 -->
<!-- lemma-52: body_md -->
\label{generictensorpartialtraces}
We have the two following partial traces
\begin{eqnarray}
\hspace{-2cm}\begin{array}{rcrclccrcrcl}
&  &\zeta^{{{ \relax{S}}_{A}}{{ \relax{S}}_{B}}}_{(1)} : \;\;\;\;\;\; \overline{{ \relax{S}}_A \widehat{\otimes} { \relax{S}}_{B}} & \longrightarrow & \overline{{ \relax{S}}_{A}}  & & &  &  &\zeta^{{{ \relax{S}}_{A}}{{ \relax{S}}_{B}}}_{(2)} : \;\;\;\;\;\; \overline{{ \relax{S}}_A \widehat{\otimes} { \relax{S}}_{B}} & \longrightarrow & \overline{{ \relax{S}}_{B}}  \\
& & \bigsqcap{}^{{}^{\overline{{ \relax{S}}_A} \widetilde{\otimes} \overline{{ \relax{S}}_{B}}}}_{i\in I} \sigma_{i,A} \widetilde{\otimes} \sigma_{i,B} & \mapsto & \bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{A}}}}}_{i\in I} \sigma_{i,A}  & & & & & \bigsqcap{}^{{}^{\overline{{ \relax{S}}_A} \widetilde{\otimes} \overline{{ \relax{S}}_{B}}}}_{i\in I} \sigma_{i,A} \widetilde{\otimes} \sigma_{i,B} & \mapsto & \bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{B}}}}}_{i\in I}  \sigma_{i,B}
\end{array}
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end lemma-52 -->
<!-- proof-71: body_md -->
Direct consequence of Theorem {{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@theorempartialtracesminimal\endcsname\@firstoftwo{theorempartialtracesminimal}}}.
<!-- end proof-71 -->
<!-- theorem-34: body_md -->
The tensor product ${ \relax{S}}_{A}\widehat{\otimes} { \relax{S}}_{B}$ defined in Definition {{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@definitiongenerictensorproduct\endcsname\@firstoftwo{definitiongenerictensorproduct}}} satisfies the requirements addressed in subsection {{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@subsectioncompoundfirstremarks\endcsname\@firstoftwo{subsectioncompoundfirstremarks}}} for the description of generic bipartite experiments.
<!-- end theorem-34 -->
<!-- proof-72: body_md -->
According to subsection {{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@subsectioncompoundfirstremarks\endcsname\@firstoftwo{subsectioncompoundfirstremarks}}}, this is a direct consequence of Lemma {{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@generictensordowncomplete\endcsname\@firstoftwo{generictensordowncomplete}}}, Lemma {{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@generictensorstarstructure\endcsname\@firstoftwo{generictensorstarstructure}}}, Lemma {{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@generictensorpuretensors\endcsname\@firstoftwo{generictensorpuretensors}}}, Lemma {{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@generictensorbimorphic\endcsname\@firstoftwo{generictensorbimorphic}}}, Lemma {{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@generictensorlocaltomography\endcsname\@firstoftwo{generictensorlocaltomography}}}, Lemma {{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@generictensorpartialtraces\endcsname\@firstoftwo{generictensorpartialtraces}}}.
<!-- end proof-72 -->
<!-- theorem-35: body_md -->
\label{theoremirreducibilitytensor}
If $(\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{A}},\star)$ and $(\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{B}},\star)$ are completely indeterministic spaces of states,  then $(\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{A}}\widetilde{\otimes} \overline{{ \relax{S}}_{B}},\star)$ is also a completely indeterministic space of states.
<!-- end theorem-35 -->
<!-- proof-73: body_md -->
Let us consider $(\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{A}},\star)$ and $(\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{B}},\star)$ two completely indeterministic spaces of states. Let us consider $\sigma:=\sigma_A\widetilde{\otimes}\sigma_B, \lambda:=\lambda_A\widetilde{\otimes}\lambda_B\in (\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{A}}\widetilde{\otimes}\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{B}})^{{}^{pure}}$ such that $\sigma\underline{\perp}\lambda$. We recall that $\sigma\underline{\perp}\lambda$ means  $\lambda_A\widetilde{\otimes}\lambda_B \sqsupseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}_{A}\widetilde{\otimes} { \relax{S}}_{B}}} (\sigma_A^\star\widetilde{\otimes}\bot_{{}_{\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{B}}}} \sqcap_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}_{A}\widetilde{\otimes} { \relax{S}}_{B}}} \bot_{{}_{\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{A}}}}\widetilde{\otimes} \sigma_B^\star)$ which means $\lambda_A \sqsupseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}_{A}}}\sigma_A^\star$ or $\lambda_B \sqsupseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}_{B}}}\sigma_B^\star$, i.e. $\sigma_A\underline{\perp}\lambda_A$ or $\sigma_B\underline{\perp}\lambda_B$. Let us distinguish the three different cases.\\
(1) $\sigma_A\underline{\perp}\lambda_A$ and $\sigma_B\underline{\perp}\lambda_B$. $(\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{A}},\star)$ and $(\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{B}},\star)$ being two completely indeterministic spaces of states, we deduce that there exists $\kappa_A\in \overline{{ \relax{S}}_{A}}{}^{{}^{pure}}$ and $\kappa_B\in \overline{{ \relax{S}}_{B}}{}^{{}^{pure}}$ such that $\kappa_A\not\!\!\!\underline{\perp} \lambda_A$, $\kappa_A\not\!\!\!\underline{\perp} \sigma_A$, and $\kappa_B\not\!\!\!\underline{\perp} \lambda_B$, $\kappa_B\not\!\!\!\underline{\perp} \sigma_B$, i.e. $\kappa_A \not\sqsupseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}_{A}}}\sigma_A^\star$ and $\kappa_A \not\sqsupseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}_{A}}}\lambda_A^\star$ and $\kappa_B \not\sqsupseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}_{B}}}\lambda_B^\star$ and $\kappa_B \not\sqsupseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}_{B}}}\sigma_B^\star$.  Then, we have $(\kappa_A\widetilde{\otimes}\kappa_B) \not\sqsupseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}_{A}\widetilde{\otimes} { \relax{S}}_{B}}} (\sigma_A^\star\widetilde{\otimes}\bot_{{}_{\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{B}}}} \sqcap_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}_{A}\widetilde{\otimes} { \relax{S}}_{B}}} \bot_{{}_{\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{A}}}}\widetilde{\otimes} \sigma_B^\star)$ and $(\kappa_A\widetilde{\otimes}\kappa_B) \not\sqsupseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}_{A}\widetilde{\otimes} { \relax{S}}_{B}}} (\lambda_A^\star\widetilde{\otimes}\bot_{{}_{\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{B}}}} \sqcap_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}_{A}\widetilde{\otimes} { \relax{S}}_{B}}} \bot_{{}_{\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{A}}}}\widetilde{\otimes} \lambda_B^\star)$, i.e. $(\kappa_A\widetilde{\otimes}\kappa_B) \not\!\!\!\underline{\perp} (\sigma_A\widetilde{\otimes}\sigma_B)$ and $(\kappa_A\widetilde{\otimes}\kappa_B) \not\!\!\!\underline{\perp} (\lambda_A\widetilde{\otimes}\lambda_B)$.\\
(2) $\sigma_A\underline{\perp}\lambda_A$ and $\sigma_B\not\!\!\!\underline{\perp}\lambda_B$. $(\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{A}},\star)$ being a completely indeterministic spaces of states, we deduce that there exists $\kappa_A\in \overline{{ \relax{S}}_{A}}{}^{{}^{pure}}$ such that $\kappa_A\not\!\!\!\underline{\perp} \lambda_A$, $\kappa_A\not\!\!\!\underline{\perp} \sigma_A$, i.e. $\kappa_A \not\sqsupseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}_{A}}}\sigma_A^\star$ and $\kappa_A \not\sqsupseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}_{A}}}\lambda_A^\star$. Let us fix $\kappa_B:=\lambda_B$. We then note that  $\kappa_B \not\sqsupseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}_{B}}}\lambda_B^\star$ and $\kappa_B \not\sqsupseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}_{B}}}\sigma_B^\star$. We then have $(\kappa_A\widetilde{\otimes}\kappa_B) \not\sqsupseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}_{A}\widetilde{\otimes} { \relax{S}}_{B}}} (\sigma_A^\star\widetilde{\otimes}\bot_{{}_{\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{B}}}} \sqcap_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}_{A}\widetilde{\otimes} { \relax{S}}_{B}}} \bot_{{}_{\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{A}}}}\widetilde{\otimes} \sigma_B^\star)$ and $(\kappa_A\widetilde{\otimes}\kappa_B) \not\sqsupseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}_{A}\widetilde{\otimes} { \relax{S}}_{B}}} (\lambda_A^\star\widetilde{\otimes}\bot_{{}_{\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{B}}}} \sqcap_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}_{A}\widetilde{\otimes} { \relax{S}}_{B}}} \bot_{{}_{\overline{{ \relax{S}}_{A}}}}\widetilde{\otimes} \lambda_B^\star)$, i.e.  $(\kappa_A\widetilde{\otimes}\kappa_B) \not\!\!\!\underline{\perp} (\sigma_A\widetilde{\otimes}\sigma_B)$ and $(\kappa_A\widetilde{\otimes}\kappa_B) \not\!\!\!\underline{\perp} (\lambda_A\widetilde{\otimes}\lambda_B)$.\\
(3) idem.\\
This concludes the proof.
<!-- end proof-73 -->
<!-- definition-48: body_md -->
\label{definitionjointmorphism}
$N$ real measurement maps ${\phi}_1,\cdots,{\phi}_N\in \overline{ \relax{M}}_{ \relax{S}}$ are said to be {\em jointly compatible} iff there exists a map $\Psi_{{}_{({\phi}_1,\cdots,{\phi}_N)}}$, called {\em joint morphism}, defined from ${ \relax{S}}$ to ${\relax{B}}^{\widetilde{\otimes}N}$ and satisfying
\begin{eqnarray}
\forall \sigma_1,\sigma_2\in { \relax{S}},&& \Psi_{{}_{({\phi}_1,\cdots,{\phi}_N)}}(\sigma_1\sqcap_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma_2)=\Psi_{{}_{({\phi}_1,\cdots,{\phi}_N)}}(\sigma_1)\sqcap_{{}_{{\relax{B}}^{\widetilde{\otimes}N}}}\Psi_{{}_{({\phi}_1,\cdots,{\phi}_N)}}(\sigma_2),\label{relationsjointchannelmorphism}\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\\
&& \Psi_{{}_{({\phi}_1,\cdots,{\phi}_N)}}^\ast (\overline{ \relax{E}}_{{{\relax{B}}^{\widetilde{\otimes}N}}})\subseteq \overline{ \relax{E}}_{ \relax{S}},\label{relationsjointchannelreal}\\
\forall i=1,\cdots,N, && {\phi}_i = \zeta^{{}^{{\relax{B}}\cdots{\relax{B}}}}_{(i)}  \circ \Psi_{{}_{({\phi}_1,\cdots,{\phi}_N)}}.\label{relationsjointchannel}
\end{eqnarray}
We recall that $\zeta^{{}^{{\relax{B}}\cdots{\relax{B}}}}_{(i)} $ is the partial trace projecting the tensor product ${\relax{B}}^{\widetilde{\otimes}N}$ on its $i-$th component. Here, we have denoted by $\Psi_{{}_{({\phi}_1,\cdots,{\phi}_N)}}^\ast$ the right component of the Chu morphism $(\Psi_{{}_{({\phi}_1,\cdots,{\phi}_N)}},\Psi_{{}_{({\phi}_1,\cdots,{\phi}_N)}}^\ast)$.
<!-- end definition-48 -->
<!-- definition-49: body_md -->
A {\em compatibility context} $U$ is defined to be a subset of $\overline{ \relax{E}}_{ \relax{S}}$ such that the elements of $\{\,{ \relax{m}}_{ \relax{l}}\;\vert\; { \relax{l}}\in U\,\}$ form a family of jointly compatible real measurements. A {\em compatibility cover} ${ \mathcal{C}}$ is defined as a family of {\em maximal compatibility contexts} covering the whole set of real measurements. In other words,
\begin{eqnarray}\left\{
\begin{array}{l}
(\bigcup_{{}_{C\in { \mathcal{C}}}} C) = \overline{ \relax{E}}_{ \relax{S}}\\
\forall C,C’ \in { \mathcal{C}},\;\;\; C \subseteq C’ \;\Rightarrow \; C =C’\\
\forall C\in { \mathcal{C}},\; \textit{\rm the elements of}\;\{\,{ \relax{m}}_{ \relax{l}}\;\vert\; { \relax{l}}\in C\,\} \;\textit{\rm are jointly compatible}.
\end{array}
\right.
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end definition-49 -->
<!-- theorem-36: body_md -->
\label{theoremcompatiblemeasurements}
Let ${ \relax{S}}$ be a simplex. \\ 
We note that ${ \relax{S}}=\overline{ \relax{S}}$, $\overline{ \relax{E}}_{ \relax{S}}={ \relax{E}}_{ \relax{S}}$ and all measurements are real.\\
Let us consider any two measurement morphisms ${ \relax{m}}_{{ \relax{l}}_{(\sigma_1,\sigma'_1)}}$ and ${ \relax{m}}_{{ \relax{l}}_{(\sigma_2,\sigma'_2)}}$.  These morphisms are necessarily compatible.
<!-- end theorem-36 -->
<!-- proof-74: body_md -->
We define the map $\Psi$ as a map from ${ \relax{S}}$ to ${ \relax{B}}\widetilde{\otimes}{ \relax{B}}$ which satisfies, for any $\sigma\in { \relax{S}}$, 
\begin{eqnarray}
\Psi (\sigma) &:=& \bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{ \relax{B}}\widetilde{\otimes}{ \relax{B}}}}_{\sigma'\in \underline{\sigma}_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}}} \Psi (\sigma')\label{equalitiypsisigma}
\end{eqnarray}
and for any $\sigma\in { \relax{S}}^{{}^{pure}}=Max({ \relax{S}})$
\begin{eqnarray}
\hspace{-1cm} && \left\{
\begin{array}{ll}
\Psi(\sigma)=\textit{\bf Y}\widetilde{\otimes}\textit{\bf Y} 
&\textit{\rm if} \;\; \epsilon^{{ \relax{S}}}_{{ \relax{l}}_{(\sigma_1,\sigma'_1)}}(\sigma)=\textit{\bf Y}\;\; \textit{\rm and} \;\; \epsilon^{{ \relax{S}}}_{{ \relax{l}}_{(\sigma_2,\sigma'_2)}}(\sigma)=\textit{\bf Y},\\
\Psi(\sigma)=\textit{\bf Y}\widetilde{\otimes}\textit{\bf Y}\sqcap_{{}_{{ \relax{B}}\widetilde{\otimes}{ \relax{B}}}}  \textit{\bf Y}\widetilde{\otimes}\textit{\bf N} &\textit{\rm if} \;\; \epsilon^{{ \relax{S}}}_{{ \relax{l}}_{(\sigma_1,\sigma'_1)}}(\sigma)=\textit{\bf Y} \;\textit{\rm and}\;  \epsilon^{{ \relax{S}}}_{{ \relax{l}}_{(\sigma_2,\sigma'_2)}}(\sigma)=\bot, \\
\Psi(\sigma)=\textit{\bf Y}\widetilde{\otimes}\textit{\bf Y}\sqcap_{{}_{{ \relax{B}}\widetilde{\otimes}{ \relax{B}}}}  \textit{\bf N}\widetilde{\otimes}\textit{\bf Y} &\textit{\rm if} \;\; \epsilon^{{ \relax{S}}}_{{ \relax{l}}_{(\sigma_1,\sigma'_1)}}(\sigma)=\bot \;\textit{\rm and}\;  \epsilon^{{ \relax{S}}}_{{ \relax{l}}_{(\sigma_2,\sigma'_2)}}(\sigma)=\textit{\bf Y}, \\
\Psi(\sigma)=\textit{\bf N}\widetilde{\otimes}\textit{\bf N} &
\textit{\rm if} \;\; \epsilon^{{ \relax{S}}}_{{ \relax{l}}_{(\sigma_1,\sigma'_1)}}(\sigma)=\textit{\bf N}\;\; \textit{\rm and} \;\; \epsilon^{{ \relax{S}}}_{{ \relax{l}}_{(\sigma_2,\sigma'_2)}}(\sigma)=\textit{\bf N},\\
\Psi(\sigma)=\textit{\bf N}\widetilde{\otimes}\textit{\bf N}\sqcap_{{}_{{ \relax{B}}\widetilde{\otimes}{ \relax{B}}}}  \textit{\bf N}\widetilde{\otimes}\textit{\bf Y} &\textit{\rm if} \;\; \epsilon^{{ \relax{S}}}_{{ \relax{l}}_{(\sigma_1,\sigma'_1)}}(\sigma)=\textit{\bf N} \;\textit{\rm and}\;  \epsilon^{{ \relax{S}}}_{{ \relax{l}}_{(\sigma_2,\sigma'_2)}}(\sigma)=\bot, \\
\Psi(\sigma)=\textit{\bf N}\widetilde{\otimes}\textit{\bf N}\sqcap_{{}_{{ \relax{B}}\widetilde{\otimes}{ \relax{B}}}}  \textit{\bf Y}\widetilde{\otimes}\textit{\bf N} &\textit{\rm if} \;\; \epsilon^{{ \relax{S}}}_{{ \relax{l}}_{(\sigma_1,\sigma'_1)}}(\sigma)=\bot\;\textit{\rm and}\;  \epsilon^{{ \relax{S}}}_{{ \relax{l}}_{(\sigma_2,\sigma'_2)}}(\sigma)=\textit{\bf N} , \\
\Psi(\sigma)=\textit{\bf Y}\widetilde{\otimes}\textit{\bf N} &
\textit{\rm if} \;\; \epsilon^{{ \relax{S}}}_{{ \relax{l}}_{(\sigma_1,\sigma'_1)}}(\sigma)=\textit{\bf Y}\;\; \textit{\rm and} \;\; \epsilon^{{ \relax{S}}}_{{ \relax{l}}_{(\sigma_2,\sigma'_2)}}(\sigma)=\textit{\bf N},\\
\Psi(\sigma)=\textit{\bf N}\widetilde{\otimes}\textit{\bf Y} &
\textit{\rm if} \;\; \epsilon^{{ \relax{S}}}_{{ \relax{l}}_{(\sigma_1,\sigma'_1)}}(\sigma)=\textit{\bf N}\;\; \textit{\rm and} \;\; \epsilon^{{ \relax{S}}}_{{ \relax{l}}_{(\sigma_2,\sigma'_2)}}(\sigma)=\textit{\bf Y},\\
\Psi(\sigma)=\bot \widetilde{\otimes}\bot &
\textit{\rm if} \;\; \epsilon^{{ \relax{S}}}_{{ \relax{l}}_{(\sigma_1,\sigma'_1)}}(\sigma)=\bot\;\; \textit{\rm and} \;\; \epsilon^{{ \relax{S}}}_{{ \relax{l}}_{(\sigma_2,\sigma'_2)}}(\sigma)=\bot.
\end{array}\right. \;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\label{equalitiypsisigmapure}
\end{eqnarray}
We observe that $\Psi_{({ \relax{m}}_{{ \relax{l}}_{(\sigma_1,\sigma'_1)}},{ \relax{m}}_{{ \relax{l}}_{(\sigma_2,\sigma'_2)}})}$ is {unambiguously} defined by ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@equalitiypsisigma\endcsname\@firstoftwo{equalitiypsisigma}}}) because ${ \relax{S}}$ is a simplex and then satisfies ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@simplexdecompunique\endcsname\@firstoftwo{simplexdecompunique}}}).\\
Secondly, $\Psi_{({ \relax{m}}_{{ \relax{l}}_{(\sigma_1,\sigma'_1)}},{ \relax{m}}_{{ \relax{l}}_{(\sigma_2,\sigma'_2)}})}$ is a morphism by construction.\\
Endly, we can check easily for any $\sigma\in { \relax{S}}$ (the proof begins on each expressions of ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@equalitiypsisigmapure\endcsname\@firstoftwo{equalitiypsisigmapure}}}) by a simple computation and is extended to the whole set of elements of ${\relax{S}}$ using the expression  ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@equalitiypsisigma\endcsname\@firstoftwo{equalitiypsisigma}}}) and the homomorphic properties of ${ \relax{m}}_{{ \relax{l}}_{(\sigma_1,\sigma'_1)}}$ and ${ \relax{m}}_{{ \relax{l}}_{(\sigma_2,\sigma'_2)}}$)
\begin{eqnarray}
&&(\zeta^{{}^{{\relax{B}}{\relax{B}}}}_{(1)} \circ \Psi_{({ \relax{m}}_{{ \relax{l}}_{(\sigma_1,\sigma'_1)}},{ \relax{m}}_{{ \relax{l}}_{(\sigma_2,\sigma'_2)}})})(\sigma)={ \relax{m}}_{{ \relax{l}}_{(\sigma_1,\sigma'_1)}}(\sigma)\\
&&(\zeta^{{}^{{\relax{B}}{\relax{B}}}}_{(2)} \circ \Psi_{({ \relax{m}}_{{ \relax{l}}_{(\sigma_1,\sigma'_1)}},{ \relax{m}}_{{ \relax{l}}_{(\sigma_2,\sigma'_2)}})})(\sigma)={ \relax{m}}_{{ \relax{l}}_{(\sigma_2,\sigma'_2)}}(\sigma).
\end{eqnarray}
$\Psi$ is then the joint morphism $\Psi_{({ \relax{m}}_{{ \relax{l}}_{(\sigma_1,\sigma'_1)}},{ \relax{m}}_{{ \relax{l}}_{(\sigma_2,\sigma'_2)}})}$.
<!-- end proof-74 -->
<!-- theorem-37: body_md -->
\label{theoremNcompatiblemeasurements}
If ${ \relax{S}}$ is a simplex then the whole set of elements of $\{\,{ \relax{m}}_{{ \relax{l}}} \;\vert\; {{ \relax{l}}}\in { \relax{E}}_{ \relax{S}}\,\}$ are jointly compatible measurement maps.  In other words, the compatibility cover ${ \mathcal{C}}$ is then reduced to the singleton $\{\overline{ \relax{E}}_{ \relax{S}}\}$.
<!-- end theorem-37 -->
<!-- proof-75: body_md -->
Straightforward using the generalization of the construction used in previous Theorem for the joint-morphism.
<!-- end proof-75 -->
<!-- lemma-53: body_md -->
\label{genmeasurementselfcompatible}
If the $N-$uple of real measurement maps $({ \relax{m}}_{{ \relax{l}}_1},\cdots, { \relax{m}}_{{ \relax{l}}_N})$ are jointly compatible, then the $(N+1)-$uple of real measurement maps $({ \relax{m}}_{{ \relax{l}}_1},{ \relax{m}}_{{ \relax{l}}_1},\cdots, { \relax{m}}_{{ \relax{l}}_N})$ are jointly-compatible, for any ${ \relax{l}}_1,\cdots,{ \relax{l}}_N\in { \relax{E}}$.
<!-- end lemma-53 -->
<!-- proof-76: body_md -->
Let us consider that the $N-$uple of real measurement maps $({ \relax{m}}_{{ \relax{l}}_1},\cdots, { \relax{m}}_{{ \relax{l}}_N})$ are jointly compatible. There exists a joint morphism $\Psi_{{}_{({ \relax{m}}_{{ \relax{l}}_1},\cdots, { \relax{m}}_{{ \relax{l}}_N})}}$ satisfying the required conditions mentioned in Definition {{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@definitionjointmorphism\endcsname\@firstoftwo{definitionjointmorphism}}}.  Using the map $\varphi$ defined as a morphism from ${\relax{B}}$ to ${\relax{B}}^{\widetilde{\otimes}2}$ by 
\begin{eqnarray}
\varphi (\textit{\bf Y}):=\textit{\bf Y}\widetilde{\otimes}\textit{\bf Y} && \varphi (\textit{\bf N}):=\textit{\bf N}\widetilde{\otimes}\textit{\bf N}
\end{eqnarray}
we then build a map denoted $\Phi$ from ${ \relax{S}}$ to ${\relax{B}}^{\widetilde{\otimes}(N+1)}$ by
\begin{eqnarray}
\Phi &:= & (\varphi\widetilde{\otimes}id^{\widetilde{\otimes}(N-1)}) \circ \Psi_{{}_{({ \relax{m}}_{{ \relax{l}}_1},\cdots, { \relax{m}}_{{ \relax{l}}_N})}}
\end{eqnarray}
It is easy to check that $\Phi$ is a joint morphism for the $(N+1)-$uple of measurement maps $({ \relax{m}}_{{ \relax{l}}_1},{ \relax{m}}_{{ \relax{l}}_1},\cdots, { \relax{m}}_{{ \relax{l}}_N})$.  In other words,
\begin{eqnarray}
\Phi &=& \Psi_{{}_{({ \relax{m}}_{{ \relax{l}}_1},{ \relax{m}}_{{ \relax{l}}_1},\cdots, { \relax{m}}_{{ \relax{l}}_N})}}.
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end proof-76 -->
<!-- lemma-54: body_md -->
\label{genmeasurementconjugatecompatible} 
If the $N-$uple of real measurement maps $({ \relax{m}}_{{ \relax{l}}_1},\cdots, { \relax{m}}_{{ \relax{l}}_{N}})$ are jointly compatible, then the $(N+1)-$uple of real measurement maps $({ \relax{m}}_{\overline{{ \relax{l}}_{1}}},{ \relax{m}}_{{ \relax{l}}_{1}},\cdots, { \relax{m}}_{{ \relax{l}}_{N}})$ are also jointly-compatible.
<!-- end lemma-54 -->
<!-- proof-77: body_md -->
We first note that
\begin{eqnarray}
&&{ \relax{m}}_{\overline{\, \relax{l}\,}} = \omega \circ { \relax{m}}_{{ \relax{l}}}\\
&\textit{\rm with}& \forall \alpha\in { \relax{B}},\;\omega(\alpha):=\overline{\,\alpha\,}.
\end{eqnarray}
On another part, using the Lemma {{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@genmeasurementselfcompatible\endcsname\@firstoftwo{genmeasurementselfcompatible}}}, we know that there exists a joint morphism for for the $(N+1)-$uple of measurement maps $({ \relax{m}}_{{ \relax{l}}_1},{ \relax{m}}_{{ \relax{l}}_1},\cdots, { \relax{m}}_{{ \relax{l}}_N})$, it is denoted $\Psi_{{}_{({ \relax{m}}_{{ \relax{l}}_1},{ \relax{m}}_{{ \relax{l}}_1},\cdots, { \relax{m}}_{{ \relax{l}}_N})}}$. \\
We then  define the map denoted $\Phi'$ from ${ \relax{S}}$ to ${\relax{B}}^{\widetilde{\otimes}(N+1)}$ by
\begin{eqnarray}
\Phi &:= & (\omega \widetilde{\otimes}id^{\widetilde{\otimes}N}) \circ \Psi_{{}_{({ \relax{m}}_{{ \relax{l}}_1},{ \relax{m}}_{{ \relax{l}}_1},\cdots, { \relax{m}}_{{ \relax{l}}_N})}}.
\end{eqnarray}
We check easily that $\Phi$ is a joint morphism for the $(N+1)-$uple of real measurement maps $({ \relax{m}}_{\overline{{ \relax{l}}_{1}}},{ \relax{m}}_{{ \relax{l}}_{1}},\cdots, { \relax{m}}_{{ \relax{l}}_{N}})$. In other words,
\begin{eqnarray}
\Phi' &=& \Psi_{{}_{({ \relax{m}}_{\overline{{ \relax{l}}_1}},{ \relax{m}}_{{ \relax{l}}_1},\cdots, { \relax{m}}_{{ \relax{l}}_N})}}.
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end proof-77 -->
<!-- lemma-55: body_md -->
\label{genmeasurementconstantcompatible} 
For any $\eta\in { \relax{B}}$, we define the morphism $\tau_{\eta}$ as the constant map from ${ \relax{S}}$ to ${ \relax{B}}$ sending any state to $\eta$.\\
If the $N-$uple of real measurement maps $({ \relax{m}}_{{ \relax{l}}_{1}},\cdots, { \relax{m}}_{{ \relax{l}}_{N}})$ are jointly compatible, then the $(N+1)-$uple of real measurement maps $(\tau_{\eta},{ \relax{m}}_{{ \relax{l}}_{1}},\cdots, { \relax{m}}_{{ \relax{l}}_{N}})$ are jointly compatible.
<!-- end lemma-55 -->
<!-- proof-78: body_md -->
Direct consequence of Lemma {{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@genmeasurementselfcompatible\endcsname\@firstoftwo{genmeasurementselfcompatible}}} using the property 
\begin{eqnarray}
\tau_{\eta} &=& \tau_{\eta} \circ { \relax{m}}_{{ \relax{l}}}.
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end proof-78 -->
<!-- lemma-56: body_md -->
\label{genmeasurementwedgecompatible} For any $\eta\in { \relax{B}}$, if the $N-$uple of real measurement maps $({ \relax{m}}_{{ \relax{l}}_{1}},\cdots, { \relax{m}}_{{ \relax{l}}_{N}})$ are jointly compatible ($N\geq 2$), then the $(N+1)-$ uple of real measurement maps $({ \relax{m}}_{({ \relax{l}}_{1} 
\sqcap_{{}_{{ \relax{E}}_{ \relax{S}}}}
{ \relax{l}}_{2})}$,${ \relax{m}}_{{ \relax{l}}_{1}},\cdots, { \relax{m}}_{{ \relax{l}}_{N}})$ are jointly compatible.
<!-- end lemma-56 -->
<!-- proof-79: body_md -->
Let us fix $N=2$ for simplicity.\\
First of all, we remark that, if we denote by $\Psi_{({ \relax{m}}_{{ \relax{l}}_{1}},{ \relax{m}}_{{ \relax{l}}_{2}})}$ the joint morphism associated to the compatible real measurement maps $({ \relax{m}}_{{ \relax{l}}_{1}},{ \relax{m}}_{{ \relax{l}}_{2}})$, the property ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@relationsjointchannelreal\endcsname\@firstoftwo{relationsjointchannelreal}}}), i.e. $\Psi_{{}_{({ \relax{m}}_{{ \relax{l}}_{1}},{ \relax{m}}_{{ \relax{l}}_{2}})}}^\ast (\overline{ \relax{E}}_{{{\relax{B}}^{\widetilde{\otimes}2}}})\subseteq \overline{ \relax{E}}_{ \relax{S}}$ implies immediately 
\begin{eqnarray}
({ \relax{l}}_{1} \sqcap_{{}_{{ \relax{E}}_{ \relax{S}}}} { \relax{l}}_{2}) &\in & \overline{ \relax{E}}_{ \relax{S}}.\label{precisionrealmorphism}
\end{eqnarray}
Let us then consider the morphism denoted $\Omega$ and defined from ${ \relax{B}}\widetilde{\otimes} { \relax{B}}$ to ${ \relax{B}}\widetilde{\otimes} { \relax{B}}\widetilde{\otimes} { \relax{B}}$ as follows. For any $\sigma \in { \relax{B}}\widetilde{\otimes} { \relax{B}}$, we adopt the writing of $\sigma$ in terms of pure states  
$\sigma=(\bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{ \relax{B}}\widetilde{\otimes} { \relax{B}}}}_{i\in I}\alpha_i\widetilde{\otimes} \beta_i)$ with $\alpha_i,\beta_i\in \{\,\textit{\bf Y}\,,\, \textit{\bf N}\,\}$, then $\Omega(\sigma)$ is defined by
\begin{eqnarray}
&& \Omega (\bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{ \relax{B}}\widetilde{\otimes} { \relax{B}}}}_{i\in I}\alpha_i\widetilde{\otimes} \beta_i) := \bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{ \relax{B}}\widetilde{\otimes} { \relax{B}}\widetilde{\otimes} { \relax{B}}}}_{i\in I}(\alpha_i\widetilde{\otimes}\alpha_i\widetilde{\otimes} \beta_i \sqcap_{{}_{{ \relax{B}}\widetilde{\otimes} { \relax{B}}\widetilde{\otimes} { \relax{B}}}} \beta_i\widetilde{\otimes}\alpha_i\widetilde{\otimes} \beta_i)
\end{eqnarray}
The map $\Omega$ is build as a morphism Moreover, we have immediately
\begin{eqnarray}
&&\zeta^{{}^{{ \relax{B}} { \relax{B}}{ \relax{B}}}}_{(2)} \circ \Omega \circ \Psi_{({ \relax{m}}_{{ \relax{l}}_{1}},{ \relax{m}}_{{ \relax{l}}_{2}})}= \zeta^{{}^{{ \relax{B}}{ \relax{B}}}}_{(1)}\circ \Psi_{({ \relax{m}}_{{ \relax{l}}_{1}},{ \relax{m}}_{{ \relax{l}}_{2}})}={ \relax{m}}_{{ \relax{l}}_{1}},\\
&& \zeta^{{}^{{ \relax{B}} { \relax{B}}{ \relax{B}}}}_{(3)} \circ \Omega \circ \Psi_{({ \relax{m}}_{{ \relax{l}}_{1}},{ \relax{m}}_{{ \relax{l}}_{2}})} = \zeta^{{}^{{ \relax{B}}{ \relax{B}}}}_{2}\circ \Psi_{({ \relax{m}}_{{ \relax{l}}_{1}},{ \relax{m}}_{{ \relax{l}}_{2}})}={ \relax{m}}_{{ \relax{l}}_{2}},\\
&& \zeta^{{}^{{ \relax{B}} { \relax{B}}{ \relax{B}}}}_{(1)} \circ \Omega \circ \Psi_{({ \relax{m}}_{{ \relax{l}}_{1}},{ \relax{m}}_{{ \relax{l}}_{2}})} ={ \relax{m}}_{({ \relax{l}}_{1} 
\sqcap_{{}_{{ \relax{E}}_{ \relax{S}}}}
{ \relax{l}}_{2})}.
\end{eqnarray}
Then, $\Omega \circ \Psi_{({ \relax{m}}_{{ \relax{l}}_{1}},{ \relax{m}}_{{ \relax{l}}_{2}})}$ is a joint morphism for the triple $({ \relax{m}}_{({ \relax{l}}_{1} 
\sqcap_{{}_{{ \relax{E}}_{ \relax{S}}}}
{ \relax{l}}_{2})},{ \relax{m}}_{{ \relax{l}}_{1}}$, ${ \relax{m}}_{{ \relax{l}}_{2}})$.\\
As a result, ${ \relax{m}}_{{ \relax{l}}_{1}}$, ${ \relax{m}}_{{ \relax{l}}_{2}}$ and ${ \relax{m}}_{({ \relax{l}}_{1} 
\sqcap_{{}_{{ \relax{E}}_{ \relax{S}}}}
{ \relax{l}}_{2})}$ are jointly compatible.
<!-- end proof-79 -->
<!-- theorem-38: body_md -->
\label{synthesiscontexts}
Let $C \in { \mathcal{C}}$ designate a maximal compatibility context, we have 
\begin{eqnarray}
&&{ \relax{Y}}_{{ \relax{E}}_{ \relax{S}}}\in C \;\;\textit{\rm and}\;\; \bot_{{ \relax{E}}_{ \relax{S}}}\in C  \;\;\textit{\rm and}\;\;  \overline{{ \relax{Y}}_{{ \relax{E}}_{ \relax{S}}}}\in C
,\label{contexteta}\\
&& \forall { \relax{l}}\in C,\;\;\overline{\; \relax{l}\;}\in C,\label{contextbar}\\
&&\forall { \relax{l}}_1,{ \relax{l}}_2\in C,\;\;({ \relax{l}}_1\sqcap_{{}_{{{ \relax{E}}_{ \relax{S}}}}}{ \relax{l}}_2)\in C.\label{contextwedge}
\end{eqnarray}
We note the following fact, implicit in ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@contextwedge\endcsname\@firstoftwo{contextwedge}}}) and clarified in Lemma {{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@genmeasurementwedgecompatible\endcsname\@firstoftwo{genmeasurementwedgecompatible}}} :
\begin{eqnarray}
\forall { \relax{l}}_1,{ \relax{l}}_2\in \overline{ \relax{E}}_{ \relax{S}},&& ({ \relax{l}}_1\sqcap_{{}_{{{ \relax{E}}_{ \relax{S}}}}}{ \relax{l}}_2)\in { \relax{E}}_{ \relax{S}}\smallsetminus \overline{ \relax{E}}_{ \relax{S}}\;\;\Rightarrow \;\; \left(\nexists C\in {\mathcal{C}}\;\;\vert\;\;{ \relax{l}}_1,{ \relax{l}}_2\in C\right).\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end theorem-38 -->
<!-- definition-50: body_md -->
Once is known the compatibility cover ${ \mathcal{C}}$, we define an {\em operational description} ${ \relax{D}}$ to be a family of maps $({ \relax{d}}^{C})_{C \in { \mathcal{C}}}$,  where each map ${ \relax{d}}^{C}$ is an element of ${ \relax{B}}^C$ (i.e.  a counterfactual statement in ${ \relax{B}}$ is attributed to any of the jointly compatible measurements ${ \relax{m}}_{ \relax{l}}$ for any ${ \relax{l}}\in C$), these maps being assigned to satisfy the following conditions
\begin{eqnarray}
&& \forall C\in { \mathcal{C}},\;\; { \relax{d}}^{C}({ \relax{Y}}_{\overline{ \relax{E}}_{ \relax{S}}})=\textit{\bf Y}                                                                                                                                                                                                                          
\label{sheafdistributioneta}\\
&& \forall C\in { \mathcal{C}},\forall { \relax{l}}\in C,\;\; { \relax{d}}^{C}(\overline{\; \relax{l}\;})= \overline{{ \relax{d}}^{C}({ \relax{l}})},\label{sheafdistributionbar}\\
&& \forall C\in { \mathcal{C}},\forall \{\,{ \relax{l}}_i\;\vert\; i\in I\,\}\subseteq C,\;\; { \relax{d}}^{C}(\bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{ \relax{E}}_{ \relax{S}}}}_{i\in I}{ \relax{l}}_i)= \bigwedge{}_{i\in I} \;{ \relax{d}}^{C}({ \relax{l}}_i).\label{sheafdistributionwedge}
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end definition-50 -->
<!-- definition-51: body_md -->
If the operational description ${ \relax{D}}:=({ \relax{d}}^{C})_{C \in { \mathcal{C}}}$  satisfies the following supplementary condition 
\begin{eqnarray}
\textit{ (sheaf condition)}&& \forall C,C'\in { \mathcal{C}},\forall { \relax{l}}\in C\cap C', \;\; { \relax{d}}^{C}({ \relax{l}})={ \relax{d}}^{C'}({ \relax{l}}),\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\label{sheafdistributionrecollement}
\end{eqnarray}
it will be designated as a {\em coherent operational description}. \\
The set of coherent  operational descriptions associated to the compatibility cover ${ \mathcal{C}}$ will be denoted ${ \mathcal{D}}$ and called {\em the empirical model} for the space of states ${ \relax{S}}$.
<!-- end definition-51 -->
<!-- definition-52: body_md -->
The empirical model ${ \mathcal{D}}$ associated to the space of states ${ \relax{S}}$ is an Inf semi-lattice by defining its infima as follows :
\begin{eqnarray}
\forall ({ \relax{d}}_1^{C})_{C \in { \mathcal{C}}},({ \relax{d}}_2^{C})_{C \in { \mathcal{C}}}\in { \mathcal{D}},\forall C\in { \mathcal{C}},\forall { \relax{l}}\in C,&& ({ \relax{d}}_1^{C}\sqcap_{{}_{{ \mathcal{D}}}} { \relax{d}}_2^{C})({ \relax{l}}):=  { \relax{d}}_1^{C}({ \relax{l}})\wedge { \relax{d}}_2^{C}({ \relax{l}}).\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end definition-52 -->
<!-- definition-53: body_md -->
If an operational description ${ \relax{D}}:=({ \relax{d}}^C)_{C\in { \mathcal{C}}}$ is such that there exists a real state $\sigma\in \overline{ \relax{S}}$ satisfying  
\begin{eqnarray}
\forall C\in { \mathcal{C}},\forall { \relax{l}}\in C&& { \relax{d}}^C({ \relax{l}}) = \epsilon^{{ \relax{S}}}_{ \relax{l}}(\sigma),\label{definglobally}
\end{eqnarray}
we will say that ${ \relax{D}}$ is {\em defined globally}. It will then be denoted $({ \relax{d}}^C_{(\sigma)})_{C\in { \mathcal{C}}}$. Note that if ${ \relax{D}}$ is defined globally, then it is trivially a coherent  operational description.
<!-- end definition-53 -->
<!-- definition-54: body_md -->
The empirical model ${ \mathcal{D}}$ is said to be {\em non-contextual} iff every ${ \relax{D}}\in { \mathcal{D}}$ is defined globally, otherwise it is said to be {\em contextual}.
<!-- end definition-54 -->
<!-- theorem-39: body_md -->
If ${ \relax{S}}$ is a simplex then every coherent  operational description ${ \relax{d}}$ are defined globally. The empirical model associated to a simplex space of states is then non-contextual.
<!-- end theorem-39 -->
<!-- proof-80: body_md -->
Direct consequence of Theorem {{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@theoremNcompatiblemeasurements\endcsname\@firstoftwo{theoremNcompatiblemeasurements}}} and Theorem {{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@blepsilonsigma\endcsname\@firstoftwo{blepsilonsigma}}}.
<!-- end proof-80 -->
<!-- definition-55: body_md -->
The {\em ontic state} associated to the operational description ${ \relax{D}}:=({ \relax{d}}^{C})_{C \in { \mathcal{C}}} \in { \mathcal{D}}$ is a family $(\Sigma^C_{ \relax{D}})_{C \in { \mathcal{C}}}\in \overline{ \relax{S}}^{{ \mathcal{C}}}$ satisfying the following conditions
\begin{eqnarray}
&&\hspace{-1.5cm} \forall C \in { \mathcal{C}}, \forall { \relax{l}}\in C,\;\; { \relax{m}}_{ \relax{l}}(\Sigma^C_{ \relax{D}})={ \relax{d}}^C({{ \relax{l}}}),\label{defonticstate1}\\
&&\hspace{-1.5cm} \forall C\in { \mathcal{C}},\Sigma^C_{ \relax{D}}=\bigsqcap{}^{{}^{ \relax{S}}}\{\,\sigma^C\in \overline{ \relax{S}}\;\vert\; \forall { \relax{l}}\in C,\;{ \relax{m}}_{ \relax{l}}(\sigma^C)\geq { \relax{d}}^C({{ \relax{l}}})\,\}.\label{defonticstate2}\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end definition-55 -->
<!-- theorem-40: body_md -->
\label{existenceonticstate}
Let us fix a coherent  operational description ${ \relax{D}}:=({ \relax{d}}^{C})_{C \in { \mathcal{C}}} \in {{ \mathcal{D}}}$ associated to the compatibility cover ${ \mathcal{C}}$.  Let us also fix a compatibility context $C$.  Then, 
\begin{eqnarray}
\exists \sigma \in \overline{ \relax{S}} &\vert & (\,\epsilon^{ \relax{S}}_{{ \relax{l}}}(\sigma)={ \relax{d}}^C({{ \relax{l}}}),\;\forall { \relax{l}}\in C\,).\label{descriptionstate}
\end{eqnarray} 
More explicitly, we will fix explicitly the solution $\sigma^C_{ \relax{D}}$ of the equation ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@descriptionstate\endcsname\@firstoftwo{descriptionstate}}}) defined by
\begin{eqnarray}
{ \relax{l}}^C_{ \relax{D}}&:=&\bigsqcap{}^{{}^{\overline{ \relax{E}}_{ \relax{S}}}}\{\, { \relax{l}}\in C \;\vert\; { \relax{d}}^C({{ \relax{l}}})=\textit{\bf Y}\,\}\label{onticstate1}\\
\sigma^C_{ \relax{D}}&:=&\bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{ \relax{S}}}}(\epsilon^{ \relax{S}}_{{ \relax{l}}^C_{ \relax{D}}})^{-1}(\textit{\bf Y}) \;\in \overline{ \relax{S}} \label{onticstate2}
\end{eqnarray}
The family $(\sigma^C_{ \relax{D}})_{C \in { \mathcal{C}}}\in \overline{ \relax{S}}{}^{\, \mathcal{C}}$ is the ontic state associated to ${ \relax{D}}$.
<!-- end theorem-40 -->
<!-- proof-81: body_md -->
Let us consider the effect ${ \relax{l}}^C_{ \relax{D}}:=\bigsqcap{}^{{}^{\overline{ \relax{E}}_{ \relax{S}}}}\{\, { \relax{l}}\in C \;\vert\; { \relax{d}}^C({{ \relax{l}}})=\textit{\bf Y}\,\}$.  Note that the infimum in the definition of ${ \relax{l}}^C_{ \relax{D}}$ exists because $\overline{ \relax{E}}_{ \relax{S}}$ is a down-complete Inf semi-lattice and because ${ \relax{Y}}_{\overline{ \relax{E}}_{ \relax{S}}}\in \{\, { \relax{l}}\in C \;\vert\; { \relax{d}}^C({{ \relax{l}}})=\textit{\bf Y}\,\}\not= \varnothing$.  Moreover, due to the property ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@contextwedge\endcsname\@firstoftwo{contextwedge}}}),                                                                                                 
 we deduce that ${ \relax{l}}^C_{ \relax{D}}$ is in $C$. \\
Secondly, ${ \relax{d}}^{C}({ \relax{l}}^C_{ \relax{D}})=\textit{\bf Y}$ because of the property ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@sheafdistributionwedge\endcsname\@firstoftwo{sheafdistributionwedge}}}). \\
Thirdly, we note that, for any ${ \relax{l}}\in C$, we have ${ \relax{l}}\sqsupseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{E}}}}{ \relax{l}}^C_{ \relax{D}}$ implies ${ \relax{d}}^{C}({ \relax{l}})=\textit{\bf Y}$ because ${ \relax{d}}^{C}({ \relax{l}})\wedge \textit{\bf Y}={ \relax{d}}^{C}({ \relax{l}})\wedge { \relax{d}}^{C}({ \relax{l}}^C_{ \relax{D}})={ \relax{d}}^{C}({ \relax{l}}\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{E}}_{ \relax{S}}}}
{ \relax{l}}^C_{ \relax{D}})={ \relax{d}}^{C}({ \relax{l}}^C_{ \relax{D}})=\textit{\bf Y}$.  Conversely, the property ${ \relax{d}}^{C}({ \relax{l}})=\textit{\bf Y}$ for ${ \relax{l}}\in C$ implies ${ \relax{l}}\sqsupseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{E}}_{ \relax{S}}}}{ \relax{l}}^C_{ \relax{D}}$ from the explicit definition of ${ \relax{l}}^C_{ \relax{D}}$.\\
As a result, we have $\{\, { \relax{l}}\in C \;\vert\; { \relax{d}}^C({{ \relax{l}}})=\textit{\bf Y}\,\}=(\uparrow^{{}^{C}}\!\!{ \relax{l}}^C_{ \relax{D}})$.\\
We also note that, due to properties ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@sheafdistributioneta\endcsname\@firstoftwo{sheafdistributioneta}}}) and the definition of ${ \relax{l}}^C_{ \relax{D}}$, we have ${ \relax{l}}^C_{ \relax{D}}={ \relax{l}}^C_{ \relax{D}} \sqcap_{{}_{{ \relax{E}}}} {{ \relax{Y}}}_{{ \relax{E}}}$. Hence, there must exist a state $\sigma^C_{ \relax{D}}\in { \relax{S}}$ such that ${ \relax{l}}^C_{ \relax{D}}={ \relax{l}}_{(\sigma^C_{ \relax{D}},\,\cdot\,)}$. In other words,  $\sigma^C_{ \relax{D}}:=\bigsqcap^{{}^{{ \relax{S}}}}(\epsilon^{ \relax{S}}_{{ \relax{l}}^C_{ \relax{D}}})^{-1}(\textit{\bf Y})$.\\
We can summarize these results by the following equivalence : 
\begin{eqnarray}
\forall C \in { \mathcal{C}},\forall { \relax{l}}\in C, &&{ \relax{d}}^C({{ \relax{l}}})=\textit{\bf Y}\;\Leftrightarrow\; \epsilon^{ \relax{S}}_{{ \relax{l}}}(\sigma^C_{ \relax{D}})=\textit{\bf Y}.
\end{eqnarray}
Using ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@etbar\endcsname\@firstoftwo{etbar}}}) and ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@sheafdistributionbar\endcsname\@firstoftwo{sheafdistributionbar}}}), we deduce also : $\epsilon^{ \relax{S}}_{{ \relax{l}}}(\sigma^C_{ \relax{D}})=\textit{\bf N} \;\Leftrightarrow\; \epsilon^{ \relax{S}}_{\overline{\, \relax{l}\,}}(\sigma^C_{ \relax{D}})=\textit{\bf Y} \;\Leftrightarrow\; { \relax{d}}^C(\overline{\,{ \relax{l}}\,})=\textit{\bf Y} \;\Leftrightarrow\; { \relax{d}}^C({ \relax{l}})=\textit{\bf N}$.  
As a final conclusion, we have for any ${ \relax{l}}\in C$ the equality $\epsilon^{ \relax{S}}_{{ \relax{l}}}(\sigma^C_{ \relax{D}})={ \relax{d}}^C({{ \relax{l}}})$.\\
Note then that the defining property ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@defonticstate1\endcsname\@firstoftwo{defonticstate1}}}) is identical to the property ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@descriptionstate\endcsname\@firstoftwo{descriptionstate}}}) satisfied by $\sigma^C_{ \relax{D}}$ for any $C \in { \mathcal{C}}$. \\
Let us now consider a family $(\rho^C)_{C \in { \mathcal{C}}}\in { \relax{S}}^{{ \mathcal{C}}}$ satisfying $\forall C \in { \mathcal{C}}, \forall { \relax{l}}\in C, \epsilon^{ \relax{S}}_{{ \relax{l}}}(\rho^C)\geq{ \relax{d}}^C({{ \relax{l}}})$. \\
We have then in particular $\epsilon^{ \relax{S}}_{{ \relax{l}}^C_{ \relax{D}}}(\rho^C)\geq 
{ \relax{d}}^C({ \relax{l}}^C_{ \relax{D}})=\textit{\bf Y}$. Then $\rho^C \sqsupseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}} \bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{ \relax{S}}}}(\epsilon^{ \relax{S}}_{{ \relax{l}}^C_{ \relax{D}}})^{-1}(\textit{\bf Y})=\sigma^C_{ \relax{D}}$.  This is the defining property ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@defonticstate2\endcsname\@firstoftwo{defonticstate2}}}).\\
As a conclusion, $(\sigma^C_{ \relax{D}})_{C \in { \mathcal{C}}}$ is the ontic state associated to ${ \relax{D}}$.
<!-- end proof-81 -->
<!-- definition-56: body_md -->
In the following, we will adopt the following notation :
\begin{eqnarray}
{ \relax{U}}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}} & :=& \left( \{ { \relax{l}}_{{}_{(\sigma,\centerdot)}}\;\vert\; \sigma\in \overline{ \relax{S}}\;\}\cup \{ { \relax{l}}_{{}_{(\centerdot,\sigma)}}\;\vert\; \sigma\in \overline{ \relax{S}}\;\}\cup \{\, { \relax{l}}_{{}_{(\centerdot,\centerdot)}}\,\}\right).
\end{eqnarray}
Let us consider a maximal compatibility context $C$ in ${ \mathcal{C}}$. We are necessarily in one of the two following cases :
\begin{itemize} 
\@par\hangindent 2em Maximal compatibility context of Type 1 :
\begin{eqnarray}
C &\subseteq & { \relax{U}}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}
\end{eqnarray}
\@par\hangindent 2em Maximal compatibility context of Type 2 : 
\begin{eqnarray}
\exists \sigma,\sigma'\in \overline{ \relax{S}}\smallsetminus \{\bot_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}}\},\sigma'\sqsupseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma^\star  & \vert &{ \relax{l}}_{(\sigma,\sigma')}\in C.
\end{eqnarray}
\end{itemize}
<!-- end definition-56 -->
<!-- lemma-57: body_md -->
\label{lemmacontext}
Let us consider a compatibility context denoted $C$ such that $C\subseteq { \relax{U}}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}$. We have necessarily
\begin{eqnarray}
&&\exists\, \omega\in \overline{ \relax{S}} \;\;\vert \;\; C\subseteq \left( \{\, { \relax{l}}_{(\sigma,\centerdot)}\;\vert\; \sigma\sqsubseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}} \omega\,\}\cup \{\, { \relax{l}}_{(\centerdot,\sigma)}\;\vert\; \sigma\sqsubseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}} \omega\,\}\cup \{\, { \relax{l}}_{(\centerdot,\centerdot)}\,\}\right),\label{lemmacontext1}\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\\
&&\textit{\rm or} \nonumber\\
&&\exists\, \gamma,\gamma',\omega,\omega'\in \overline{ \relax{S}} \;\;\vert \;\;\gamma' \sqsupseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}} \gamma^\star,\omega \sqsupseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}} \gamma, \omega' \sqsupseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}} \gamma'\nonumber\\
&&C\subseteq \left( \{\, { \relax{l}}_{(\sigma,\centerdot)}\;\vert\; \gamma \sqsubseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}} \sigma\sqsubseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}} \omega\,\}\cup \{\, { \relax{l}}_{(\centerdot,\sigma)}\;\vert\; \gamma \sqsubseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma\sqsubseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}} \omega\,\}\cup \{\, { \relax{l}}_{(\centerdot,\centerdot)}\,\}\cup \right.\nonumber\\
&&\hspace{2cm}\left.  \{\, { \relax{l}}_{(\sigma,\centerdot)}\;\vert\; \gamma' \sqsubseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}} \sigma\sqsubseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}} \omega'\,\}\cup \{\, { \relax{l}}_{(\centerdot,\sigma)}\;\vert\; \gamma' \sqsubseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma\sqsubseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}} \omega'\,\}\right)\label{lemmacontext2}\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end lemma-57 -->
<!-- proof-82: body_md -->
Let us consider a compatibility context denoted $C$ such that $C\subseteq { \relax{U}}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}$ and let us consider the following subset of ${ \mathcal{P}}(\overline{ \relax{S}})$
\begin{eqnarray}
{\relax{Q}}(\overline{ \relax{S}})&:=&\{\,U\subseteq C \;\vert\; \forall \sigma,\sigma'\in \overline{ \relax{S}}\;\;\textit{\rm s.t.}\;\; { \relax{l}}_{(\sigma,\centerdot)},{ \relax{l}}_{(\sigma',\centerdot)}\in U\;\;\textit{\rm we have}\;\;\sigma'\not\sqsupseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}'}}\sigma^\star\,\}\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;   
\end{eqnarray} 
and let us consider an element $V$ which is maximal for inclusion in ${\relax{Q}}(\overline{ \relax{S}})$.  As a trivial consequence of the requirement ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@relationsjointchannelreal\endcsname\@firstoftwo{relationsjointchannelreal}}}) (more explicitly, of the property ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@precisionrealmorphism\endcsname\@firstoftwo{precisionrealmorphism}}})), we know that $\omega:=\bigsqcup{}^{{}^{{ \relax{S}}}}\{\sigma\;\vert\; { \relax{l}}_{(\sigma,\centerdot)}\in V\}$ exists in $\overline{ \relax{S}}$.\\
If we denote $C_\omega :=\left( \{\, { \relax{l}}_{(\sigma,\centerdot)}\;\vert\; \sigma\sqsubseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}} \omega\,\}\cup \{\, { \relax{l}}_{(\centerdot,\sigma)}\;\vert\; \sigma\sqsubseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}} \omega\,\}\cup \{\, { \relax{l}}_{(\centerdot,\centerdot)}\,\}\right)$, we note that $C_\omega$ is a compatibility context (the joint morphism is built straightforwardly) and $V\subseteq C_\omega$ by construction.\\
