We will now distinguish two cases : (1) $C\smallsetminus V=\varnothing$, and (2) $C\smallsetminus V\not= \varnothing$. \\
The first case is treated immediately, we obtain ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@lemmacontext1\endcsname\@firstoftwo{lemmacontext1}}}). \\
Let us then focus on the second case.  For any $\alpha\in \overline{ \relax{S}}\smallsetminus \{\bot_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\}$ such that ${ \relax{l}}_{(\alpha,\centerdot)} \in C\smallsetminus V$, we have necessarily, due to the requirement ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@relationsjointchannelreal\endcsname\@firstoftwo{relationsjointchannelreal}}}) (more explicitly, of the property ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@precisionrealmorphism\endcsname\@firstoftwo{precisionrealmorphism}}})), for any $\sigma\in  \overline{ \relax{S}}\smallsetminus \{\bot_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\}$ such that ${ \relax{l}}_{(\sigma,\centerdot)} \in V$ the property $\alpha^\star \sqsubseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma$, i.e. $\alpha^\star \sqsubseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}} \bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{ \relax{S}}}}\{\, \sigma\in  \overline{ \relax{S}}\smallsetminus \{\bot_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\}\;\vert\;{ \relax{l}}_{(\sigma,\centerdot)} \in V\,\}$. If we denote by $\gamma :=\bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{ \relax{S}}}}\{\, \sigma\in  \overline{ \relax{S}}\smallsetminus \{\bot_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\}\;\vert\;{ \relax{l}}_{(\sigma,\centerdot)} \in V\,\}$ and $\gamma':=\bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{ \relax{S}}}}\{\, \sigma\in  \overline{ \relax{S}}\smallsetminus \{\bot_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\}\;\vert\;{ \relax{l}}_{(\sigma,\centerdot)} \in C\smallsetminus V\,\}$, we have $\gamma' \sqsupseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}} \gamma^\star$. On another part, and for the same reasons as before,  if we denote $\omega':=\bigsqcup{}^{{}^{{ \relax{S}}}}\{\, \sigma\in  \overline{ \relax{S}}\smallsetminus \{\bot_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\}\;\vert\;{ \relax{l}}_{(\sigma,\centerdot)} \in C\smallsetminus V\,\}$, then $C_{\omega'}$ is a compatibility context (the joint morphism is built straightforwardly) and $(C\smallsetminus V)\subseteq C_{\omega'}$ by construction.
\\
This concludes the proof.
<!-- end proof-82 -->
<!-- lemma-58: body_md -->
\label{lemmacontexttype1}
In the following, we will adopt the following notation
\begin{eqnarray}
&&\forall \omega\in \overline{ \relax{S}}^{{}^{pure}} \;\;\vert \;\; C^{(1)}_\omega := \left( \{\, { \relax{l}}_{(\sigma,\centerdot)}\;\vert\; \sigma\sqsubseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}} \omega\,\}\cup \{\, { \relax{l}}_{(\centerdot,\sigma)}\;\vert\; \sigma\sqsubseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}} \omega\,\}\cup \{\, { \relax{l}}_{(\centerdot,\centerdot)}\,\}\right).\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;
\end{eqnarray}
Let $C$ be a maximal compatibility context of type 1. Then, 
\begin{eqnarray}
&&\exists \textit{\bf !}\, \omega\in \overline{ \relax{S}}^{{}^{pure}} \;\;\vert \;\; C= C^{(1)}_\omega.
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end lemma-58 -->
<!-- proof-83: body_md -->
Trivial consequence of Lemma {{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@lemmacontext\endcsname\@firstoftwo{lemmacontext}}}.
<!-- end proof-83 -->
<!-- lemma-59: body_md -->
\label{lemmacontexttype2a}
Let $C$ be a maximal compatibility context of type 2 and let $\gamma,\gamma'\in \overline{ \relax{S}} \smallsetminus \{\bot_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\}$ with $\gamma'\sqsupseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\gamma^\star$ and such that ${ \relax{l}}_{(\gamma,\gamma')}\in C$. Then, 
\begin{eqnarray}
&&\exists\, \lambda,\lambda',\omega,\omega'\in \overline{ \relax{S}} \smallsetminus \{\bot_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\} \;\;\vert \;\;\lambda' \sqsupseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}} \lambda^\star,\omega \sqsupseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}} \gamma \sqsupseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}} \lambda, \omega' \sqsupseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}} \gamma' \sqsupseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}} \lambda'\nonumber\\
&&(C\cap { \relax{U}}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}})\subseteq \left( \{\, { \relax{l}}_{(\sigma,\centerdot)}\;\vert\; \lambda \sqsubseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}} \sigma\sqsubseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}} \omega\,\}\cup \{\, { \relax{l}}_{(\centerdot,\sigma)}\;\vert\; \lambda \sqsubseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma\sqsubseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}} \omega\,\}\cup \{\, { \relax{l}}_{(\centerdot,\centerdot)}\,\}\cup \right.\nonumber\\
&&\hspace{1cm}\left.  \{\, { \relax{l}}_{(\sigma,\centerdot)}\;\vert\; \lambda' \sqsubseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}} \sigma\sqsubseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}} \omega'\,\}\cup \{\, { \relax{l}}_{(\centerdot,\sigma)}\;\vert\; \lambda' \sqsubseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma\sqsubseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}} \omega'\,\}\right)
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end lemma-59 -->
<!-- proof-84: body_md -->
Let $C$ be a maximal compatibility context of type 2 and let $\gamma,\gamma'\in \overline{ \relax{S}} \smallsetminus \{\bot_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\}$ with $\gamma'\sqsupseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\gamma^\star$ and such that ${ \relax{l}}_{(\gamma,\gamma')}\in C$. \\
Let us first note that $(C\cap { \relax{U}}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}})$ is a compatibility context included in ${ \relax{U}}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}$. \\
Secondly, we remark that ${ \relax{l}}_{(\gamma,\centerdot)}, { \relax{l}}_{(\gamma',\centerdot)}\in (C\cap { \relax{U}}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}})$.  Indeed, we recall that ${ \relax{l}}_{(\gamma,\centerdot)}={ \relax{l}}_{(\gamma,\gamma')} \sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}} {\relax{Y}}_{{\relax{E}}_{\relax{S}}}$ and ${ \relax{l}}_{(\gamma',\centerdot)}=\overline{ { \relax{l}}_{(\gamma,\gamma')} \sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}} \overline{{\relax{Y}}_{{\relax{E}}_{\relax{S}}}}}$ and we have Theorem {{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@synthesiscontexts\endcsname\@firstoftwo{synthesiscontexts}}} for the maximal compatibility context $C$. Moreover, we have $\neg\widehat{\gamma\gamma'}{}^{{}^{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}$. We are then in the case ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@lemmacontext2\endcsname\@firstoftwo{lemmacontext2}}}) and not in the case ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@lemmacontext1\endcsname\@firstoftwo{lemmacontext1}}}). Because of Lemma {{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@lemmacontext\endcsname\@firstoftwo{lemmacontext}}}, we know that 
\begin{eqnarray}
&&\exists\, \lambda,\lambda',\omega,\omega'\in \overline{ \relax{S}} \smallsetminus \{\bot_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\} \;\;\vert \;\;\lambda' \sqsupseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}} \lambda^\star,\omega \sqsupseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}} \lambda, \omega' \sqsupseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}} \lambda'\nonumber\\
&&(C\cap { \relax{U}}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}})\subseteq \left( \{\, { \relax{l}}_{(\sigma,\centerdot)}\;\vert\; \lambda \sqsubseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}} \sigma\sqsubseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}} \omega\,\}\cup \{\, { \relax{l}}_{(\centerdot,\sigma)}\;\vert\; \lambda \sqsubseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma\sqsubseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}} \omega\,\}\cup \{\, { \relax{l}}_{(\centerdot,\centerdot)}\,\}\cup \right.\nonumber\\
&&\hspace{1cm}\left.  \{\, { \relax{l}}_{(\sigma,\centerdot)}\;\vert\; \lambda' \sqsubseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}} \sigma\sqsubseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}} \omega'\,\}\cup \{\, { \relax{l}}_{(\centerdot,\sigma)}\;\vert\; \lambda' \sqsubseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma\sqsubseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}} \omega'\,\}\right)
\end{eqnarray}
and we must obviously have $\lambda \sqsubseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}} \gamma$ and $\lambda' \sqsubseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}} \gamma'$, because ${ \relax{l}}_{(\gamma,\centerdot)}, { \relax{l}}_{(\gamma',\centerdot)} \in C$.
<!-- end proof-84 -->
<!-- lemma-60: body_md -->
\label{lemmacontexttype2b}
Let $C$ be a maximal compatibility context of type 2 such that there exists $\gamma\in \overline{ \relax{S}} \smallsetminus \{\bot_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\}$ with ${ \relax{l}}_{(\gamma,\gamma^\star)}\in C$. Then, 
\begin{eqnarray}
&&\exists\, \omega,\omega'\in \overline{ \relax{S}} \smallsetminus \{\bot_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\} \;\;\vert \;\;\omega \sqsupseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}} \gamma, \omega' \sqsupseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}} \gamma^\star\nonumber\\
&&(C\cap { \relax{U}}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}})\subseteq \left( \{\, { \relax{l}}_{(\sigma,\centerdot)}\;\vert\; \gamma \sqsubseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}} \sigma\sqsubseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}} \omega\,\}\cup \{\, { \relax{l}}_{(\centerdot,\sigma)}\;\vert\; \gamma \sqsubseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma\sqsubseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}} \omega\,\}\cup \{\, { \relax{l}}_{(\centerdot,\centerdot)}\,\}\cup \right.\nonumber\\
&&\hspace{2cm}\left.  \{\, { \relax{l}}_{(\sigma,\centerdot)}\;\vert\; \gamma^\star \sqsubseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}} \sigma\sqsubseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}} \omega'\,\}\cup \{\, { \relax{l}}_{(\centerdot,\sigma)}\;\vert\; \gamma^\star \sqsubseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma\sqsubseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}} \omega'\,\}\right)
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end lemma-60 -->
<!-- proof-85: body_md -->
We obviously take Lemma {{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@lemmacontexttype2a\endcsname\@firstoftwo{lemmacontexttype2a}}} as a departure point.\\
If $\gamma'=\gamma^\star$ we have then $\gamma^\star=\gamma' \sqsupseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\lambda' \sqsupseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\lambda^\star \sqsupseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}} \gamma^\star$.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  
This concludes the proof.
<!-- end proof-85 -->
<!-- lemma-61: body_md -->
For any pair $C^{(1)}_{\omega},C^{(1)}_{\omega'}$ of maximal compatibility contexts of type 1 associated to $\omega,\omega'\in \overline{ \relax{S}}^{{}^{pure}}$ (see Lemma {{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@lemmacontexttype1\endcsname\@firstoftwo{lemmacontexttype1}}}), we have
\begin{eqnarray}
\left\{\begin{array}{rcl}
\omega \sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}} \Sigma^{C^{(1)}_{\omega'}}_{ \relax{D}} & \sqsubseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}} &  \Sigma^{C^{(1)}_{\omega}}_{ \relax{D}}\\
\omega' \sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}} \Sigma^{C^{(1)}_{\omega}}_{ \relax{D}} & \sqsubseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}} &  \Sigma^{C^{(1)}_{\omega'}}_{ \relax{D}}
\end{array}
\right.\label{consitencyontic}
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end lemma-61 -->
<!-- proof-86: body_md -->
By definition of the ontic state, we have
\begin{eqnarray}
\forall { \relax{l}}\in C^{(1)}_{\omega},&& { \relax{d}}^{C^{(1)}_{\omega}}({ \relax{l}})=\epsilon^{ \relax{S}}_{ \relax{l}}(\Sigma^{C^{(1)}_{\omega}}_{ \relax{D}})
\end{eqnarray}
The consistency of ${ \relax{D}}$ implies
\begin{eqnarray}
\forall { \relax{l}}\in C^{(1)}_{\omega}\cap C^{(1)}_{\omega'},&& \epsilon^{ \relax{S}}_{ \relax{l}}(\Sigma^{C^{(1)}_{\omega}}_{ \relax{D}}) =\epsilon^{ \relax{S}}_{ \relax{l}}(\Sigma^{C^{(1)}_{\omega'}}_{ \relax{D}})
\end{eqnarray}
But, 
\begin{eqnarray}
C^{(1)}_{\omega}\cap C^{(1)}_{\omega'} &=& \left( \{\, { \relax{l}}_{(\sigma,\centerdot)}\;\vert\; \sigma\sqsubseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}} \omega \sqcap_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}}\omega'\,\}\cup \{\, { \relax{l}}_{(\centerdot,\sigma)}\;\vert\; \sigma\sqsubseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}} \omega \sqcap_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}}\omega'\,\}\cup \{\, { \relax{l}}_{(\centerdot,\centerdot)}\,\}\right).\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;
\end{eqnarray}
Hence, 
\begin{eqnarray}
\hspace{-1.3cm}\left( \sigma \sqsubseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}} \omega \sqcap_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}}\omega' \;\;\textit{\rm and}\;\; \sigma \sqsubseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}} \Sigma^{C^{(1)}_{\omega}}_{ \relax{D}}\right) \;\;\Rightarrow \;\; \left(\epsilon^{ \relax{S}}_{{ \relax{l}}_{(\sigma,\centerdot)}}(\Sigma^{C^{(1)}_{\omega}}_{ \relax{D}})=\textit{\bf Y}=\epsilon^{ \relax{S}}_{{ \relax{l}}_{(\sigma,\centerdot)}}(\Sigma^{C^{(1)}_{\omega'}}_{ \relax{D}})\right)
\;\;\Rightarrow \;\;  \sigma \sqsubseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}} \Sigma^{C^{(1)}_{\omega'}}_{ \relax{D}}.\;\;\;\;\;
\end{eqnarray}
In other words,  noting that $\Sigma^{C^{(1)}_{\omega}}_{ \relax{D}} \sqsubseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}} \omega$, we obtain $\omega' \sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}} \Sigma^{C^{(1)}_{\omega}}_{ \relax{D}}  \sqsubseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}   \Sigma^{C^{(1)}_{\omega'}}_{ \relax{D}}$. The other inequality is obtained in the same way.
<!-- end proof-86 -->
<!-- lemma-62: body_md -->
\label{lemmanexistsomega0}
If there exists $\omega,\omega'\in \overline{ \relax{S}}^{{}^{pure}}$ such that $\Sigma^{C^{(1)}_{\omega}}_{ \relax{D}}$ and $\Sigma^{C^{(1)}_{\omega'}}_{ \relax{D}}$ admit a common upper-bound in $\overline{ \relax{S}}$, then for any $\omega''\in \underline{\Sigma^{C^{(1)}_{\omega}}_{ \relax{D}} \sqcup_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}} \Sigma^{C^{(1)}_{\omega'}}_{ \relax{D}}}_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}$ we have $\Sigma^{C^{(1)}_{\omega''}}_{ \relax{D}} \sqsupseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}} (\Sigma^{C^{(1)}_{\omega}}_{ \relax{D}} \sqcup_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}} \Sigma^{C^{(1)}_{\omega'}}_{ \relax{D}})$
<!-- end lemma-62 -->
<!-- proof-87: body_md -->
Straightforward.
<!-- end proof-87 -->
<!-- lemma-63: body_md -->
\label{lemmacU=U}
For any  coherent  operational description ${ \relax{D}}$ the subset $U_{ \relax{D}}$ of $\overline{ \relax{S}}$ defined by $U_{ \relax{D}}:=\{\, \Sigma^{C^{(1)}_{\omega}}_{ \relax{D}}\;\vert\; \omega\in \overline{ \relax{S}}{}^{{}^{pure}}\,\}$ satisfies
\begin{eqnarray}
cl_c^{\overline{ \relax{S}}}(U_{ \relax{D}})=U_{ \relax{D}}
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end lemma-63 -->
<!-- proof-88: body_md -->
As a strict rewriting of property ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@consitencyontic\endcsname\@firstoftwo{consitencyontic}}}), we note that we have 
\begin{eqnarray}
\forall \omega\in \overline{ \relax{S}}{}^{{}^{pure}},\exists \alpha\in U_{ \relax{D}} &\vert & \alpha \sqsubseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}} \omega\;\textit{\rm and}\; \forall \beta\in U_{ \relax{D}},(\omega \sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\beta)  \sqsubseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}}  \alpha.
\end{eqnarray}
and then
 \begin{eqnarray}
Max\{\,\bigsqcup{}^{{}^{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}_{\kappa\in U_{ \relax{D}}} (\omega\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\kappa)\;\vert\; \omega\in \overline{ \relax{S}}{}^{{}^{pure}} \,\} \sqsubseteq U_{ \relax{D}}.\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;
\end{eqnarray}
Now, we note that
 \begin{eqnarray}
(V\sqsubseteq U_{ \relax{D}}\;\textit{\rm and}\;\widehat{V}{}^{{}^{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}) &\Rightarrow & \exists \omega\in \overline{ \relax{S}}{}^{{}^{pure}}\;\vert\; V\sqsubseteq \{\, (\omega\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\kappa)\;\vert\; \kappa\in U_{ \relax{D}} \,\}
\end{eqnarray}
and then
 \begin{eqnarray}
Max\{\,\bigsqcup{}^{{}^{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}V\;\vert\; V\sqsubseteq U_{ \relax{D}}\;\textit{\rm and}\;\widehat{V}{}^{{}^{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\} \sqsubseteq
Max\{\,\bigsqcup{}^{{}^{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}_{\kappa\in U_{ \relax{D}}} (\omega\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\kappa)\;\vert\; \omega\in \overline{ \relax{S}}{}^{{}^{pure}} \,\}.\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;
\end{eqnarray}
In other words
\begin{eqnarray}
{\relax{c}}^{\overline{ \relax{S}}}(U_{ \relax{D}})\sqsubseteq U_{ \relax{D}}
\end{eqnarray}
But we have also (see property ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@propB3\endcsname\@firstoftwo{propB3}}}))
\begin{eqnarray}
{\relax{c}}^{\overline{ \relax{S}}}(U_{ \relax{D}})\sqsupseteq U_{ \relax{D}}
\end{eqnarray}
Then, by iteration, we deduce the announced result.
<!-- end proof-88 -->
<!-- lemma-64: body_md -->
\label{lemmanexistsomega1}
The subset of $\overline{ \relax{S}}$ defined by $\{\, \Sigma^{C^{(1)}_{\omega}}_{ \relax{D}}\;\vert\; \omega\in \overline{ \relax{S}}^{{}^{pure}}\,\}$ satisfies 
\begin{eqnarray}
\nexists \gamma\in \overline{ \relax{S}} &\vert & \{\,\gamma,\gamma^\star\,\} \sqsubseteq \{\, \Sigma^{C^{(1)}_{\omega}}_{ \relax{D}}\;\vert\; \omega\in \overline{ \relax{S}}^{{}^{pure}}\,\}.
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end lemma-64 -->
<!-- proof-89: body_md -->
Let us suppose that there exists $\gamma\in \overline{ \relax{S}}$ such that $\{\,\gamma,\gamma^\star\,\} \sqsubseteq \{\, \Sigma^{C^{(1)}_{\sigma}}_{ \relax{D}}\;\vert\; \sigma\in \overline{ \relax{S}}^{{}^{pure}}\,\}$, and let us exhibit a contradiction. We denote by $\omega$ and $\omega'$ the elements of $\overline{ \relax{S}}^{{}^{pure}}$ such that $\gamma \sqsubseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}} \Sigma^{C^{(1)}_{\omega}}_{ \relax{D}}$ and $\gamma^\star \sqsubseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\Sigma^{C^{(1)}_{\omega'}}_{ \relax{D}}$. There exists a maximal compatibility context of type 2 denoted $C$ such that ${ \relax{l}}_{(\gamma,\gamma^\star)}\in C$.  Applying Theorem {{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@synthesiscontexts\endcsname\@firstoftwo{synthesiscontexts}}} to the maximal context $C$ we deduce easily that ${ \relax{l}}_{(\gamma,\centerdot)}\in C$ and ${ \relax{l}}_{(\centerdot,\gamma^\star)}\in C$. Due to the sheaf condition satisfied by ${ \relax{D}}$, we know that
\begin{eqnarray}
&&{ \relax{d}}^{C}({ \relax{l}}_{(\gamma,\centerdot)}) = { \relax{d}}^{C^{(1)}_{\omega}}({ \relax{l}}_{(\gamma,\centerdot)}) = \epsilon^{ \relax{S}}_{{ \relax{l}}_{(\gamma,\centerdot)}}(\Sigma^{C^{(1)}_{\omega}}_{ \relax{D}})=\textit{\bf Y}\label{absurd1a}\\
&&{ \relax{d}}^{C}({ \relax{l}}_{(\centerdot,\gamma^\star)}) = { \relax{d}}^{C^{(1)}_{\omega'}}({ \relax{l}}_{(\centerdot, \gamma^\star)}) = \epsilon^{ \relax{S}}_{{ \relax{l}}_{(\centerdot, \gamma^\star)}}(\Sigma^{C^{(1)}_{\omega'}}_{ \relax{D}})=\textit{\bf N}\label{absurd1b}
\end{eqnarray}
but we have also
\begin{eqnarray}
&&{ \relax{d}}^{C}({ \relax{l}}_{(\gamma,\centerdot)})={ \relax{d}}^{C}({ \relax{Y}}_{{ \relax{E}}_{ \relax{S}}} \sqcap_{{}_{{ \relax{E}}_{ \relax{S}}}} { \relax{l}}_{(\gamma,\gamma^\star)})=\textit{\bf Y} \wedge { \relax{d}}^{C}({ \relax{l}}_{(\gamma,\gamma^\star)})\label{absurd2a}
\\
&&{ \relax{d}}^{C}({ \relax{l}}_{(\centerdot,\gamma^\star)}) = { \relax{d}}^{C}(\overline{{ \relax{Y}}_{{ \relax{E}}_{ \relax{S}}}} \sqcap_{{}_{{ \relax{E}}_{ \relax{S}}}} { \relax{l}}_{(\gamma,\gamma^\star)})=\textit{\bf N} \wedge { \relax{d}}^{C}({ \relax{l}}_{(\gamma,\gamma^\star)}).\label{absurd2b}
\end{eqnarray}
From ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@absurd1a\endcsname\@firstoftwo{absurd1a}}}) and ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@absurd2a\endcsname\@firstoftwo{absurd2a}}}) we deduce that necessarily ${ \relax{d}}^{C}({ \relax{l}}_{(\gamma,\gamma^\star)})=\textit{\bf Y}$, but using ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@absurd2b\endcsname\@firstoftwo{absurd2b}}}) we deduce ${ \relax{d}}^{C}({ \relax{l}}_{(\centerdot,\gamma^\star)})=\textit{\bf N} \wedge \textit{\bf Y}=\bot$ which contradicts ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@absurd1b\endcsname\@firstoftwo{absurd1b}}}). We have then obtained the announced contradiction. This concludes the proof.
<!-- end proof-89 -->
<!-- definition-57: body_md -->
\label{definitionoperationaldescriptionadmissible}
We will say that the operational description ${ \relax{D}}$ is {\em admissible} iff $\{\, \Sigma^{C^{(1)}_{\omega}}_{ \relax{D}}\;\vert\; \omega\in \overline{ \relax{S}}^{{}^{pure}}\,\}$ is admissible, i.e. iff $\{\, \Sigma^{C^{(1)}_{\omega}}_{ \relax{D}}\;\vert\; \omega\in \overline{ \relax{S}}^{{}^{pure}}\,\}\in { \mathcal{Q}}_c(\overline{ \relax{S}})$.
<!-- end definition-57 -->
<!-- theorem-41: body_md -->
\label{theoremoperationaldescriptionadmissible}
Every operational description ${ \relax{D}}$ are admissible.
<!-- end theorem-41 -->
<!-- proof-90: body_md -->
Direct consequence of Lemma {{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@lemmanexistsomega1\endcsname\@firstoftwo{lemmanexistsomega1}}} and Lemma {{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@lemmacU=U\endcsname\@firstoftwo{lemmacU=U}}}.
<!-- end proof-90 -->
<!-- lemma-65: body_md -->
\label{lemmasolutioncontext0}
As long as the operational description ${ \relax{D}}$ is admissible (see Theorem {{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@theoremoperationaldescriptionadmissible\endcsname\@firstoftwo{theoremoperationaldescriptionadmissible}}}), the supremum
\begin{eqnarray}
\Sigma_{ \relax{D}} &:=& \bigsqcup{}^{{}^{{ \relax{S}}}}_{\omega\in \overline{ \relax{S}}^{{}^{pure}}}\; \Sigma^{C^{(1)}_{\omega}}_{ \relax{D}}\label{solutionontic1}
\end{eqnarray}
 is well defined as an element of ${ \relax{S}}$.  
Then,we have
\begin{eqnarray}
\forall \omega \in \overline{ \relax{S}}^{{}^{pure}},&&\Sigma^{C^{(1)}_{\omega}}_{ \relax{D}} = \omega \sqcap_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}} \Sigma_{ \relax{D}}\label{solutionontic2}
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end lemma-65 -->
<!-- proof-91: body_md -->
From Theorem {{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@theoremoperationaldescriptionadmissible\endcsname\@firstoftwo{theoremoperationaldescriptionadmissible}}},  we know that 
$\{\, \Sigma^{C^{(1)}_{\omega}}_{ \relax{D}}\;\vert\; \omega\in \overline{ \relax{S}}^{{}^{pure}}\,\}$ is in ${ \mathcal{Q}}_c(\overline{ \relax{S}})$ and, then, 
\begin{eqnarray}
\Sigma_{ \relax{D}} &:=& cl_c^{{{ \relax{S}}'}}(\{\, \Sigma^{C^{(1)}_{\omega}}_{ \relax{D}}\;\vert\; \omega\in \overline{ \relax{S}}^{{}^{pure}}\,\})\\
&=&\bigsqcup{}^{{}^{{ \relax{S}}}}_{\omega\in \overline{ \relax{S}}^{{}^{pure}}}\; \Sigma^{C^{(1)}_{\omega}}_{ \relax{D}}
\end{eqnarray}
 is well defined as an element of ${ \relax{S}}$.  \\
Then, $\forall \omega' \in \overline{ \relax{S}}^{{}^{pure}}, \; \omega \sqcap_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}} \Sigma^{C^{(1)}_{\omega'}}_{ \relax{D}}  \sqsubseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}}   \Sigma^{C^{(1)}_{\omega}}_{ \relax{D}}$ implies $\omega \sqcap_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}} \Sigma_{ \relax{D}}  \sqsubseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}}   \Sigma^{C^{(1)}_{\omega}}_{ \relax{D}}$. \\
On another part, $\Sigma^{C^{(1)}_{\omega}}_{ \relax{D}}  \sqsubseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}}   \Sigma_{ \relax{D}}$ implies $\omega \sqcap_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}} \Sigma^{C^{(1)}_{\omega}}_{ \relax{D}}  \sqsubseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}} \omega \sqcap_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}} \Sigma_{ \relax{D}}$.\\
Endly, we recall that $\omega \sqcap_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}} \Sigma^{C^{(1)}_{\omega}}_{ \relax{D}} = \Sigma^{C^{(1)}_{\omega}}_{ \relax{D}}$.\\
As a conclusion, we obtain $\Sigma^{C^{(1)}_{\omega}}_{ \relax{D}} = \omega \sqcap_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}} \Sigma_{ \relax{D}}$.\\
Conversely, we easily check that the expression ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@solutionontic2\endcsname\@firstoftwo{solutionontic2}}}) satisfies the constraints ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@consitencyontic\endcsname\@firstoftwo{consitencyontic}}}).
<!-- end proof-91 -->
<!-- lemma-66: body_md -->
\label{lemmasolutioncontext1}
Let us consider a maximal compatibility context of type 1 denoted $C^{(1)}_{\omega}$.  We have
\begin{eqnarray}
\forall { \relax{l}}\in C^{(1)}_{\omega},&& { \relax{d}}^{C^{(1)}_{\omega}}({ \relax{l}})=\epsilon^{ \relax{S}}_{ \relax{l}}(\Sigma_{ \relax{D}}).
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end lemma-66 -->
<!-- proof-92: body_md -->
Let us compute ${ \relax{d}}^{C^{(1)}_{\omega}}({ \relax{l}})$ for any ${ \relax{l}}\in C^{(1)}_{\omega}$.  First of all, we note that, for any $\alpha \sqsubseteq_{{}_{ \relax{S}}}\omega$, we have
\begin{eqnarray}
&&\epsilon^{ \relax{S}}_{{ \relax{l}}_{(\alpha,\centerdot)}}(\Sigma_{ \relax{D}})=\epsilon^{ \relax{S}}_{{ \relax{Y}}_{{ \relax{E}}_{ \relax{S}}} \sqcap_{{}_{{ \relax{E}}_{ \relax{S}}}}
{ \relax{l}}_{(\alpha,\centerdot)}}(\Sigma_{ \relax{D}})=\textit{\bf Y}\wedge \epsilon^{ \relax{S}}_{{ \relax{l}}_{(\alpha,\centerdot)}}(\Sigma_{ \relax{D}})
\end{eqnarray}
and then 
\begin{eqnarray}
\epsilon^{ \relax{S}}_{{ \relax{l}}_{(\alpha,\centerdot)}}(\Sigma_{ \relax{D}}) & \in & \{\textit{\bf Y},\bot\}.
\end{eqnarray}
As a consequence, we have
\begin{eqnarray}
{ \relax{d}}^{C^{(1)}_{\omega}}({ \relax{l}}_{(\alpha,\centerdot)})=\epsilon^{ \relax{S}}_{{ \relax{l}}_{(\alpha,\centerdot)}}(\Sigma^{C^{(1)}_{\omega}}_{ \relax{D}})=\epsilon^{ \relax{S}}_{{ \relax{l}}_{(\alpha,\centerdot)}}(\omega \sqcap_{{}_{ \relax{S}}}
\Sigma_{ \relax{D}})=\textit{\bf Y}\wedge
\epsilon^{ \relax{S}}_{{ \relax{l}}_{(\alpha,\centerdot)}}(\Sigma_{ \relax{D}})=\epsilon^{ \relax{S}}_{{ \relax{l}}_{(\alpha,\centerdot)}}(\Sigma_{ \relax{D}}). \;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;
\end{eqnarray}
We can check analogously 
\begin{eqnarray}
{ \relax{d}}^{C^{(1)}_{\omega}}({ \relax{l}}_{(\centerdot,\alpha)})=\epsilon^{ \relax{S}}_{{ \relax{l}}_{(\centerdot,\alpha)}}(\Sigma_{ \relax{D}}). 
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end proof-92 -->
<!-- lemma-67: body_md -->
\label{lemmasolutioncontext2}
Let us consider a maximal compatibility context of type 2 denoted by $C$. We have
\begin{eqnarray}
\forall { \relax{l}}\in C, && { \relax{d}}^{C}({ \relax{l}}) = \epsilon^{ \relax{S}}_{{ \relax{l}}}(\Sigma_{ \relax{D}}).
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end lemma-67 -->
<!-- proof-93: body_md -->
Let us consider a maximal compatibility context of type 2 denoted by $C$ and let us choose $\lambda,\lambda'\in \overline{ \relax{S}} \smallsetminus \{\bot_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\}$ such that $\lambda' \sqsupseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}} \lambda^\star$ and $\omega,\omega'\in  {\overline{ \relax{S}}}^{{}^{pure}}$ such that $\omega  \sqsupseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}} \lambda, \omega'  \sqsupseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}} \lambda'$ with 
\begin{eqnarray}
&& (C\cap { \relax{U}}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}})\subseteq \left( \{\, { \relax{l}}_{(\sigma,\centerdot)}\;\vert\; \lambda \sqsubseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}} \sigma\sqsubseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}} \omega\,\}\cup \{\, { \relax{l}}_{(\centerdot,\sigma)}\;\vert\; \lambda \sqsubseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma\sqsubseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}} \omega\,\}\cup \{\, { \relax{l}}_{(\centerdot,\centerdot)}\,\}\cup \right.\nonumber\\
&&\hspace{1cm}\left.  \{\, { \relax{l}}_{(\sigma,\centerdot)}\;\vert\; \lambda' \sqsubseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}} \sigma\sqsubseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}} \omega'\,\}\cup \{\, { \relax{l}}_{(\centerdot,\sigma)}\;\vert\; \lambda' \sqsubseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma\sqsubseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}} \omega'\,\}\right)
\end{eqnarray}
We note that
\begin{eqnarray}
\forall { \relax{l}}_{(\alpha,\alpha')}\in C, && \left( \omega \sqsupseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}} \alpha \sqsupseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}} \lambda \;\;\textit{\rm and}\;\; \omega' \sqsupseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}} \alpha' \sqsupseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}} \lambda'\right).
\end{eqnarray}
We also note that, for any ${ \relax{l}}_{(\alpha,\alpha')}\in C$, we have
\begin{eqnarray}
\textit{\bf Y}\wedge { \relax{d}}^{C}({ \relax{l}}_{(\alpha,\alpha')}) &=&{ \relax{d}}^{C}({ \relax{Y}}_{{ \relax{E}}_{ \relax{S}}} \sqcap_{{}_{{ \relax{E}}_{ \relax{S}}}}
{ \relax{l}}_{(\alpha,\alpha')})\nonumber\\
&=& { \relax{d}}^{C}({ \relax{l}}_{(\alpha,\centerdot)})\nonumber\\
&=& { \relax{d}}^{C^{(1)}_\omega}({ \relax{l}}_{(\alpha,\centerdot)})\nonumber\\
&=& \epsilon^{ \relax{S}}_{{ \relax{l}}_{(\alpha,\centerdot)}}(\Sigma_{ \relax{D}})\nonumber\\
&=& \epsilon^{ \relax{S}}_{{ \relax{Y}}_{{ \relax{E}}_{ \relax{S}}} \sqcap_{{}_{{ \relax{E}}_{ \relax{S}}}} { \relax{l}}_{(\alpha,\alpha')}}(\Sigma_{ \relax{D}})\nonumber\\
&=& \textit{\bf Y}\wedge \epsilon^{ \relax{S}}_{{ \relax{l}}_{(\alpha,\alpha')}}(\Sigma_{ \relax{D}})
\end{eqnarray}
and 
\begin{eqnarray}
\textit{\bf N}\wedge { \relax{d}}^{C}({ \relax{l}}_{(\alpha,\alpha')}) &=&{ \relax{d}}^{C}(\overline{{ \relax{Y}}_{{ \relax{E}}_{ \relax{S}}}} \sqcap_{{}_{{ \relax{E}}_{ \relax{S}}}}
{ \relax{l}}_{(\alpha,\alpha')})\nonumber\\
&=& { \relax{d}}^{C}({ \relax{l}}_{(\centerdot,\alpha')})\nonumber\\
&=& { \relax{d}}^{C^{(1)}_{\omega'}}({ \relax{l}}_{(\centerdot,\alpha')})\nonumber\\
&=& \epsilon^{ \relax{S}}_{{ \relax{l}}_{(\centerdot,\alpha')}}(\Sigma_{ \relax{D}})\nonumber\\
&=& \epsilon^{ \relax{S}}_{\overline{{ \relax{Y}}_{{ \relax{E}}_{ \relax{S}}}} \sqcap_{{}_{{ \relax{E}}_{ \relax{S}}}} { \relax{l}}_{(\alpha,\alpha')}}(\Sigma_{ \relax{D}})\nonumber\\
&=& \textit{\bf N}\wedge \epsilon^{ \relax{S}}_{{ \relax{l}}_{(\alpha,\alpha')}}(\Sigma_{ \relax{D}}).
\end{eqnarray}
From these two relations, we deduce immediately
\begin{eqnarray}
{ \relax{d}}^{C}({ \relax{l}}_{(\alpha,\alpha')}) &=& \epsilon^{ \relax{S}}_{{ \relax{l}}_{(\alpha,\alpha')}}(\Sigma_{ \relax{D}}).
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end proof-93 -->
<!-- theorem-42: body_md -->
\label{DSigmaepsilon}
Let us consider an operational description ${ \relax{D}}$. We have then necessarily the following property :
\begin{eqnarray}
\exists \Sigma_{ \relax{D}}:=  (\bigsqcup{}^{{}^{{ \relax{S}}}}_{\omega\in \overline{ \relax{S}}^{{}^{pure}}}\; \Sigma^{C^{(1)}_{\omega}}_{ \relax{D}}) &\vert & \forall C\in {\mathcal{C}},\forall { \relax{l}}\in C,\;\; { \relax{d}}^{C}({ \relax{l}})=\epsilon^{ \relax{S}}_{ \relax{l}}(\Sigma_{ \relax{D}}).\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end theorem-42 -->
<!-- proof-94: body_md -->
Direct consequence of Lemma {{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@lemmasolutioncontext0\endcsname\@firstoftwo{lemmasolutioncontext0}}}, Lemma {{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@lemmasolutioncontext1\endcsname\@firstoftwo{lemmasolutioncontext1}}},Lemma {{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@lemmasolutioncontext2\endcsname\@firstoftwo{lemmasolutioncontext2}}}.
<!-- end proof-94 -->
<!-- theorem-43: body_md -->
\label{DSigmaisomorphism}
The map from ${ \mathcal{D}}$ to ${ \relax{S}}$, sending ${ \relax{D}}$ to $\Sigma_{ \relax{D}}:=  (\bigsqcup{}^{{}^{{ \relax{S}}}}_{\omega\in \overline{ \relax{S}}^{{}^{pure}}}\; \Sigma^{C^{(1)}_{\omega}}_{ \relax{D}})$ is an isomorphism.
<!-- end theorem-43 -->
<!-- proof-95: body_md -->
First of all, we note that we can effectively associate to any ${ \relax{D}}\in { \mathcal{D}}$ an element $\Sigma_{ \relax{D}}$ satisfying
\begin{eqnarray}
\forall C\in {\mathcal{C}},\forall { \relax{l}}\in C, && { \relax{d}}^{C}({ \relax{l}})=\epsilon^{ \relax{S}}_{ \relax{l}}(\Sigma_{ \relax{D}}).
\end{eqnarray}
This point is guarantied by Lemma {{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@lemmasolutioncontext0\endcsname\@firstoftwo{lemmasolutioncontext0}}}, Lemma {{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@lemmasolutioncontext1\endcsname\@firstoftwo{lemmasolutioncontext1}}} and Lemma {{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@lemmasolutioncontext2\endcsname\@firstoftwo{lemmasolutioncontext2}}}.  More explicitly, we have $\Sigma_{ \relax{D}}:=  (\bigsqcup{}^{{}^{{ \relax{S}}}}_{\omega\in \overline{ \relax{S}}^{{}^{pure}}}\; \Sigma^{C^{(1)}_{\omega}}_{ \relax{D}})\in { \relax{S}}$ where the state $\Sigma^{C^{(1)}_{\omega}}_{ \relax{D}}$ is defined in reference to ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@onticstate1\endcsname\@firstoftwo{onticstate1}}}) ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@onticstate2\endcsname\@firstoftwo{onticstate2}}}) and Lemma {{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@lemmacontexttype1\endcsname\@firstoftwo{lemmacontexttype1}}}.\\
Note that the supremum defining $\Sigma_{ \relax{D}}$ exists in ${ \relax{S}}$ because ${ \relax{D}}$ is admissible.\\
Secondly, this map is clearly injective.  Indeed, let us consider a pair ${ \relax{D}},{ \relax{D}}'$ of coherent  operational descriptions such that $\Sigma_{ \relax{D}}=\Sigma_{ \relax{D}'}$.  We have obviously $\forall C\in {\mathcal{C}},\forall { \relax{l}}\in C,\;\; { \relax{d}}^{C}({ \relax{l}})=\epsilon^{ \relax{S}}_{ \relax{l}}(\Sigma_{ \relax{D}})=\epsilon^{ \relax{S}}_{ \relax{l}}(\Sigma_{ \relax{D}'})={ \relax{d}'}^{C}({ \relax{l}})$.\\
Endly, this map is also clearly a surjection. Indeed, we can associate, to any $\alpha\in { \relax{S}}$,  a coherent  operational description ${ \relax{D}}_\alpha:=({ \relax{d}}_{(\alpha)}^{C})_{C\in {\mathcal{C}}}$ by $\forall C\in {\mathcal{C}},\forall { \relax{l}}\in C,{ \relax{d}}_{(\alpha)}^{C}({ \relax{l}}):=\epsilon^{ \relax{S}}_{ \relax{l}}(\alpha)$.  We have then, for any $\omega\in \overline{ \relax{S}}^{{}^{pure}}$, 
\begin{eqnarray}
\Sigma^{C^{(1)}_{\omega}}_{ \relax{D}_\alpha} &=& \alpha \sqcap_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}} \omega.
\end{eqnarray}
We then build as usual $\Sigma_{ \relax{D}_\alpha}:=  (\bigsqcup{}^{{}^{{ \relax{S}}}}_{\omega\in \overline{ \relax{S}}^{{}^{pure}}}\; \Sigma^{C^{(1)}_{\omega}}_{ \relax{D}_\alpha})$. We have by construction $\forall C\in {\mathcal{C}},\forall { \relax{l}}\in C,\epsilon^{ \relax{S}}_{ \relax{l}}(\Sigma_{ {\relax{D}}_{(\alpha)}})=\epsilon^{ \relax{S}}_{ \relax{l}}(\alpha)$. Using ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@realChuseparated\endcsname\@firstoftwo{realChuseparated}}}), we then conclude that $\Sigma_{ {\relax{D}}_{(\alpha)}} =\alpha$.\\
Endly, we derive easily the homomorphic property from the properties of the evaluation map $\epsilon^{ \relax{S}}$ :
\begin{eqnarray}
\forall C\in {\mathcal{C}},\forall { \relax{l}}\in C,&& ({ \relax{d}}^{C}\sqcap_{{}_{\mathcal{D}}} { \relax{d}'}^{C})({ \relax{l}})=\epsilon^{ \relax{S}}_{ \relax{l}}(\Sigma_{ \relax{D}})\wedge \epsilon^{ \relax{S}}_{ \relax{l}}(\Sigma_{ \relax{D}'})
=\epsilon^{ \relax{S}}_{ \relax{l}}(\Sigma_{ \relax{D}}\sqcap_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}} \Sigma_{ \relax{D}'}).\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end proof-95 -->
<!-- theorem-44: body_md -->
Let us consider $\mu,\nu,\phi\in \overline{ \relax{S}}{}^{{}^{pure}}$ and $\gamma\in \overline{ \relax{S}}$ such that $\gamma=(\phi\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{\relax{S}}}}\nu)\raisebox{1.3ex}{\,\rotatebox{180}{$\sqsupseteq$}}\,_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}} \phi,\nu$ and $\mu^\star\not\sqsubseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\gamma$, we have
\begin{eqnarray}
                                                                                                                                                
\chi:=(\mu^\star\sqcup_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}}\gamma)\;\;\textit{\rm exists in}\;{ \relax{S}}.
\label{thirdcoveringpropertySbari}
\end{eqnarray}
We have then either $\chi\in \overline{ \relax{S}}{}^{{}^{pure}}$ or $\chi\in { \relax{S}}\smallsetminus \overline{ \relax{S}}$ and then, in the last case,  denoting as usual $\Theta^{\overline{ \relax{S}}}(\chi):=Max((\downarrow_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}}\chi)\cap \overline{ \relax{S}})$, we have
\begin{eqnarray}
&&\forall \alpha\in \Theta^{\overline{ \relax{S}}}(\chi),\;\;  (\exists \kappa\in \overline{ \relax{S}}{}^{{}^{pure}}\;\vert\; \alpha\raisebox{1.3ex}{\,\rotatebox{180}{$\sqsupseteq$}}\,_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\kappa)\;\textit{\rm and}\;
\alpha\raisebox{1.3ex}{\,\rotatebox{180}{$\sqsupseteq$}}\,_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}} \chi 
\label{thirdcoveringpropertySbarii}\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\\
&& \forall \alpha,\beta\in \Theta^{\overline{ \relax{S}}}(\chi),\;\alpha\not=\beta,\;\;\;\;(\alpha\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\beta)\raisebox{1.3ex}{\,\rotatebox{180}{$\sqsupseteq$}}\,_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}} \alpha,\beta,\label{thirdcoveringpropertySbariii}\\
&&\forall \alpha,\beta,\delta\in \Theta^{\overline{ \relax{S}}}(\chi)\;\textit{\rm distinct}, \;\;\;\;(\alpha\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\beta)\not=(\alpha\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\delta),\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\label{thirdcoveringpropertySbariv}
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 
\end{eqnarray}

Let us once again consider $\mu\in \overline{ \relax{S}}{}^{{}^{pure}}$ and $\gamma\in \overline{ \relax{S}}$ such that $\mu^\star\not\sqsubseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\gamma$.
Let us assume that there exists $\nu\in \overline{ \relax{S}}{}^{{}^{pure}}$ such that $\gamma=(\mu\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{\relax{S}}}}\nu)\raisebox{1.3ex}{\,\rotatebox{180}{$\sqsupseteq$}}\,_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}} \mu,\nu$ then let us here again denote $\chi=(\mu^\star\sqcup_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}}\gamma)$.\\ 
If we have $\chi\in \overline{ \relax{S}}$, then necessarily $\chi\in \overline{ \relax{S}}{}^{{}^{pure}}$, and if we have $\chi\in { \relax{S}}\smallsetminus \overline{ \relax{S}}$ then
\begin{eqnarray}
&&\exists (\varphi_{\epsilon})_{\epsilon},(\psi_{\epsilon})_{\epsilon} \in (\overline{ \relax{S}}{}^{{}^{pure}})^{\Theta^{\overline{ \relax{S}}}(\chi)}\;\vert\; \nonumber\\
&&\hspace{0.3cm}\varphi_{\gamma}:=\mu,\psi_{\gamma}:=\nu, \;\;\forall \alpha\in \Theta^{\overline{ \relax{S}}}(\chi)\smallsetminus \{\gamma\},\;\;\; \varphi_\gamma^\star\sqsubseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}} \varphi_\alpha,\;\;\varphi_\gamma^\star \sqsubseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}} \psi_\alpha,\label{thirdcoveringpropertySbar0}\\
&&\hspace{0.3cm}\forall \epsilon\in \Theta^{\overline{ \relax{S}}}(\chi)\smallsetminus\{\gamma\},\;\;\;
\psi_{\epsilon},\varphi_{\epsilon}\raisebox{1.3ex}{\,\rotatebox{180}{$\sqsubseteq$}}\,_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\epsilon,\;\;
\psi_{\epsilon}\not=\varphi_{\epsilon}\label{thirdcoveringpropertySbar0bis}\\
&&\hspace{0.3cm}\forall \epsilon\in \Theta^{\overline{ \relax{S}}}(\chi)\smallsetminus \{\gamma\},\;\;\;\varphi_{\epsilon}^\star \sqsubseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}}\psi_{\epsilon},                    
\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\label{thirdcoveringpropertySbarviic}\\
&&\hspace{0.3cm}\forall \alpha,\beta\in \Theta^{\overline{ \relax{S}}}(\chi)\smallsetminus \{\gamma\},\alpha\not=\beta,\;\;\; \varphi_{\alpha}^\star \sqsubseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\varphi_{\beta},\;\;\varphi_{\alpha}^\star \not\sqsubseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\psi_{\beta},\label{thirdcoveringpropertySbarviib}\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\\
&&\hspace{0.3cm}\forall \alpha,\beta\in \Theta^{\overline{ \relax{S}}}(\chi)\smallsetminus \{\gamma\},\alpha\not=\beta,\;\exists \lambda_{\alpha\beta}\in \overline{ \relax{S}}{}^{{}^{pure}}\;\vert\; 
(\varphi_{\beta}\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\psi_{\alpha}), (\psi_{\beta}\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\varphi_{\alpha})\raisebox{1.3ex}{\,\rotatebox{180}{$\sqsupseteq$}}\,_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\lambda_{\alpha\beta},
\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\nonumber\\
&&\hspace{6.5cm}\textit{\rm and}\;\lambda_{\alpha\beta}^\star \sqsubseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\varphi_{\alpha},\;\;\lambda_{\alpha\beta}^\star \sqsubseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\varphi_{\beta},\label{thirdcoveringpropertySbarviia}\\
&&\hspace{0.3cm}\forall \alpha\in \Theta^{\overline{ \relax{S}}}(\chi)\smallsetminus \{\gamma\},\exists \mu_{\alpha\gamma}\in \overline{ \relax{S}}{}^{{}^{pure}}\;\vert\; 
(\varphi_{\gamma}\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\varphi_{\alpha}), (\psi_{\gamma}\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\psi_{\alpha})\raisebox{1.3ex}{\,\rotatebox{180}{$\sqsupseteq$}}\,_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\mu_{\alpha\gamma}
\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\nonumber\\
&&\hspace{6.5cm}\textit{\rm and}\;\mu_{\alpha\gamma}^\star \sqsubseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\psi_{\alpha},\label{thirdcoveringpropertySbarviiabis}
\end{eqnarray}
The collections $(\varphi_{\epsilon})_{\epsilon},(\psi_{\epsilon})_{\epsilon} \in (\overline{ \relax{S}}{}^{{}^{pure}})^{\Theta^{\overline{ \relax{S}}}(\chi)}$ satisfying the properties ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@thirdcoveringpropertySbar0\endcsname\@firstoftwo{thirdcoveringpropertySbar0}}})({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@thirdcoveringpropertySbarviic\endcsname\@firstoftwo{thirdcoveringpropertySbarviic}}})({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@thirdcoveringpropertySbarviib\endcsname\@firstoftwo{thirdcoveringpropertySbarviib}}}) are {unique} up to a permutation on the elements of $\Theta^{\overline{ \relax{S}}}(\chi)\smallsetminus \{\gamma\}$. \\

Let us once again consider $\mu\in \overline{ \relax{S}}{}^{{}^{pure}}$ and $\gamma\in \overline{ \relax{S}}$ such that $\mu^\star\not\sqsubseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\gamma$.
If there exists $\nu\in \overline{ \relax{S}}{}^{{}^{pure}}$ such that $\gamma=(\mu\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{\relax{S}}}}\nu)\raisebox{1.3ex}{\,\rotatebox{180}{$\sqsupseteq$}}\,_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}} \mu,\nu$ then let us here again denote $\chi=(\mu^\star\sqcup_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}}\gamma)$. If we have $\chi\in { \relax{S}}\smallsetminus \overline{ \relax{S}}$ then
\begin{eqnarray}
&&\forall \beta\in \Theta^{\overline{ \relax{S}}}(\chi)\smallsetminus \{\gamma\},\exists \omega,\kappa\in \overline{ \relax{S}}{}^{{}^{pure}}\;\vert\; \nonumber\\
&&\hspace{3cm}(\omega\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\kappa)\raisebox{1.3ex}{\,\rotatebox{180}{$\sqsupseteq$}}\,_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\omega,\kappa,\;\textit{\rm and}\;
\omega^\star\sqcup_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}}(\omega\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\kappa)=\beta\sqcup_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}}\gamma^\star                                                                                     
\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;
\label{thirdcoveringpropertySbarvi}
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end theorem-44 -->
<!-- proof-96: body_md -->
We will consider $\alpha,\alpha',\alpha''\in \overline{ \relax{S}}{}_{A}^{{}^{pure}}$ and $\beta,\beta',\beta''\in \overline{ \relax{S}}{}_{B}^{{}^{pure}}$ and we intent to compute 
$$cl_c^{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}\left(
\left\{(\alpha''\widetilde{\otimes}\beta''\sqcap_{{}_{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}}\!\!\!\alpha'\widetilde{\otimes}\beta')
\,,\,(\alpha\widetilde{\otimes}\beta)^\star\right\}\right)$$ with $\alpha'\not=\alpha''$ or $\beta'\not=\beta''$, and with $(\alpha\widetilde{\otimes}\beta)^\star\not\sqsubseteq_{{}_{{{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}}}}(\alpha''\widetilde{\otimes}\beta''\sqcap_{{}_{{{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}}}}\!\!\!\alpha'\widetilde{\otimes}\beta')$.\\

We will distinguish different cases.\\

(1) $\alpha'\not=\alpha''$  and $\beta''=\beta'$.  We have $(\alpha''\widetilde{\otimes}\beta''\sqcap_{{}_{{{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}}}}\!\!\!\alpha'\widetilde{\otimes}\beta')=\bot_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}_{A}}}\widetilde{\otimes}\beta'$ and then $\alpha^\star\widetilde{\otimes}\beta'$ is the supremum of $(\alpha''\widetilde{\otimes}\beta''\sqcap_{{}_{{{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}}}}\!\!\!\alpha'\widetilde{\otimes}\beta')$ and $(\alpha^\star \widetilde{\otimes}\bot_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}_{B}}})\sqcap_{{}_{{{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}}}} (\bot_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}_{A}}}\widetilde{\otimes} \beta^\star)$.  Hence, $$cl_c^{{{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}}}\left(
\left\{(\alpha''\widetilde{\otimes}\beta''\sqcap_{{}_{{{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}}}}\!\!\!\alpha'\widetilde{\otimes}\beta')
\,,\,(\alpha\widetilde{\otimes}\beta)^\star\right\}\right)=\{\alpha^\star\widetilde{\otimes}\beta'\}\;\in \; {\mathcal{K}}({{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}})$$

(2) $\alpha'=\alpha''$  and $\beta''\not=\beta'$.  We have $(\alpha''\widetilde{\otimes}\beta''\sqcap_{{}_{{{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}}}}\!\!\!\alpha'\widetilde{\otimes}\beta')=\alpha'\widetilde{\otimes}\bot_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}_{A}}}$ and then $\alpha'\widetilde{\otimes}\beta^\star$ is the supremum of $(\alpha''\widetilde{\otimes}\beta''\sqcap_{{}_{{{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}}}}\!\!\!\alpha'\widetilde{\otimes}\beta')$ and $(\alpha^\star \widetilde{\otimes}\bot_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}_{B}}})\sqcap_{{}_{{{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}}}} (\bot_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}_{A}}}\widetilde{\otimes} \beta^\star)$.  Hence, $$cl_c^{{{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}}}\left(
\left\{(\alpha''\widetilde{\otimes}\beta''\sqcap_{{}_{{{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}}}}\!\!\!\alpha'\widetilde{\otimes}\beta')
\,,\,(\alpha\widetilde{\otimes}\beta)^\star\right\}\right)=\{\alpha'\widetilde{\otimes}\beta^\star\}\;\in \; {\mathcal{K}}({{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}})$$

(3) $\alpha''\not=\alpha'$ or $\beta''\not=\beta'$.  We have to distinguish different sub-cases :\\
(3A) $\alpha'\sqsupseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}_{A}}} \alpha^\star$ or $\beta'\sqsupseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}_{A}}} \beta^\star$. Then, $\alpha'\widetilde{\otimes}\beta'$ is the supremum in ${{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}}$ of $(\alpha''\widetilde{\otimes}\beta''\sqcap_{{}_{{{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}}}}\!\!\!\alpha'\widetilde{\otimes}\beta')$ and $(\alpha^\star \widetilde{\otimes}\bot_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}_{B}}})\sqcap_{{}_{{{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}}}} (\bot_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}_{A}}}\widetilde{\otimes} \beta^\star)$. And then, $$cl_c^{{{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}}}\left(
\left\{(\alpha''\widetilde{\otimes}\beta''\sqcap_{{}_{{{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}}}}\!\!\!\alpha'\widetilde{\otimes}\beta')
\,,\,(\alpha\widetilde{\otimes}\beta)^\star\right\}\right)=\{\alpha'\widetilde{\otimes}\beta'\}\;\in \; {\mathcal{K}}({{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}})$$
(3B) $\alpha''\sqsupseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}_{A}}} \alpha^\star$ or $\beta''\sqsupseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}_{A}}} \beta^\star$. Then, $\alpha''\widetilde{\otimes}\beta''$ is the supremum in ${{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}}$ of $(\alpha''\widetilde{\otimes}\beta''\sqcap_{{}_{{{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}}}}\!\!\!\alpha'\widetilde{\otimes}\beta')$ and $(\alpha^\star \widetilde{\otimes}\bot_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}_{B}}})\sqcap_{{}_{{{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}}}} (\bot_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}_{A}}}\widetilde{\otimes} \beta^\star)$. And then, $$cl_c^{{{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}}}\left(
\left\{(\alpha''\widetilde{\otimes}\beta''\sqcap_{{}_{{{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}}}}\!\!\!\alpha'\widetilde{\otimes}\beta')
\,,\,(\alpha\widetilde{\otimes}\beta)^\star\right\}\right)=\{\alpha''\widetilde{\otimes}\beta''\}\;\in \; {\mathcal{K}}({{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}})$$
(3C) $\alpha'\not\sqsupseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}_{A}}} \alpha^\star$ and $\beta'\not\sqsupseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}_{A}}} \beta^\star$ and $\alpha''\sqsupseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}_{A}}} \alpha^\star$ or $\beta''\sqsupseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}_{A}}} \beta^\star$. Then, we note that $(\alpha''\widetilde{\otimes}\beta'')\sqcap_{{}_{{{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}}}}\!\!\!(\alpha'\widetilde{\otimes}\beta')$ and $(\alpha^\star \widetilde{\otimes}\bot_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}_{B}}})\sqcap_{{}_{{{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}}}} (\bot_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}_{A}}}\widetilde{\otimes} \beta^\star)$ have no common upper-bound in ${{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}}$. We have then to note that $(\alpha'' \widetilde{\otimes}\bot_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}_{B}}})\sqcap_{{}_{{{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}}}} (\bot_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}_{A}}}\widetilde{\otimes} \beta')$ and $(\alpha^\star \widetilde{\otimes}\bot_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}_{B}}})\sqcap_{{}_{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}} (\bot_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}_{A}}}\widetilde{\otimes} \beta^\star)$ admit a supremum in ${{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}}$ which is $(\alpha'' \widetilde{\otimes}\beta^\star)\sqcap_{{}_{{{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}}}} (\alpha^\star\widetilde{\otimes} \beta')$. We note also that $(\alpha' \widetilde{\otimes}\bot_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}_{B}}})\sqcap_{{}_{{{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}}}} (\bot_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}_{A}}}\widetilde{\otimes} \beta'')$ and $(\alpha^\star \widetilde{\otimes}\bot_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}_{B}}})\sqcap_{{}_{{{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}}}} (\bot_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}_{A}}}\widetilde{\otimes} \beta^\star)$ admit a supremum in ${{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}}$ which is $(\alpha' \widetilde{\otimes}\beta^\star)\sqcap_{{}_{{{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}}}} (\alpha^\star\widetilde{\otimes} \beta'')$. Hence, we check directly that 
\begin{eqnarray}
&&{ \relax{c}}^{{{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}}}\left(
\left\{(\alpha''\widetilde{\otimes}\beta'')\sqcap_{{}_{{{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}}}}\!\!\!(\alpha'\widetilde{\otimes}\beta')
\,,\,(\alpha\widetilde{\otimes}\beta)^\star\right\}\right) =:U \nonumber\\
&&U= \left\{ (\alpha''\widetilde{\otimes}\beta'')\sqcap_{{}_{{{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}}}}\!\!\!(\alpha'\widetilde{\otimes}\beta')
\,,\,
(\alpha'' \widetilde{\otimes}\beta^\star)\sqcap_{{}_{{{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}}}} (\alpha^\star\widetilde{\otimes} \beta')\,,\,
(\alpha' \widetilde{\otimes}\beta^\star)\sqcap_{{}_{{{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}}}} (\alpha^\star\widetilde{\otimes} \beta'')
\right\}\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;
\end{eqnarray}
It is then rather easy to check that ${ \relax{c}}^{{{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}}}(U)=U$. Hence, $cl_c^{{{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}}}(U)=U$. 
Endly, we check directly that $U\in {\mathcal{K}}({{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}})$ (note that this check uses explicitly the properties  $\alpha'\not\sqsupseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}_{A}}} \alpha^\star$ and $\beta'\not\sqsupseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}_{A}}} \beta^\star$  and $\alpha''\sqsupseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}_{A}}} \alpha^\star$ or $\beta''\sqsupseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}_{A}}} \beta^\star$ assumed in case 3C). As a result
\begin{eqnarray}
&&cl_c^{{{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}}}\left(
\left\{(\alpha''\widetilde{\otimes}\beta'')\sqcap_{{}_{{{{ \overline{S}}}}_{AB}}}\!\!\!(\alpha'\widetilde{\otimes}\beta')
\,,\,(\alpha\widetilde{\otimes}\beta)^\star\right\}\right) =:U \nonumber\\
&&U= \left\{ (\alpha''\widetilde{\otimes}\beta'')\sqcap_{{}_{{{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}}}}\!\!\!(\alpha'\widetilde{\otimes}\beta')
\,,\,
(\alpha'' \widetilde{\otimes}\beta^\star)\sqcap_{{}_{{{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}}}} (\alpha^\star\widetilde{\otimes} \beta')\,,\,
(\alpha' \widetilde{\otimes}\beta^\star)\sqcap_{{}_{{{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}}}} (\alpha^\star\widetilde{\otimes} \beta'')
\right\}\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\label{computationexample}
\end{eqnarray}

As a conclusion of this case analysis we have proved the property ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@thirdcoveringpropertySbari\endcsname\@firstoftwo{thirdcoveringpropertySbari}}}). By the way we can check directly on the expressions of $cl_c^{{{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}}}\left(
\left\{(\alpha''\widetilde{\otimes}\beta'')\sqcap_{{}_{{{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}}}}\!\!\!(\alpha'\widetilde{\otimes}\beta')
\,,\,(\alpha\widetilde{\otimes}\beta)^\star\right\}\right)$ established along this case analysis the properties ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@thirdcoveringpropertySbarii\endcsname\@firstoftwo{thirdcoveringpropertySbarii}}})({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@thirdcoveringpropertySbariii\endcsname\@firstoftwo{thirdcoveringpropertySbariii}}})({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@thirdcoveringpropertySbariv\endcsname\@firstoftwo{thirdcoveringpropertySbariv}}}) and also the properties ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@thirdcoveringpropertySbarviic\endcsname\@firstoftwo{thirdcoveringpropertySbarviic}}})({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@thirdcoveringpropertySbarviib\endcsname\@firstoftwo{thirdcoveringpropertySbarviib}}}) if we restrict ourselves to the case $\alpha=\alpha''$ and $\beta''=\beta$.\\

Let us summarize. If $\chi:=(\alpha\widetilde{\otimes}\beta)^\star \sqcup_{{}_{{{{ \widetilde{\relax{S}}}}}}}
(\alpha\widetilde{\otimes}\beta\sqcap_{{}_{{{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}}}}\!\!\!\alpha'\widetilde{\otimes}\beta')$ is in ${ \relax{S}}\smallsetminus \overline{ \relax{S}}$, we have
\begin{eqnarray}
\Theta^{{{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}}}\left(\chi\right)&=&\{\gamma,\delta, \epsilon\}\\
\gamma=(\alpha\widetilde{\otimes}\beta\sqcap_{{}_{{{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}}}}\!\!\!\alpha'\widetilde{\otimes}\beta'),&& \varphi_\gamma=\alpha\widetilde{\otimes}\beta,\;\;\;\;\psi_\gamma=\alpha'\widetilde{\otimes}\beta',\nonumber\\
\delta=(\alpha\widetilde{\otimes}\beta^\star\sqcap_{{}_{{{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}}}}\!\!\!\alpha^\star\widetilde{\otimes}\beta'),&& \varphi_\delta=\alpha\widetilde{\otimes}\beta^\star,\;\;\;\;\psi_\delta=\alpha^\star\widetilde{\otimes}\beta',\nonumber\\
\epsilon=(\alpha'\widetilde{\otimes}\beta^\star\sqcap_{{}_{{{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}}}}\!\!\!\alpha^\star\widetilde{\otimes}\beta),&& \varphi_\epsilon=\alpha^\star\widetilde{\otimes}\beta,\;\;\;\;\psi_\epsilon=\alpha'\widetilde{\otimes}\beta^\star,\nonumber\\
\lambda_{\delta\epsilon}=\alpha^\star\widetilde{\otimes}\beta^\star,&& \mu_{\gamma\delta}=\alpha\widetilde{\otimes}\beta',\;\;\;\;\mu_{\gamma\epsilon}=\alpha'\widetilde{\otimes}\beta.\nonumber
\end{eqnarray}
The collections $(\varphi_{\epsilon})_{\epsilon},(\psi_{\epsilon})_{\epsilon} \in (\overline{ \relax{S}}{}^{{}^{pure}})^{\Theta^{\overline{ \relax{S}}}(\chi)}$ given above satisfy the properties ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@thirdcoveringpropertySbar0\endcsname\@firstoftwo{thirdcoveringpropertySbar0}}})({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@thirdcoveringpropertySbarviic\endcsname\@firstoftwo{thirdcoveringpropertySbarviic}}})({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@thirdcoveringpropertySbarviib\endcsname\@firstoftwo{thirdcoveringpropertySbarviib}}}). They are {unique} up to a permutation on the set $\{\delta,\epsilon\}$ because of the following basic property
\begin{eqnarray}
\forall \alpha\in \{\gamma,\delta, \epsilon\},&& \underline{\,\alpha\,}_{{{{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}}}}=\{\varphi_\alpha,\psi_\alpha\}
\end{eqnarray}
inherited from ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@developmentetildeordersimplify\endcsname\@firstoftwo{developmentetildeordersimplify}}}). \\ 
The properties ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@thirdcoveringpropertySbarviia\endcsname\@firstoftwo{thirdcoveringpropertySbarviia}}})({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@thirdcoveringpropertySbarviiabis\endcsname\@firstoftwo{thirdcoveringpropertySbarviiabis}}}) can be checked directly.\\

Concerning the property ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@thirdcoveringpropertySbarvi\endcsname\@firstoftwo{thirdcoveringpropertySbarvi}}}), it suffice to compute
\begin{eqnarray}
&&cl_c^{{{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}}}\left(
\left\{\left((\alpha\widetilde{\otimes}\beta)\sqcap_{{}_{{{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}}}}\!\!\!(\alpha'\widetilde{\otimes}\beta')\right)^\star
\,,\, 
(\alpha \widetilde{\otimes}\beta^\star)\sqcap_{{}_{{{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}}}} (\alpha^\star\widetilde{\otimes} \beta')
\right\}\right) = \nonumber\\
&&= \left\{ (\alpha^\star\widetilde{\otimes}\beta'{}^\star)\sqcap_{{}_{{{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}}}}\!\!\!(\alpha'{}^\star\widetilde{\otimes}\beta^\star)
\,,\,
(\alpha \widetilde{\otimes}\beta^\star)\sqcap_{{}_{{{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}}}} (\alpha^\star\widetilde{\otimes} \beta')\,,\,
(\alpha \widetilde{\otimes}\beta'{}^\star)\sqcap_{{}_{{{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}}}} (\alpha'{}^\star\widetilde{\otimes} \beta')
\right\}\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;
\end{eqnarray}
and to observe then that
\begin{eqnarray}
&&cl_c^{{{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}}}\left(
\left\{\left((\alpha\widetilde{\otimes}\beta)\sqcap_{{}_{{{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}}}}\!\!\!(\alpha'\widetilde{\otimes}\beta')\right)^\star
\,,\, 
(\alpha \widetilde{\otimes}\beta^\star)\sqcap_{{}_{{{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}}}} (\alpha^\star\widetilde{\otimes} \beta')
\right\}\right) = \nonumber\\
&&cl_c^{{{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}}}\left(\left\{ 
(\alpha^\star\widetilde{\otimes}\beta'{}^\star)^\star
\,,\, 
(\alpha^\star\widetilde{\otimes}\beta'{}^\star)\sqcap_{{}_{{{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}}}}\!\!\!(\alpha'{}^\star\widetilde{\otimes}\beta^\star)
\right\}\right)
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end proof-96 -->
<!-- definition-58: body_md -->
\label{definwr}
Let us consider $\nu$  and $\phi$ two  elements of ${{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}}{}^{{}^{pure}}$. We will define the following reflexive and symmetric binary relation
\begin{eqnarray}
\hspace{-1cm}\nu \wr \phi\;\;&:\Leftrightarrow & (\,\exists I\subseteq\{1,\cdots,N\}, Card(I)\geq N-2\;\vert\; \forall i\in I, \zeta^{{}^{{\relax{S}}_{A_1}\cdots{\relax{S}}_{A_N}}}_{(i)}(\nu) = \zeta^{{}^{{\relax{S}}_{A_1}\cdots{\relax{S}}_{A_N}}}_{(i)}(\phi)\,).\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end definition-58 -->
<!-- definition-59: body_md -->
\label{definUpsilonDelta}
Let us fix $\nu\in {{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}}{}^{{}^{pure}}$ and $j,k\in \{1,\cdots,N\}$ with $j<k$. 
Let us denote, for any $\kappa\in {{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}}{}^{{}^{pure}}$, 
\begin{eqnarray}
\Upsilon^{(j,k)}_{\kappa}:=\zeta^{{}^{{\relax{S}}_{A_1}\cdots{\relax{S}}_{A_N}}}_{(j)}(\kappa)\widetilde{\otimes}\zeta^{{}^{{\relax{S}}_{A_1}\cdots{\relax{S}}_{A_N}}}_{(k)}(\kappa)\in \overline{\relax{S}}{}_{A_j}^{{}^{pure}}\widetilde{\otimes}\overline{\relax{S}}{}_{A_k}^{{}^{pure}}
\end{eqnarray}
and, for any $(\alpha\widetilde{\otimes}\beta)\in \overline{\relax{S}}{}_{A_j}^{{}^{pure}}\widetilde{\otimes}\overline{\relax{S}}{}_{A_k}^{{}^{pure}}$,
\begin{eqnarray}
\Delta^{(j,k);\nu}_{\alpha\widetilde{\otimes}\beta}:=\delta_1\widetilde{\otimes}\cdots\widetilde{\otimes}\delta_{j-1}\widetilde{\otimes}\alpha\widetilde{\otimes}\delta_{j+1}\widetilde{\otimes}\cdots\widetilde{\otimes}\delta_{k-1}\widetilde{\otimes}\beta \widetilde{\otimes} \delta_{k+1}\widetilde{\otimes}\cdots\widetilde{\otimes}\delta_{N}
\end{eqnarray}
with $\delta_m:=\zeta^{{}^{{\relax{S}}_{A_1}\cdots{\relax{S}}_{A_N}}}_{(m)}(\nu)$ for any $m\in \{1,\cdots,N\}$.
<!-- end definition-59 -->
<!-- theorem-45: body_md -->
\label{lambdawr}
Let us consider $\nu$   
and $\phi$ 
 two distinct elements of ${{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}}{}^{{}^{pure}}$ and $\mu$ 
 another element of ${{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}}{}^{{}^{pure}}$.  Let us assume that $\mu \not\!\!\!\underline{\perp}\nu,\phi$. 
 We have
\begin{eqnarray}
&&\hspace{-2cm}(\,\exists \chi\in ({{{ \widetilde{\relax{S}}}}}\smallsetminus \overline{\relax{S}}) \;\vert\; (\,(\nu\sqcap_{{}_{{{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}}}}\phi) \raisebox{1.3ex}{\,\rotatebox{180}{$\sqsupseteq$}}\,_{{}_{{{{ \widetilde{\relax{S}}}}}}}\chi \;\;\;\;\textit{\rm and}\;\;\;\; \chi\,\underline{\perp}\,\mu\,)\,)\;\;\Leftrightarrow\\
&&\hspace{-2cm}(\,\exists I\subseteq\{1,\cdots,N\}, Card(I)= N-2\;\vert\; \nonumber\\
&&\hspace{-1.5cm}\forall i\in I, \forall \sigma,\kappa\in \overline{\relax{S}}{}^{{}^{pure}},(\,(\sigma \sqcap_{{}_{{{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}}}}\chi) \raisebox{1.3ex}{\,\rotatebox{180}{$\sqsupseteq$}}\,_{{}_{{{{ \widetilde{\relax{S}}}}}}}\sigma,\chi,\;\;(\kappa \sqcap_{{}_{{{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}}}}\chi) \raisebox{1.3ex}{\,\rotatebox{180}{$\sqsupseteq$}}\,_{{}_{{{{ \widetilde{\relax{S}}}}}}}\kappa,\chi\,)\;\;\Rightarrow\;\; \zeta^{{}^{{\relax{S}}_{A_1}\cdots{\relax{S}}_{A_N}}}_{(i)}(\sigma) = \zeta^{{}^{{\relax{S}}_{A_1}\cdots{\relax{S}}_{A_N}}}_{(i)}(\kappa)\,). \nonumber
\end{eqnarray}
In particular, $\exists \chi\in {{{ \widetilde{\relax{S}}}}}\;\vert\; (\,(\nu\sqcap_{{}_{{{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}}}}\phi) \raisebox{1.3ex}{\,\rotatebox{180}{$\sqsupseteq$}}\,_{{}_{{{{ \widetilde{\relax{S}}}}}}}\chi \;\;\;\;\textit{\rm and}\;\;\;\; \chi\,\underline{\perp}\,\mu\,)\,)$ implies $\forall i\in I,\;\; \zeta^{{}^{{\relax{S}}_{A_1}\cdots{\relax{S}}_{A_N}}}_{(i)}(\nu) = \zeta^{{}^{{\relax{S}}_{A_1}\cdots{\relax{S}}_{A_N}}}_{(i)}(\phi)$.\\
 
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                
Let us denote $j,k\in \{1,\cdots,N\}$ with $j<k$ such that for any $i\in \{1,\cdots,N\}\smallsetminus \{j,k\}$ we have 
$\zeta^{{}^{{\relax{S}}_{A_1}\cdots{\relax{S}}_{A_N}}}_{(i)}(\nu) = \zeta^{{}^{{\relax{S}}_{A_1}\cdots{\relax{S}}_{A_N}}}_{(i)}(\phi)$.  Endly, let us denote $\alpha:=\zeta^{{}^{{\relax{S}}_{A_1}\cdots{\relax{S}}_{A_N}}}_{(j)}(\mu)$, $\beta:=\zeta^{{}^{{\relax{S}}_{A_1}\cdots{\relax{S}}_{A_N}}}_{(k)}(\mu)$, 
$\alpha':=\zeta^{{}^{{\relax{S}}_{A_1}\cdots{\relax{S}}_{A_N}}}_{(j)}(\nu)$, $\beta':=\zeta^{{}^{{\relax{S}}_{A_1}\cdots{\relax{S}}_{A_N}}}_{(k)}(\nu)$, 
$\alpha'':=\zeta^{{}^{{\relax{S}}_{A_1}\cdots{\relax{S}}_{A_N}}}_{(j)}(\phi)$, $\beta'':=\zeta^{{}^{{\relax{S}}_{A_1}\cdots{\relax{S}}_{A_N}}}_{(k)}(\phi)$.\\
As long as $\lambda:=\mu\sqcup_{{}_{\relax{S}}}(\nu\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{\relax{S}}}}\phi)$ exists in ${{\relax{S}}}\smallsetminus {\overline{\relax{S}}}$, we have (see ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@computationexample\endcsname\@firstoftwo{computationexample}}}))
\begin{eqnarray}
\Theta^{\overline{\relax{S}}}(\lambda) &=& \left\{ \Delta^{(j,k);\nu}_{\alpha''\widetilde{\otimes}\beta''}\sqcap_{{}_{{{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}}}}\!\!\!\Delta^{(j,k);\nu}_{\alpha'\widetilde{\otimes}\beta'}
\,,\,
\Delta^{(j,k);\nu}_{\alpha'' \widetilde{\otimes}\beta^\star}\sqcap_{{}_{{{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}}}} \Delta^{(j,k);\nu}_{\alpha^\star\widetilde{\otimes} \beta'}\,,\,
\Delta^{(j,k);\nu}_{\alpha' \widetilde{\otimes}\beta^\star}\sqcap_{{}_{{{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}}}} \Delta^{(j,k);\nu}_{\alpha^\star\widetilde{\otimes} \beta''}
\right\}\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end theorem-45 -->
<!-- proof-97: body_md -->
Once again we will fix $N=3$.
It suffices to remark, using the expression ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@expressionchiN=3\endcsname\@firstoftwo{expressionchiN=3}}}), the expression of the infimum ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@infimumJprop\endcsname\@firstoftwo{infimumJprop}}}), the property ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@thirdcoveringpropertySbarii\endcsname\@firstoftwo{thirdcoveringpropertySbarii}}}) and the expansion formula ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@developmentetildeordersimplify\endcsname\@firstoftwo{developmentetildeordersimplify}}}), that the relations $(\sigma \sqcap_{{}_{{{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}}}}\chi) \raisebox{1.3ex}{\,\rotatebox{180}{$\sqsupseteq$}}\,_{{}_{{{{ \widetilde{\relax{S}}}}}}}\sigma,\chi$ and $(\kappa \sqcap_{{}_{{{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}}}}\chi) \raisebox{1.3ex}{\,\rotatebox{180}{$\sqsupseteq$}}\,_{{}_{{{{ \widetilde{\relax{S}}}}}}}\kappa,\chi$ impose necessarily $\sigma$ and $\kappa$ to be both elements of the following subset of pure states
\begin{eqnarray}
&&\hspace{-1cm}\{ (\sigma_{A_1}'\widetilde{\otimes}\sigma_{A_2}''\widetilde{\otimes}\sigma_{A_3}'')\,, \,(\sigma_{A_1}'\widetilde{\otimes}\sigma'_{A_2}\widetilde{\otimes}\sigma'_{A_3})\,,\,(\sigma_{A_1}'\widetilde{\otimes}\sigma_{A_2}^\star\widetilde{\otimes}\sigma_{A_3}'')\,,\, \nonumber\\
&&\hspace{2cm}(\sigma_{A_1}'\widetilde{\otimes}\sigma'_{A_2}\widetilde{\otimes}\sigma_{A_3}^\star)\,,\, (\sigma_{A_1}'\widetilde{\otimes}\sigma_{A_2}''\widetilde{\otimes}\sigma_{A_3}^\star)\,,\, (\sigma_{A_1}'\widetilde{\otimes}\sigma_{A_2}^\star\widetilde{\otimes}\sigma'_{A_3})\}\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;
\end{eqnarray}
This concludes the proof, which can be straightforwardly generalized to generic $N$.
<!-- end proof-97 -->
<!-- theorem-46: body_md -->
\begin{eqnarray}
\hspace{-0.5cm}\forall \alpha,\beta\in {{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}}{}^{{}^{pure}},&& \beta\not=\alpha \;\;\Rightarrow \;\; (\alpha\sqcap_{{}_{{{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}}}}\beta) \raisebox{1.3ex}{\,\rotatebox{180}{$\sqsupseteq$}}\,_{{}_{{{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}}}}\alpha,\beta.\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\label{coveringpropertySbar}
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end theorem-46 -->
<!-- proof-98: body_md -->
The property ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@coveringpropertySbar\endcsname\@firstoftwo{coveringpropertySbar}}}) is obtained by a trivial recursion proof (on the number $N$) using Theorem {{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@firstcoveringlemma\endcsname\@firstoftwo{firstcoveringlemma}}}.
<!-- end proof-98 -->
<!-- theorem-47: body_md -->
We have the following basic property
\begin{eqnarray}
&&\hspace{-0.5cm}\forall \lambda,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,\delta\in {{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}}{}^{{}^{pure}} \;\textit{\rm distinct},\nonumber\\
&& (\,(\alpha\sqcap_{{}_{{{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}}}}\beta)\not=(\gamma\sqcap_{{}_{{{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}}}}\delta)\;\;\;\textit{\rm and}\;\;\;(\alpha\sqcap_{{}_{{{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}}}}\beta),(\gamma\sqcap_{{}_{{{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}}}}\delta)\raisebox{1.3ex}{\,\rotatebox{180}{$\sqsupseteq$}}\,_{{}_{\overline{\relax{S}}}}\lambda \,) \;\;\Rightarrow \nonumber\\
&&\hspace{1cm} (\alpha\sqcap_{{}_{{{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}}}}\beta\sqcap_{{}_{{{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}}}}\gamma\sqcap_{{}_{{{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}}}}\delta) \raisebox{1.3ex}{\,\rotatebox{180}{$\sqsupseteq$}}\,_{{}_{{{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}}}}(\alpha\sqcap_{{}_{{{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}}}}\beta),(\gamma\sqcap_{{}_{{{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}}}}\delta).\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\label{secondcoveringpropertySbar}
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end theorem-47 -->
<!-- proof-99: body_md -->
The property ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@secondcoveringpropertySbar\endcsname\@firstoftwo{secondcoveringpropertySbar}}}) is obtained by a trivial recursion proof (on the number $N$) using Theorem {{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@secondcoveringlemma\endcsname\@firstoftwo{secondcoveringlemma}}}.
<!-- end proof-99 -->
<!-- theorem-48: body_md -->
\label{zetalambda}
\begin{eqnarray}
&&\hspace{-2cm}\forall \lambda,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,\delta\in {{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}}{}^{{}^{pure}} \;\textit{\rm distinct},
(\,(\alpha\sqcap_{{}_{{{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}}}}\beta)\not=(\gamma\sqcap_{{}_{{{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}}}}\delta)\;\;\;\textit{\rm and}\;\;\;(\alpha\sqcap_{{}_{{{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}}}}\beta),(\gamma\sqcap_{{}_{{{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}}}}\delta)\raisebox{1.3ex}{\,\rotatebox{180}{$\sqsupseteq$}}\,_{{}_{\overline{\relax{S}}}}\lambda \,) \;\;\Rightarrow \label{secondcoveringpropertySbarbis}\\
&&\hspace{-2cm}\exists I\subseteq\{1,\cdots,N\}, Card(I)= N-2\;\vert\; \forall i\in I, \forall \sigma,\kappa\in \{\lambda,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,\delta\},\;\;\zeta^{{}^{{\relax{S}}_{A_1}\cdots{\relax{S}}_{A_N}}}_{(i)}(\sigma) = \zeta^{{}^{{\relax{S}}_{A_1}\cdots{\relax{S}}_{A_N}}}_{(i)}(\kappa).\;\;\;\;\;\;\nonumber
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end theorem-48 -->
<!-- proof-100: body_md -->
Direct consequence of the expansion formula ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@developmentetildeordersimplify\endcsname\@firstoftwo{developmentetildeordersimplify}}}).  Let us consider $\lambda:=\sigma^{\lambda}_{A_1}\widetilde{\otimes}\cdots\widetilde{\otimes}\sigma^{\lambda}_{A_N}$, $\alpha:=\sigma^{\alpha}_{A_1}\widetilde{\otimes}\cdots\widetilde{\otimes}\sigma^{\alpha}_{A_N}$, $\beta:=\sigma^{\beta}_{A_1}\widetilde{\otimes}\cdots\widetilde{\otimes}\sigma^{\beta}_{A_N}$. The property $(\alpha\sqcap_{{}_{{{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}}}}\beta)\raisebox{1.3ex}{\,\rotatebox{180}{$\sqsupseteq$}}\,_{{}_{\overline{\relax{S}}}}\lambda$ imposes 
\begin{eqnarray}
\hspace{-1cm}\exists i\in \{1,\cdots,N\}, \;\vert\; (\,\forall j\in \{1,\cdots,N\}\smallsetminus\{i\}, \;\;\sigma^{\alpha}_{A_j}=\sigma^{\beta}_{A_j}=\sigma^{\lambda}_{A_j}
\;\;\textit{\rm and}\;\;(\sigma^{\alpha}_{A_i}\sqcap_{{}_{{{{ \overline{\relax{S}}_{A_i}}}}}}\!\!\sigma^{\beta}_{A_i})\raisebox{1.3ex}{\,\rotatebox{180}{$\sqsupseteq$}}\,_{{}_{{{{ \overline{\relax{S}}_{A_i}}}}}}\sigma^{\lambda}_{A_i}\,).\;\;\;\;\;\;
\end{eqnarray}
This leads directly to the announced result.
<!-- end proof-100 -->
<!-- definition-60: body_md -->
We will define the following subset of  ${ \relax{S}}$ :
\begin{eqnarray}
\hspace{-1.5cm}{\check{\relax{S}}} &:= & \overline{ \relax{S}}\cup \left\{\chi\in { \relax{S}}\smallsetminus \overline{ \relax{S}}\;\vert\; \exists \mu,\nu,\phi\in \overline{ \relax{S}}{}^{{}^{pure}},\;\;\;\;\gamma:=
\nu\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\phi
\raisebox{1.3ex}{\,\rotatebox{180}{$\sqsupseteq$}}\,_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\nu,\phi,\;\;\;\;\gamma\not\sqsupseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\mu^\star,\;\;\;\; \chi=\mu^\star\sqcup_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}}\gamma \right\}\label{defSbarhat}\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\\
                
\hspace{-1.5cm}{\widecheck{\relax{S}}} &:= &  \overline{ \relax{S}}\cup \left\{\chi\in { \relax{S}}\smallsetminus \overline{ \relax{S}}\;\vert\; \exists \mu,\phi\in \overline{ \relax{S}}{}^{{}^{pure}},\;\;\mu\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\phi
\raisebox{1.3ex}{\,\rotatebox{180}{$\sqsupseteq$}}\,_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\mu,\phi,\;\;\;\;\; \chi=\mu^\star\sqcup_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}}(\mu\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\phi) \right\}\label{defSwidecheck}\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;
\end{eqnarray}
and 
\begin{eqnarray}
{\relax{G}}^{\check{\relax{S}}} &:=&\overline{ \relax{S}}{}^{{}^{pure}} \cup ({\check{\relax{S}}}\smallsetminus \overline{ \relax{S}}),\\
{\relax{G}}^{\widecheck{\relax{S}}} &:=&\overline{ \relax{S}}{}^{{}^{pure}} \cup ({\widecheck{\relax{S}}}\smallsetminus \overline{ \relax{S}}).
\end{eqnarray}
We note obviously that ${\check{\relax{S}}}\supseteq {\widecheck{\relax{S}}}$ and ${\relax{G}}^{\check{\relax{S}}}\supseteq {\relax{G}}^{\widecheck{\relax{S}}}$.
<!-- end definition-60 -->
<!-- definition-61: body_md -->
On ${\relax{G}}^{\check{\relax{S}}}$, we will define the {\em consistency relation}, denoted $\asymp$                                                                 
, as follows (see Definition {{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@definwr\endcsname\@firstoftwo{definwr}}} for a definition of $\wr$):
\begin{eqnarray}
&&\hspace{-1cm}\forall \chi,\chi'\in {\check{\relax{S}}}\smallsetminus \overline{ \relax{S}},\;\;\;\;\chi \asymp \chi'\;\;:\Leftrightarrow\;\; (\,\chi=\chi'\;\;\textit{\rm or}\;\;\exists \epsilon\in \Theta^{\overline{ \relax{S}}}(\chi)\cap \Theta^{\overline{ \relax{S}}}(\chi'),\;\;\epsilon=(\chi\sqcap_{{}_{{\relax{S}}}}\chi')\,)\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\\
&&\hspace{-1cm}\forall \chi\in {\check{\relax{S}}}\smallsetminus \overline{ \relax{S}},\forall \sigma\in \overline{ \relax{S}}{}^{{}^{pure}},\;\;\;\;\chi \asymp \sigma\;\;\Leftrightarrow\;\; \sigma \asymp \chi \;\;:\Leftrightarrow\;\; (\,\exists \epsilon\in\Theta^{\overline{ \relax{S}}}(\chi)\;\vert\; \epsilon \raisebox{1.3ex}{\,\rotatebox{180}{$\sqsupseteq$}}\,_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma\,)\\
&&\hspace{-1cm}\forall \sigma,\sigma'\in \overline{ \relax{S}}{}^{{}^{pure}},\;\;\;\;\sigma \asymp \sigma'\;\;:\Leftrightarrow\;\; \sigma \wr \sigma'                                                                                                                                                                                                     
\end{eqnarray}
Note that, due to the property ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@coveringpropertySbar\endcsname\@firstoftwo{coveringpropertySbar}}}) we have $\forall \sigma,\sigma'\in \overline{ \relax{S}}{}^{{}^{pure}},(\sigma\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{\relax{S}}}}\sigma') \raisebox{1.3ex}{\,\rotatebox{180}{$\sqsupseteq$}}\,_{{}_{\overline{  \relax{S}}}}\sigma,\sigma'\;\textit{\rm or }\; \sigma=\sigma'$.
<!-- end definition-61 -->
<!-- remark-5: body_md -->
Note that, using ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@thirdcoveringpropertySbarii\endcsname\@firstoftwo{thirdcoveringpropertySbarii}}}), we obtain easily 
\begin{eqnarray}
\hspace{-1.2cm}\forall \chi,\chi'\in {\check{\relax{S}}}\smallsetminus \overline{ \relax{S}},&&(\,\chi \asymp \chi'\;\textit{\rm and}\;\chi \not= \chi'\,)\;\;\Rightarrow\;\; Card(\Theta^{\overline{ \relax{S}}}(\chi)\cap \Theta^{\overline{ \relax{S}}}(\chi'))=1.\label{Rek1}
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end remark-5 -->
<!-- remark-6: body_md -->
Note that, using ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@thirdcoveringpropertySbarii\endcsname\@firstoftwo{thirdcoveringpropertySbarii}}}), we obtain easily 
\begin{eqnarray}
\hspace{-1.2cm}\forall \chi\in {\check{\relax{S}}}\smallsetminus \overline{ \relax{S}},\forall \sigma\in \overline{\relax{S}}{}^{{}^{pure}},&& 
(\,\chi \asymp \sigma\,)\;\;\Rightarrow\;\; Card(\Theta^{\overline{ \relax{S}}}(\chi)\cap (\downarrow_{{}_{\overline{\relax{S}}}}\sigma))=1.\label{Rek2}
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end remark-6 -->
<!-- definition-62: body_md -->
A {\em consistent subset of states} is defined to be a subset of ${\relax{G}}^{\check{\relax{S}}}$ such that all its elements are pairwise consistent.
<!-- end definition-62 -->
<!-- definition-63: body_md -->
The {\em consistency cover} of ${\relax{G}}^{\check{\relax{S}}}$, denoted ${ \relax{E}}^{\check{\relax{S}}}$, is defined as a family of maximal consistent subsets covering the whole set of elements of ${\relax{G}}^{\check{\relax{S}}}$ :
\begin{eqnarray}\left\{
\begin{array}{l}
(\bigcup_{{}_{U\in { \relax{E}}^{\check{\relax{S}}}}} U) = {\relax{G}}^{\check{\relax{S}}}\\
\forall U,U’ \in { \relax{E}}^{\check{\relax{S}}},\;\;\; U \subseteq U’ \;\Rightarrow \; U =U’\\
\forall U\in { \relax{E}}^{\check{\relax{S}}},\;\forall \sigma,\sigma'\in U,\;\sigma\asymp \sigma'.
\end{array}
\right.
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end definition-63 -->
<!-- definition-64: body_md -->
Let us consider any consistent subset $U\in { \relax{E}}^{\check{\relax{S}}}$. \\
We define a ternary relation ${\relax{r}}^U$ on $U$ (it will be called {\em colinearity}) as follows
\begin{eqnarray}
\forall \sigma_1,\sigma_2,\sigma_3\in U,&&{\relax{r}}^U(\sigma_1,\sigma_2,\sigma_3)\;\;:\Leftrightarrow\;\; (\, \sigma_2=\sigma_3\;\textit{\rm or}\; (\sigma_2 \sqcap_{{}_{{\relax{S}}}}\sigma_3)\raisebox{1.3ex}{\,\rotatebox{180}{$\sqsupseteq$}}\,_{{}_{{\relax{S}}}}\sigma_1\,).\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end definition-64 -->
<!-- lemma-68: body_md -->
\label{lemmaproj0}
We note the following sheaf condition
\begin{eqnarray}
\hspace{-1cm}\forall \sigma_1,\sigma_2,\sigma_3\in { \relax{G}}^{\check{\relax{S}}},\forall U,U'\in { \relax{E}}^{\check{\relax{S}}},&& \sigma_1,\sigma_2,\sigma_3\in U\cap U'\;\Rightarrow \; {\relax{r}}^U(\sigma_1,\sigma_2,\sigma_3)={\relax{r}}^{U'}(\sigma_1,\sigma_2,\sigma_3).\label{VeblenYoung0}\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end lemma-68 -->
<!-- lemma-69: body_md -->
The ternary relation ${\relax{r}}^U$ defined on the consistent subset $U$ is symmetric under any permutation of its arguments.
<!-- end lemma-69 -->
<!-- proof-101: body_md -->
It suffices to prove that it is symmetric under the exchange of the two first arguments (because it is already symmetric under the exchange of its two last arguments).  This is a simple computation. We reproduce only one of its cases. \\
Let us then consider $\sigma_1,\sigma_2,\sigma_3\in {\relax{G}}^{\check{\relax{S}}}$ such that $\sigma_1,\sigma_2,\sigma_3$ are pairwise compatible.  We will choose for example $\sigma_2,\sigma_3\in {\check{\relax{S}}}\smallsetminus \overline{ \relax{S}}$. \\ 
Let us first consider that $\sigma_2\not=\sigma_3$.  Then, ${\relax{r}}^U(\sigma_1,\sigma_2,\sigma_3)$ is equivalent to $\sigma_1\raisebox{1.3ex}{\,\rotatebox{180}{$\sqsubseteq$}}\,_{{}_{{\relax{S}}}}(\sigma_2 \sqcap_{{}_{{\relax{S}}}}\sigma_3)$, which means that there exists $\epsilon \raisebox{1.3ex}{\,\rotatebox{180}{$\sqsupseteq$}}\,_{{}_{{\relax{S}}}}\sigma_1$ where $\{\epsilon\}= \Theta^{\overline{ \relax{S}}}(\sigma_2)\cap \Theta^{\overline{ \relax{S}}}(\sigma_3)$ (here we use property ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@Rek1\endcsname\@firstoftwo{Rek1}}}) or ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@Rek2\endcsname\@firstoftwo{Rek2}}})). We then deduce that $(\sigma_1 \sqcap_{{}_{{\relax{S}}}}\sigma_3)=\epsilon$ and using $\epsilon\in \Theta^{\overline{ \relax{S}}}(\sigma_2)$ we obtain $\sigma_2\raisebox{1.3ex}{\,\rotatebox{180}{$\sqsubseteq$}}\,_{{}_{{\relax{S}}}}(\sigma_1 \sqcap_{{}_{{\relax{S}}}}\sigma_3)$ from ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@thirdcoveringpropertySbarii\endcsname\@firstoftwo{thirdcoveringpropertySbarii}}}). This proves ${\relax{r}}^U(\sigma_2,\sigma_1,\sigma_3)$. \\
Let us now consider that $\sigma_2=\sigma_3$. Then, we have immediately ${\relax{r}}^U(\sigma_1,\sigma_2,\sigma_3)$.  We have also trivially $\sigma_2\raisebox{1.3ex}{\,\rotatebox{180}{$\sqsubseteq$}}\,_{{}_{{\relax{S}}}}(\sigma_1 \sqcap_{{}_{{\relax{S}}}}\sigma_2)$ which means that we have also ${\relax{r}}^U(\sigma_2,\sigma_1,\sigma_3)$.
<!-- end proof-101 -->
<!-- lemma-70: body_md -->
{\bf [Veblen-Young's first geometric property]}\label{lemmaproj1}
\begin{eqnarray}
\forall U\in { \relax{E}}^{\check{\relax{S}}}, \forall \sigma_1,\sigma_2\in U,&&{\relax{r}}^U(\sigma_1,\sigma_2,\sigma_2).\label{VeblenYoung3}
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end lemma-70 -->
<!-- proof-102: body_md -->
Trivial.
<!-- end proof-102 -->
<!-- lemma-71: body_md -->
\label{lemmazetacup}
Let us consider $\chi\in ({\check{\relax{S}}}\smallsetminus \overline{\relax{S}})$. We have
\begin{eqnarray}
&&\hspace{0.5cm} \forall \sigma_1,\sigma_2\in \Theta^{\overline{ \relax{S}}}(\chi),\sigma_1\not=\sigma_2,\;\;\;\; \sigma_1\sqcup_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma_2=\chi.\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;
\label{thirdcoveringpropertySbarv}
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end lemma-71 -->
<!-- proof-103: body_md -->
From property ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@thirdcoveringpropertySbarii\endcsname\@firstoftwo{thirdcoveringpropertySbarii}}}) we know that
$\forall \sigma\in \Theta^{\overline{ \relax{S}}}(\chi),\;\;  
\sigma\raisebox{1.3ex}{\,\rotatebox{180}{$\sqsupseteq$}}\,_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}} \chi$. Then, if we consider $\sigma_1,\sigma_2\in \Theta^{\overline{ \relax{S}}}(\chi)$ with $\sigma_1\not=\sigma_2$, we have $\sigma_1 \sqsubset_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}} (\sigma_1\sqcup_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma_2) \sqsubseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}} \chi$ and $\sigma_1\raisebox{1.3ex}{\,\rotatebox{180}{$\sqsupseteq$}}\,_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}} \chi$. Then, we conclude that $(\sigma_1\sqcup_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma_2)= \chi$.
<!-- end proof-103 -->
<!-- lemma-72: body_md -->
\label{nondegenerateallsigmapure}
Let $U\subseteq {\relax{G}}^{\check{\relax{S}}}$ be a consistent subset of states, such that there exists $\sigma_1,\sigma_2,\sigma_3,\sigma_4,\lambda\in U$ satisfying
\begin{eqnarray}
                                                                              
\forall i,j\in \{1,2,3,4\}, i\not=j,&& \sigma_i\not=\sigma_j\\
\forall i\in \{1,2,3,4\}, && \sigma_i\not=\lambda\\
\forall i,j,k,l\in \{1,2,3,4\}, \{i,j\}\not=\{k,l\},&& (\sigma_i\sqcap_{{}_{{\relax{S}}}}\sigma_j)\not=(\sigma_k\sqcap_{{}_{{\relax{S}}}}\sigma_l),\\
\lambda \raisebox{1.3ex}{\,\rotatebox{180}{$\sqsubseteq$}}\,_{{}_{{\relax{S}}}} (\sigma_1 \sqcap_{{}_{{\relax{S}}}}\sigma_2),&&\lambda \raisebox{1.3ex}{\,\rotatebox{180}{$\sqsubseteq$}}\,_{{}_{{\relax{S}}}} (\sigma_3 \sqcap_{{}_{{\relax{S}}}}\sigma_4),
\end{eqnarray}
then we have necessarily 
\begin{eqnarray}
&&\forall i\in \{1,2,3,4\},\; \sigma_i\in \overline{\relax{S}}{}^{{}^{pure}}.
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end lemma-72 -->
<!-- proof-104: body_md -->
The proof is in the Appendix.
<!-- end proof-104 -->
<!-- lemma-73: body_md -->
\label{typoU}
Let us consider $U\in { \relax{E}}^{\check{\relax{S}}}$ such that there exists $\chi\in ({\check{\relax{S}}}\smallsetminus \overline{ \relax{S}})$ with $\chi\in U$.  The subset $U$ is necessarily of one of the two following types
\begin{itemize}
\@par\hangindent 2em (Consistent Type 1) $\exists \textit{\bf !} \alpha\in \Theta^{\overline{ \relax{S}}}(\chi)$ such that $\forall \sigma\in U$ we have $(\sigma\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\chi)=\alpha$.
\@par\hangindent 2em (Consistent Type 2) $\exists \alpha,\beta\in \Theta^{\overline{ \relax{S}}}(\chi),\alpha\not=\beta$ and $\exists \sigma,\sigma'\in U\cap \overline{ \relax{S}}{}^{{}^{pure}}$ such that $(\sigma\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\chi)=\alpha$ and $(\sigma'\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\chi)=\beta$.
\end{itemize}
<!-- end lemma-73 -->
<!-- proof-105: body_md -->
Direct consequence of Lemma {{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@nondegenerateallsigmapure\endcsname\@firstoftwo{nondegenerateallsigmapure}}} and the assumption of maximality on $U$.
<!-- end proof-105 -->
<!-- lemma-74: body_md -->
\label{lemmaconsistenttype2}
Let us consider a maximal consistent subset of states $U\in { \relax{E}}^{\check{\relax{S}}}$ and let us assume that there exists $\lambda\in ({\check{\relax{S}}}\smallsetminus \overline{ \relax{S}})$ and $\sigma_1,\sigma_2,\sigma_3,\sigma_4\in \overline{ \relax{S}}{}^{{}^{pure}}$ such that $\lambda,\sigma_1,\sigma_2,\sigma_3,\sigma_4\in U$  and such that ${\relax{r}}^U(\lambda,\sigma_1,\sigma_2)$ and ${\relax{r}}^U(\lambda,\sigma_3,\sigma_4)$ and $\forall \mu,\nu,\rho\in \{\sigma_1,\sigma_2,\sigma_3,\sigma_4\}, \;\neg\; {\relax{r}}^U(\mu,\nu,\rho)$.  Then, the consistent subset $U$ is necessarily of {\em consistent type 2}                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       
.
<!-- end lemma-74 -->
<!-- proof-106: body_md -->
As long as $\lambda\in ({\check{\relax{S}}}\smallsetminus \overline{ \relax{S}})$, $\Theta^{\overline{\relax{S}}}(\lambda) $ is given as in Theorem {{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@lambdawr\endcsname\@firstoftwo{lambdawr}}}.\\
