The conditions ${\relax{r}}^U(\lambda,\sigma_1,\sigma_2)$ and ${\relax{r}}^U(\lambda,\sigma_3,\sigma_4)$ and $\forall \mu,\nu,\rho\in \{\sigma_1,\sigma_2,\sigma_3,\sigma_4\}, \;\neg\; {\relax{r}}^U(\mu,\nu,\rho)$ impose the existence of $\epsilon,\delta\in \Theta^{\overline{\relax{S}}}(\lambda)$ such that $\epsilon\not=\delta$ and $(\sigma_1\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{\relax{S}}}}\sigma_2)=\epsilon$ and $(\sigma_3\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{\relax{S}}}}\sigma_4)=\delta$.  We note that these conditions impose also the distinctness of the elements $\sigma_i$, i.e.  $\alpha'\not=\alpha''$ and $ \beta'\not=\beta''$.
<!-- end proof-106 -->
<!-- lemma-75: body_md -->
{\bf [Veblen-Young's second geometric property]}\label{lemmaproj2}
\begin{eqnarray}
\hspace{-1cm}\forall U\in { \relax{E}}^{\check{\relax{S}}}, \forall \sigma_1,\sigma_2,\sigma_3,\sigma_4\in U,&& (\,{\relax{r}}^U(\sigma_1,\sigma_3,\sigma_4)\;\textit{\rm and}\;{\relax{r}}^U(\sigma_2,\sigma_3,\sigma_4)\,)\;\;\Rightarrow\;\; {\relax{r}}^U(\sigma_1,\sigma_2,\sigma_3).\label{VeblenYoung2}\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end lemma-75 -->
<!-- proof-107: body_md -->
This is a straightforward check.  We reproduce one of its cases. Let us then consider for example                                                                                                     
 $\sigma_3,\sigma_4\in ({\check{\relax{S}}}\smallsetminus \overline{\relax{S}})$ with $\sigma_3\not=\sigma_4$.  \\
Then, ${\relax{r}}^U(\sigma_1,\sigma_3,\sigma_4)$ is equivalent to $\sigma_1\raisebox{1.3ex}{\,\rotatebox{180}{$\sqsubseteq$}}\,_{{}_{{\relax{S}}}}(\sigma_3 \sqcap_{{}_{{\relax{S}}}}\sigma_4)$ or, using property ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@Rek1\endcsname\@firstoftwo{Rek1}}}),  $\epsilon \raisebox{1.3ex}{\,\rotatebox{180}{$\sqsupseteq$}}\,_{{}_{\overline{\relax{S}}}} \sigma_1$ with $\{\epsilon\}=\Theta^{\overline{ \relax{S}}}(\sigma_3)\cap \Theta^{\overline{ \relax{S}}}(\sigma_4)$. Analogously,  ${\relax{r}}^U(\sigma_2,\sigma_3,\sigma_4)$ is equivalent to $\sigma_2\raisebox{1.3ex}{\,\rotatebox{180}{$\sqsubseteq$}}\,_{{}_{{\relax{S}}}}(\sigma_3 \sqcap_{{}_{{\relax{S}}}}\sigma_4)$ or, using property ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@Rek1\endcsname\@firstoftwo{Rek1}}})                 
,  $\mu \raisebox{1.3ex}{\,\rotatebox{180}{$\sqsupseteq$}}\,_{{}_{\overline{\relax{S}}}} \sigma_2$ with $\{\mu\}=\Theta^{\overline{ \relax{S}}}(\sigma_3)\cap \Theta^{\overline{ \relax{S}}}(\sigma_4)$. Using property ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@Rek1\endcsname\@firstoftwo{Rek1}}})                 
, we also know that $\mu=\epsilon$.  We then note that $\mu=(\sigma_2 \sqcap_{{}_{{\relax{S}}}}\sigma_3)$ and then $\sigma_1\raisebox{1.3ex}{\,\rotatebox{180}{$\sqsubseteq$}}\,_{{}_{{\relax{S}}}}(\sigma_2 \sqcap_{{}_{{\relax{S}}}}\sigma_3)$, i.e. ${\relax{r}}^U(\sigma_1,\sigma_2,\sigma_3)$.
<!-- end proof-107 -->
<!-- lemma-76: body_md -->
{\bf [Veblen-Young's third geometric property]}\label{lemmaproj3}\\
We will consider $\sigma_1,\sigma_2,\sigma_3,\sigma_4\in { \relax{E}}^{\check{\relax{S}}}$. We have the following result
 \begin{eqnarray}
&&\hspace{-1.5cm}(\,\exists U\in { \relax{E}}^{\check{\relax{S}}},\sigma_1,\sigma_2,\sigma_3,\sigma_4\in U,\exists \lambda\in U\;\vert\; {\relax{r}}^U(\lambda,\sigma_1,\sigma_2)\;\textit{\rm and}\;{\relax{r}}^U(\lambda,\sigma_3,\sigma_4)
\,)\;\;\Rightarrow\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\nonumber\\
                                                                                                                                  
&&\hspace{-1.5cm} (\,(\exists U',U''\in { \relax{E}}^{\check{\relax{S}}}\;\vert\;\sigma_1,\sigma_2,\sigma_3,\sigma_4\in U',U'')\;\textit{\rm and}\;\exists\mu\in U'\;\vert\; {\relax{r}}^{U'}(\mu,\sigma_1,\sigma_3)\;\textit{\rm and}\;{\relax{r}}^{U'}(\mu,\sigma_2,\sigma_4) \nonumber\\
&&\hspace{3.5cm} \textit{\rm and}\;\exists\chi\in U''\;\vert\; {\relax{r}}^{U''}(\chi,\sigma_2,\sigma_3)\;\textit{\rm and}\;{\relax{r}}^{U''}(\chi,\sigma_1,\sigma_4)\,).\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\label{VeblenYoung1}
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end lemma-76 -->
<!-- proof-108: body_md -->
Let us first note that if $(\sigma_1\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma_2)=(\sigma_3\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma_4)$ then we have also $(\sigma_1\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma_3)=(\sigma_2\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma_4)$ and also $(\sigma_1\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma_4)=(\sigma_2\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma_3)$ and then the proof of ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@VeblenYoung1\endcsname\@firstoftwo{VeblenYoung1}}}) is trivial. We will then assume $(\sigma_1\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma_2)\not=(\sigma_3\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma_4)$ and $(\sigma_1\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma_3)\not=(\sigma_2\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma_4)$ and $(\sigma_1\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma_4)\not=(\sigma_2\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma_3)$.\\
We will also assume $\lambda\not=\sigma_1,\lambda\not=\sigma_2,\lambda\not=\sigma_3,\lambda\not=\sigma_4$. Indeed, if we have for example $\lambda=\sigma_1$ then it suffices to take $\mu:=\sigma_4$ and $\chi:=\sigma_3$ to satisfy the announced properties.\\
We will then assume the existence of $\lambda\in U\in { \relax{E}}^{\check{\relax{S}}}$ such that ${\relax{r}}^U(\lambda,\sigma_1,\sigma_2)\;\textit{\rm and}\;{\relax{r}}^U(\lambda,\sigma_3,\sigma_4)$. \\
The assumption ${\relax{r}}^U(\lambda,\sigma_1,\sigma_2)\;\textit{\rm and}\;{\relax{r}}^U(\lambda,\sigma_3,\sigma_4)$ is equivalent to 
\begin{eqnarray}
(\sigma_1\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma_2)\raisebox{1.3ex}{\,\rotatebox{180}{$\sqsupseteq$}}\,_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}}\lambda, && (\sigma_3\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma_4)\raisebox{1.3ex}{\,\rotatebox{180}{$\sqsupseteq$}}\,_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}}\lambda.\label{reformassumption}
\end{eqnarray}
We have then, using ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@thirdcoveringpropertySbariii\endcsname\@firstoftwo{thirdcoveringpropertySbariii}}}) (if $\lambda\in  ({\check{\relax{S}}}\smallsetminus \overline{\relax{S}})$) or using ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@secondcoveringpropertySbar\endcsname\@firstoftwo{secondcoveringpropertySbar}}}) (if $\lambda\in \overline{\relax{S}}{}^{{}^{pure}}$), the properties 
\begin{eqnarray}
(\sigma_1\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma_2\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma_3\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma_4)\raisebox{1.3ex}{\,\rotatebox{180}{$\sqsupseteq$}}\,_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}} (\sigma_1\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma_2),(\sigma_3\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma_4)\label{4=3}
\end{eqnarray}
We know from Theorem {{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@zetalambda\endcsname\@firstoftwo{zetalambda}}} and Theorem {{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@lambdawr\endcsname\@firstoftwo{lambdawr}}} that
\begin{eqnarray}
&&\hspace{-2cm}\exists I\subseteq\{1,\cdots,N\}, Card(I)= N-2\;\vert\; \forall i\in I, \forall \alpha,\beta\in \{\sigma_1,\sigma_2,\sigma_3,\sigma_4\},\;\;\zeta^{{}^{{\relax{S}}_{A_1}\cdots{\relax{S}}_{A_N}}}_{(i)}(\alpha) = \zeta^{{}^{{\relax{S}}_{A_1}\cdots{\relax{S}}_{A_N}}}_{(i)}(\beta).\nonumber\\
&&\label{conditionzeta}
\end{eqnarray}
Having noted the property $(\sigma_1\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma_3)\not=(\sigma_2\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma_4)$,  we will consider any $\xi\in \overline{\relax{S}}{}^{{}^{pure}}$ such that 
\begin{eqnarray}
\hspace{-1cm}\xi\sqsupseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}} (\sigma_1\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma_3)^\star, && \xi\not\sqsupseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}} (\sigma_2\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma_4)^\star,\;\;\;\;\;\;\forall i\in I, \zeta^{{}^{{\relax{S}}_{A_1}\cdots{\relax{S}}_{A_N}}}_{(i)}(\xi) = \zeta^{{}^{{\relax{S}}_{A_1}\cdots{\relax{S}}_{A_N}}}_{(i)}(\sigma_1)\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;
\label{assumptionxi}
\end{eqnarray}
(we note that $\sigma_1\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma_3$ and $\sigma_2\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma_4$ are different from $\bot_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}$).\\
From ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@thirdcoveringpropertySbari\endcsname\@firstoftwo{thirdcoveringpropertySbari}}}), and using $\xi\not\sqsupseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}} (\sigma_2\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma_4)^\star$ and property ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@conditionzeta\endcsname\@firstoftwo{conditionzeta}}}), we know that there exists $\upsilon\in {\relax{G}}^{\check{\relax{S}}}$ such that
\begin{eqnarray}
\upsilon := \xi^\star \sqcup_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}}(\sigma_2\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma_4)
\end{eqnarray}
From ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@thirdcoveringpropertySbarii\endcsname\@firstoftwo{thirdcoveringpropertySbarii}}}), we know that $\upsilon\raisebox{1.3ex}{\,\rotatebox{180}{$\sqsubseteq$}}\,_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}} (\sigma_2\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma_4)$ and then ${\relax{r}}^U(\upsilon,\sigma_2,\sigma_4)$. 
We intent to show that we have also ${\relax{r}}^U(\upsilon,\sigma_1,\sigma_3)$. \\
We then consider any $\omega\in \overline{\relax{S}}{}^{{}^{pure}}$ such that 
\begin{eqnarray}
\omega\sqsupseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}} (\sigma_1\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma_3)^\star, && \omega\not=\xi,\;\;\;\;\;\;\forall i\in I, \zeta^{{}^{{\relax{S}}_{A_1}\cdots{\relax{S}}_{A_N}}}_{(i)}(\omega) = \zeta^{{}^{{\relax{S}}_{A_1}\cdots{\relax{S}}_{A_N}}}_{(i)}(\xi)\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\label{omegazeta}
\end{eqnarray}
and we intent to show that $\omega^\star\sqsubseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}}\upsilon$ (we note that  
$(\sigma_1\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma_3)^\star$ is not in $\overline{\relax{S}}{}^{{}^{pure}}$ and then, such an $\omega$ different from $\xi$ always exists).\\
We first note that $(\xi\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\omega)^\star\not\sqsubseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma_2$. Indeed, if we had $(\xi\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\omega)^\star\sqsubseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma_2$, and using the fact that $(\xi\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\omega)^\star\sqsubseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}(\sigma_1\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma_3)$, we would have $(\xi\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\omega)^\star\sqsubseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}(\sigma_1\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma_3\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma_2)$. But now,  using ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@4=3\endcsname\@firstoftwo{4=3}}}), we have in particular $\sigma_1\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma_3\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma_2=(\sigma_1\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma_2\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma_3\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma_4)$. As a consequence, we would have $(\xi\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\omega)^\star\sqsubseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}
(\sigma_1\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma_2\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma_3\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma_4) \sqsubseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}} (\sigma_2\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma_4)$, and then $\xi^\star\sqsubseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}
 (\sigma_2\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma_4)$ which is false by assumption ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@assumptionxi\endcsname\@firstoftwo{assumptionxi}}}). \\
Then, from ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@thirdcoveringpropertySbari\endcsname\@firstoftwo{thirdcoveringpropertySbari}}}), and using the fact that $\sigma_2$ is in $\overline{ \relax{S}}{}^{{}^{pure}}$ (consequence of Lemma {{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@nondegenerateallsigmapure\endcsname\@firstoftwo{nondegenerateallsigmapure}}}) and the fact that $(\xi\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\omega)^\star\not\sqsubseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma_2$ and also the property ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@omegazeta\endcsname\@firstoftwo{omegazeta}}}), we know that there exists $\nu\in {\relax{G}}^{\check{\relax{S}}}$ such that 
\begin{eqnarray}
\nu := \sigma_2^\star \sqcup_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}}(\xi\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\omega).\label{defnu}
\end{eqnarray}
Using $(\xi\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\omega)\sqsupseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}(\sigma_1\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma_3)^\star$, we deduce as before
\begin{eqnarray}
\nu \sqsupseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}} (\sigma_2\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma_1\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma_3)^\star=(\sigma_1\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma_2\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma_3\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma_4)^\star
\end{eqnarray}
(we note using, for example,  the property ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@thirdcoveringpropertySbariii\endcsname\@firstoftwo{thirdcoveringpropertySbariii}}}) and ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@reformassumption\endcsname\@firstoftwo{reformassumption}}}) that $(\sigma_1\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma_2\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma_3\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma_4)$ is different from $\bot_{{}_{\overline{\relax{S}}}}$).\\
We then deduce
\begin{eqnarray}
\nu \sqsupseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}} (\sigma_2\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma_4)^\star.\label{propnu}
\end{eqnarray}
From this inequality we deduce that
\begin{eqnarray}
\exists \alpha\in \Theta^{\overline{ \relax{S}}}(\nu) &\vert & \alpha \sqsupseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}} (\sigma_2\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma_4)^\star.
\end{eqnarray}
Let us fix one of these $\alpha$.\\
We recall that, as long as $\xi\in \overline{\relax{S}}{}^{{}^{pure}}$ we have $(\xi \sqcap_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}}\nu)=Max(\{\,\xi\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}} \kappa\;\vert\; \kappa\in  \Theta^{\overline{ \relax{S}}}(\nu)\,\})$. Moreover, we have $(\xi \sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\omega)\in \Theta^{\overline{ \relax{S}}}(\nu)$. Then, using ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@thirdcoveringpropertySbarii\endcsname\@firstoftwo{thirdcoveringpropertySbarii}}})                                   
we deduce as well 
\begin{eqnarray}
\xi \sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\omega &=& \xi \sqcap_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}}\nu.
\end{eqnarray}
As a result, we obtain for the chosen $\alpha$
\begin{eqnarray}
\xi \sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\omega &\sqsupseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}& \xi \sqcap_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}}\alpha.\label{eqinterm}
\end{eqnarray}
Now, since $\upsilon \sqsupseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}}\xi^\star$ and $\upsilon \sqsupseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}}(\sigma_2\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma_4)$ and $ \alpha \sqsupseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}} (\sigma_2\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma_4)^\star$, we deduce that 
\begin{eqnarray}
&& \upsilon \sqsupseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}} (\xi^\star \sqcup_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}} \alpha^\star).
\end{eqnarray}
and then using ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@eqinterm\endcsname\@firstoftwo{eqinterm}}})
\begin{eqnarray}
&& \upsilon \sqsupseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}} (\xi^\star\sqcup_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}} \omega^\star)\sqsupseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}} \omega^\star
\end{eqnarray}
We have then obtained the announced intermediary result : for any $\omega\in \overline{\relax{S}}{}^{{}^{pure}}$ such that the conditions ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@omegazeta\endcsname\@firstoftwo{omegazeta}}}) are satisfied, we have $\omega^\star\sqsubseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}}\upsilon$.  We note that we have also by assumption $\xi\sqsupseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}} (\sigma_1\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma_3)^\star$ and $\xi^\star\sqsubseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}}\upsilon$.  \\
Hence, we can conclude 
\begin{eqnarray}
&& \upsilon \sqsupseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}}(\sigma_1\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma_3)\label{conclusionupsilon}
\end{eqnarray}
i.e. explicitly ${\relax{r}}^{U'}(\upsilon,\sigma_1,\sigma_3)$.  Obviously, we have $\upsilon\asymp \sigma_1,\upsilon\asymp \sigma_2,\upsilon\asymp \sigma_3,\upsilon\asymp \sigma_4$ and then the existence of the consistent subset $U'$ does not pose any problem.\\
As a final conclusion, we obtain the existence of $\mu:=\upsilon\in {\relax{G}}^{\check{\relax{S}}}$ such that ${\relax{r}}^{U'}(\mu,\sigma_1,\sigma_3)$ and ${\relax{r}}^{U'}(\mu,\sigma_2,\sigma_4)$. \\
By exchanging the roles of $\sigma_3$ and $\sigma_4$ in our construction, we obtain also the existence of $\chi\in {\relax{G}}^{\check{\relax{S}}}$ such that ${\relax{r}}^{U''}(\chi,\sigma_1,\sigma_4)$ and ${\relax{r}}^{U''}(\chi,\sigma_2,\sigma_3)$.
<!-- end proof-108 -->
<!-- theorem-49: body_md -->
${ \relax{E}}^{\check{\relax{S}}}$ is equipped with a structure of {\em projective sheaf}.
In other words, apart from the sheaf condition ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@VeblenYoung0\endcsname\@firstoftwo{VeblenYoung0}}}), we have proved the Veblen-Young's geometric axioms of projective spaces ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@VeblenYoung3\endcsname\@firstoftwo{VeblenYoung3}}})({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@VeblenYoung2\endcsname\@firstoftwo{VeblenYoung2}}})({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@VeblenYoung1\endcsname\@firstoftwo{VeblenYoung1}}}).
<!-- end theorem-49 -->
<!-- proof-109: body_md -->
This result summarizes Lemma {{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@lemmaproj0\endcsname\@firstoftwo{lemmaproj0}}}, Lemma {{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@lemmaproj1\endcsname\@firstoftwo{lemmaproj1}}}, Lemma {{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@lemmaproj2\endcsname\@firstoftwo{lemmaproj2}}}, Lemma {{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@lemmaproj3\endcsname\@firstoftwo{lemmaproj3}}}.
<!-- end proof-109 -->
<!-- definition-65: body_md -->
For any pair $\sigma_1,\sigma_2\in { \relax{G}}^{\check{\relax{S}}}$, we define the line $\ell_{(\sigma_1\sigma_2)}$ to be the set of elements $\sigma_3$ in ${ \relax{G}}^{\check{\relax{S}}}$ such that $\sigma_3=\sigma_1$ or $\sigma_3=\sigma_2$ or $\sigma_3\raisebox{1.3ex}{\,\rotatebox{180}{$\sqsubseteq$}}\,_{{}_{{\relax{S}}}}(\sigma_1\sqcap_{{}_{{\relax{S}}}}\sigma_2)$.
<!-- end definition-65 -->
<!-- definition-66: body_md -->
For any triple $\sigma_1,\sigma_2,\sigma_3\in { \relax{G}}^{\check{\relax{S}}}$ distinct, such that $\sigma_i\notin \ell_{(\sigma_j\sigma_k)}$ for any $\{i,j,k\}=\{1,2,3\}$, we define the plane $\wp_{(\sigma_1,\sigma_2,\sigma_3)}$ to be the set of elements $\sigma_4$ in ${ \relax{G}}^{\check{\relax{S}}}$ such that there exists $i,j,k$ with $\{i,j,k\}=\{1,2,3\}$ and 
$\lambda\in { \relax{G}}^{\check{\relax{S}}}$ and $\lambda\in \ell_{(\sigma_i\sigma_4)}$ and $\lambda\in \ell_{(\sigma_j\sigma_k)}$. \\
The set of planes on ${ \relax{G}}^{\check{\relax{S}}}$ will be denoted $\wp^{\check{\relax{S}}}$.\\
Any element of $\wp^{\check{\relax{S}}}$ has a structure of a projective sheaf.
<!-- end definition-66 -->
<!-- remark-7: body_md -->
Any plane is stable under the application of the third Veblen-Young's property.  In other words,  if there exists $U\in { \relax{E}}^{\check{\relax{S}}}$ and $\lambda, \sigma_1,\sigma_2,\sigma_3,\sigma_4\in { \relax{G}}^{\check{\relax{S}}}$ such that $\lambda,\sigma_1,\sigma_2,\sigma_3,\sigma_4\in U$  and such that ${\relax{r}}^U(\lambda,\sigma_1,\sigma_2)$ and ${\relax{r}}^U(\lambda,\sigma_3,\sigma_4)$ and $\forall \mu,\nu,\rho\in \{\sigma_1,\sigma_2,\sigma_3,\sigma_4\}, \;\neg\; {\relax{r}}^U(\mu,\nu,\rho)$. Then,   $\lambda,\sigma_1,\sigma_2,\sigma_3,\sigma_4$ are in a same plane $\wp$. Moreover, if we introduce $U'\in { \relax{E}}^{\check{\relax{S}}}$ and the element $\mu\in U'$  such that ${\relax{r}}^{U'}(\mu,\sigma_1,\sigma_3)$ and ${\relax{r}}^{U'}(\mu,\sigma_2,\sigma_4)$, and if we introduce  $U''\in { \relax{E}}^{\check{\relax{S}}}$
 and $\chi\in U''$ such that ${\relax{r}}^{U''}(\chi,\sigma_2,\sigma_3)$ and ${\relax{r}}^{U''}(\chi,\sigma_1,\sigma_4)\,)$ we have necessarily $\mu,\chi\in \wp$.
<!-- end remark-7 -->
<!-- definition-67: body_md -->
\label{completenessU}
A consistent subset of states $U\subseteq { \relax{G}}^{\check{\relax{S}}}$ is said to be {\em orthogonally complete} iff
\begin{eqnarray}
&&\hspace{-2.2cm}\forall \sigma_1,\sigma_2,\sigma_3\in U,\;\textit{\rm distinct},\;\; {\relax{r}}^U(\sigma_1,\sigma_2,\sigma_3) \;\Rightarrow \;(\,\sigma_1\underline{\perp}\sigma_2\;\textit{\rm or}\;\sigma_1\underline{\perp}\sigma_3\;\textit{\rm or}\;\sigma_2\underline{\perp}\sigma_3\,).\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\label{orthogcompletecondition1}\\
&&\hspace{-2.2cm}\forall \sigma_1,\sigma_2,\sigma_3,\sigma_4\in U\;\vert\; (\,\exists \lambda\in U, \;{\relax{r}}^U(\lambda,\sigma_1,\sigma_2),\;{\relax{r}}^U(\lambda,\sigma_3,\sigma_4)\;\textit{\rm and}\; \forall\mu,\nu,\rho\in \{\sigma_1,\sigma_2,\sigma_3,\sigma_4\}, \;\neg\; {\relax{r}}^U(\mu,\nu,\rho)\,)\nonumber\\
&&\hspace{2cm}\exists \alpha,\beta,\gamma\in \{\sigma_1,\sigma_2,\sigma_3,\sigma_4\},\;                                                                                                           
\alpha\underline{\perp}\beta\;\;\textit{\rm and}\;\; \alpha\underline{\perp}\gamma
.\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\label{orthogcompletecondition2}
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end definition-67 -->
<!-- definition-68: body_md -->
For any $\sigma_1,\sigma_2,\sigma_3\in \overline{ \relax{S}}{}^{{}{pure}}$ satisfying the following conditions
\begin{enumerate}
\@par\hangindent 2em there exists $I\subseteq\{1,\cdots,N\}, Card(I)= N-2\;\vert\;$ $\forall m\in I,\;\;\zeta^{{}^{{\relax{S}}_{A_1}\cdots{\relax{S}}_{A_N}}}_{(m)}(\sigma_1) = \zeta^{{}^{{\relax{S}}_{A_1}\cdots{\relax{S}}_{A_N}}}_{(m)}(\sigma_2)=\zeta^{{}^{{\relax{S}}_{A_1}\cdots{\relax{S}}_{A_N}}}_{(m)}(\sigma_3)$, 
\@par\hangindent 2em if we denote $j,k\in \{1,\cdots,N\}\smallsetminus I$ with $j<k$,  there exists $\alpha\in \overline{\relax{S}}{}_{A_j}^{{}^{pure}}$ and $\beta\in \overline{\relax{S}}{}_{A_k}^{{}^{pure}}$ such that
$\Upsilon^{(j,k)}_{\sigma_1}=\alpha\widetilde{\otimes}\beta$, $\Upsilon^{(j,k)}_{\sigma_2}=\alpha^\star\widetilde{\otimes}\beta$, $\Upsilon^{(j,k)}_{\sigma_3}=\alpha\widetilde{\otimes}\beta^\star$.
\end{enumerate}
we say that the plane $\wp_{(\sigma_1,\sigma_2,\sigma_3)}$ is a {\em starred plane}. The set of starred planes on ${ \relax{G}}^{\check{\relax{S}}}$ will be denoted $\wp_\star^{\check{\relax{S}}}$.
<!-- end definition-68 -->
<!-- lemma-77: body_md -->
\label{natureorthocompleteU}
Let us consider a consistent subset of states $U\in { \relax{E}}^{\check{\relax{S}}}$ and let us assume that there exists $\chi\in ({\check{\relax{S}}}\smallsetminus \overline{ \relax{S}})$ and that the consistent subset $U$ is of {\em consistent type 2}.\\ 
Let us now assume that $U$ is orthogonally complete. Then, we have necessarily $\chi\in ({\widecheck{\relax{S}}}\smallsetminus \overline{ \relax{S}})$.\\
Conversely,  let us assume that $\chi\in ({\widecheck{\relax{S}}}\smallsetminus \overline{ \relax{S}})$ and that $U$ is maximal,  then we have
\begin{eqnarray}
&&\hspace{-0.5cm}U =  \{\chi\}\cup\{\,\varphi_\alpha\;\vert\; \alpha\in \Theta^{\overline{ \relax{S}}}(\chi)\,\}\cup\{\,\psi_\alpha\;\vert\; \alpha\in \Theta^{\overline{ \relax{S}}}(\chi)\,\}\label{orthocompletestructure0}\\
&& \forall \alpha\in \Theta^{\overline{ \relax{S}}}(\chi),\;\varphi_\alpha,\psi_\alpha\in\overline{ \relax{S}}{}^{{}^{pure}}  \;\textit{\rm and}\; \varphi_\alpha,\psi_\alpha \raisebox{1.3ex}{\,\rotatebox{180}{$\sqsubseteq$}}\,_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\alpha\;\;\textit{\rm and}\;\;\varphi_\alpha\not=\psi_\alpha\label{orthocompletestructure1}\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\\
&& \exists \textit{\bf !}\, \gamma\in \Theta^{\overline{ \relax{S}}}(\chi)\;\vert\; \varphi_\gamma \underline{\perp} \chi,\;\;\varphi_\gamma \not\!\!\!\underline{\perp} \psi_\gamma,\;\;\forall \alpha\in \Theta^{\overline{ \relax{S}}}(\chi)\smallsetminus \{\gamma\},\; \varphi_\gamma \underline{\perp} \varphi_\alpha,\;\;\varphi_\gamma \underline{\perp} \psi_\alpha,\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\label{orthocompletestructure2}\\
&&\forall \alpha\in \Theta^{\overline{ \relax{S}}}(\chi)\smallsetminus \{\gamma\}, \varphi_{\alpha}\underline{\perp}\psi_{\alpha},\;\;\varphi_{\alpha} \not\!\!\!\underline{\perp}\chi,\;\;\psi_{\alpha} \not\!\!\!\underline{\perp}\chi,\label{orthocompletestructure3}\\
&&\forall \alpha,\beta\in \Theta^{\overline{ \relax{S}}}(\chi)\smallsetminus \{\gamma\},\alpha\not=\beta,\; \varphi_{\alpha}\underline{\perp}\varphi_{\beta},\;\;\varphi_{\alpha}\not\!\!\!\underline{\perp}\psi_{\beta},\label{orthocompletestructure4}\\
&&\forall \alpha,\beta\in \Theta^{\overline{ \relax{S}}}(\chi)\smallsetminus \{\gamma\},\alpha\not=\beta,\exists \lambda_{\alpha\beta}\in \overline{ \relax{S}}{}^{{}^{pure}}\;\vert\; 
(\varphi_{\beta}\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\psi_{\alpha}), (\psi_{\beta}\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\varphi_{\alpha})\raisebox{1.3ex}{\,\rotatebox{180}{$\sqsupseteq$}}\,_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\lambda_{\alpha\beta}
\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\nonumber\\
&&\hspace{6.5cm}\textit{\rm and}\;\lambda_{\alpha\beta}\underline{\perp}\varphi_{\alpha},\;\;\lambda_{\alpha\beta}\underline{\perp}\varphi_{\beta},\label{orthocompletestructure5}\\
&&\forall \alpha\in \Theta^{\overline{ \relax{S}}}(\chi)\smallsetminus \{\gamma\},\exists \mu_{\alpha\gamma}\in \overline{ \relax{S}}{}^{{}^{pure}}\;\vert\; 
(\varphi_{\gamma}\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\varphi_{\alpha}), (\psi_{\gamma}\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\psi_{\alpha})\raisebox{1.3ex}{\,\rotatebox{180}{$\sqsupseteq$}}\,_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\mu_{\alpha\gamma}
\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\nonumber\\
&&\hspace{6.5cm}\textit{\rm and}\;\mu_{\alpha\gamma}\underline{\perp}\psi_{\alpha},\label{orthocompletestructure6}
\end{eqnarray}
and then necessarily $U$ is orthogonally complete.
<!-- end lemma-77 -->
<!-- proof-110: body_md -->
As long as $\lambda\in ({\check{\relax{S}}}\smallsetminus \overline{ \relax{S}})$, $\Theta^{\overline{\relax{S}}}(\lambda) $ is given as in Theorem {{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@lambdawr\endcsname\@firstoftwo{lambdawr}}}.\\
Now we use the condition of orthogonal completeness to conclude that necessarily $(\alpha''=\alpha,\beta''=\beta)$ or $(\alpha'=\alpha,\beta'=\beta)$. This concludes the proof of the first assertion, i.e. $\lambda\in ({\widecheck{\relax{S}}}\smallsetminus \overline{ \relax{S}})$.\\
Then, in ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@orthocompletestructure0\endcsname\@firstoftwo{orthocompletestructure0}}})--({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@orthocompletestructure6\endcsname\@firstoftwo{orthocompletestructure6}}}), we adopt the same notation as in ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@thirdcoveringpropertySbar0\endcsname\@firstoftwo{thirdcoveringpropertySbar0}}}) ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@thirdcoveringpropertySbar0bis\endcsname\@firstoftwo{thirdcoveringpropertySbar0bis}}}) ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@thirdcoveringpropertySbarviic\endcsname\@firstoftwo{thirdcoveringpropertySbarviic}}}) ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@thirdcoveringpropertySbarviib\endcsname\@firstoftwo{thirdcoveringpropertySbarviib}}}) for $\varphi_{\alpha}$ and $\psi_{\alpha}$ with $\alpha$ any element of $\Theta^{\overline{ \relax{S}}}(\chi)$.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               
With these formulas, the last assertion is trivial to check.
<!-- end proof-110 -->
<!-- lemma-78: body_md -->
\label{natureorthocompleteUbis}
Let us consider an orthogonally complete consistent subset such that there exists $\chi\in ({\widecheck{\relax{S}}}\smallsetminus \overline{ \relax{S}})$ with $\chi\in U$.  We adopt the same notation as in ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@thirdcoveringpropertySbar0\endcsname\@firstoftwo{thirdcoveringpropertySbar0}}}) ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@thirdcoveringpropertySbar0bis\endcsname\@firstoftwo{thirdcoveringpropertySbar0bis}}}) ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@thirdcoveringpropertySbarviic\endcsname\@firstoftwo{thirdcoveringpropertySbarviic}}}) ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@thirdcoveringpropertySbarviib\endcsname\@firstoftwo{thirdcoveringpropertySbarviib}}}) for $\gamma$ and for $\varphi_{\alpha}$ and $\psi_{\alpha}$ with $\alpha$ any element of $\Theta^{\overline{ \relax{S}}}(\chi)$. \\ 
Let us now assume that $U$ is of {\em consistent type 1}, i.e. $\exists \textit{\bf !} \delta\in \Theta^{\overline{ \relax{S}}}(\chi)$ such that $\forall \sigma\in U$ we have $(\sigma\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\chi)=\delta$.  Let us fix this element $\delta$. \\
Then,  we are in one of the two following cases \\
(1) $\delta\in \Theta^{\overline{ \relax{S}}}(\chi)\smallsetminus \{\gamma\}$. Then, there exists $\chi'\in {\widecheck{\relax{S}}}\smallsetminus {\overline{\relax{S}}}$ such that
\begin{eqnarray}
&&\hspace{-0.5cm}U =  \{\chi,\varphi_\delta,\psi_\delta,\chi'\,\}\label{orthocompletestructure0bis}\\
&&\varphi_\delta,\psi_\delta\in\overline{ \relax{S}}{}^{{}^{pure}}  \;\textit{\rm and}\; \varphi_\delta,\psi_\delta \raisebox{1.3ex}{\,\rotatebox{180}{$\sqsubseteq$}}\,_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\delta\;\;\textit{\rm and}\;\;\varphi_\delta\not=\psi_\delta\label{orthocompletestructure1bis}\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\\
&&\varphi_{\delta}\underline{\perp}\psi_{\delta},\;\;\varphi_{\delta} \not\!\!\!\underline{\perp}\chi,\;\;\psi_{\delta} \not\!\!\!\underline{\perp}\chi,\;\;\varphi_{\delta} \not\!\!\!\underline{\perp}\chi',\;\;\psi_{\delta} \not\!\!\!\underline{\perp}\chi',\;\;\chi\underline{\perp}\chi'\label{orthocompletestructure3bis}
\end{eqnarray}
(2) $\delta=\gamma$. Then, there exists $\chi'\in {\widecheck{\relax{S}}}\smallsetminus {\overline{\relax{S}}}$ such that
\begin{eqnarray}
&&\hspace{-0.5cm}U =  \{\chi,\varphi_\gamma,\psi_\gamma,\chi'\,\}\label{orthocompletestructure0ter}\\
&&\varphi_\gamma,\psi_\gamma\in\overline{ \relax{S}}{}^{{}^{pure}}  \;\textit{\rm and}\; \varphi_\gamma,\psi_\gamma \raisebox{1.3ex}{\,\rotatebox{180}{$\sqsubseteq$}}\,_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\gamma\;\;\textit{\rm and}\;\;\varphi_\gamma\not=\psi_\gamma\label{orthocompletestructure1ter}\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\\
&&\varphi_{\gamma}\not\!\!\!\underline{\perp}\psi_{\gamma},\;\;\varphi_{\gamma} \underline{\perp}\chi,\;\;\psi_{\gamma} \not\!\!\!\underline{\perp}\chi,\;\;\varphi_{\gamma} \not\!\!\!\underline{\perp}\chi',\;\;\psi_{\gamma} \underline{\perp}\chi',\;\;\chi\not\!\!\!\underline{\perp}\chi'\label{orthocompletestructure3ter}
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end lemma-78 -->
<!-- proof-111: body_md -->
We also adopt the same notation as in ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@thirdcoveringpropertySbar0\endcsname\@firstoftwo{thirdcoveringpropertySbar0}}}) ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@thirdcoveringpropertySbar0bis\endcsname\@firstoftwo{thirdcoveringpropertySbar0bis}}}) ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@thirdcoveringpropertySbarviic\endcsname\@firstoftwo{thirdcoveringpropertySbarviic}}}). Without the constraint imposed by the Lemma {{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@nondegenerateallsigmapure\endcsname\@firstoftwo{nondegenerateallsigmapure}}}, and for the maximality of $U$,  we can consider the existence of an element $\chi'\in  {\widecheck{\relax{S}}}\smallsetminus {\overline{\relax{S}}}$ distinct from $\chi$ such that $\chi'\in U$. In order to guaranty that $U$ is orthogonality complete, we have to require new orthogonality conditions.\\
In the first configuration, i.e. $\delta\in \Theta^{\overline{ \relax{S}}}(\chi)\smallsetminus \{\gamma\}$. We choose $\chi':=\delta \sqcup_{{}_{\relax{S}}}\gamma^\star$. Such an element does effectively exist in ${\widecheck{\relax{S}}}\smallsetminus {\overline{\relax{S}}}$ because of property ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@thirdcoveringpropertySbarvi\endcsname\@firstoftwo{thirdcoveringpropertySbarvi}}}). The announced orthogonality relations are easy to check.\\
In the second configuration, i.e. $\delta=\gamma$. We choose $\chi':=\psi_\gamma^\star \sqcup_{{}_{\relax{S}}}\gamma$. Such an element does effectively exist in ${\widecheck{\relax{S}}}\smallsetminus {\overline{\relax{S}}}$. The announced orthogonality relations are easy to check.
<!-- end proof-111 -->
<!-- definition-69: body_md -->
We will denote by 
${ \relax{E}}_{\underline{\perp}}^{\check{\relax{S}}}$ the following consistency cover of ${ \relax{G}}^{\widecheck{\relax{S}}}$ (Note that we have a cover of ${ \relax{G}}^{\widecheck{\relax{S}}}$ and not ${ \relax{G}}^{\check{\relax{S}}}$ because of Lemma {{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@natureorthocompleteU\endcsname\@firstoftwo{natureorthocompleteU}}}) :
\begin{eqnarray}
{ \relax{E}}_{\underline{\perp}}^{\check{\relax{S}}} &:=& \{\,U \;\vert\;\exists V\in { \relax{E}}^{\check{\relax{S}}}, U\subseteq V,  \;\textit{\rm and $U$ is orthogonally complete} \,\}.
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end definition-69 -->
<!-- lemma-79: body_md -->
\label{caseanalysisUSpure}
Let us consider $U\in { \relax{E}}_{\underline{\perp}}^{\check{\relax{S}}}$ such that $U\subseteq \overline{ \relax{S}}{}^{{}^{pure}}$.  Let us moreover consider $\lambda,\sigma_1,\sigma_2,\sigma_3,\sigma_4\in U$, all distinct, such that ${\relax{r}}^U(\lambda,\sigma_1,\sigma_2)$ and ${\relax{r}}^U(\lambda,\sigma_3,\sigma_4)$ and $\forall\mu,\nu,\rho\in \{\sigma_1,\sigma_2,\sigma_3,\sigma_4\}, \;\neg\; {\relax{r}}^U(\mu,\nu,\rho)$.  Endly, we will suppose that the plane to which $\lambda,\sigma_1,\sigma_2,\sigma_3,\sigma_4$ belong is not a starred plane.\\
Then, there exists $\mu\in { \relax{G}}^{\widecheck{\relax{S}}}\smallsetminus \overline{ \relax{S}}$ and there exists $U'\in { \relax{E}}_{\underline{\perp}}^{\check{\relax{S}}}$ with $\mu, \sigma_1,\sigma_2,\sigma_3,\sigma_4\in U'$ such that ${\relax{r}}^{U'}(\mu,\sigma_1,\sigma_3)$ and ${\relax{r}}^{U'}(\mu,\sigma_2,\sigma_4)$, and there exists $\nu\in { \relax{G}}^{\widecheck{\relax{S}}}\smallsetminus \overline{ \relax{S}}$ and there exists $U'\in { \relax{E}}_{\underline{\perp}}^{\check{\relax{S}}}$ with $\nu, \sigma_1,\sigma_2,\sigma_3,\sigma_4\in U'$ such that ${\relax{r}}^{U'}(\nu,\sigma_2,\sigma_3)$ and ${\relax{r}}^{U'}(\nu,\sigma_1,\sigma_4)$.
<!-- end lemma-79 -->
<!-- proof-112: body_md -->
From Theorem {{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@zetalambda\endcsname\@firstoftwo{zetalambda}}}, we know that the conditions ${\relax{r}}^U(\lambda,\sigma_1,\sigma_2)$ and ${\relax{r}}^U(\lambda,\sigma_3,\sigma_4)$ and $\forall\mu,\nu,\rho\in \{\sigma_1,\sigma_2,\sigma_3,\sigma_4\}, \;\neg\; {\relax{r}}^U(\mu,\nu,\rho)$ with $\lambda,\sigma_1,\sigma_2,\sigma_3,\sigma_4\in U\subseteq \overline{ \relax{S}}{}^{{}^{pure}}$ imply $\exists I\subseteq\{1,\cdots,N\}, Card(I)=N-2\;\vert\; \forall i\in I, \forall \sigma,\kappa\in \{\lambda,\sigma_1,\sigma_2,\sigma_3,\sigma_4\},\;\;\zeta^{{}^{{\relax{S}}_{A_1}\cdots{\relax{S}}_{A_N}}}_{(i)}(\sigma) = \zeta^{{}^{{\relax{S}}_{A_1}\cdots{\relax{S}}_{A_N}}}_{(i)}(\kappa)$.  Let us now denote $j$ and $k$ such that $\{j,k\}=\{1,\cdots,N\}\smallsetminus I$ and $j<k$ and let us now adopt the notations of Definition {{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@definUpsilonDelta\endcsname\@firstoftwo{definUpsilonDelta}}}.\\
The condition ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@orthogcompletecondition1\endcsname\@firstoftwo{orthogcompletecondition1}}}) imposed on $U$ by the requirement of orthogonal completeness ensures that $\lambda,\sigma_1,\sigma_2,\sigma_3,\sigma_4$ can be written in terms of four elements $\alpha,\alpha'\in \overline{ \relax{S}}{}_A^{{}^{pure}},\beta,\beta'\in \overline{ \relax{S}}{}_B^{{}^{pure}}$ with $\alpha'\not=\alpha,\alpha^\star$ and $\beta'\not=\beta,\beta^\star$, in one of the following configurations
\begin{eqnarray}
&&\hspace{-1.5cm}(i)\;\;\; \Upsilon^{(j,k)}_{\lambda}:=\alpha\widetilde{\otimes}\beta,\;\;\Upsilon^{(j,k)}_{\sigma_1}:=\alpha'\widetilde{\otimes}\beta,\;\;\Upsilon^{(j,k)}_{\sigma_2}:=\alpha^\star\widetilde{\otimes}\beta,\;\;\Upsilon^{(j,k)}_{\sigma_3}:=\alpha\widetilde{\otimes}\beta',\;\;\Upsilon_{\sigma_4}:=\alpha\widetilde{\otimes}\beta^\star\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\\
&&\hspace{-1.5cm}(ii)\;\;\; \Upsilon^{(j,k)}_{\lambda}:=\alpha'\widetilde{\otimes}\beta,\;\;\Upsilon^{(j,k)}_{\sigma_1}:=\alpha\widetilde{\otimes}\beta,\;\;\Upsilon^{(j,k)}_{\sigma_2}:=\alpha^\star\widetilde{\otimes}\beta,\;\;\Upsilon^{(j,k)}_{\sigma_3}:=\alpha'\widetilde{\otimes}\beta',\;\;\Upsilon^{(j,k)}_{\sigma_4}:=\alpha'\widetilde{\otimes}\beta^\star\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\\
&&\hspace{-1.5cm}(iii)\;\;\; \Upsilon^{(j,k)}_{\lambda}:=\alpha\widetilde{\otimes}\beta',\;\;\Upsilon^{(j,k)}_{\sigma_1}:=\alpha'\widetilde{\otimes}\beta',\;\;\Upsilon^{(j,k)}_{\sigma_2}:=\alpha^\star\widetilde{\otimes}\beta',\;\;\Upsilon^{(j,k)}_{\sigma_3}:=\alpha\widetilde{\otimes}\beta,\;\;\Upsilon^{(j,k)}_{\sigma_4}:=\alpha\widetilde{\otimes}\beta^\star\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\\
&&\hspace{-1.5cm}(iv)\;\;\; \Upsilon_{\lambda}:=\alpha'\widetilde{\otimes}\beta',\;\;\Upsilon_{\sigma_1}:=\alpha\widetilde{\otimes}\beta',\;\;\Upsilon_{\sigma_2}:=\alpha^\star\widetilde{\otimes}\beta',\;\;\Upsilon_{\sigma_3}:=\alpha'\widetilde{\otimes}\beta,\;\;\Upsilon_{\sigma_4}:=\alpha'\widetilde{\otimes}\beta^\star.\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;
\end{eqnarray}
The condition ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@orthogcompletecondition2\endcsname\@firstoftwo{orthogcompletecondition2}}}) imposed on $U$ by the requirement of orthogonal completeness ensures that the configuration $(iv)$ is excluded.\\
Endly, the condition requiring that the plane to which $\lambda,\sigma_1,\sigma_2,\sigma_3,\sigma_4$ belong is not a starred plane ensures that the configuration $(i)$ is excluded.\\
                                         
                 
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                
               
On another part we note the following properties.\\
In the configuration $(ii)$ 
\begin{eqnarray}
&&(\sigma_1\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma_3)\sqcup_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}}(\sigma_2\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma_4)=(\Delta^{(j,k);\sigma_1}_{\alpha\widetilde{\otimes}\beta})^\star \sqcup_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}} (\Delta^{(j,k);\sigma_1}_{\alpha\widetilde{\otimes}\beta} \sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}} \Delta^{(j,k);\sigma_1}_{\alpha'\widetilde{\otimes}\beta'}) \;\in { \relax{G}}^{\widecheck{\relax{S}}}\smallsetminus \overline{ \relax{S}}\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\\
&&(\sigma_1\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma_4)\sqcup_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}}(\sigma_2\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma_3)=(\Delta^{(j,k);\sigma_1}_{\alpha^\star\widetilde{\otimes}\beta})^\star \sqcup_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}} (\Delta^{(j,k);\sigma_1}_{\alpha^\star\widetilde{\otimes}\beta} \sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}} \Delta^{(j,k);\sigma_1}_{\alpha'\widetilde{\otimes}\beta'}) \;\in { \relax{G}}^{\widecheck{\relax{S}}}\smallsetminus \overline{ \relax{S}}.\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;
\end{eqnarray}
In the configuration $(iii)$ 
\begin{eqnarray}
&&(\sigma_1\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma_3)\sqcup_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}}(\sigma_2\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma_4)=(\Delta^{(j,k);\sigma_1}_{\alpha\widetilde{\otimes}\beta})^\star \sqcup_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}} (\Delta^{(j,k);\sigma_1}_{\alpha\widetilde{\otimes}\beta} \sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}} \Delta^{(j,k);\sigma_1}_{\alpha'\widetilde{\otimes}\beta'}) \;\in { \relax{G}}^{\widecheck{\relax{S}}}\smallsetminus \overline{ \relax{S}}\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\\
&&(\sigma_1\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma_4)\sqcup_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}}(\sigma_2\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma_3)=(\Delta^{(j,k);\sigma_1}_{\alpha\widetilde{\otimes}\beta^\star})^\star \sqcup_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}} (\Delta^{(j,k);\sigma_1}_{\alpha\widetilde{\otimes}\beta^\star} \sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}} \Delta^{(j,k);\sigma_1}_{\alpha'\widetilde{\otimes}\beta'}) \;\in { \relax{G}}^{\widecheck{\relax{S}}}\smallsetminus \overline{ \relax{S}}.\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;
\end{eqnarray}
                                          
                 
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          
               
This concludes the proof.
<!-- end proof-112 -->
<!-- remark-8: body_md -->
\label{remarkstarredplanes}
Let us formulate a simple remark justifying the introduction of starred planes.\\
In the configuration $(i)$ we have the following problem
\begin{eqnarray}
&&\hspace{-1cm}\chi:=(\sigma_1\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma_3)\sqcup_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}}(\sigma_2\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma_4)= (\Delta^{(j,k);\sigma_1}_{\alpha^\star\widetilde{\otimes}\beta^\star})^\star \sqcup_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}} (\Delta^{(j,k);\sigma_1}_{\alpha^\star\widetilde{\otimes}\beta'} \sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}} \Delta^{(j,k);\sigma_1}_{\alpha'\widetilde{\otimes}\beta^\star})\;\in { \relax{G}}^{\check{\relax{S}}}\smallsetminus { \relax{G}}^{\widecheck{\relax{S}}}.\label{casproblematique}\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;
   
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                
\end{eqnarray}
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                
We could still hope to have a property of the type $\forall \sigma\in \overline{\relax{S}}{}^{{}^{pure}}\;\vert\; \sigma\asymp \chi,\;\; \exists \lambda\in {\relax{S}}\;\vert\; \chi\sqcap_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma \raisebox{1.3ex}{\,\rotatebox{180}{$\sqsupseteq$}}\,_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}} \lambda\;\textit{\rm and}\; \chi\underline{\perp}\lambda$. In other words, we could still hope to have $\forall \mu\in \Theta^{\overline{ \relax{S}}}(\chi), \exists \nu\in \Theta^{\overline{ \relax{S}}}(\chi)$ such that $\mu^\star \sqcup_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}} \nu\in { \relax{S}}$. But this point is false.  Indeed, we have for
\begin{eqnarray}
\Theta^{\overline{ \relax{S}}}(\chi)=\left\{ (\alpha\widetilde{\otimes}\beta')\sqcap_{{}_{{{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}}}}\!\!\!(\alpha'\widetilde{\otimes}\beta)
\,,\,
(\alpha \widetilde{\otimes}\beta^\star)\sqcap_{{}_{{{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}}}} (\alpha^\star\widetilde{\otimes} \beta)\,,\,
(\alpha' \widetilde{\otimes}\beta^\star)\sqcap_{{}_{{{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}}}} (\alpha^\star\widetilde{\otimes} \beta')
\right\}\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;
\end{eqnarray}
the following result
\begin{eqnarray}
&&cl_c^{\overline{ \relax{S}}}\left\{ 
((\alpha\widetilde{\otimes}\beta')\sqcap_{{}_{{{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}}}}\!\!\!(\alpha'\widetilde{\otimes}\beta))^\star\,,\, ((\alpha \widetilde{\otimes}\beta^\star)\sqcap_{{}_{{{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}}}} (\alpha^\star\widetilde{\otimes} \beta))\right\}=\nonumber\\
&&= 
cl_c^{\overline{ \relax{S}}}\left\{ 
 ((\alpha^\star\widetilde{\otimes}\bot)\sqcap_{{}_{{{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}}}}\!\!\!(\bot\widetilde{\otimes}\beta'{}^\star))
 \,,\,
 ((\bot\widetilde{\otimes}\beta^\star)\sqcap_{{}_{{{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}}}}\!\!\!(\alpha'{}^\star\widetilde{\otimes}\bot))
 \,,\,((\alpha \widetilde{\otimes}\beta^\star)\sqcap_{{}_{{{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}}}} (\alpha^\star\widetilde{\otimes} \beta))
 \right\}=\nonumber\\
 &&= 
cl_c^{\overline{ \relax{S}}}\left\{ 
((\alpha^\star\widetilde{\otimes}\bot)\sqcap_{{}_{{{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}}}}\!\!\!(\bot\widetilde{\otimes}\beta'{}^\star))
\,,\,
(\alpha \widetilde{\otimes}\beta^\star)
\right\}
\end{eqnarray}
but we have also easily
\begin{eqnarray}
\left\{(\alpha^\star \widetilde{\otimes}\beta^\star)\,,\,(\alpha \widetilde{\otimes}\beta^\star)
\right\}
\sqsubseteq
cl_c^{\overline{ \relax{S}}}\left\{ 
((\alpha^\star\widetilde{\otimes}\bot)\sqcap_{{}_{{{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}}}}\!\!\!(\bot\widetilde{\otimes}\beta'{}^\star))
\,,\,
(\alpha \widetilde{\otimes}\beta^\star)
\right\}
\end{eqnarray}
and then, as a consequence,
\begin{eqnarray}
cl_c^{\overline{ \relax{S}}}\left\{ 
((\alpha\widetilde{\otimes}\beta')\sqcap_{{}_{{{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}}}}\!\!\!(\alpha'\widetilde{\otimes}\beta))^\star\,,\, ((\alpha \widetilde{\otimes}\beta^\star)\sqcap_{{}_{{{{ \overline{\relax{S}}}}}}} (\alpha^\star\widetilde{\otimes} \beta))\right\}&\notin& {\mathcal{Q}}_c(\overline{ \relax{S}}).
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end remark-8 -->
<!-- lemma-80: body_md -->
\label{firstlemmawidecheck}
We will consider $\sigma_1,\sigma_2,\sigma_3,\sigma_4\in {\overline{\relax{S}}}{}^{{}^{pure}}$ and $\lambda \in { \relax{G}}^{\widecheck{\relax{S}}}\smallsetminus {\overline{\relax{S}}}$ and we will assume the existence of $U\in { \relax{E}}_{\underline{\perp}}^{\check{\relax{S}}}$ with $\lambda, \sigma_1,\sigma_2,\sigma_3,\sigma_4\in U$ and such that ${\relax{r}}^U(\lambda,\sigma_1,\sigma_2)$ and ${\relax{r}}^U(\lambda,\sigma_3,\sigma_4)$ and $\forall\omega,\nu,\rho\in \{\sigma_1,\sigma_2,\sigma_3,\sigma_4\}, \;\neg\; {\relax{r}}^U(\omega,\nu,\rho)$. Endly, we will assume that the plane to which $\sigma_1,\sigma_2,\sigma_3,\sigma_4$ belong is not a starred plane.\\ 
Then, there exists $\mu\in {\overline{\relax{S}}}{}^{{}^{pure}}$ and there exists $U'\in { \relax{E}}_{\underline{\perp}}^{\check{\relax{S}}}$ with $\mu, \sigma_1,\sigma_2,\sigma_3,\sigma_4\in U'$ such that ${\relax{r}}^{U'}(\mu,\sigma_1,\sigma_3)$ and ${\relax{r}}^{U'}(\mu,\sigma_2,\sigma_4)$ and there exists $\chi\in { \relax{G}}^{\widecheck{\relax{S}}}\smallsetminus {\overline{\relax{S}}}$ and there exists $U''\in { \relax{E}}_{\underline{\perp}}^{\check{\relax{S}}}$ with $\chi, \sigma_1,\sigma_2,\sigma_3,\sigma_4\in U''$ such that ${\relax{r}}^{U''}(\chi,\sigma_2,\sigma_3)$ and ${\relax{r}}^{U''}(\chi,\sigma_1,\sigma_4)$, 
\underline{or} there exists $\mu\in {\overline{\relax{S}}}{}^{{}^{pure}}$ and there exists $U'\in { \relax{E}}_{\underline{\perp}}^{\check{\relax{S}}}$ with $\mu, \sigma_1,\sigma_2,\sigma_3,\sigma_4\in U'$ such that ${\relax{r}}^{U'}(\mu,\sigma_2,\sigma_3)$ and ${\relax{r}}^{U'}(\mu,\sigma_1,\sigma_4)$ and there exists $\chi\in { \relax{G}}^{\widecheck{\relax{S}}}\smallsetminus {\overline{\relax{S}}}$ and there exists $U''\in { \relax{E}}_{\underline{\perp}}^{\check{\relax{S}}}$ with $\chi, \sigma_1,\sigma_2,\sigma_3,\sigma_4\in U''$ such that ${\relax{r}}^{U''}(\chi,\sigma_1,\sigma_3)$ and ${\relax{r}}^{U''}(\chi,\sigma_2,\sigma_4)$.
<!-- end lemma-80 -->
<!-- proof-113: body_md -->
As long as $\lambda\in ({\check{\relax{S}}}\smallsetminus \overline{ \relax{S}})$, we have the results of Lemma {{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@natureorthocompleteU\endcsname\@firstoftwo{natureorthocompleteU}}} 
and we can adopt the notations of this lemma.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          

We note that the conditions ${\relax{r}}^U(\lambda,\sigma_1,\sigma_2)$ and ${\relax{r}}^U(\lambda,\sigma_3,\sigma_4)$ and $\forall\omega,\nu,\rho\in \{\sigma_1,\sigma_2,\sigma_3,\sigma_4\}, \;\neg\; {\relax{r}}^U(\omega,\nu,\rho)$ impose the existence of $\delta,\epsilon\in \Theta^{\overline{\relax{S}}}(\lambda)$ such that $\epsilon\not=\delta$ and $(\sigma_1\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{\relax{S}}}}\sigma_2)=\epsilon$ and $(\sigma_3\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{\relax{S}}}}\sigma_4)=\delta$.\\

Let us now distinguish the different cases exhibited from the condition of orthogonal completeness.  We denote as usual $\gamma$ the unique element of $\Theta^{\overline{ \relax{S}}}(\lambda)$ such that $\lambda=\varphi_\gamma^\star\sqcup\gamma$ and $\gamma:=(\varphi_\gamma\sqcap_{{}_{{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}}\psi_\gamma)\raisebox{1.3ex}{\,\rotatebox{180}{$\sqsupseteq$}}\,_{{}_{{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}}\varphi_\gamma,\psi_\gamma$.\\

\noindent If $\sigma_2\sqsupseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}} (\sigma_1\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma_3)^\star$ we are then in one of the two following configurations \\ 
(i) $\gamma=\delta$ and then $\varphi_\gamma=\sigma_3$,  $\psi_\gamma=\sigma_4$ and $\{\varphi_\epsilon,\psi_\epsilon\}=\{\sigma_1,\sigma_2\}$, \\
(ii) $\gamma\not=\delta,\gamma\not=\epsilon$ and then $\varphi_\delta=\sigma_3$,$\psi_\delta=\sigma_4$,$\varphi_\epsilon=\sigma_2$, $\psi_\epsilon=\sigma_1$.\\

In the configuration (i) and if $\sigma_1=\varphi_\epsilon$ , using ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@orthocompletestructure6\endcsname\@firstoftwo{orthocompletestructure6}}}), we deduce that there exists $\mu:=\mu_{\epsilon\gamma}\in {\overline{\relax{S}}}{}^{{}^{pure}}$ such that $(\sigma_1\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma_3)=(\varphi_{\gamma}\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\varphi_{\epsilon})\raisebox{1.3ex}{\,\rotatebox{180}{$\sqsupseteq$}}\,_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\mu$ and 
$(\sigma_2\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma_4)=(\psi_{\gamma}\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\psi_{\epsilon})\raisebox{1.3ex}{\,\rotatebox{180}{$\sqsupseteq$}}\,_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\mu$. Moreover, we have $\mu_{\alpha\gamma}\underline{\perp}\psi_{\epsilon}$, i.e. $\mu\underline{\perp}\sigma_2$, and $\varphi_\gamma\underline{\perp}\varphi_\epsilon$, i.e. $\sigma_1\underline{\perp}\sigma_3$.  As a result, there exists $U'\in { \relax{E}}_{\underline{\perp}}^{\check{\relax{S}}}$ with $\mu, \sigma_1,\sigma_2,\sigma_3,\sigma_4\in U'$ such that ${\relax{r}}^{U'}(\mu,\sigma_1,\sigma_3)$ and ${\relax{r}}^{U'}(\mu,\sigma_2,\sigma_4)$. Now we can use Lemma {{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@caseanalysisUSpure\endcsname\@firstoftwo{caseanalysisUSpure}}} to deduce that there exists $U''\in { \relax{E}}_{\underline{\perp}}^{\check{\relax{S}}}$ and $\chi\in { \relax{G}}^{\widecheck{\relax{S}}}\smallsetminus {\overline{\relax{S}}}$ with $\chi, \sigma_1,\sigma_2,\sigma_3,\sigma_4\in U''$ such that ${\relax{r}}^{U''}(\chi,\sigma_2,\sigma_3)$ and ${\relax{r}}^{U''}(\chi,\sigma_1,\sigma_4)$.\\

In the configuration (i) and if $\sigma_1=\psi_\epsilon$ , using ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@orthocompletestructure6\endcsname\@firstoftwo{orthocompletestructure6}}}), we deduce analogously that there exists $\mu\in {\overline{\relax{S}}}{}^{{}^{pure}}$ and $U'\in { \relax{E}}_{\underline{\perp}}^{\check{\relax{S}}}$ with $\mu, \sigma_1,\sigma_2,\sigma_3,\sigma_4\in U'$ such that ${\relax{r}}^{U'}(\mu,\sigma_2,\sigma_3)$ and ${\relax{r}}^{U'}(\mu,\sigma_1,\sigma_4)$. Now we can use Lemma {{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@caseanalysisUSpure\endcsname\@firstoftwo{caseanalysisUSpure}}} to deduce that there exists $U''\in { \relax{E}}_{\underline{\perp}}^{\check{\relax{S}}}$ and $\chi\in { \relax{G}}^{\widecheck{\relax{S}}}\smallsetminus {\overline{\relax{S}}}$ with $\chi, \sigma_1,\sigma_2,\sigma_3,\sigma_4\in U''$ such that ${\relax{r}}^{U''}(\chi,\sigma_1,\sigma_3)$ and ${\relax{r}}^{U''}(\chi,\sigma_2,\sigma_4)$.\\

In the configuration (ii), using ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@orthocompletestructure5\endcsname\@firstoftwo{orthocompletestructure5}}}), we deduce that there exists $\mu:=\lambda_{\epsilon\delta}\in {\overline{\relax{S}}}{}^{{}^{pure}}$ such that $(\sigma_1\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma_3)=(\varphi_{\delta}\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\psi_{\epsilon})\raisebox{1.3ex}{\,\rotatebox{180}{$\sqsupseteq$}}\,_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\mu$ and 
$(\sigma_2\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma_4)=(\psi_{\delta}\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\varphi_{\epsilon})\raisebox{1.3ex}{\,\rotatebox{180}{$\sqsupseteq$}}\,_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\mu$.  Moreover,  we have $\mu=\lambda_{\epsilon\delta}\underline{\perp}\varphi_{\epsilon}=\sigma_2$ and $\mu=\lambda_{\epsilon\delta}\underline{\perp}\varphi_{\delta}=\sigma_3$. In other words, there exists $U'\in { \relax{E}}_{\underline{\perp}}^{\check{\relax{S}}}$ with $\mu, \sigma_1,\sigma_2,\sigma_3,\sigma_4\in U'$ such that ${\relax{r}}^{U'}(\mu,\sigma_1,\sigma_3)$ and ${\relax{r}}^{U'}(\mu,\sigma_2,\sigma_4)$. 
 Now we can use Lemma {{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@caseanalysisUSpure\endcsname\@firstoftwo{caseanalysisUSpure}}} to deduce that there exists $U''\in { \relax{E}}_{\underline{\perp}}^{\check{\relax{S}}}$ and $\chi\in { \relax{G}}^{\widecheck{\relax{S}}}\smallsetminus {\overline{\relax{S}}}$ with $\chi, \sigma_1,\sigma_2,\sigma_3,\sigma_4\in U''$ such that ${\relax{r}}^{U''}(\chi,\sigma_2,\sigma_3)$ and ${\relax{r}}^{U''}(\chi,\sigma_1,\sigma_4)$.\\

\noindent If we have $\sigma_3\sqsupseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}} (\sigma_2\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma_4)^\star$ or $\sigma_1\sqsupseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}} (\sigma_2\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma_4)^\star$ or $\sigma_4\sqsupseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}} (\sigma_1\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma_3)^\star$, and using the natural symmetries of the assumption ($\sigma_1 \leftrightarrow \sigma_2$, $\sigma_3 \leftrightarrow \sigma_4$, $(\sigma_1,\sigma_2) \leftrightarrow (\sigma_3,\sigma_4)$), we obtain the same result.\\

\noindent If we have $\sigma_1\sqsupseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}} (\sigma_3\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma_4)^\star$, the situation is even simpler. Indeed, we have necessarily $\gamma=\delta$ and $\varphi_\gamma=\sigma_1$,$\psi_\gamma=\sigma_2$,$\{\varphi_\epsilon, \psi_\epsilon\}=\{\sigma_3,\sigma_4\}$.\\
If $\sigma_3=\varphi_\epsilon$ , using ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@orthocompletestructure6\endcsname\@firstoftwo{orthocompletestructure6}}}), we deduce that there exists $\mu:=\mu_{\epsilon\gamma}\in {\overline{\relax{S}}}{}^{{}^{pure}}$ such that $(\sigma_1\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma_3)=(\varphi_{\gamma}\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\varphi_{\epsilon})\raisebox{1.3ex}{\,\rotatebox{180}{$\sqsupseteq$}}\,_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\mu$ and 
$(\sigma_2\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma_4)=(\psi_{\gamma}\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\psi_{\epsilon})\raisebox{1.3ex}{\,\rotatebox{180}{$\sqsupseteq$}}\,_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\mu$. Moreover, we have $\mu_{\alpha\gamma}\underline{\perp}\psi_{\epsilon}$, i.e. $\mu\underline{\perp}\sigma_4$, and $\varphi_\gamma\underline{\perp}\varphi_\epsilon$, i.e. $\sigma_1\underline{\perp}\sigma_3$.  As a result, there exists $U'\in { \relax{E}}_{\underline{\perp}}^{\check{\relax{S}}}$ with $\mu, \sigma_1,\sigma_2,\sigma_3,\sigma_4\in U'$ such that ${\relax{r}}^{U'}(\mu,\sigma_1,\sigma_3)$ and ${\relax{r}}^{U'}(\mu,\sigma_2,\sigma_4)$. Now we can use Lemma {{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@caseanalysisUSpure\endcsname\@firstoftwo{caseanalysisUSpure}}} to deduce that there exists $U''\in { \relax{E}}_{\underline{\perp}}^{\check{\relax{S}}}$ and $\chi\in { \relax{G}}^{\widecheck{\relax{S}}}\smallsetminus {\overline{\relax{S}}}$ with $\chi, \sigma_1,\sigma_2,\sigma_3,\sigma_4\in U''$ such that ${\relax{r}}^{U''}(\chi,\sigma_2,\sigma_3)$ and ${\relax{r}}^{U''}(\chi,\sigma_1,\sigma_4)$.\\

If $\sigma_4=\varphi_\epsilon$ , using ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@orthocompletestructure6\endcsname\@firstoftwo{orthocompletestructure6}}}), we deduce analogously that there exists $\mu\in {\overline{\relax{S}}}{}^{{}^{pure}}$ and $U'\in { \relax{E}}_{\underline{\perp}}^{\check{\relax{S}}}$ with $\mu, \sigma_1,\sigma_2,\sigma_3,\sigma_4\in U'$ such that ${\relax{r}}^{U'}(\mu,\sigma_2,\sigma_3)$ and ${\relax{r}}^{U'}(\mu,\sigma_1,\sigma_4)$. Now we can use Lemma {{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@caseanalysisUSpure\endcsname\@firstoftwo{caseanalysisUSpure}}} to deduce that there exists $U''\in { \relax{E}}_{\underline{\perp}}^{\check{\relax{S}}}$ and $\chi\in { \relax{G}}^{\widecheck{\relax{S}}}\smallsetminus {\overline{\relax{S}}}$ with $\chi, \sigma_1,\sigma_2,\sigma_3,\sigma_4\in U''$ such that ${\relax{r}}^{U''}(\chi,\sigma_1,\sigma_3)$ and ${\relax{r}}^{U''}(\chi,\sigma_2,\sigma_4)$.\\

\noindent If we have $\sigma_2\sqsupseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}} (\sigma_3\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma_4)^\star$ or $\sigma_3\sqsupseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}} (\sigma_1\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma_2)^\star$ or $\sigma_4\sqsupseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}} (\sigma_1\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma_2)^\star$, and using the natural symmetries of the assumption ($\sigma_1 \leftrightarrow \sigma_2$, $\sigma_3 \leftrightarrow \sigma_4$, $(\sigma_1,\sigma_2) \leftrightarrow (\sigma_3,\sigma_4)$), we obtain the same result.\\
<!-- end proof-113 -->
<!-- theorem-50: body_md -->
{\bf [restricted Veblen-Young's third geometric property]}\label{theoremwidecheck}\\
Let us consider $U\in { \relax{E}}_{\underline{\perp}}^{\check{\relax{S}}}$ and $\lambda, \sigma_1,\sigma_2,\sigma_3,\sigma_4\in U$ such that ${\relax{r}}^U(\lambda,\sigma_1,\sigma_2)$ and ${\relax{r}}^U(\lambda,\sigma_3,\sigma_4)$ and $\forall\mu,\nu,\rho\in \{\sigma_1,\sigma_2,\sigma_3,\sigma_4\}, \;\neg\; {\relax{r}}^U(\mu,\nu,\rho)$.  Endly, we will assume that the plane to which $\sigma_1,\sigma_2,\sigma_3,\sigma_4$ belong is not a starred plane.\\
From Lemma {{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@nondegenerateallsigmapure\endcsname\@firstoftwo{nondegenerateallsigmapure}}}, we know that $\sigma_1,\sigma_2,\sigma_3,\sigma_4\in \overline{\relax{S}}{}^{{}^{pure}}$. From Lemma {{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@natureorthocompleteU\endcsname\@firstoftwo{natureorthocompleteU}}}, we know that, as long as $U$ is orthogonally complete, we have $\lambda\in {\relax{G}}^{\widecheck{\relax{S}}}$. Endly, from Lemma {{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@firstlemmawidecheck\endcsname\@firstoftwo{firstlemmawidecheck}}} and Lemma {{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@caseanalysisUSpure\endcsname\@firstoftwo{caseanalysisUSpure}}}, we know that there exists $U'\in { \relax{E}}_{\underline{\perp}}^{\check{\relax{S}}}$ with $\sigma_1,\sigma_2,\sigma_3,\sigma_4\in U'$ and $\lambda'\in U'\cap {\relax{G}}^{\widecheck{\relax{S}}}$ satisfying ${\relax{r}}^{U'}(\lambda',\sigma_1,\sigma_3)$ and ${\relax{r}}^{U'}(\lambda',\sigma_2,\sigma_4)$, and there exists $U''\in { \relax{E}}_{\underline{\perp}}^{\check{\relax{S}}},\sigma_1,\sigma_2,\sigma_3,\sigma_4\in U''$ and $\lambda''\in U''\cap {\relax{G}}^{\widecheck{\relax{S}}}$ satisfying ${\relax{r}}^{U''}(\lambda'',\sigma_1,\sigma_4)$ and ${\relax{r}}^{U''}(\lambda'',\sigma_2,\sigma_3)$.
<!-- end theorem-50 -->
<!-- theorem-51: body_md -->
{\bf [Orthogonality properties]}\label{theoremorthoproj}\\
The restriction to ${\relax{G}}^{\widecheck{\relax{S}}}$ of the orthogonality relation $\underline{\perp}$ satisfies the following properties.
\begin{eqnarray}
\hspace{-1cm}\forall \alpha,\beta\in {\relax{G}}^{\widecheck{\relax{S}}},&& \alpha \underline{\perp}\beta \;\;\Rightarrow\;\; \alpha\not=\beta,\label{propO1}\\
\forall \alpha,\beta\in {\relax{G}}^{\widecheck{\relax{S}}},&& \alpha \underline{\perp}\beta \;\;\Rightarrow\;\; \beta \underline{\perp}\alpha,\label{propO2}\\
\forall U\in { \relax{E}}_{\underline{\perp}}^{\check{\relax{S}}}, \forall \alpha,\beta,\epsilon,\delta\in U,&& (\,\alpha\not=\beta,\;\;\alpha \underline{\perp}\epsilon,\;\;\beta \underline{\perp}\epsilon,\;\;{\relax{r}}^U(\delta,\alpha,\beta)\,)\;\; \Rightarrow \;\; (\,\epsilon \underline{\perp} \delta\,),\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\label{propO3}\\
\forall \alpha,\beta\in {\relax{G}}^{\widecheck{\relax{S}}},\;\alpha\not=\beta,\alpha\asymp\beta,&& \exists U\in { \relax{E}}_{\underline{\perp}}^{\check{\relax{S}}}, \alpha,\beta\in U, \exists \epsilon\in U\;\;\vert\;\; {\relax{r}}^U(\epsilon,\alpha,\beta)\;\textit{\rm and}\; \epsilon \underline{\perp} \alpha.\label{propO4}\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end theorem-51 -->
<!-- proof-114: body_md -->
The properties ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@propO1\endcsname\@firstoftwo{propO1}}}) and ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@propO2\endcsname\@firstoftwo{propO2}}}) are trivial.\\

Let us now check the property ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@propO3\endcsname\@firstoftwo{propO3}}}).  As long as $\alpha \underline{\perp}\epsilon$ and $\beta \underline{\perp}\epsilon$, we have $\epsilon^\star \sqsubseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}} (\alpha\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{\relax{S}}}}\beta)$, but we have also $ (\alpha\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{\relax{S}}}}\beta)\raisebox{1.3ex}{\,\rotatebox{180}{$\sqsupseteq$}}\,_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}}\delta$ because ${\relax{r}}^U(\delta,\alpha,\beta)$. We then have $\epsilon^\star\sqsubseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}} \delta$, which means $\epsilon \underline{\perp}\delta$.\\

Let us now check the property ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@propO4\endcsname\@firstoftwo{propO4}}}). We have to distinguish the different cases. \\
Let us begin with $\alpha,\beta\in \overline{\relax{S}}{}^{{}^{pure}}$ with $\alpha\not=\beta$ and $\alpha\asymp\beta$. From Lemma {{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@lambdawr\endcsname\@firstoftwo{lambdawr}}} and $\alpha\asymp\beta$, we know that $\epsilon:=\alpha^\star \sqcup_{{}_{{\relax{S}}}}(\alpha\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{\relax{S}}}}\beta)$ exists in ${\relax{G}}^{\widecheck{\relax{S}}}$.  Moreover, using ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@thirdcoveringpropertySbarii\endcsname\@firstoftwo{thirdcoveringpropertySbarii}}}), we have $(\alpha\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{\relax{S}}}}\beta)\raisebox{1.3ex}{\,\rotatebox{180}{$\sqsupseteq$}}\,_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}}\epsilon$, i.e. ${\relax{r}}^U(\epsilon,\alpha,\beta)$. Endly, we have $\alpha^\star\sqsubseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}} \epsilon$,  i.e. $\epsilon \underline{\perp} \alpha$.\\
Secondly, let us consider the case where $\alpha\in \overline{\relax{S}}{}^{{}^{pure}}$ and $\beta\in {\relax{G}}^{\widecheck{\relax{S}}}\smallsetminus \overline{\relax{S}}{}^{{}^{pure}}$. The same analysis with the same expression for $\epsilon$ gives the same result.\\
Thirdly,  let us consider the case where $\beta\in \overline{\relax{S}}{}^{{}^{pure}}$ and $\alpha\in {\relax{G}}^{\widecheck{\relax{S}}}\smallsetminus \overline{\relax{S}}{}^{{}^{pure}}$.  By definition, there exists $\gamma\in \Theta^{\overline{\relax{S}}}(\alpha)$ and $\varphi_\gamma,\psi_\gamma\in \overline{\relax{S}}{}^{{}^{pure}}$ such that $\gamma=(\varphi_\gamma\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{\relax{S}}}}\psi_\gamma)\raisebox{1.3ex}{\,\rotatebox{180}{$\sqsupseteq$}}\,_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}}\varphi_\gamma,\psi_\gamma$ and $\alpha=\varphi_\gamma^\star \sqcup_{{}_{{\relax{S}}}}\gamma$. Let us denote by $\delta:=\beta\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{\relax{S}}}}\alpha \;\in \Theta^{\overline{\relax{S}}}(\alpha)$. We have to distinguish between two sub-cases :\\
(i) $\delta=\gamma$. In this case, it suffice to choose $\epsilon:=\varphi_\gamma$ and we check immediately $(\alpha\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{\relax{S}}}}\beta)\raisebox{1.3ex}{\,\rotatebox{180}{$\sqsupseteq$}}\,_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}}\epsilon$ and $\epsilon^\star \sqsubseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}} \alpha$.\\
(ii) $\delta\not=\gamma$. In this case, it suffice to choose $\epsilon:= \delta\sqcup_{{}_{{\relax{S}}}}\gamma^\star $ which is an element of ${\relax{G}}^{\widecheck{\relax{S}}}$ because of property ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@thirdcoveringpropertySbarvi\endcsname\@firstoftwo{thirdcoveringpropertySbarvi}}}).  We check immediately $(\alpha\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{\relax{S}}}}\beta)\raisebox{1.3ex}{\,\rotatebox{180}{$\sqsupseteq$}}\,_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}}\epsilon$ using property ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@thirdcoveringpropertySbarii\endcsname\@firstoftwo{thirdcoveringpropertySbarii}}}). We check also trivially $\gamma^\star \sqsubseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}} \epsilon$ and $\gamma \sqsubseteq_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}} \alpha$, which means $\epsilon \underline{\perp} \alpha$.\\
Fourthly, let us consider the case where $\beta,\alpha\in {\relax{G}}^{\widecheck{\relax{S}}}\smallsetminus \overline{\relax{S}}{}^{{}^{pure}}$.  The same construction as above leads to the result.
<!-- end proof-114 -->
<!-- theorem-52: body_md -->
{\bf [Irreducibility]}\label{theoremirredproj}\\
The space of states ${ \relax{S}}$ equipped with its real structure $(\overline{ \relax{S}},\star)$ satisfies the following irreducibility property
\begin{eqnarray}
\hspace{-1.3cm}\forall \sigma,\lambda\in { \relax{G}}^{\widecheck{\relax{S}}}, \sigma\not=\lambda, \sigma\asymp\lambda,\;\; \exists U\in  { \relax{E}}_{\underline{\perp}}^{\check{\relax{S}}},\sigma,\lambda\in U, \exists \kappa \in U\;\vert\; (\,\kappa\not=\sigma\;\textit{\rm and}\; \kappa\not=\lambda\;\textit{\rm and}\; {\relax{r}}^U(\kappa,\lambda,\sigma)\,).\;\;\;\;\;\;\label{propirreducibility}
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end theorem-52 -->
<!-- proof-115: body_md -->
First of all, we note that, if $\sigma\not\!\!\!\underline{\perp}\lambda$ and $\lambda\not=\sigma$ and $\sigma\asymp\lambda$,  using property ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@propO4\endcsname\@firstoftwo{propO4}}}), we deduce the existence of $U\in  { \relax{E}}^{\widecheck{\relax{S}}}$ such that $\sigma,\lambda\in U$ and the existence of $\kappa \in U$ such that ${\relax{r}}^U(\kappa,\lambda,\sigma)$ and $\sigma\underline{\perp}\kappa$. As long as $\sigma\underline{\perp}\kappa$ we deduce $\sigma\not=\kappa$, and as long as $\sigma\not\!\!\!\underline{\perp}\lambda$ we deduce $\kappa\not=\lambda$. This proves the property ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@propirreducibility\endcsname\@firstoftwo{propirreducibility}}}) when $\sigma\not\!\!\!\underline{\perp}\lambda$.\\

It remains to study the case $\sigma\underline{\perp}\lambda$, $\sigma\asymp\lambda$. Let us distinguish the different cases.\\

\noindent (1) Let us first study the case $\sigma,\lambda\in {\overline{\relax{S}}}{}^{{}^{pure}}$ with $\sigma\asymp\lambda$ and $\sigma\underline{\perp}\lambda$.  We will introduce $I\subseteq\{1,\cdots,N\}$ such that $Card(I)=N-2$ and $\forall i\in I,\zeta^{{}^{{\relax{S}}_{A_1}\cdots{\relax{S}}_{A_N}}}_{(i)}(\sigma) = \zeta^{{}^{{\relax{S}}_{A_1}\cdots{\relax{S}}_{A_N}}}_{(i)}(\lambda)$. We will also denote $j$ and $k$ such that $\{j,k\}=\{1,\cdots,N\}\smallsetminus I$ and $j<k$.\\
Then, we are in one of the two following sub-cases :\\
(1A) there exists $\alpha\in \overline{ \relax{S}}{}_{A_j}^{{}^{pure}}$ and $\beta,\beta'\in \overline{ \relax{S}}{}_{A_k}^{{}^{pure}}$ such that $\Upsilon^{(j,k)}_{\sigma}=\alpha\widetilde{\otimes}\beta$ and $\Upsilon^{(j,k)}_{\lambda}=\alpha^\star\widetilde{\otimes}\beta'$.  If $\beta=\beta'$ then for any $\alpha'\in \overline{ \relax{S}}{}_{A_j}^{{}^{pure}}$ such that $\alpha'\not=\alpha,\alpha^\star$, we can define $\kappa:=\alpha'\widetilde{\otimes}\beta$ which satisfies the announced constraints.  If $\beta\not=\beta'$, then, for any $\alpha'\in \overline{ \relax{S}}{}_{A_j}^{{}^{pure}}$ such that $\alpha'\not=\alpha,\alpha^\star$ we can define ${\kappa}:=(\Delta^{(j,k);\sigma}_{\alpha\widetilde{\otimes}\beta^\star})^\star \sqcup_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}}(\Delta^{(j,k);\sigma}_{\alpha\widetilde{\otimes}\beta^\star}\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\Delta^{(j,k);\sigma}_{\alpha'\widetilde{\otimes}\beta'})$ which satisfies indeed $\kappa\not=\sigma$,  $\kappa\not=\lambda$ and $(\sigma\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\lambda)\in \Theta^{{\overline{\relax{S}}}}(\kappa)$.\\
(1B) there exists $\alpha,\alpha'\in \overline{ \relax{S}}{}_{A_j}^{{}^{pure}}$ and $\beta\in \overline{ \relax{S}}{}_{A_k}^{{}^{pure}}$ such that $\Upsilon^{(j,k)}_{\sigma}=\alpha\widetilde{\otimes}\beta$ and $\Upsilon^{(j,k)}_{\lambda}=\alpha'\widetilde{\otimes}\beta^\star$.  Same treatment.\\

\noindent (2) Let us now study the case $\sigma\in {\overline{\relax{S}}}{}^{{}^{pure}}$, $\lambda\in { \relax{G}}^{\widecheck{\relax{S}}}\smallsetminus {\overline{\relax{S}}}{}^{{}^{pure}}$ with $\sigma\asymp\lambda$ and $\sigma\underline{\perp}\lambda$. We deduce that $\lambda=\varphi_\gamma^\star\sqcup_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}}(\varphi_\gamma\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\psi_\gamma)$ and $\sigma=\varphi_\gamma$ (we have adopted the same notation as in ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@thirdcoveringpropertySbar0\endcsname\@firstoftwo{thirdcoveringpropertySbar0}}}) ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@thirdcoveringpropertySbar0bis\endcsname\@firstoftwo{thirdcoveringpropertySbar0bis}}}) ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@thirdcoveringpropertySbarviic\endcsname\@firstoftwo{thirdcoveringpropertySbarviic}}}) ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@thirdcoveringpropertySbarviib\endcsname\@firstoftwo{thirdcoveringpropertySbarviib}}})). It then suffices to choose $\kappa:=\psi_\gamma$ to obtain $\kappa\not=\sigma$,  $\kappa\not=\lambda$ and $(\sigma\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\lambda)\in \Theta^{{\overline{\relax{S}}}}(\kappa)$.\\

\noindent (3) Let us now study the case $\sigma,\lambda\in { \relax{G}}^{\widecheck{\relax{S}}}\smallsetminus {\overline{\relax{S}}}{}^{{}^{pure}}$ with $\sigma\asymp\lambda$ and $\sigma\underline{\perp}\lambda$.  In this case, it suffices to choose $\kappa:=\psi_\alpha$ for $\{\alpha\}:=\Theta^{{\overline{\relax{S}}}}(\sigma)\cap\Theta^{{\overline{\relax{S}}}}(\lambda)$.\\

This concludes the proof.
<!-- end proof-115 -->
<!-- definition-70: body_md -->
{\bf [Broadcasting]}\\
We will say that a given space of states ${ \relax{S}}$ allows the broadcasting iff 
\begin{eqnarray}
\exists \Psi \in \overline{\relax{C}}({ \relax{S}},{ \relax{S}}\widetilde{\otimes}{ \relax{S}})&\vert &\forall \sigma\in \overline{\relax{S}},\;(\zeta^{{{ \relax{S}}}{{ \relax{S}}}}_{(1)}\circ \Psi)(\sigma) = (\zeta^{{{ \relax{S}}}{{ \relax{S}}}}_{(2)}\circ \Psi)(\sigma) = \sigma.\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end definition-70 -->
<!-- lemma-81: body_md -->
\label{lemmabroadcasting}
Let ${ \relax{m}}_1,{ \relax{m}}_2\in  \overline{\relax{M}}_{{}_{{ \relax{S}}}}$ be two real measurements on the space of states ${ \relax{S}}$ (they are real morphisms from ${ \relax{S}}$ to ${ \relax{B}}$).\\
If there exists a real morphism $\Psi \in \overline{\relax{C}}({ \relax{S}},{ \relax{S}}\widetilde{\otimes}{ \relax{S}})$ such that $\forall \sigma\in \overline{\relax{S}},\;(\zeta^{{{ \relax{S}}}{{ \relax{S}}}}_{(1)}\circ \Psi)(\sigma) = (\zeta^{{{ \relax{S}}}{{ \relax{S}}}}_{(2)}\circ \Psi)(\sigma) = \sigma$, then there exists a real morphism $\Psi_{({ \relax{m}}_1,{ \relax{m}}_2)} \in \overline{\relax{C}}({ \relax{S}},{ \relax{B}}\widetilde{\otimes}{ \relax{B}})$ such that $\forall \sigma\in \overline{\relax{S}}, (\zeta^{{{ \relax{B}}}{{ \relax{B}}}}_{(1)}\circ \Psi_{({ \relax{m}}_1,{ \relax{m}}_2)})(\sigma) = { \relax{m}}_1(\sigma)$ and $(\zeta^{{{ \relax{B}}}{{ \relax{B}}}}_{(2)}\circ \Psi_{({ \relax{m}}_1,{ \relax{m}}_2)})(\sigma) = { \relax{m}}_2(\sigma)$.
<!-- end lemma-81 -->
<!-- proof-116: body_md -->
It suffices to choose $\Psi_{({ \relax{m}}_1,{ \relax{m}}_2)}:= ({ \relax{m}}_1\widetilde{\otimes}{ \relax{m}}_2)\circ \Psi$.
<!-- end proof-116 -->
<!-- theorem-53: body_md -->
{\bf [No-broadcasting theorem]}\\
If the space of states ${ \relax{S}}$ (equipped with its real structure $(\overline{ \relax{S}},\star)$) is not deterministic, it does not allow the broadcasting.
<!-- end theorem-53 -->
<!-- proof-117: body_md -->
Let us consider the space of states ${ \relax{S}}$, and let us assume that it is NOT deterministic. We know, from the definition of indeterminism, that there exists $\sigma_1,\sigma_2\in  \overline{ \relax{S}}{}^{{}^{pure}}$ such that $\sigma_2\not=\sigma_1$ and $\sigma_2\not\sqsupseteq_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}} \sigma_1^\star$. Let us then define the following real measurements : ${ \relax{m}}_1:={ \relax{m}}_{{ \relax{l}}_{(\sigma_1,\sigma_1^\star)}}$ and ${ \relax{m}}_2:={ \relax{m}}_{{ \relax{l}}_{(\sigma_2,\sigma_2^\star)}}$. Let us now suppose that there exists a real morphism $\Psi_{({ \relax{m}}_1,{ \relax{m}}_2)} \in \overline{\relax{C}}({ \relax{S}},{ \relax{B}}\widetilde{\otimes}{ \relax{B}})$ such that $\zeta^{{{ \relax{B}}}{{ \relax{B}}}}_{(1)}\circ \Psi_{({ \relax{m}}_1,{ \relax{m}}_2)} = { \relax{m}}_1$ and $\zeta^{{{ \relax{B}}}{{ \relax{B}}}}_{(2)}\circ \Psi_{({ \relax{m}}_1,{ \relax{m}}_2)} = { \relax{m}}_2$, and let us exhibit a contradiction.\\
From ${ \relax{m}}_1(\sigma_1)=\textit{\bf Y}$ and ${ \relax{m}}_2(\sigma_1)=\bot$, we deduce that $\Psi_{({ \relax{m}}_1,{ \relax{m}}_2)}(\sigma_1)=\textit{\bf Y}\widetilde{\otimes} \bot$.\\
From ${ \relax{m}}_1(\sigma_1^\star)=\textit{\bf N}$ and ${ \relax{m}}_2(\sigma_1^\star)=\bot$, we deduce that $\Psi_{({ \relax{m}}_1,{ \relax{m}}_2)}(\sigma_1^\star)=\textit{\bf N}\widetilde{\otimes} \bot$.\\
From ${ \relax{m}}_1(\sigma_2^\star)=\bot$ and ${ \relax{m}}_2(\sigma_2^\star)=\textit{\bf N}$, we deduce that $\Psi_{({ \relax{m}}_1,{ \relax{m}}_2)}(\sigma_2^\star)=\bot\widetilde{\otimes} \textit{\bf N}$.\\

From $\Psi_{({ \relax{m}}_1,{ \relax{m}}_2)}(\sigma_1)=\textit{\bf Y}\widetilde{\otimes} \bot$ and $\Psi_{({ \relax{m}}_1,{ \relax{m}}_2)}(\sigma_1^\star)=\textit{\bf N}\widetilde{\otimes} \bot$ and the homomorphic properties satisfied by $\Psi_{({ \relax{m}}_1,{ \relax{m}}_2)}$ we deduce that
$\Psi_{({ \relax{m}}_1,{ \relax{m}}_2)}(\bot_{{}_{\relax{S}}})=\Psi_{({ \relax{m}}_1,{ \relax{m}}_2)}(\sigma_1\sqcap_{{}_{\relax{S}}}\sigma_1^\star)=\textit{\bf Y}\widetilde{\otimes} \bot \sqcap_{{}_{{ \relax{B}}^{\widetilde{\otimes}2}}} \textit{\bf N}\widetilde{\otimes} \bot=\bot\widetilde{\otimes} \bot$.\\
On another part, from $\Psi_{({ \relax{m}}_1,{ \relax{m}}_2)}(\sigma_2^\star)=\bot\widetilde{\otimes} \textit{\bf N}$ and $\Psi_{({ \relax{m}}_1,{ \relax{m}}_2)}(\sigma_1^\star)=\textit{\bf N}\widetilde{\otimes} \bot$ and the homomorphic properties satisfied by $\Psi_{({ \relax{m}}_1,{ \relax{m}}_2)}$ we deduce that
$\Psi_{({ \relax{m}}_1,{ \relax{m}}_2)}(\bot_{{}_{\relax{S}}})=\Psi_{({ \relax{m}}_1,{ \relax{m}}_2)}(\sigma_1^\star\sqcap_{{}_{\relax{S}}}\sigma_2^\star)=\bot\widetilde{\otimes}\textit{\bf N}\sqcap_{{}_{{ \relax{B}}^{\widetilde{\otimes}2}}} \textit{\bf N}\widetilde{\otimes} \bot$.\\
We have then obtained a contradiction.\\
As a conclusion,  and using Lemma {{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@lemmabroadcasting\endcsname\@firstoftwo{lemmabroadcasting}}}, we deduce that there cannot exist a real morphism $\Psi \in \overline{\relax{C}}({ \relax{S}},{ \relax{S}}\widetilde{\otimes}{ \relax{S}})$ such that $\forall \sigma\in \overline{\relax{S}},\;(\zeta^{{{ \relax{S}}}{{ \relax{S}}}}_{(1)}\circ \Psi)(\sigma) = (\zeta^{{{ \relax{S}}}{{ \relax{S}}}}_{(2)}\circ \Psi)(\sigma) = \sigma$. Hence, there is no broadcasting.
<!-- end proof-117 -->
<!-- lemma-82: body_md -->
If there exists two pairs of real measurements ${\phi}_1\in \overline{ \relax{C}}({ \relax{S}}_A,{ \relax{B}})$ and ${\phi}_2\in \overline{ \relax{C}}({ \relax{S}}_A,{ \relax{B}})$,  ${\rho}_1\in \overline{ \relax{C}}({ \relax{S}}_D,{ \relax{B}})$ and ${\rho}_2\in \overline{ \relax{C}}({ \relax{S}}_D, { \relax{B}})$ such that there exists no state $\Lambda \in  { \relax{B}}^{{\widetilde{\otimes}}4}$ satisfying  simultaneously the four relations  ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@bell1\endcsname\@firstoftwo{bell1}}}) ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@bell2\endcsname\@firstoftwo{bell2}}}) ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@bell3\endcsname\@firstoftwo{bell3}}}) ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@bell4\endcsname\@firstoftwo{bell4}}}), then the state ${\Sigma}$ is {\em a Bell non-local state}.
<!-- end lemma-82 -->
<!-- proof-118: body_md -->
see \@nx\protect\@empty\@nx\csname cite \endcsname{PlavalaA}.
<!-- end proof-118 -->
<!-- theorem-54: body_md -->
Bell non-local states do exist in ${{{ \widetilde{S}}}}_{AB}$.
<!-- end theorem-54 -->
<!-- proof-119: body_md -->
We will consider $\sigma_1,\sigma_2\in \overline{\relax{S}}{}^{{}^{pure}}_{A}$ and $\tau_1,\tau_2\in \overline{\relax{S}}{}^{{}^{pure}}_{B}$ such that $\sigma_1\not=\sigma_2,\sigma_2^\star$ and $\tau_1\not=\tau_2,\tau_2^\star$.  Let us now introduce a particular hidden-state. 

\begin{eqnarray}
\Sigma & := & (\sigma_1 \widetilde{\otimes} \tau_1 \sqcap_{{}_{\overline{S}_{AB}}} \sigma_2 \widetilde{\otimes} \tau_2) \sqcup_{{}_{\hat{S}_{AB}}} (\sigma_1^\star  \widetilde{\otimes} \bot_{{}_{ \relax{S}_B}} \sqcap_{{}_{\overline{S}_{AB}}} \bot_{{}_{ \relax{S}_A}} \widetilde{\otimes} \tau_1^\star).
\end{eqnarray}
This state do exist in the ontic completion $\hat{S}_{AB}:={ \relax{J}}^c_{\overline{{S}}_{AB}}$ of the real space $\overline{ {S}}_{AB}:={\overline{ \relax{S}}_A}\widetilde{\otimes}{\overline{ \relax{S}}_B}$.  More precisely, we have $\Sigma\in \hat{S}_{AB}\smallsetminus \overline{S}_{AB}$.

Indeed, as shown in subsection {{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@subsectionpreliminaryNdim\endcsname\@firstoftwo{subsectionpreliminaryNdim}}}, we have
\begin{eqnarray}
&&\hspace{-2cm} cl_c^{\overline{{S}}_{AB}}\left(
\left\{(\sigma_1 \widetilde{\otimes} \tau_1 \sqcap_{{}_{\overline{S}_{AB}}} \sigma_2 \widetilde{\otimes} \tau_2)\; ,\; (\sigma_1^\star  \widetilde{\otimes} \bot_{{}_{ \relax{S}_B}} \sqcap_{{}_{\overline{S}_{AB}}} \bot_{{}_{ \relax{S}_A}} \widetilde{\otimes} \tau_1^\star)\right\}\right)=\nonumber\\
&&\hspace{-1cm} =\left\{(\sigma_1 \widetilde{\otimes} \tau_1 \sqcap_{{}_{\overline{S}_{AB}}} \sigma_2 \widetilde{\otimes} \tau_2)\;,\; (\sigma_1 \widetilde{\otimes} \tau_1^\star \sqcap_{{}_{\overline{S}_{AB}}} \sigma_1^\star \widetilde{\otimes} \tau_2) \;,\; (\sigma_2 \widetilde{\otimes} \tau_1^\star \sqcap_{{}_{\overline{S}_{AB}}} \sigma_1^\star \widetilde{\otimes} \tau_1)\right\}\;\in {\mathcal{K}}(\overline{{S}}_{AB})\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;
\end{eqnarray}
     
Let us now consider the following real measurement operators 
\begin{eqnarray}
{\phi}_1:={ \relax{m}}_{{ \relax{l}}_{(\sigma_1,\sigma_1^\star)}}, && {\phi}_2:={ \relax{m}}_{{ \relax{l}}_{(\sigma_2,\sigma_2^\star)}}, \\
{\rho}_1:={ \relax{m}}_{{ \relax{l}}_{(\tau_1,\tau_1^\star)}}, &&{\rho}_2:={ \relax{m}}_{{ \relax{l}}_{(\tau_2,\tau_2^\star)}}.
\end{eqnarray}
