We now intent to prove that $\Sigma$ is a Bell non-local state with respect to the pairs of incompatible real measurements $(\phi_1,\phi_2)$ and $(\rho_1,\rho_2)$. In the following computation we use obviously the defining property ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@morphismtensorindeterminism\endcsname\@firstoftwo{morphismtensorindeterminism}}}).\\

The equality
\begin{eqnarray}
\Phi_{13} :=(\phi_1\widetilde{\otimes} \rho_1)({\Sigma})= \textit{\bf N} \,\widetilde{\otimes} \bot \sqcap_{{}_{{ \relax{B}}^{\widetilde{\otimes}2}}} \textit{\bf Y} \widetilde{\otimes}\, \textit{\bf N}.
\end{eqnarray} 
and the property $\zeta^{{ \relax{B}} { \relax{B}} { \relax{B}} { \relax{B}}}_{(1)(3)}(\Lambda) = \Phi_{13}$ imply
\begin{eqnarray}
\Lambda =  \bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{ \relax{B}}^{\widetilde{\otimes}4}}}_i\textit{\bf N} \,\widetilde{\otimes} \alpha_i \,\widetilde{\otimes}\textit{\bf N} \,\widetilde{\otimes} \beta_i \; \sqcap_{{}_{{ \relax{B}}^{\widetilde{\otimes}4}}}
\bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{ \relax{B}}^{\widetilde{\otimes}4}}}_j\textit{\bf N} \,\widetilde{\otimes} \gamma_j \,\widetilde{\otimes}\textit{\bf Y} \,\widetilde{\otimes} \delta_j \; \sqcap_{{}_{{ \relax{B}}^{\widetilde{\otimes}4}}} \bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{ \relax{B}}^{\widetilde{\otimes}4}}}_k\textit{\bf Y} \,\widetilde{\otimes} \epsilon_k \,\widetilde{\otimes}\textit{\bf N} \,\widetilde{\otimes} \varphi_k \;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;
\end{eqnarray} 
for certain collections $(\alpha_i,\beta_i)_i$, $(\gamma_j,\delta_j)_j$, $(\epsilon_k,\varphi_k)_k$ of pairs of elements of $\{\,\textit{\bf Y}\,,\, \textit{\bf N}\,\}$.\\

The equality
\begin{eqnarray}
\Phi_{14} :=(\phi_1\widetilde{\otimes} \rho_2)({\Sigma})= \textit{\bf Y} \,\widetilde{\otimes} \bot \sqcap_{{}_{{ \relax{B}}^{\widetilde{\otimes}2}}} \textit{\bf N} \widetilde{\otimes}\, \textit{\bf Y}.
\end{eqnarray} 
and the property $\zeta^{{ \relax{B}} { \relax{B}} { \relax{B}} { \relax{B}}}_{(1)(4)}(\Lambda) = \Phi_{14}$ imply
\begin{eqnarray}
\bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{ \relax{B}}^{\widetilde{\otimes}2}}}_i\textit{\bf N}  \,\widetilde{\otimes} \beta_i \; \sqcap_{{}_{{ \relax{B}}^{\widetilde{\otimes}2}}}
\bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{ \relax{B}}^{\widetilde{\otimes}2}}}_j\textit{\bf N}  \,\widetilde{\otimes} \delta_j \; \sqcap_{{}_{{ \relax{B}}^{\widetilde{\otimes}2}}} \bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{ \relax{B}}^{\widetilde{\otimes}2}}}_k\textit{\bf Y}  \,\widetilde{\otimes} \varphi_k  &=& \textit{\bf Y} \,\widetilde{\otimes} \bot \sqcap_{{}_{{ \relax{B}}^{\widetilde{\otimes}2}}} \textit{\bf N} \widetilde{\otimes}\, \textit{\bf Y},\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\; 
\end{eqnarray} 
and then
\begin{eqnarray}
\bigwedge{}_i \beta_i \wedge
\bigwedge{}_j \delta_j = \textit{\bf Y}, & & \bigwedge{}_k \varphi_k = \bot.
\end{eqnarray} 



The equality
\begin{eqnarray}
\Phi_{23}:=(\phi_2\widetilde{\otimes} \rho_1)({\Sigma}) = \textit{\bf Y} \,\widetilde{\otimes} \textit{\bf N} \sqcap_{{}_{{ \relax{B}}^{\widetilde{\otimes}2}}} \bot \widetilde{\otimes}\, \textit{\bf Y}.
\end{eqnarray} 
and $\zeta^{{ \relax{B}} { \relax{B}} { \relax{B}} { \relax{B}}}_{(2)(3)}(\Lambda) = \Phi_{23}$ imply 
\begin{eqnarray}
\bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{ \relax{B}}^{\widetilde{\otimes}2}}}_i \alpha_i  \,\widetilde{\otimes} \textit{\bf N} \; \sqcap_{{}_{{ \relax{B}}^{\widetilde{\otimes}2}}}
 \bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{ \relax{B}}^{\widetilde{\otimes}2}}}_j \gamma_j  \,\widetilde{\otimes} \textit{\bf Y} \; \sqcap_{{}_{{ \relax{B}}^{\widetilde{\otimes}2}}} \bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{ \relax{B}}^{\widetilde{\otimes}2}}}_k \epsilon_k  \,\widetilde{\otimes} \textit{\bf N}  &=& \textit{\bf Y} \,\widetilde{\otimes} \textit{\bf N} \sqcap_{{}_{{ \relax{B}}^{\widetilde{\otimes}2}}} \bot \widetilde{\otimes}\, \textit{\bf Y},\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\; 
\end{eqnarray} 
and then
\begin{eqnarray}
\bigwedge{}_i \alpha_i \wedge \bigwedge{}_k \epsilon_k = \textit{\bf Y}, &  & \bigwedge{}_j \gamma_j = \bot.
\end{eqnarray} 



If we summarize what we have obtained, we have
\begin{eqnarray}
\Lambda &=& \textit{\bf N} \,\widetilde{\otimes} \textit{\bf Y} \,\widetilde{\otimes}\textit{\bf N} \,\widetilde{\otimes} \textit{\bf Y} \; \sqcap_{{}_{{ \relax{B}}^{\widetilde{\otimes}4}}}
\textit{\bf N} \,\widetilde{\otimes} \bot \,\widetilde{\otimes}\textit{\bf Y} \,\widetilde{\otimes} \textit{\bf Y} \; 
\sqcap_{{}_{{ \relax{B}}^{\widetilde{\otimes}4}}} 
\textit{\bf Y} \,\widetilde{\otimes} \textit{\bf Y} \,\widetilde{\otimes}\textit{\bf N} \,\widetilde{\otimes} \bot 
\end{eqnarray} 


Now we use the equality
\begin{eqnarray}
\Phi_{24} :=(\phi_2\widetilde{\otimes} \rho_2)({\Sigma})= \bot \,\widetilde{\otimes} \bot.
\end{eqnarray} 
and  $\zeta^{{ \relax{B}} { \relax{B}} { \relax{B}} { \relax{B}}}_{(2)(4)}(\Lambda) = \Phi_{24}$ to obtain the announced contradiction. Indeed, we have
\begin{eqnarray}
\textit{\bf Y} \,\widetilde{\otimes} \bot \sqcap_{{}_{{ \relax{B}}^{\widetilde{\otimes}2}}} \bot \widetilde{\otimes} \textit{\bf Y} \not= \bot \,\widetilde{\otimes}\, \bot.
\end{eqnarray} 

As a  conclusion,  the state $\Sigma$ is Bell non-local and the pairs $(\phi_1,\phi_2)$ et $(\rho_1,\rho_2)$ are pairs of incompatible real measurements.
<!-- end proof-119 -->
